text_content: Three days later, the Dursleys were showing no sign of relenting and Harry couldn’t see any way out of his situation. He lay on his bed watching the sun sinking behind the bars on the window and wondered miserably what was going to happen to him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: What was the good of magicking himself out of his room if Hogwarts would expel him for doing it? Yet life at Privet Drive had reached an all-time low. Now the Dursleys knew they weren’t going to wake up as fruitbats, he had lost his only weapon. Dobby might have saved Harry from horrible happenings at Hogwarts, but the way things were going, he’d probably starve to death anyway.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The cat-flap rattled and Aunt Petunia’s hand appeared, pushing a bowl of tinned soup into the room. Harry, whose insides were aching with hunger, jumped off his bed and seized it. The soup was stone cold, but he drank half of it in one gulp. Then he crossed the room to Hedwig’s cage and tipped the soggy vegetables at the bottom of the bowl into her empty food tray. She ruffled her feathers and gave him a look of deep disgust.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s no good turning your beak up at it, that’s all we’ve got,’ said Harry grimly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He put the empty bowl back on the floor next to the cat-flap and lay back down on the bed, somehow even hungrier than he had been before the soup.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Supposing he was still alive in another four weeks, what would happen if he didn’t turn up at Hogwarts? Would someone be sent to see why he hadn’t come back? Would they be able to make the Dursleys let him go?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The room was growing dark. Exhausted, stomach rumbling, mind spinning over the same unanswerable questions, Harry fell into an uneasy sleep.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He dreamed that he was on show in a zoo, with a card reading ‘Underage Wizard’ attached to his cage. People goggled through the bars at him as he lay, starving and weak, on a bed of straw. He saw Dobby’s face in the crowd and shouted out, asking for help, but Dobby called, ‘Harry Potter is safe there, sir!’ and vanished. Then the Dursleys appeared and Dudley rattled the bars of the cage, laughing at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Stop it,’ Harry muttered, as the rattling pounded in his sore head. ‘Leave me alone … cut it out … I’m trying to sleep …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He opened his eyes. Moonlight was shining through the bars on the window. And someone was goggling through the bars at him: a freckle-faced, red-haired, long-nosed someone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron Weasley was outside Harry’s window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron!’ breathed Harry, creeping to the window and pushing it up so they could talk through the bars. ‘Ron, how did you - what the -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry’s mouth fell open as the full impact of what he was seeing hit him. Ron was leaning out of the back window of an old turquoise car, which was parked in mid-air. Grinning at Harry from the front seats were Fred and George, Ron’s elder twin brothers.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘All right, Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s been going on?’ said Ron. ‘Why haven’t you been answering my letters? I’ve asked you to stay about twelve times, and then Dad came home and said you’d got an official warning for using magic in front of Muggles …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It wasn’t me - and how did he know?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He works for the Ministry,’ said Ron. ‘You know we’re not supposed to do spells outside school -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Bit rich coming from you,’ said Harry, staring at the floating car.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, this doesn’t count,’ said Ron. ‘We’re only borrowing this, it’s Dad’s, we didn’t enchant it. But doing magic in front of those Muggles you live with …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I told you, I didn’t - but it’ll take too long to explain now. Look, can you explain to them at Hogwarts that the Dursleys have locked me up and won’t let me come back, and obviously I can’t magic myself out, because the Ministry’ll think that’s the second spell I’ve done in three days, so -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Stop gibbering,’ said Ron, ‘we’ve come to take you home with us.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But you can’t magic me out either -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We don’t need to,’ said Ron, jerking his head towards the front seats and grinning. ‘You forget who I’ve got with me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Tie that round the bars,’ said Fred, throwing the end of a rope to Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘If the Dursleys wake up, I’m dead,’ said Harry, as he tied the rope tightly around a bar and Fred revved up the car.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t worry,’ said Fred, ‘and stand back.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry moved back into the shadows next to Hedwig, who seemed to have realised how important this was and kept still and silent. The car revved louder and louder and suddenly, with a crunching noise, the bars were pulled clean out of the window as Fred drove straight up in the air - Harry ran back to the window to see the bars dangling a few feet above the ground. Panting, Ron hoisted them up into the car. Harry listened anxiously, but there was no sound from the Dursleys’ bedroom.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When the bars were safely in the back seat with Ron, Fred reversed as close as possible to Harry’s window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Get in,’ Ron said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But all my Hogwarts stuff … my wand … my broomstick …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Where is it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Locked in the cupboard under the stairs, and I can’t get out of this room -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No problem,’ said George from the front passenger seat. ‘Out of the way, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fred and George climbed carefully through the window into Harry’s room. You had to hand it to them, thought Harry, as George took an ordinary hairpin from his pocket and started to pick the lock.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘A lot of wizards think it’s a waste of time, knowing this sort of Muggle trick,’ said Fred, ‘but we feel they’re skills worth learning, even if they are a bit slow.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a small click and the door swung open.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So - we’ll get your trunk - you grab anything you need from your room and hand it out to Ron,’ whispered George.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Watch out for the bottom stair, it creaks,’ Harry whispered back, as the twins disappeared onto the dark landing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry dashed around his room, collecting his things together and passing them out of the window to Ron. Then he went to help Fred and George heave his trunk up the stairs. Harry heard Uncle Vernon cough.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: At last, panting, they reached the landing, then carried the trunk through Harry’s room to the open window. Fred climbed back into the car to pull with Ron, and Harry and George pushed from the bedroom side. Inch by inch, the trunk slid through the window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Uncle Vernon coughed again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘A bit more,’ panted Fred, who was pulling from inside the car, ‘one good push …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and George threw their shoulders against the trunk and it slid out of the window into the back seat of the car.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘OK, let’s go,’ George whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But as Harry climbed onto the window-sill there came a sudden loud screech from behind him, followed immediately by the thunder of Uncle Vernon’s voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘THAT RUDDY OWL!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve forgotten Hedwig!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry tore back across the room as the landing light clicked on. He snatched up Hedwig’s cage, dashed to the window and passed it out to Ron. He was scrambling back onto the chest of drawers when Uncle Vernon hammered on the unlocked door - and it crashed open.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: For a split second, Uncle Vernon stood framed in the doorway; then he let out a bellow like an angry bull and dived at Harry, grabbing him by the ankle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron, Fred and George seized Harry’s arms and pulled as hard as they could.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Petunia!’ roared Uncle Vernon. ‘He’s getting away! HE’S GETTING AWAY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Weasleys gave a gigantic tug and Harry’s leg slid out of Uncle Vernon’s grasp. As soon as Harry was in the car and had slammed the door shut, Ron yelled, ‘Put your foot down, Fred!’ and the car shot suddenly towards the moon.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry couldn’t believe it - he was free. He wound down the window, the night air whipping his hair, and looked back at the shrinking rooftops of Privet Drive. Uncle Vernon, Aunt Petunia and Dudley were all hanging, dumbstruck, out of Harry’s window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘See you next summer!’ Harry yelled.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Weasleys roared with laughter and Harry settled back in his seat, grinning from ear to ear.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Let Hedwig out,’ he told Ron, ‘she can fly behind us. She hasn’t had a chance to stretch her wings for ages.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: George handed the hairpin to Ron and a moment later, Hedwig had soared joyfully out of the window to glide alongside them like a ghost.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So - what’s the story, Harry?’ said Ron impatiently. ‘What’s been happening?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry told them all about Dobby, the warning he’d given Harry and the fiasco of the violet pudding. There was a long shocked silence when he had finished.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Very fishy,’ said Fred finally.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Definitely dodgy,’ agreed George. ‘So he wouldn’t even tell you who’s supposed to be plotting all this stuff?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t think he could,’ said Harry. ‘I told you, every time he got close to letting something slip, he started banging his head against the wall.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He saw Fred and George look at each other.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What, you think he was lying to me?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well,’ said Fred, ‘put it this way - house-elves have got powerful magic of their own, but they can’t usually use it without their masters’ permission. I reckon old Dobby was sent to stop you coming back to Hogwarts. Someone’s idea of a joke. Can you think of anyone at school with a grudge against you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Harry and Ron together, instantly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Draco Malfoy,’ Harry explained. ‘He hates me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Draco Malfoy?’ said George, turning round. ‘Not Lucius Malfoy’s son?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Must be, it’s not a very common name, is it?’ said Harry. ‘Why?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve heard Dad talking about him,’ said George. ‘He was a big supporter of You Know Who.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And when You Know Who disappeared,’ said Fred, craning around to look at Harry, ‘Lucius Malfoy came back saying he’d never meant any of it. Load of dung - Dad reckons he was right in You Know Who’s inner circle.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had heard these rumours about Malfoy’s family before, and they didn’t surprise him at all. Draco Malfoy made Dudley Dursley look like a kind, thoughtful and sensitive boy.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t know whether the Malfoys own a house-elf …’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, whoever owns him will be an old wizarding family, and they’ll be rich,’ said Fred.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, Mum’s always wishing we had a house-elf to do the ironing,’ said George. ‘But all we’ve got is a lousy old ghoul in the attic and gnomes all over the garden. House-elves come with big old manors and castles and places like that, you wouldn’t catch one in our house …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry was silent. Judging by the fact that Draco Malfoy usually had the best of everything, his family was rolling in wizard gold; he could just see Malfoy strutting around a large manor house. Sending the family servant to stop Harry going back to Hogwarts also sounded exactly like the sort of thing Malfoy would do. Had Harry been stupid to take Dobby seriously?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m glad we came to get you, anyway,’ said Ron. ‘I was getting really worried when you didn’t answer any of my letters. I thought it was Errol’s fault at first -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Who’s Errol?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Our owl. He’s ancient. It wouldn’t be the first time he’d collapsed on a delivery. So then I tried to borrow Hermes -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Who?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The owl Mum and Dad bought Percy when he was made a prefect,’ said Fred from the front.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But Percy wouldn’t lend him to me,’ said Ron. ‘Said he needed him.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Percy’s been acting very oddly this summer,’ said George, frowning. ‘And he has been sending a lot of letters and spending a load of time shut up in his room … I mean, there’s only so many times you can polish a prefect badge … You’re driving too far west, Fred,’ he added, pointing at a compass on the dashboard. Fred twiddled the steering wheel.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So, does your dad know you’ve got the car?’ said Harry, guessing the answer.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Er, no,’ said Ron, ‘he had to work tonight. Hopefully we’ll be able to get it back in the garage without Mum noticing we flew it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What does your dad do at the Ministry of Magic, anyway?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He works in the most boring department,’ said Ron. ‘The Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The what?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all to do with bewitching things that are Muggle-made, you know, in case they end up back in a Muggle shop or house. Like, last year, some old witch died and her tea set was sold to an antiques shop. This Muggle woman bought it, took it home and tried to serve her friends tea in it. It was a nightmare - Dad was working overtime for weeks.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What happened?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The teapot went berserk and squirted boiling tea all over the place and one man ended up in hospital with the sugar tongs clamped to his nose. Dad was going frantic, it’s only him and an old warlock called Perkins in the office, and they had to do Memory Charms and all sorts to cover it up …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But your dad … this car …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fred laughed. ‘Yeah, Dad’s mad about everything to do with Muggles, our shed’s full of Muggle stuff. He takes it apart, puts spells on it and puts it back together again. If he raided our house he’d have to put himself straight under arrest. It drives Mum mad.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s the main road,’ said George, peering down through the windscreen. ‘We’ll be there in ten minutes … just as well, it’s getting light …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A faint pinkish glow was visible along the horizon to the east.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fred brought the car lower and Harry saw a dark patchwork of fields and clumps of trees.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re a little way outside the village,’ said George. ‘Ottery St Catchpole …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Lower and lower went the flying car. The edge of a brilliant red sun was now gleaming through the trees.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Touchdown!’ said Fred as, with a slight bump, they hit the ground. They had landed next to a tumbledown garage in a small yard and Harry looked out for the first time at Ron’s house.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It looked as though it had once been a large stone pigsty, but extra rooms had been added here and there until it was several storeys high and so crooked it looked as though it was held up by magic (which, Harry reminded himself, it probably was). Four or five chimneys were perched on top of the red roof. A lop-sided sign stuck in the ground near the entrance read ‘The Burrow’. Round the front door lay a jumble of wellington boots and a very rusty cauldron. Several fat brown chickens were pecking their way around the yard.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s not much,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s brilliant,‘ said Harry happily, thinking of Privet Drive.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They got out of the car.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, we’ll go upstairs really quietly,’ said Fred, ‘and wait for Mum to call us for breakfast. Then Ron, you come bounding downstairs going, ‘Mum, look who turned up in the night!’ and she’ll be all pleased to see Harry and no one need ever know we flew the car.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Ron. ‘Come on, Harry, I sleep at the -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron had gone a nasty greenish colour, his eyes fixed on the house. The other three wheeled around.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mrs Weasley was marching across the yard, scattering chickens, and for a short, plump, kind-faced woman, it was remarkable how much she looked like a sabre-toothed tiger.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ah,’ said Fred.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh dear,’ said George.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mrs Weasley came to a halt in front of them, her hands on her hips, staring from one guilty face to the next. She was wearing a flowered apron with a wand sticking out of the pocket.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ she said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Morning, Mum,’ said George, in what he clearly thought was a jaunty, winning voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Have you any idea how worried I’ve been?’ said Mrs Weasley in a deadly whisper.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Sorry, Mum, but see, we had to -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: All three of Mrs Weasley’s sons were taller than she was, but they cowered as her rage broke over them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Beds empty! No note! Car gone … could have crashed … out of my mind with worry … did you care? … never, as long as I’ve lived … you wait until your father gets home, we never had trouble like this from Bill or Charlie or Percy …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Perfect Percy,’ muttered Fred.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘YOU COULD DO WITH TAKING A LEAF OUT OF PERCY’S BOOK!’ yelled Mrs Weasley, prodding a finger in Fred’s chest. ‘You could have died, you could have been seen, you could have lost your father his job -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It seemed to go on for hours. Mrs Weasley had shouted herself hoarse before she turned on Harry, who backed away.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m very pleased to see you, Harry, dear,’ she said, ‘Come in and have some breakfast.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She turned and walked back into the house and Harry, after a nervous glance at Ron, who nodded encouragingly, followed her.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The kitchen was small and rather cramped. There was a scrubbed wooden table and chairs in the middle and Harry sat down on the edge of his seat, looking around. He had never been in a wizard house before.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The clock on the wall opposite him had only one hand and no numbers at all. Written around the edge were things like ‘Time to make tea’, ‘Time to feed the chickens’ and ‘You’re late’. Books were stacked three deep on the mantelpiece, books with titles like Charm Your Own Cheese, Enchantment in Baking and One Minute Feasts - It’s Magic! And unless Harry’s ears were deceiving him, the old radio next to the sink had just announced that coming up was ‘Witching Hour, with the popular singing sorceress, Celestina Warbeck’.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mrs Weasley was clattering around, cooking breakfast a little haphazardly, throwing dirty looks at her sons as she threw sausages into the frying pan. Every now and then she muttered things like ‘don’t know what you were thinking of’ and ‘never would have believed it’.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t blame you, dear,’ she assured Harry, tipping eight or nine sausages onto his plate. ‘Arthur and I have been worried about you, too. Just last night we were saying we’d come and get you ourselves if you hadn’t written back to Ron by Friday. But really’ (she was now adding three fried eggs to his plate), ‘flying an illegal car halfway across the country -anyone could have seen you -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She flicked her wand casually at the washing-up in the sink, which began to clean itself, clinking gently in the background.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It was cloudy, Mum!’ said Fred.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You keep your mouth closed while you’re eating!’ Mrs Weasley snapped.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘They were starving him, Mum!’ said George.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And you!’ said Mrs Weasley, but it was with a slightly softened expression that she started cutting Harry bread and buttering it for him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: At that moment, there was a diversion in the form of a small, red-headed figure in a long nightdress, who appeared in the kitchen, gave a small squeal, and ran out again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ginny,’ said Ron in an undertone to Harry. ‘My sister. She’s been talking about you all summer.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, she’ll be wanting your autograph, Harry,’ grinned Fred, but he caught his mother’s eye and bent his face over his plate without another word. Nothing more was said until all four plates were clean, which took a surprisingly short time.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Blimey, I’m tired,’ yawned Fred, setting down his knife and fork at last. ‘I think I’ll go to bed and -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You will not,’ snapped Mrs Weasley. ‘It’s your own fault you’ve been up all night. You’re going to de-gnome the garden for me, they’re getting completely out of hand again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, Mum -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And you two,’ she said, glaring at Ron and George. ‘You can go up to bed, dear,’ she added to Harry. ‘You didn’t ask them to fly that wretched car.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Harry, who felt wide awake, said quickly, ‘I’ll help Ron, I’ve never seen a de-gnoming -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s very sweet of you, dear, but it’s dull work,’ said Mrs Weasley. ‘Now, let’s see what Lockhart’s got to say on the subject.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And she pulled a heavy book from the stack on the mantelpiece. George groaned.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Mum, we know how to de-gnome a garden.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked at the cover of Mrs Weasley’s book. Written across it in fancy gold letters were the words: Gilderoy Lockhart’s Guide to Household Pests. There was a big photograph on the front of a very good-looking wizard with wavy blond hair and bright blue eyes. As always in the wizarding world, the photograph was moving; the wizard, who Harry supposed was Gilderoy Lockhart, kept winking cheekily up at them all. Mrs Weasley beamed down at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, he is marvellous,’ she said, ‘he knows his household pests, all right, it’s a wonderful book …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Mum fancies him,’ said Fred, in a very audible whisper.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

text_content: Innumerable candles were hovering in mid-air over four long, crowded tables, making the golden plates and goblets sparkle. Overhead, the bewitched ceiling which always mirrored the sky outside, sparkled with stars.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Through the forest of pointed black Hogwarts hats, Harry saw a long line of scared-looking first-years filing into the Hall. Ginny was amongst them, easily visible because of her vivid Weasley hair. Meanwhile, Professor McGonagall, a bespectacled witch with her hair in a tight bun, was placing the famous Hogwarts Sorting Hat on a stool before the newcomers.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Every year, this aged old hat, patched, frayed and dirty, sorted new students into the four Hogwarts houses (Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw and Slytherin). Harry well remembered putting it on, exactly one year ago, and waiting, petrified, for its decision as it muttered aloud in his ear. For a few horrible seconds he had feared that the hat was going to put him in Slytherin, the house which had turned out more dark witches and wizards than any other - but he had ended up in Gryffindor, along with Ron, Hermione and the rest of the Weasleys. Last term, Harry and Ron had helped Gryffindor win the House Championship, beating Slytherin for the first time in seven years.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A very small, mousey-haired boy had been called forward to place the hat on his head. Harry’s eyes wandered past him to where Professor Dumbledore, the Headmaster, sat watching the Sorting from the staff table, his long silver beard and half-moon glasses shining brightly in the candlelight. Several seats along, Harry saw Gilderoy Lockhart, dressed in robes of aquamarine. And there at the end was Hagrid, huge and hairy, drinking deeply from his goblet.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hang on …’ Harry muttered to Ron. ‘There’s an empty chair at the staff table … Where’s Snape?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor Severus Snape was Harry’s least favourite teacher. Harry also happened to be Snape’s least favourite student. Cruel, sarcastic and disliked by everybody except the students from his own house (Slytherin), Snape taught Potions.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Maybe he’s ill!’ said Ron hopefully.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Maybe he’s left,‘ said Harry, ‘because he missed out on the Defence Against the Dark Arts job again!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Or he might have been sacked!’ said Ron enthusiastically. ‘I mean, everyone hates him -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Or maybe,’ said a very cold voice right behind them, ‘he’s waiting to hear why you two didn’t arrive on the school train.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry spun around. There, his black robes rippling in a cold breeze, stood Severus Snape. He was a thin man with sallow skin, a hooked nose and greasy, shoulder-length black hair, and at this moment, he was smiling in a way that told Harry he and Ron were in very deep trouble.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Follow me,’ said Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Not daring even to look at each other, Harry and Ron followed Snape up the steps into the vast, echoing Entrance Hall, which was lit with flaming torches. A delicious smell of food was wafting from the Great Hall, but Snape led them away from the warmth and light, down a narrow stone staircase that led into the dungeons.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘In!’ he said, opening a door halfway down the cold passageway and pointing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They entered Snape’s office, shivering. The shadowy walls were lined with shelves of large glass jars, in which floated all manner of revolting things Harry didn’t really want to know the name of at the moment. The fireplace was dark and empty. Snape closed the door and turned to look at them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ he said softly, ‘the train isn’t good enough for the famous Harry Potter and his faithful sidekick Weasley. Wanted to arrive with a bang, did we, boys?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No, sir, it was the barrier at King’s Cross, it -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Silence!’ said Snape coldly. ‘What have you done with the car?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron gulped. This wasn’t the first time Snape had given Harry the impression of being able to read minds. But a moment later, he understood, as Snape unrolled today’s issue of the Evening Prophet.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You were seen,’ he hissed, showing them the headline: FLYING FORD ANGLIA MYSTIFIES MUGGLES. He began to read aloud. ‘“Two Muggles in London, convinced they saw an old car flying over the Post Office tower … at noon in Norfolk, Mrs Hetty Bayliss, while hanging out her washing … Mr Angus Fleet, of Peebles, reported to police” … six or seven Muggles in all. I believe your father works in the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office?’ he said, looking up at Ron and smiling still more nastily. ‘Dear, dear … his own son …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry felt as though he’d just been walloped in the stomach by one of the mad tree’s larger branches. If anyone found out Mr Weasley had bewitched the car … he hadn’t thought of that …

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I noticed, in my search of the park, that considerable damage seems to have been done to a very valuable Whomping Willow,’ Snape went on.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That tree did more damage to us than we -‘ Ron blurted out.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Silence!’ snapped Snape again. ‘Most unfortunately, you are not in my house and the decision to expel you does not rest with me. I shall go and fetch the people who do have that happy power. You will wait here.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron stared at each other, white-faced. Harry didn’t feel hungry any more. He now felt extremely sick. He tried not to look at a large, slimy something suspended in green liquid on a shelf behind Snape’s desk. If Snape had gone to fetch Professor McGonagall, head of Gryffindor house, they were hardly any better off. She might be fairer than Snape, but she was still extremely strict.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ten minutes later, Snape returned, and sure enough it was Professor McGonagall who accompanied him. Harry had seen Professor McGonagall angry on several occasions, but either he had forgotten just how thin her mouth could go, or he had never seen her this angry before. She raised her wand the moment she entered. Harry and Ron both flinched, but she merely pointed it at the empty fireplace, where flames suddenly erupted.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Sit,’ she said, and they both backed into chairs by the fire.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Explain,’ she said, her glasses glinting ominously.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron launched into the story, starting with the barrier at the station refusing to let them through.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… so we had no choice, Professor, we couldn’t get on the train.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Why didn’t you send us a letter by owl? I believe you have an owl?’ Professor McGonagall said coldly to Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry gaped at her. Now she said it, that seemed the obvious thing to have done.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I - I didn’t think -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That,’ said Professor McGonagall, ‘is obvious.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a knock on the office door and Snape, now looking happier than ever, opened it. There stood the Headmaster, Professor Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry’s whole body went numb. Dumbledore was looking unusually grave. He stared down his very crooked nose at them and Harry suddenly found himself wishing he and Ron were still being beaten up by the Whomping Willow.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a long silence. Then Dumbledore said, ‘Please explain why you did this.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It would have been better if he had shouted. Harry hated the disappointment in his voice. For some reason, he was unable to look Dumbledore in the eyes, and spoke instead to his knees. He told Dumbledore everything except that Mr Weasley owned the bewitched car, making it sound as though he and Ron had happened to find a flying car parked outside the station. He knew Dumbledore would see through this at once, but Dumbledore asked no questions about the car. When Harry had finished, he merely continued to peer at them through his spectacles.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ll go and get our stuff,’ said Ron in a hopeless sort of voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What are you talking about, Weasley?’ barked Professor McGonagall.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, you’re expelling us, aren’t you?’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked quickly at Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Not today, Mr Weasley,’ said Dumbledore. ‘But I must impress upon both of you the seriousness of what you have done. I will be writing to both your families tonight. I must also warn you that if you do anything like this again, I will have no choice but to expel you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Snape looked as though Christmas had been cancelled. He cleared his throat and said, ‘Professor Dumbledore, these boys have flouted the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Wizardry, caused serious damage to an old and valuable tree … surely acts of this nature …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It will be for Professor McGonagall to decide on these boys’ punishments, Severus,’ said Dumbledore calmly. ‘They are in her house and are therefore her responsibility.’ He turned to Professor McGonagall. ‘I must go back to the feast, Minerva, I’ve got to give out a few notices. Come, Severus, there’s a delicious-looking custard tart I want to sample.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Snape shot a look of pure venom at Harry and Ron as he allowed himself to be swept out of his office, leaving them alone with Professor McGonagall, who was still eyeing them like a wrathful eagle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’d better get along to the hospital wing, Weasley, you’re bleeding.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Not much,’ said Ron, hastily wiping the cut over his eye with his sleeve. ‘Professor, I wanted to watch my sister being Sorted -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The Sorting Ceremony is over,’ said Professor McGonagall. ‘Your sister is also in Gryffindor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, good,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And speaking of Gryffindor -‘ Professor McGonagall said sharply, but Harry cut in: ‘Professor, when we took the car, term hadn’t started, so - so Gryffindor shouldn’t really have points taken from it, should it?’ he finished, watching her anxiously.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor McGonagall gave him a piercing look, but he was sure she had almost smiled. Her mouth looked less thin, anyway.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I will not take any points from Gryffindor,’ she said, and Harry’s heart lightened considerably. ‘But you will both get a detention.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was better than Harry had expected. As for Dumbledore’s writing to the Dursleys, that was nothing. Harry knew perfectly well they’d just be disappointed that the Whomping Willow hadn’t squashed him flat.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor McGonagall raised her wand again and pointed it at Snape’s desk. A large plate of sandwiches, two silver goblets and a jug of iced pumpkin juice appeared with a pop.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You will eat in here and then go straight up to your dormitory,’ she said. ‘I must also return to the feast.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When the door had closed behind her, Ron let out a long, low whistle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I thought we’d had it,’ he said, grabbing a sandwich.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So did I,’ said Harry, taking one too.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Can you believe our luck, though?’ said Ron thickly through a mouthful of chicken and ham. ‘Fred and George must’ve flown that car five or six times and no Muggle ever saw them.‘ He swallowed and took another huge bite. ‘Why couldn’t we get through the barrier?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry shrugged. ‘We’ll have to watch our step from now on, though,’ he said, taking a grateful swig of pumpkin juice. ‘Wish we could’ve gone up to the feast …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘She didn’t want us showing off,’ said Ron sagely. ‘Doesn’t want people to think it’s clever, arriving by flying car.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When they had eaten as many sandwiches as they could (the plate kept re-filling itself) they rose and left the office, treading the familiar path to Gryffindor Tower. The castle was quiet; it seemed that the feast was over. They walked past muttering portraits and creaking suits of armour, and climbed narrow flights of stone stairs, until at last they reached the passage where the secret entrance to Gryffindor Tower was hidden, behind an oil painting of a very fat woman in a pink silk dress.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Password?’ she said, as they approached.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Er -‘ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They didn’t know the new year’s password, not having met a Gryffindor Prefect yet, but help came almost immediately; they heard hurrying feet behind them and turned to see Hermione dashing towards them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘There you are! Where have you been? The most ridiculous rumours -someone said you’d been expelled for crashing a flying car.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, we haven’t been expelled,’ Harry assured her.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re not telling me you did fly here?’ said Hermione, sounding almost as severe as Professor McGonagall.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Skip the lecture,’ said Ron impatiently, ‘and tell us the new password.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s “wattlebird”,’ said Hermione impatiently, ‘but that’s not the point -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Her words were cut short, however, as the portrait of the fat lady swung open and there was a sudden storm of clapping. It looked as though the whole of Gryffindor house was still awake, packed into the circular common room, standing on the lop-sided tables and squashy armchairs, waiting for them to arrive. Arms reached through the portrait hole to pull Harry and Ron inside, leaving Hermione to scramble in after them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Brilliant!’ yelled Lee Jordan. ‘Inspired! What an entrance! Flying a car right into the Whomping Willow, people’ll be talking about that one for years!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good on you,’ said a fifth-year Harry had never spoken to; someone was patting him on the back as though he’d just won a marathon. Fred and George pushed their way to the front of the crowd and said together, ‘Why couldn’t you’ve called us back, eh?’ Ron was scarlet in the face, grinning embarrassedly, but Harry could see one person who didn’t look happy at all. Percy was visible over the heads of some excited first-years, and he seemed to be trying to get near enough to start telling them off. Harry nudged Ron in the ribs and nodded in Percy’s direction. Ron got the point at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Got to get upstairs - bit tired,’ he said, and the two of them started pushing their way towards the door on the other side of the room, which led to a spiral staircase and the dormitories.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Night,’ Harry called back to Hermione, who was wearing a scowl just like Percy’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They managed to get to the other side of the common room, still having their backs slapped, and gained the peace of the staircase. They hurried up it, right to the top, and at last reached the door of their old dormitory, which now had a sign on it saying ‘second-years’. They entered the familiar, circular room, with its five four-posters hung with red velvet and its high, narrow windows. Their trunks had been brought up for them and placed at the ends of their beds.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron grinned guiltily at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I know I shouldn’t’ve enjoyed that or anything, but -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The dormitory door flew open and in came the other second-year Gryffindor boys, Seamus Finnigan, Dean Thomas and Neville Longbottom.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Unbelievable!’ beamed Seamus.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Cool,’ said Dean.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Amazing,’ said Neville, awestruck.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry couldn’t help it. He grinned, too.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The next day, however, Harry barely grinned once. Things started to go downhill from breakfast in the Great Hall. The four long house tables were laden with tureens of porridge, plates of kippers, mountains of toast and dishes of eggs and bacon, beneath the enchanted ceiling (today, a dull, cloudy grey). Harry and Ron sat down at the Gryffindor table next to Hermione, who had her copy of Voyages with Vampires propped open against a milk jug. There was a slight stiffness in the way she said ‘Morning’ which told Harry that she was still disapproving of the way they had arrived. Neville Longbottom, on the other hand, greeted them cheerfully. Neville was a round-faced and accident-prone boy with the worst memory of anyone Harry had ever met.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Post’s due any minute - I think Gran’s sending on a few things I forgot.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had only just started his porridge when, sure enough, there was a rushing sound overhead and a hundred or so owls streamed in, circling the Hall and dropping letters and packages into the chattering crowd. A big, lumpy parcel bounced off Neville’s head, and a second later, something large and grey fell into Hermione’s jug, spraying them all with milk and feathers.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Errol!’ said Ron, pulling the bedraggled owl out by the feet. Errol slumped, unconscious, onto the table, his legs in the air and a damp red envelope in his beak.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh no -‘ Ron gasped.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all right, he’s still alive,’ said Hermione, prodding Errol gently with the tip of her finger.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s not that - it’s that.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron was pointing at the red envelope. It looked quite ordinary to Harry, but Ron and Neville were both looking at it as though they expected it to explode.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s the matter?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘She’s - she’s sent me a Howler,’ said Ron faintly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’d better open it, Ron,’ said Neville, in a timid whisper. ‘It’ll be worse if you don’t. My Gran sent me one once, and I ignored it and -‘ he gulped, ‘it was horrible.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked from their petrified faces to the red envelope.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s a Howler?’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Ron’s whole attention was fixed on the letter, which had begun to smoke at the corners.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Open it,’ Neville urged. ‘It’ll all be over in a few minutes …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron stretched out a shaking hand, eased the envelope from Errol’s beak and slit it open. Neville stuffed his fingers in his ears. A split second later, Harry knew why. He thought for a moment it had exploded; a roar of sound filled the huge Hall, shaking dust from the ceiling.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… STEALING THE CAR, I WOULDN’T HAVE BEEN SURPRISED IF THEY’D EXPELLED YOU, YOU WAIT TILL I GET HOLD OF YOU, I DON’T SUPPOSE YOU STOPPED TO THINK WHAT YOUR FATHER AND I WENT THROUGH WHEN WE SAW IT HAD GONE …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mrs Weasley’s yells, a hundred times louder than usual, made the plates and spoons rattle on the table, and echoed deafeningly off the stone walls. People throughout the Hall were swivelling around to see who had received the Howler and Ron sank so low in his chair that only his crimson forehead could be seen.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… LETTER FROM DUMBLEDORE LAST NIGHT, I THOUGHT YOUR FATHER WOULD DIE OF SHAME, WE DIDN’T BRING YOU UP TO BEHAVE LIKE THIS, YOU AND HARRY COULD BOTH HAVE DIED …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had been wondering when his name was going to crop up. He tried very hard to look as though he couldn’t hear the voice that was making his eardrums throb.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTED, YOUR FATHER’S FACING AN INQUIRY AT WORK, IT’S ENTIRELY YOUR FAULT AND IF YOU PUT ANOTHER TOE OUT OF LINE WE’LL BRING YOU STRAIGHT BACK HOME.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A ringing silence fell. The red envelope, which had dropped from Ron’s hand, burst into flames and curled into ashes. Harry and Ron sat stunned, as though a tidal wave had just passed over them. A few people laughed and gradually, a babble of talk broke out again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione closed Voyages with Vampires and looked down at the top of Ron’s head.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I don’t know what you expected, Ron, but you -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t tell me I deserved it,’ snapped Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry pushed his porridge away. His insides were burning with guilt. Mr Weasley was facing an inquiry at work. After all Mr and Mrs Weasley had done for him over the summer …

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But he had no time to dwell on this; Professor McGonagall was moving along the Gryffindor table, handing out timetables. Harry took his, and saw that they had double Herbology with the Hufflepuffs first.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry, Ron and Hermione left the castle together, crossed the vegetable patch and made for the greenhouses, where the magical plants were kept. At least the Howler had done one good thing: Hermione seemed to think they had now been punished enough and was being perfectly friendly again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: As they neared the greenhouses they saw the rest of the class standing outside, waiting for Professor Sprout. Harry, Ron and Hermione had only just joined them when she came striding into view across the lawn, accompanied by Gilderoy Lockhart. Professor Sprout’s arms were full of bandages, and with another twinge of guilt, Harry spotted the Whomping Willow in the distance, several of its branches now in slings.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor Sprout was a squat little witch who wore a patched hat over her flyaway hair; there was usually a large amount of earth on her clothes, and her fingernails would have made Aunt Petunia faint. Gilderoy Lockhart, however, was immaculate in sweeping robes of turquoise, his golden hair shining under a perfectly positioned turquoise hat with gold trimming.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, hello there!’ Lockhart called, beaming around at the assembled students. ‘Just been showing Professor Sprout the right way to doctor a Whomping Willow! But I don’t want you running away with the idea that I’m better at Herbology than she is! I just happen to have met several of these exotic plants on my travels …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Greenhouse Three today, chaps!’ said Professor Sprout, who was looking distinctly disgruntled, not at all her usual cheerful self.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a murmur of interest. They had only ever worked in Greenhouse One before - Greenhouse Three housed far more interesting and dangerous plants. Professor Sprout took a large key from her belt and unlocked the door. Harry caught a whiff of damp earth and fertiliser, mingling with the heavy perfume of some giant, umbrella-sized flowers dangling from the ceiling. He was about to follow Ron and Hermione inside when Lockhart’s hand shot out.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry! I’ve been wanting a word - you don’t mind if he’s a couple of minutes late, do you, Professor Sprout?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Judging by Professor Sprout’s scowl, she did mind, but Lockhart said, ‘That’s the ticket,’ and closed the greenhouse door in her face.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry,’ said Lockhart, his large white teeth gleaming in the sunlight as he shook his head. ‘Harry, Harry, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Completely nonplussed, Harry said nothing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘When I heard - well, of course, it was all my fault. Could have kicked myself.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had no idea what he was talking about. He was about to say so when Lockhart went on, ‘Don’t know when I’ve been more shocked. Flying a car to Hogwarts! Well, of course, I knew at once why you’d done it. Stood out a mile. Harry, Harry, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was remarkable how he could show every one of those brilliant teeth even when he wasn’t talking.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Gave you a taste for publicity, didn’t I?’ said Lockhart. ‘Gave you the bug. You got onto the front page of the paper with me and you couldn’t wait to do it again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh - no, Professor, see -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, Harry, Harry,’ said Lockhart, reaching out and grasping his shoulder. ‘I understand. Natural to want a bit more once you’ve had that first taste - and I blame myself for giving you that, because it was bound to go to your head - but see here, young man, you can’t start flying cars to try and get yourself noticed. Just calm down, all right? Plenty of time for all that when you’re older. Yes, yes, I know what you’re thinking! “It’s all right for him, he’s an internationally famous wizard already!” But when I was twelve, I was just as much of a nobody as you are now. In fact, I’d say I was even more of a nobody! I mean, a few people have heard of you, haven’t they? All that business with He Who Must Not Be Named!’ He glanced at the lightning scar on Harry’s forehead. ‘I know, I know, it’s not quite as good as winning Witch Weekly’s Most-Charming-Smile Award five times in a row, as I have - but it’s a start, Harry, it’s a start.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He gave Harry a hearty wink and strode off. Harry stood stunned for a few seconds, then, remembering he was supposed to be in the greenhouse, he opened the door and slid inside.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor Sprout was standing behind a trestle bench in the centre of the greenhouse. About twenty pairs of different-coloured earmuffs were lying on the bench. When Harry had taken his place between Ron and Hermione, she said, ‘We’ll be re-potting Mandrakes today. Now, who can tell me the properties of the Mandrake?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: To nobody’s surprise, Hermione’s hand was first into the air.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Mandrake, or Mandragora, is a powerful restorative,’ said Hermione, sounding as usual as though she had swallowed the textbook. ‘It is used to return people who have been transfigured or cursed, to their original state.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Excellent. Ten points to Gryffindor,’ said Professor Sprout. ‘The Mandrake forms an essential part of most antidotes. It is also, however, dangerous. Who can tell me why?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione’s hand narrowly missed Harry’s glasses as it shot up again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The cry of the Mandrake is fatal to anyone who hears it,’ she said promptly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Precisely. Take another ten points,’ said Professor Sprout. ‘Now, the Mandrakes we have here are still very young.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She pointed to a row of deep trays as she spoke and everyone shuffled forward for a better look. A hundred or so tufty little plants, purplish green in colour, were growing there in rows. They looked quite unremarkable to Harry, who didn’t have the slightest idea what Hermione meant by the ‘cry’ of the Mandrake.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Everyone take a pair of earmuffs,’ said Professor Sprout.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a scramble as everyone tried to seize a pair that wasn’t pink and fluffy.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘When I tell you to put them on, make sure your ears are completely covered,’ said Professor Sprout. ‘When it is safe to remove them, I will give you the thumbs-up. Right - earmuffs on.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry snapped the earmuffs over his ears. They shut out sound completely. Professor Sprout put a pink fluffy pair over her own ears, rolled up the sleeves of her robes, grasped one of the tufty plants firmly, and pulled hard.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry let out a gasp of surprise that no one could hear.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Instead of roots, a small, muddy and extremely ugly baby popped out of the earth. The leaves were growing right out of his head. He had pale green, mottled skin, and was clearly bawling at the top of his lungs.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor Sprout took a large plant pot from under the table and plunged the Mandrake into it, burying him in dark, damp compost until only the tufted leaves were visible. Professor Sprout dusted off her hands, gave them all the thumbs-up and removed her own earmuffs.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘As our Mandrakes are only seedlings, their cries won’t kill yet,’ she said calmly, as though she’d just done nothing more exciting than water a begonia. ‘However, they will knock you out for several hours, and as I’m sure none of you want to miss your first day back, make sure your earmuffs are securely in place while you work. I will attract your attention when it is time to pack up.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Four to a tray - there is a large supply of pots here - compost in the sacks over there - and be careful of the Venomous Tentacula, it’s teething.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She gave a sharp slap to a spiky, dark red plant as she spoke, making it draw in the long feelers that had been inching sneakily over her shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry, Ron and Hermione were joined at their tray by a curly-haired Hufflepuff boy Harry knew by sight, but had never spoken to.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Justin Finch-Fletchley,’ he said brightly, shaking Harry by the hand. ‘Know who you are, of course, the famous Harry Potter … and you’re Hermione Granger - always top in everything …’ (Hermione beamed as she had her hand shaken, too) ‘and Ron Weasley. Wasn’t that your flying car?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron didn’t smile. The Howler was obviously still on his mind.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That Lockhart’s something, isn’t he?’ said Justin happily, as they began filling their plant pots with dragon-dung compost. ‘Awfully brave chap. Have you read his books? I’d have died of fear if I’d been cornered in a telephone box by a werewolf, but he stayed cool and - zap - just fantastic.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘My name was down for Eton, you know, I can’t tell you how glad I am I came here instead. Of course, mother was slightly disappointed, but since I made her read Lockhart’s books I think she’s begun to see how useful it’ll be to have a fully trained wizard in the family …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: After that they didn’t have much chance to talk. Their earmuffs were back on and they needed to concentrate on the Mandrakes. Professor Sprout had made it look extremely easy, but it wasn’t. The Mandrakes didn’t like coming out of the earth, but didn’t seem to want to go back into it either. They squirmed, kicked, flailed their sharp little fists and gnashed their teeth; Harry spent ten whole minutes trying to squash a particularly fat one into a pot.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: By the end of the class, Harry, like everyone else, was sweaty, aching and covered in earth. They traipsed back to the castle for a quick wash and then the Gryffindors hurried off to Transfiguration.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor McGonagall’s classes were always hard work, but today was especially difficult. Everything Harry had learned last year seemed to have leaked out of his head during the summer. He was supposed to be turning a beetle into a button, but all he managed to do was give his beetle a lot of exercise as it scuttled over the desk top avoiding his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron was having far worse problems. He had patched up his wand with some borrowed Spellotape, but it seemed to be damaged beyond repair. It kept crackling and sparking at odd moments, and every time Ron tried to transfigure his beetle it engulfed him in thick grey smoke which smelled of rotten eggs. Unable to see what he was doing, Ron accidentally squashed his beetle with his elbow and had to ask for a new one. Professor McGonagall wasn’t pleased.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry was relieved to hear the lunch bell. His brain felt like a wrung sponge. Everyone filed out of the classroom except him and Ron, who was whacking his wand furiously on the desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Stupid … useless … thing …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Write home for another one,’ Harry suggested, as the wand let off a volley of bangs like a firecracker.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yeah, and get another Howler back,’ said Ron, stuffing the now hissing wand into his bag. ‘It’s your own fault your wand got snapped -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They went down to lunch, where Ron’s mood was not improved by Hermione showing them the handful of perfect coat buttons she had produced in Transfiguration.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’ve we got this afternoon?’ said Harry, hastily changing the subject.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Defence Against the Dark Arts,’ said Hermione at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Why,’ demanded Ron, seizing her timetable, ‘have you outlined all Lockhart’s lessons in little hearts?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione snatched the timetable back, flushing furiously.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They finished lunch and went outside into the overcast courtyard. Hermione sat down on a stone step and buried her nose in Voyages with Vampires again. Harry and Ron stood talking about Quidditch for several minutes before Harry became aware that he was being closely watched. Looking up, he saw the very small, mousey-haired boy he’d seen trying on the Sorting Hat last night, staring at Harry as though transfixed. He was clutching what looked like an ordinary Muggle camera, and the moment Harry looked at him, he went bright red.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘All right, Harry? I’m - I’m Colin Creevey,’ he said breathlessly, taking a tentative step forward. ‘I’m in Gryffindor, too. D’you think - would it be all right if - can I have a picture?’ he said, raising the camera hopefully.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘A picture?’ Harry repeated blankly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So I can prove I’ve met you,’ said Colin Creevey eagerly, edging further forwards. ‘I know all about you. Everyone’s told me. About how you survived when You Know Who tried to kill you and how he disappeared and everything and how you’ve still got a lightning scar on your forehead’ (his eyes raked Harry’s hairline), ‘and a boy in my dormitory said if I develop the film in the right potion, the pictures’ll move.‘ Colin drew a great shuddering breath of excitement and said, ‘It’s brilliant here, isn’t it? And it’d be really good if I had one of you -‘ he looked imploringly at Harry, ‘- maybe your friend could take it and I could stand next to you? And then, could you sign it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Signed photos? You’re giving out signed photos, Potter?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Loud and scathing, Draco Malfoy’s voice echoed around the courtyard. He had stopped right behind Colin, flanked, as he always was at Hogwarts, by his large and thuggish cronies, Crabbe and Goyle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No, I’m not,’ said Harry angrily, his fists clenching. ‘Shut up, Malfoy.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re just jealous,’ piped up Colin, whose entire body was about as thick as Crabbe’s neck.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Crabbe and Goyle were sniggering stupidly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Eat slugs, Malfoy,’ said Ron angrily. Crabbe stopped laughing and started rubbing his conker-like knuckles in a menacing way.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A knot of Slytherin fifth-years nearby laughed loudly at this.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Weasley would like a signed photo, Potter,’ smirked Malfoy. ‘It’d be worth more than his family’s whole house.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron whipped out his Spellotaped wand, but Hermione shut Voyages with Vampires with a snap and whispered, ‘Look out!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Pinned to Lockhart’s side and burning with humiliation, Harry saw Malfoy slide smirking back into the crowd.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on then, Mr Creevey,’ said Lockhart, beaming at Colin. ‘A double portrait, can’t say fairer than that, and we’ll both sign it for you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Colin fumbled for his camera and took the picture as the bell rang behind them, signalling the start of afternoon classes.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Off you go, move along there,’ Lockhart called to the crowd, and he set off back to the castle with Harry, who was wishing he knew a good vanishing spell, still clasped to his side.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Deaf to Harry’s stammers, Lockhart swept him down a corridor lined with staring students and up a staircase.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Let me just say that handing out signed pictures at this stage of your career isn’t sensible - looks a tad bigheaded, Harry, to be frank. There may well come a time when, like me, you’ll need to keep a stack handy wherever you go, but -‘ he gave a little chortle, ‘I don’t think you’re quite there yet.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They had reached Lockhart’s classroom and he let Harry go at last. Harry yanked his robes straight and headed for a seat at the very back of the class, where he busied himself with piling all seven of Lockhart’s books in front of him, so that he could avoid looking at the real thing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The rest of the class came clattering in and Ron and Hermione sat down on either side of Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You could’ve fried an egg on your face,’ said Ron. ‘You’d better hope Creevey doesn’t meet Ginny, they’ll be starting a Harry Potter fan club.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Shut up,’ snapped Harry. The last thing he needed was for Lockhart to hear the phrase ‘Harry Potter fan club’.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When the whole class was seated, Lockhart cleared his throat loudly and silence fell. He reached forward, picked up Neville Longbottom’s copy of Travels with Trolls and held it up to show his own, winking portrait on the front.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Me,’ he said, pointing at it and winking as well, ‘Gilderoy Lockhart, Order of Merlin, Third Class, Honorary Member of the Dark Force Defence League and five times winner of Witch Weekly’s Most-Charming-Smile Award - but I don’t talk about that. I didn’t get rid of the Bandon Banshee by smiling at her!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He waited for them to laugh; a few people smiled weakly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I see you’ve all bought a complete set of my books - well done. I thought we’d start today with a little quiz. Nothing to worry about - just to check how well you’ve read them, how much you’ve taken in …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When he had handed out the test papers he returned to the front of the class and said, ‘You have thirty minutes. Start - now!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked down at his paper and read:

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: 1. What is Gilderoy Lockhart’s favourite colour? 2. What is Gilderoy Lockhart’s secret ambition? 3. What, in your opinion, is Gilderoy Lockhart’s greatest achievement to date?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: On and on it went, over three sides of paper, right down to:

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: 54. When is Gilderoy Lockhart’s birthday, and what would his ideal gift be?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Half an hour later, Lockhart collected in the papers and rifled through them in front of the class.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Tut, tut - hardly any of you remembered that my favourite colour is lilac. I say so in Year with a Yeti. And a few of you need to read Wanderings with Werewolves more carefully - I clearly state in chapter twelve that my ideal birthday gift would be harmony between all magic and non-magic peoples -though I wouldn’t say no to a large bottle of Ogden’s Old Firewhisky!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He gave them another roguish wink. Ron was now staring at Lockhart with an expression of disbelief on his face; Seamus Finnigan and Dean Thomas, who were sitting in front, were shaking with silent laughter. Hermione, on the other hand, was listening to Lockhart with rapt attention, and gave a start when he mentioned her name.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… but Miss Hermione Granger knew my secret ambition is to rid the world of evil and market my own range of hair-care potions - good girl! In fact -‘ he flipped her paper over, ‘full marks! Where is Miss Hermione Granger?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione raised a trembling hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Excellent!’ beamed Lockhart. ‘Quite excellent! Take ten points for Gryffindor! And so, to business …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He bent down behind his desk and lifted a large, covered cage onto it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now - be warned! It is my job to arm you against the foulest creatures known to wizardkind! You may find yourselves facing your worst fears in this room. Know only that no harm can befall you whilst I am here. All I ask is that you remain calm.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: In spite of himself, Harry leaned around his pile of books for a better look at the cage. Lockhart placed a hand on the cover. Dean and Seamus had stopped laughing now. Neville was cowering in his front-row seat.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I must ask you not to scream,’ said Lockhart in a low voice. ‘It might provoke them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: As the whole class held its breath, Lockhart whipped off the cover.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ he said dramatically. ‘Freshly caught Cornish pixies.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Seamus Finnigan couldn’t control himself. He let out a snort of laughter which even Lockhart couldn’t mistake for a scream of terror.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes?’ he smiled at Seamus.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
