book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t be so sure!’ said Lockhart, waggling a finger annoyingly at Seamus. ‘Devilish tricky little blighters they can be!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The pixies were electric blue and about eight inches high, with pointed faces and voices so shrill it was like listening to a lot of budgies arguing. The moment the cover had been removed, they had started jabbering and rocketing around, rattling the bars and pulling bizarre faces at the people nearest them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Right then,’ Lockhart said loudly. ‘Let’s see what you make of them!’ And he opened the cage.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was pandemonium. The pixies shot in every direction like rockets. Two of them seized Neville by the ears and lifted him into the air. Several shot straight through the window, showering the back row with broken glass. The rest proceeded to wreck the classroom more effectively than a rampaging rhino. They grabbed ink bottles and sprayed the class with them, shredded books and papers, tore pictures from the walls, upended the waste bin, grabbed bags and books and threw them out of the smashed window; within minutes, half the class was sheltering under desks and Neville was swinging from the candelabra in the ceiling.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on now, round them up, round them up, they’re only pixies …’ Lockhart shouted.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He rolled up his sleeves, brandished his wand and bellowed, ‘Peskipiksi Pesternomi!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The bell rang and there was a mad rush towards the exit. In the relative calm that followed, Lockhart straightened up, caught sight of Harry, Ron and Hermione, who were almost at the door, and said, ‘Well, I’ll ask you three to just nip the rest of them back into their cage.’ He swept past them and shut the door quickly behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Can you believe him?’ roared Ron, as one of the remaining pixies bit him painfully on the ear.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He just wants to give us some hands-on experience,’ said Hermione, immobilising two pixies at once with a clever Freezing Charm and stuffing them back into their cage.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hands on?’ said Harry, who was trying to grab a pixie dancing out of reach with its tongue out. ‘Hermione, he didn’t have a clue what he was doing.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Rubbish,’ said Hermione. ‘You’ve read his books - look at all those amazing things he’s done …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He says he’s done,’ Ron muttered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry spent a lot of time over the next few days dodging out of sight whenever he saw Gilderoy Lockhart coming down a corridor. Harder to avoid was Colin Creevey, who seemed to have memorised Harry’s timetable. Nothing seemed to give Colin a bigger thrill than to say, ‘All right, Harry?’ six or seven times a day and hear, ‘Hullo, Colin,’ back, however exasperated Harry sounded when he said it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hedwig was still angry with Harry about the disastrous car journey and Ron’s wand was still malfunctioning, surpassing itself on Friday morning by shooting out of Ron’s hand in Charms and hitting tiny old Professor Flitwick squarely between the eyes, creating a large, throbbing green boil where it had struck. So, with one thing and another, Harry was quite glad to reach the weekend. He, Ron and Hermione were planning to visit Hagrid on Saturday morning. Harry, however, was shaken awake several hours earlier than he would have liked by Oliver Wood, captain of the Gryffindor Quidditch team.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Whassamatter?’ said Harry groggily.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Quidditch practice!’ said Wood. ‘Come on!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry squinted at the window. There was a thin mist hanging across the pink and gold sky. Now he was awake, he couldn’t understand how he could have slept through the racket the birds were making.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oliver,’ Harry croaked, ‘it’s the crack of dawn.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Exactly,’ said Wood. He was a tall and burly sixth-year and, at the moment, his eyes were gleaming with a mad enthusiasm. ‘It’s part of our new training programme. Come on, grab your broom and let’s go,’ said Wood heartily. ‘None of the other teams have started training yet, we’re going to be first off the mark this year …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Yawning and shivering slightly, Harry climbed out of bed and tried to find his Quidditch robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good man,’ said Wood. ‘Meet you on the pitch in fifteen minutes.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When he’d found his scarlet team robes and pulled on his cloak for warmth, Harry scribbled a note to Ron explaining where he’d gone and went down the spiral staircase to the common room, his Nimbus Two Thousand on his shoulder. He had just reached the portrait hole when there was a clatter behind him and Colin Creevey came dashing down the spiral staircase, his camera swinging madly around his neck and something clutched in his hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I heard someone saying your name on the stairs, Harry! Look what I’ve got here! I’ve had it developed, I wanted to show you -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked bemusedly at the photograph Colin was brandishing under his nose.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A moving, black and white Lockhart was tugging hard on an arm Harry recognised as his own. He was pleased to see that his photographic self was putting up a good fight and refusing to be dragged into view. As Harry watched, Lockhart gave up and slumped, panting, against the white edge of the picture.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Will you sign it?’ said Colin eagerly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry flatly, glancing around to check that the room was really deserted. ‘Sorry, Colin, I’m in a hurry - Quidditch practice.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He climbed through the portrait hole.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh wow! Wait for me! I’ve never watched a Quidditch game before!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Colin scrambled through the hole after him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’ll be really boring,’ Harry said quickly, but Colin ignored him, his face shining with excitement.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You were the youngest house player in a hundred years, weren’t you, Harry? Weren’t you?’ said Colin, trotting alongside him. ‘You must be brilliant. I’ve never flown. Is it easy? Is that your own broom? Is that the best one there is?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t know how to get rid of him. It was like having an extremely talkative shadow.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t really understand Quidditch,’ said Colin breathlessly. ‘Is it true there are four balls? And two of them fly round trying to knock people off their brooms?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Harry heavily, resigned to explaining the complicated rules of Quidditch. ‘They’re called Bludgers. There are two Beaters on each team, who carry clubs to beat the Bludgers away from their side. Fred and George Weasley are the Gryffindor Beaters.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And what are the other balls for?’ Colin asked, tripping down a couple of steps because he was gazing open-mouthed at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, the Quaffle - that’s the biggish red one - is the one that scores goals. Three Chasers on each team throw the Quaffle to each other and try and get it through the goalposts at the end of the pitch - they’re three long poles with hoops on the end.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And the fourth ball -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘- is the Golden Snitch,’ said Harry, ‘and it’s very small, very fast and difficult to catch. But that’s what the Seeker’s got to do, because a game of Quidditch doesn’t end until the Snitch has been caught. And whichever team’s Seeker gets the Snitch earns his team an extra hundred and fifty points.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And you’re Gryffindor Seeker, aren’t you?’ said Colin in awe.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Harry, as they left the castle and started across the dew-drenched grass. ‘And there’s the Keeper, too. He guards the goalposts. That’s it, really.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Colin didn’t stop questioning Harry all the way down the sloping lawns to the Quidditch pitch, and Harry only shook him off when he reached the changing rooms. Colin called after him in a piping voice, ‘I’ll go and get a good seat, Harry!’ and hurried off to the stands.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The rest of the Gryffindor team were already in the changing room. Wood was the only person who looked truly awake. Fred and George Weasley were sitting, puffy-eyed and tousle-haired, next to fourth-year Alicia Spinnet, who seemed to be nodding off against the wall behind her. Her fellow Chasers, Katie Bell and Angelina Johnson, were yawning, side by side, opposite them.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘There you are, Harry, what kept you?’ said Wood briskly. ‘Now, I wanted a quick talk with you all before we actually get onto the pitch, because I spent the summer devising a whole new training programme, which I really think will make all the difference …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Wood was holding up a large diagram of a Quidditch pitch, on which were drawn many lines, arrows and crosses in different-coloured inks. He took out his wand, tapped the board and the arrows began to wiggle over the diagram like caterpillars. As Wood launched into a speech about his new tactics, Fred Weasley’s head drooped right onto Alicia Spinnet’s shoulder and he began to snore.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The first board took nearly twenty minutes to explain, but there was another board under that, and a third under that one. Harry sank into a stupor as Wood droned on and on.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ said Wood, at long last, jerking Harry from a wistful fantasy about what he could be eating for breakfast at this very moment up at the castle, ‘is that clear? Any questions?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve got a question, Oliver,’ said George, who had woken with a start. ‘Why couldn’t you have told us all this yesterday when we were awake?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Wood wasn’t pleased.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, listen here, you lot,’ he said, glowering at them all, ‘we should have won the Quidditch Cup last year. We’re easily the best team. But unfortunately, owing to circumstances beyond our control …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry shifted guiltily in his seat. He had been unconscious in the hospital wing for the final match of the previous year, meaning that Gryffindor had been a player short and had suffered their worst defeat in three hundred years.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Wood took a moment to regain control of himself. Their last defeat was clearly still torturing him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So, this year, we train harder than ever before … OK, let’s go and put our new theories into practice!’ Wood shouted, seizing his broomstick and leading the way out of the changing rooms. Stiff-legged and still yawning, his team followed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They had been in the changing room so long that the sun was up properly now, although remnants of mist hung over the grass in the stadium. As Harry walked onto the pitch, he saw Ron and Hermione sitting in the stands.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Aren’t you finished yet?’ called Ron incredulously.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Haven’t even started,’ said Harry, looking jealously at the toast and marmalade Ron and Hermione had brought out of the Great Hall. ‘Wood’s been teaching us new moves.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He mounted his broomstick and kicked at the ground, soaring up into the air. The cool morning air whipped his face, waking him far more effectively than Wood’s long talk. It felt wonderful to be back on the Quidditch pitch. He soared right around the stadium at full speed, racing Fred and George.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s that funny clicking noise?’ called Fred, as they hurtled around the corner.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked into the stands. Colin was sitting in one of the highest seats, his camera raised, taking picture after picture, the sound strangely magnified in the deserted stadium.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Look this way, Harry! This way!’ he cried shrilly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Who’s that?’ said Fred.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No idea,’ Harry lied, putting on a spurt of speed that took him as far away as possible from Colin.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s going on?’ said Wood, frowning, as he skimmed through the air towards them. ‘Why’s that first-year taking pictures? I don’t like it. He could be a Slytherin spy, trying to find out about our new training programme.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s in Gryffindor,’ said Harry quickly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And the Slytherins don’t need a spy, Oliver,’ said George.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What makes you say that?’ said Wood testily.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Because they’re here in person,’ said George, pointing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Several people in green robes were walking onto the pitch, broomsticks in their hands.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t believe it!’ Wood hissed in outrage. ‘I booked the pitch for today! We’ll see about this!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Wood shot towards the ground, landing rather harder than he meant to in his anger, staggering slightly as he dismounted. Harry, Fred and George followed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Flint!’ Wood bellowed at the Slytherin captain. ‘This is our practice time! We got up specially! You can clear off now!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Marcus Flint was even larger than Wood. He had a look of trollish cunning on his face as he replied, ‘Plenty of room for all of us, Wood.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Angelina, Alicia and Katie had come over, too. There were no girls on the Slytherin team - who stood, shoulder to shoulder, facing the Gryffindors, leering to a man.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But I booked the pitch!’ said Wood, positively spitting with rage. ‘I booked it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ah,’ said Flint, ‘but I’ve got a specially signed note here from Professor Snape. I, Professor S. Snape, give the Slytherin team permission to practise today on the Quidditch pitch, owing to the need to train their new Seeker.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ve got a new Seeker?’ said Wood, distracted. ‘Where?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And from behind the six large figures before them came a seventh, smaller boy, smirking all over his pale, pointed face. It was Draco Malfoy.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Aren’t you Lucius Malfoy’s son?’ said Fred, looking at Malfoy with dislike.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Funny you should mention Draco’s father,’ said Flint, as the whole Slytherin team smiled still more broadly. ‘Let me show you the generous gift he’s made to the Slytherin team.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: All seven of them held out their broomsticks. Seven highly polished, brand-new handles and seven sets of fine gold lettering spelling the words ‘Nimbus Two Thousand and One’ gleamed under the Gryffindors’ noses in the early-morning sun.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Very latest model. Only came out last month,’ said Flint carelessly, flicking a speck of dust from the end of his own. ‘I believe it outstrips the old Two Thousand series by a considerable amount. As for the old Cleansweeps,’ he smiled nastily at Fred and George, who were both clutching Cleansweep Fives, ‘sweeps the board with them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: None of the Gryffindor team could think of anything to say for a moment. Malfoy was smirking so broadly his cold eyes were reduced to slits.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh look,’ said Flint. ‘A pitch invasion.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron and Hermione were crossing the grass to see what was going on.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s happening?’ Ron asked Harry. ‘Why aren’t you playing? And what’s he doing here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He was looking at Malfoy, taking in his Slytherin Quidditch robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m the new Slytherin Seeker, Weasley,’ said Malfoy, smugly. ‘Everyone’s just been admiring the brooms my father’s bought our team.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron gaped, open-mouthed, at the seven superb broomsticks in front of him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good, aren’t they?’ said Malfoy smoothly. ‘But perhaps the Gryffindor team will be able to raise some gold and get new brooms, too. You could raffle off those Cleansweep Fives, I expect a museum would bid for them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Slytherin team howled with laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘At least no one on the Gryffindor team had to buy their way in,’ said Hermione sharply. ‘They got in on pure talent.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The smug look on Malfoy’s face flickered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No one asked your opinion, you filthy little Mudblood,’ he spat.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry knew at once that Malfoy had said something really bad because there was an instant uproar at his words. Flint had to dive in front of Malfoy to stop Fred and George jumping on him, Alicia shrieked, ‘How dare you!’ and Ron plunged his hand into his robes, pulled out his wand, yelling, ‘You’ll pay for that one, Malfoy!’ and pointed it furiously under Flint’s arm at Malfoy’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A loud bang echoed around the stadium and a jet of green light shot out of the wrong end of Ron’s wand, hitting him in the stomach and sending him reeling backwards onto the grass.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron! Ron! Are you all right?’ squealed Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron opened his mouth to speak, but no words came out. Instead he gave an almighty belch and several slugs dribbled out of his mouth onto his lap.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Slytherin team were paralysed with laughter. Flint was doubled up, hanging on to his new broomstick for support. Malfoy was on all fours, banging the ground with his fist. The Gryffindors were gathered around Ron, who kept belching large, glistening slugs. Nobody seemed to want to touch him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’d better get him to Hagrid’s, it’s nearest,’ said Harry to Hermione, who nodded bravely, and the pair of them pulled Ron up by the arms.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What happened, Harry? What happened? Is he ill? But you can cure him, can’t you?’ Colin had run down from his seat and was now dancing alongside them as they left the pitch. Ron gave a huge heave and more slugs dribbled down his front.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oooh,’ said Colin, fascinated and raising his camera. ‘Can you hold him still, Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Get out of the way, Colin!’ said Harry angrily. He and Hermione supported Ron out of the stadium and across the grounds towards the edge of the Forest.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Nearly there, Ron,’ said Hermione, as the gamekeeper’s cabin came into view. ‘You’ll be all right in a minute … almost there …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They were within twenty feet of Hagrid’s house when the front door opened, but it wasn’t Hagrid who emerged. Gilderoy Lockhart, wearing robes of palest mauve today, came striding out.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Quick, behind here,’ Harry hissed, dragging Ron behind a nearby bush. Hermione followed, somewhat reluctantly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s a simple matter if you know what you’re doing!’ Lockhart was saying loudly to Hagrid. ‘If you need help, you know where I am! I’ll let you have a copy of my book - I’m surprised you haven’t already got one. I’ll sign one tonight and send it over. Well, goodbye!’ And he strode away towards the castle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry waited until Lockhart was out of sight, then pulled Ron out of the bush and up to Hagrid’s front door. They knocked urgently.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid appeared at once, looking very grumpy, but his expression brightened when he saw who it was.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Bin wonderin’ when you’d come ter see me - come in, come in - thought you mighta bin Professor Lockhart back again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Hermione supported Ron over the threshold, into the one-roomed cabin, which had an enormous bed in one corner, a fire crackling merrily in another. Hagrid didn’t seem perturbed by Ron’s slug problem, which Harry hastily explained as he lowered Ron into a chair.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Better out than in,’ he said cheerfully, plonking a large copper basin in front of him. ‘Get ‘em all up, Ron.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t think there’s anything to do except wait for it to stop,’ said Hermione anxiously, watching Ron bend over the basin. ‘That’s a difficult curse to work at the best of times, but with a broken wand …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid was bustling around, making them tea. His boarhound, Fang, was slobbering over Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What did Lockhart want with you, Hagrid?’ Harry asked, scratching Fang’s ears.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Givin’ me advice on gettin’ kelpies out of a well,’ growled Hagrid, moving a half-plucked rooster off his scrubbed table and setting down the teapot. ‘Like I don’ know. An’ bangin’ on about some Banshee he banished. If one word of it was true, I’ll eat my kettle.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was most unlike Hagrid to criticise a Hogwarts teacher and Harry looked at him in surprise. Hermione, however, said in a voice somewhat higher than usual, ‘I think you’re being a bit unfair. Professor Dumbledore obviously thought he was the best man for the job -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He was the on’y man for the job,’ said Hagrid, offering them a plate of treacle toffee, while Ron coughed squelchily into his basin. ‘An’ I mean the on’y one. Gettin’ very difficult ter find anyone fer the Dark Arts job. People aren’t too keen ter take it on, see. They’re startin’ ter think it’s jinxed. No one’s lasted long fer a while now. So tell me,’ said Hagrid, jerking his head at Ron, ‘who was he tryin’ ter curse?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Malfoy called Hermione something. It must’ve been really bad, because everyone went mad.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It was bad,’ said Ron hoarsely, emerging over the table top, looking pale and sweaty. ‘Malfoy called her “Mudblood”, Hagrid -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron dived out of sight again as a fresh wave of slugs made their appearance. Hagrid looked outraged.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He didn’!’ he growled at Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘He did,’ she said. ‘But I don’t know what it means. I could tell it was really rude, of course …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s about the most insulting thing he could think of,’ gasped Ron, coming back up. ‘Mudblood’s a really foul name for someone who was Muggle-born - you know, non-magic parents. There are some wizards - like Malfoy’s family - who think they’re better than everyone else because they’re what people call pure-blood.’ He gave a small burp, and a single slug fell into his outstretched hand. He threw it into the basin and continued, ‘I mean, the rest of us know it doesn’t make any difference at all. Look at Neville Longbottom - he’s pure-blood and he can hardly stand a cauldron the right way up.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘An’ they haven’t invented a spell our Hermione can’t do,’ said Hagrid proudly, making Hermione go a brilliant shade of magenta.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s a disgusting thing to call someone,’ said Ron, wiping his sweaty brow with a shaking hand. ‘Dirty blood, see. Common blood. It’s mad. Most wizards these days are half-blood anyway. If we hadn’t married Muggles we’d’ve died out.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He retched and ducked out of sight again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I don’ blame yeh fer tryin’ ter curse him, Ron,’ said Hagrid loudly over the thuds of more slugs hitting the basin. ‘Bu’ maybe it was a good thing yer wand backfired. ‘Spect Lucius Malfoy would’ve come marchin’ up ter school if yeh’d cursed his son. Least yer not in trouble.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry would have pointed out that trouble didn’t come much worse than having slugs pouring out of your mouth, but he couldn’t; Hagrid’s treacle toffee had cemented his jaws together.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry,’ said Hagrid suddenly, as though struck by a sudden thought, ‘gotta bone ter pick with yeh. I’ve heard you’ve bin givin’ out signed photos. How come I haven’t got one?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Furious, Harry wrenched his teeth apart.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I have not been giving out signed photos,’ he said hotly. ‘If Lockhart’s still putting that about -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But then he saw that Hagrid was laughing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m on’y jokin’,’ he said, patting Harry genially on the back and sending him, face first, into the table. ‘I knew yeh hadn’t really. I told Lockhart yeh didn’ need teh. Yer more famous than him without tryin’.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Bet he didn’t like that,’ said Harry, sitting up and rubbing his chin.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’ think he did,’ said Hagrid, his eyes twinkling. ‘An’ then I told him I’d never read one o’ his books an’ he decided ter go. Treacle toffee, Ron?’ he added, as Ron re-appeared.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No thanks,’ said Ron weakly. ‘Better not risk it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Come an’ see what I’ve bin growin’,’ said Hagrid, as Harry and Hermione finished the last of their tea.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: In the small vegetable patch behind Hagrid’s house were a dozen of the largest pumpkins Harry had ever seen. Each was the size of a large boulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Gettin’ on well, aren’t they?’ said Hagrid happily. ‘Fer the Hallowe’en feast … should be big enough by then.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’ve you been feeding them?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid looked over his shoulder to check that they were alone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I’ve bin givin’ them - you know - a bit o’ help.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry noticed Hagrid’s flowery pink umbrella leaning against the back wall of the cabin. Harry had had reason to believe before now that this umbrella was not all it looked; in fact, he had the strong impression that Hagrid’s old school wand was concealed inside it. Hagrid wasn’t supposed to use magic. He had been expelled from Hogwarts in his third year, but Harry had never found out why - any mention of the matter and Hagrid would clear his throat loudly and become mysteriously deaf until the subject was changed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘An Engorgement Charm, I suppose?’ said Hermione, halfway between disapproval and amusement. ‘Well, you’ve done a good job on them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s what yer little sister said,’ said Hagrid, nodding at Ron. ‘Met her jus’ yesterday.’ Hagrid looked sideways at Harry, his beard twitching. ‘Said she was jus’ lookin’ round the grounds, but I reckon she was hopin’ she might run inter someone else at my house.’ He winked at Harry. ‘If yeh ask me, she wouldn’ say no ter a signed -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, shut up,’ said Harry. Ron snorted with laughter and the ground was sprayed with slugs.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Watch it!’ Hagrid roared, pulling Ron away from his precious pumpkins.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was nearly lunchtime and as Harry had only had one bit of treacle toffee since dawn, he was keen to go back to school to eat. They said goodbye to Hagrid and walked back up to the castle, Ron hiccoughing occasionally, but only bringing up two, very small slugs.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They had barely set foot in the cool Entrance Hall when a voice rang out. ‘There you are, Potter, Weasley.’ Professor McGonagall was walking towards them, looking stern. ‘You will both do your detentions this evening.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What are we doing, Professor?’ said Ron, nervously suppressing a burp.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You will be polishing the silver in the trophy room with Mr Filch,’ said Professor McGonagall. ‘And no magic, Weasley - elbow grease.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron gulped. Argus Filch, the caretaker, was loathed by every student in the school.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And you, Potter, will be helping Professor Lockhart answer his fan mail,’ said Professor McGonagall.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh no - can’t I go and do the trophy room, too?’ said Harry desperately.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Certainly not,’ said Professor McGonagall, raising her eyebrows. ‘Professor Lockhart requested you particularly. Eight o’clock sharp, both of you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron slouched into the Great Hall in states of deepest gloom, Hermione behind them, wearing a well-you-did-break-school-rules sort of expression. Harry didn’t fancy his shepherd’s pie as much as he’d thought. Both he and Ron felt they’d got the worse deal.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Filch’ll have me there all night,’ said Ron heavily. ‘No magic! There must be about a hundred cups in that room. I’m no good at Muggle cleaning.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’d swap any time,’ said Harry hollowly. ‘I’ve had loads of practice with the Dursleys. Answering Lockhart’s fan mail … he’ll be a nightmare …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Saturday afternoon seemed to melt away, and in what seemed like no time, it was five minutes to eight, and Harry was dragging his feet along the second-floor corridor to Lockhart’s office. He gritted his teeth and knocked.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The door flew open at once. Lockhart beamed down at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ah, here’s the scallywag!’ he said. ‘Come in, Harry, come in.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Shining brightly on the walls by the light of many candles were countless framed photographs of Lockhart. He had even signed a few of them. Another large pile lay on his desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You can address the envelopes!’ Lockhart told Harry, as though this was a huge treat. ‘This first one’s to Gladys Gudgeon, bless her - huge fan of mine.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

text_content: Harry woke early on Saturday morning and lay for a while thinking about the coming Quidditch match. He was nervous, mainly at the thought of what Wood would say if Gryffindor lost, but also at the idea of facing a team mounted on the fastest racing brooms gold could buy. He had never wanted to beat Slytherin so badly. After half an hour of lying there with his insides churning, he got up, dressed, and went down to breakfast early, where he found the rest of the Gryffindor team huddled at the long, empty table, all looking uptight and not speaking much.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

Ron and Hermione came hurrying over to wish Harry good luck as he entered the changing rooms. The team pulled on their scarlet Gryffindor robes, then sat down to listen to Wood’s usual pre-match pep talk.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Slytherin have better brooms than us,’ he began, ‘no point denying it. But we’ve got better people on our brooms. text_content: Through the thicket of legs around him, Harry spotted Fred and George Weasley, wrestling the rogue Bludger into a box. It was still putting up a terrific fight.

text_content: Harry gaped at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

text_content: Harry’s mouth fell open.

text_content: The castle was darker than it usually was in daytime, because of the thick, swirling grey snow at every window. Professor McGonagall was shouting at someone who, by the sound of it, had turned his friend into a badger. Resisting the urge to take a look, Harry walked on by, thinking that Justin might be using his free lesson to catch up on some work, and deciding to check the library first.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A group of the Hufflepuffs who should have been in Herbology were indeed sitting at the back of the library, but they didn’t seem to be working. text_content: Ernie lowered his voice mysteriously, the Hufflepuffs bent closer, and Harry edged nearer so that he could catch Ernie’s words.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hello,’ said Harry. ‘I’m looking for Justin Finch-Fletchley.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He turned to squint at what he’d fallen over, and felt as though his stomach had dissolved.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Justin Finch-Fletchley was lying on the floor, rigid and cold, a look of shock frozen on his face, his eyes staring blankly at the ceiling. And that wasn’t all. Next to him was another figure, the strangest sight Harry had ever seen.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was Nearly Headless Nick, no longer pearly-white and transparent, but black and smoky, floating immobile and horizontal, six inches off the floor. His head was half off and his face wore an expression of shock identical to Justin’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry got to his feet, his breathing fast and shallow, his heart doing a kind of drum-roll against his ribs. He looked wildly up and down the deserted corridor and saw a line of spiders scuttling as fast as they could away from the bodies. The only sounds were the muffled voices of teachers from the classes on either side.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He could run, and no one would ever know he had been there. But he couldn’t just leave them lying here … he had to get help. Would anyone believe he hadn’t had anything to do with this?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: As he stood there, panicking, a door right next to him opened with a bang. Peeves the poltergeist came shooting out.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Why, it’s potty wee Potter!’ cackled Peeves, knocking Harry’s glasses askew as he bounced past him. ‘What’s Potter up to? Why’s Potter lurking -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Peeves stopped, halfway through a mid-air somersault. Upside-down, he spotted Justin and Nearly Headless Nick. He flipped the right way up, filled his lungs and, before Harry could stop him, screamed, ‘ATTACK! ATTACK! ANOTHER ATTACK! NO MORTAL OR GHOST IS SAFE! RUN FOR YOUR LIVES! ATTAAAACK!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Crash - crash - crash: door after door flew open along the corridor and people flooded out. For several long minutes, there was a scene of such confusion that Justin was in danger of being squashed and people kept standing in Nearly Headless Nick. Harry found himself pinned against the wall as the teachers shouted for quiet. Professor McGonagall came running, followed by her own class, one of whom still had black and white striped hair. She used her wand to set off a loud bang, which restored silence, and ordered everyone back into their classes. No sooner had the scene cleared somewhat than Ernie the Hufflepuff arrived, panting, on the scene.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Caught in the act!’ Ernie yelled, his face stark white, pointing his finger dramatically at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That will do, Macmillan!’ said Professor McGonagall sharply.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Peeves was bobbing overhead, now grinning wickedly, surveying the scene; Peeves always loved chaos. As the teachers bent over Justin and Nearly Headless Nick, examining them, Peeves broke into song:

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh Potter, you rotter, oh what have you done?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: You’re killing off students, you think it’s good fun -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s enough Peeves!’ barked Professor McGonagall, and Peeves zoomed away backwards, with his tongue out at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘This way, Potter,’ she said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

text_content: ‘Sherbet lemon!’ she said. This was evidently a password, because the gargoyle sprang suddenly to life, and hopped aside as the wall behind him split in two. As he and Professor McGonagall stepped onto it, Harry heard the wall thud closed behind them. They rose upwards in circles, higher and higher, until at last, slightly dizzy, Harry could see a gleaming oak door ahead, with a brass knocker in the shape of a griffon.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He knew where he was being taken. This must be where Dumbledore lived.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They stepped off the stone staircase at the top and Professor McGonagall rapped on the door. It opened silently and they entered. Professor McGonagall told Harry to wait, and left him there, alone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked around. One thing was certain: of all the teachers’ offices Harry had visited so far this year, Dumbledore’s was by far the most interesting. If he hadn’t been scared out of his wits that he was about to be thrown out of school, he would have been very pleased to have a chance to look around it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was a large and beautiful circular room, full of funny little noises. A number of curious silver instruments stood on spindle-legged tables, whirring and emitting little puffs of smoke. The walls were covered with portraits of old headmasters and headmistresses, all of whom were snoozing gently in their frames. There was also an enormous, claw-footed desk, and, sitting on a shelf behind it, a shabby, tattered wizard’s hat - the Sorting Hat.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry hesitated. He cast a wary eye around the sleeping witches and wizards on the walls. Surely it couldn’t hurt if he took the Hat down and tried it on again? Just to see … just to make sure it had put him in the right house.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He walked quietly around the desk, lifted the Hat from its shelf, and lowered it slowly onto his head. It was much too large and slipped down over his eyes, just as it had done the last time he’d put it on. Harry stared at the black inside of the Hat, waiting. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry’s stomach plummeted. He grabbed the point of the Hat and pulled it off. It hung limply in his hand, grubby and faded. Harry pushed it back onto its shelf, feeling sick.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He wasn’t alone after all. Standing on a golden perch behind the door was a decrepit-looking bird which resembled a half-plucked turkey. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The office door opened. Dumbledore came in, looking very sombre.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor,’ Harry gasped, ‘your bird - I couldn’t do anything - he just caught fire -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He chuckled at the stunned look on Harry’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked down in time to see a tiny, wrinkled, new-born bird poke its head out of the ashes. It was quite as ugly as the old one.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s a shame you had to see him on a Burning Day,’ said Dumbledore, seating himself behind his desk. ‘He’s really very handsome most of the time: wonderful red and gold plumage. Fascinating creatures, phoenixes. They can carry immensely heavy loads, their tears have healing powers and they make highly faithful pets.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: In the shock of Fawkes catching fire, Harry had forgotten what he was there for, but it all came back to him as Dumbledore settled himself in the high-backed chair behind the desk and fixed Harry with his penetrating, light-blue stare.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Before Dumbledore could speak another word, however, the door of the office flew open with an almighty bang and Hagrid burst in, a wild look in his eyes, his balaclava perched on top of his shaggy black head and the dead rooster still swinging from his hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It wasn’ Harry, Professor Dumbledore!’ said Hagrid urgently. ‘I was talkin’ ter him seconds before that kid was found, he never had time, sir …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore tried to say something, but Hagrid went ranting on, waving the rooster around in his agitation, sending feathers everywhere.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… It can’t’ve bin him, I’ll swear it in front o’ the Ministry o’ Magic if I have to …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid, I -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘… Yeh’ve got the wrong boy, sir, I know Harry never -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid!’ said Dumbledore loudly. ‘I do not think that Harry attacked those people.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ said Hagrid, the rooster falling limply at his side. ‘Right. I’ll wait outside then, Headmaster.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And he stomped out looking embarrassed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You don’t think it was me, Professor?’ Harry repeated hopefully, as Dumbledore brushed rooster feathers off his desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No, Harry, I don’t,’ said Dumbledore, though his face was sombre again. ‘But I still want to talk to you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry waited nervously while Dumbledore considered him, the tips of his long fingers together.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I must ask you, Harry, whether there is anything you’d like to tell me,’ he said gently. ‘Anything at all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t know what to say. He thought of Malfoy shouting, ‘You’ll be next, Mudbloods!’ and of the Polyjuice Potion, simmering away in Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom. Then he thought of the disembodied voice he had heard twice and remembered what Ron had said: ‘Hearing voices no one else can hear isn’t a good sign, even in the wizarding world.’ He thought, too, about what everyone was saying about him, and his growing dread that he was somehow connected with Salazar Slytherin …

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry, ‘there isn’t anything, Professor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The double attack on Justin and Nearly Headless Nick turned what had hitherto been nervousness into real panic. Curiously, it was Nearly Headless Nick’s fate that seemed to worry people most. What could possibly do that to a ghost, people asked each other; what terrible power could harm someone who was already dead? There was almost a stampede to book seats on the Hogwarts Express so that students could go home for Christmas.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘At this rate, we’ll be the only ones left,’ Ron told Harry and Hermione. ‘Us, Malfoy, Crabbe and Goyle. What a jolly holiday it’s going to be.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Crabbe and Goyle, who always did whatever Malfoy did, had signed up to stay over the holidays too. But Harry was glad that most people were leaving. He was tired of people skirting around him in the corridors, as though he was about to sprout fangs or spit poison; tired of all the muttering, pointing and hissing as he passed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fred and George, however, found all this very funny. They went out of their way to march ahead of Harry down the corridors, shouting, ‘Make way for the heir of Slytherin, seriously evil wizard coming through …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Percy was deeply disapproving of this behaviour.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It is not a laughing matter,’ he said coldly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, get out of the way, Percy,’ said Fred. ‘Harry’s in a hurry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, he’s nipping off to the Chamber of Secrets for a cup of tea with his fanged servant,’ said George, chortling.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ginny didn’t find it amusing either.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, don’t,’ she wailed every time Fred asked Harry loudly who he was planning to attack next, or George pretended to ward Harry off with a large clove of garlic when they met.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t mind; it made him feel better that Fred and George, at least, thought the idea of his being Slytherin’s heir was quite ludicrous. But their antics seemed to be aggravating Draco Malfoy, who looked increasingly sour each time he saw them at it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s because he’s bursting to say it’s really him,’ said Ron knowingly. ‘You know how he hates anyone beating him at anything, and you’re getting all the credit for his dirty work.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Not for long,’ said Hermione in a satisfied tone. ‘The Polyjuice Potion’s nearly ready. We’ll be getting the truth out of him any day now.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: At last the term ended, and a silence deep as the snow on the grounds descended on the castle. Harry found it peaceful, rather than gloomy, and enjoyed the fact that he, Hermione and the Weasleys had the run of Gryffindor Tower, which meant they could play Exploding Snap loudly without bothering anyone, and practise duelling in private. Fred, George and Ginny had chosen to stay at school rather than visit Bill in Egypt with Mr and Mrs Weasley. Percy, who disapproved of what he termed their childish behaviour, didn’t spend much time in the Gryffindor common room. He had already told them pompously that he was only staying over Christmas because it was his duty as a Prefect to support the teachers during this troubled time.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Christmas morning dawned, cold and white. Harry and Ron, the only ones left in their dormitory, were woken very early by Hermione, who burst in, fully dressed and carrying presents for them both.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Wake up,’ she said loudly, pulling back the curtains at the window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione - you’re not supposed to be in here,’ said Ron, shielding his eyes against the light.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Merry Christmas to you, too,’ said Hermione, throwing him his present. ‘I’ve been up for nearly an hour, adding more lacewings to the Potion. It’s ready.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry sat up, suddenly wide awake.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you sure?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Positive,’ said Hermione, shifting Scabbers the rat so that she could sit down on the end of his four-poster. ‘If we’re going to do it, I say it should be tonight.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: At that moment, Hedwig swooped into the room, carrying a very small package in her beak.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hello,’ said Harry happily, as she landed on his bed, ‘are you speaking to me again?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She nibbled his ear in an affectionate sort of way, which was a far better present than the one which she had brought him, which turned out to be from the Dursleys. They had sent Harry a toothpick and a note telling him to find out whether he’d be able to stay at Hogwarts for the summer holidays, too.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The rest of Harry’s Christmas presents were far more satisfactory. Hagrid had sent him a large tin of treacle fudge, which Harry decided to soften by the fire before eating; Ron had given him a book called Flying with the Cannons, a book of interesting facts about his favourite Quidditch team; and Hermione had bought him a luxury eagle-feather quill. Harry opened the last present to find a new, hand-knitted jumper from Mrs Weasley, and a large plum cake. He put up her card with a fresh surge of guilt, thinking about Mr Weasley’s car, which hadn’t been seen since its crash with the Whomping Willow, and the bout of rule-breaking he and Ron were planning next.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: No one, not even someone dreading taking Polyjuice Potion later, could fail to enjoy Christmas dinner at Hogwarts.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Great Hall looked magnificent. Not only were there a dozen frost-covered Christmas trees and thick streamers of holly and mistletoe criss-crossing the ceiling, but enchanted snow was falling, warm and dry, from the ceiling. Dumbledore led them in a few of his favourite carols, Hagrid booming more and more loudly with every goblet of eggnog he consumed. Percy, who hadn’t noticed that Fred had bewitched his prefect badge so that it now read ‘Pinhead’, kept asking them all what they were sniggering at. Harry didn’t even care that Draco Malfoy was making loud, snide remarks about his new jumper from the Slytherin table. With a bit of luck, Malfoy would be getting his come-uppance in a few hours’ time.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron had barely finished their third helpings of Christmas pudding when Hermione ushered them out of the Hall to finalise their plans for the evening.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We still need a bit of the people you’re changing into,’ said Hermione matter-of-factly, as though she was sending them to the supermarket for washing-powder. ‘And obviously, it’ll be best if you can get something of Crabbe and Goyle’s; they’re Malfoy’s best friends, he’ll tell them anything. And we also need to make sure the real Crabbe and Goyle can’t burst in on us while we’re interrogating him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve got it all worked out,’ she went on smoothly, ignoring Harry and Ron’s stupefied faces. She held up two plump chocolate cakes. ‘I’ve filled these with a simple Sleeping Draught. All you have to do is make sure Crabbe and Goyle find them. You know how greedy they are, they’re bound to eat them. Once they’re asleep, pull out a few of their hairs and hide them in a broom cupboard.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron looked incredulously at each other.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione, I don’t think -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That could go seriously wrong -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Hermione had a steely glint in her eye not unlike the one Professor McGonagall sometimes had.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The Potion will be useless without Crabbe and Goyle’s hair,’ she said sternly. ‘You do want to investigate Malfoy, don’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, all right, all right,’ said Harry. ‘But what about you? Whose hair are you ripping out?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve already got mine!’ said Hermione brightly, pulling a tiny bottle out of her pocket and showing them the single hair inside it. ‘Remember Millicent Bulstrode wrestling with me at the Duelling Club? She left this on my robes when she was trying to strangle me! And she’s gone home for Christmas - so I’ll just have to tell the Slytherins I’ve decided to come back.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: When Hermione had bustled off to check on the Polyjuice Potion again, Ron turned to Harry with a doom-laden expression.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Have you ever heard of a plan where so many things could go wrong?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But to Harry and Ron’s utter amazement, stage one of the operation went just as smoothly as Hermione had said. They lurked in the deserted Entrance Hall after Christmas tea, waiting for Crabbe and Goyle, who had remained alone at the Slytherin table, shovelling down fourth helpings of trifle. Harry had perched the chocolate cakes on the end of the banisters. When they spotted Crabbe and Goyle coming out of the Great Hall, Harry and Ron hid quickly behind a suit of armour next to the front door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘How thick can you get?’ Ron whispered ecstatically, as Crabbe gleefully pointed out the cakes to Goyle and grabbed them. Grinning stupidly, they stuffed the cakes whole into their large mouths. For a moment, both of them chewed greedily, looks of triumph on their faces. Then, without the smallest change of expression, they both keeled over backwards onto the floor.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Much the most difficult bit was hiding them in the cupboard across the hall. Once they were safely stowed amongst the buckets and mops, Harry yanked out a couple of the bristles that covered Goyle’s forehead and Ron pulled out several of Crabbe’s hairs. They also stole their shoes, because their own were far too small for Crabbe- and Goyle-sized feet. Then, still stunned at what they had just done, they sprinted up to Moaning Myrtle’s bathroom.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They could hardly see for the thick black smoke issuing from the cubicle in which Hermione was stirring the cauldron. Pulling their robes up over their faces, Harry and Ron knocked softly on the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They heard the scrape of the lock and Hermione emerged, shiny-faced and looking anxious. Behind her they heard the gloop gloop of the bubbling, treacle-thick Potion. Three glass tumblers stood ready on the toilet seat.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you get them?’ Hermione asked breathlessly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry showed her Goyle’s hair.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good. And I sneaked these spare robes out of the laundry,’ Hermione said, holding up a small sack. ‘You’ll need bigger sizes once you’re Crabbe and Goyle.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The three of them stared into the cauldron. Close up, the Potion looked like thick, dark mud, bubbling sluggishly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m sure I’ve done everything right,’ said Hermione, nervously re-reading the splotched page of Moste Potente Potions. ‘It looks like the book says it should … Once we’ve drunk it, we’ll have exactly an hour before we change back into ourselves.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now what?’ Ron whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We separate it into three glasses and add the hairs.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione ladled large dollops of the Potion into each of the glasses. Then, her hand trembling, she shook Millicent Bulstrode’s hair out of its bottle into the first glass.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Add yours, then,’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hang on,’ said Harry, as Ron and Hermione reached for their glasses. ‘We’d better not all drink them in here: once we turn into Crabbe and Goyle we won’t fit. And Millicent Bulstrode’s no pixie.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good thinking,’ said Ron, unlocking the door. ‘We’ll take separate cubicles.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Careful not to spill a drop of his Polyjuice Potion, Harry slipped into the middle cubicle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ready?’ he called.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ready,’ came Ron and Hermione’s voices.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘One … two … three …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Pinching his nose, Harry drank the Potion down in two large gulps. It tasted like overcooked cabbage.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Immediately, his insides started writhing as though he’d just swallowed live snakes - doubled up, he wondered whether he was going to be sick -then a burning sensation spread rapidly from his stomach to the very ends of his fingers and toes.
