text_content: Harry stood, irresolute, trying to catch the voice again, but people were now emerging from the Great Hall behind him, talking loudly, exiting through the front doors on their way to the Quidditch pitch.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’d better get moving,’ said Ron. ‘It’s nearly eleven - the match.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry raced up to Gryffindor Tower, collected his Nimbus Two Thousand and joined the large crowd swarming across the grounds, but his mind was still in the castle, along with the bodiless voice, and as he pulled on his scarlet robes in the changing room, his only comfort was that everyone was now outside to watch the game.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The teams walked onto the pitch to tumultuous applause. Oliver Wood took off for a warm-up flight around the goalposts, Madam Hooch released the balls. The Hufflepuffs, who played in canary yellow, were standing in a huddle, having a last-minute discussion of tactics.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry was just mounting his broom when Professor McGonagall came half-marching, half-running across the pitch, carrying an enormous purple megaphone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry’s heart dropped like a stone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘This match has been cancelled,’ Professor McGonagall called through the megaphone, addressing the packed stadium. There were boos and shouts. Oliver Wood, looking devastated, landed and ran towards Professor McGonagall without getting off his broomstick.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But Professor!’ he shouted. ‘We’ve got to play … the Cup … Gryffindor …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor McGonagall ignored him and continued to shout through her megaphone: ‘All students are to make their way back to the house common rooms, where their Heads of Houses will give them further information. As quickly as you can, please!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Then she lowered the megaphone and beckoned Harry over to her.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Potter, I think you’d better come with me …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Wondering how she could possibly suspect him this time, Harry saw Ron detach himself from the complaining crowd; he came running up to them as they set off towards the castle. To Harry’s surprise, Professor McGonagall didn’t object.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, perhaps you’d better come too, Weasley.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Some of the students swarming around them were grumbling about the match being cancelled, others looked worried. Harry and Ron followed Professor McGonagall back into the school and up the marble staircase. But they weren’t taken to anybody’s office this time.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘This will be a bit of a shock,’ said Professor McGonagall in a surprisingly gentle voice as they approached the hospital wing. ‘There has been another attack … another double attack.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry’s insides did a horrible somersault. Professor McGonagall pushed the door open and he and Ron entered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Madam Pomfrey was bending over a sixth-year girl with long curly hair. Harry recognised her as the Ravenclaw they’d accidentally asked for directions to the Slytherin common room. And on the bed next to her was -

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione!’ Ron groaned.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hermione lay utterly still, her eyes open and glassy.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘They were found near the library,’ said Professor McGonagall. ‘I don’t suppose either of you can explain this? It was on the floor next to them …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She was holding up a small, circular mirror.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron shook their heads, both staring at Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I will escort you back to Gryffindor Tower,’ said Professor McGonagall heavily. ‘I need to address the students in any case.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘All students will return to their house common rooms by six o’clock in the evening. No student is to leave the dormitories after that time. You will be escorted to each lesson by a teacher. No student is to use the bathroom unaccompanied by a teacher. All further Quidditch training and matches are to be postponed. There will be no more evening activities.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Gryffindors packed inside the common room listened to Professor McGonagall in silence. She rolled up the parchment from which she had been reading and said in a somewhat choked voice, ‘I need hardly add that I have rarely been so distressed. It is likely that the school will be closed unless the culprit behind these attacks is caught. I would urge anyone who thinks they might know anything about them to come forward.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: She climbed somewhat awkwardly out of the portrait hole, and the Gryffindors began talking immediately.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s two Gryffindors down, not counting a Gryffindor ghost, one Ravenclaw and one Hufflepuff,’ said the Weasley twins’ friend Lee Jordan, counting on his fingers. ‘Haven’t any of the teachers noticed that the Slytherins are all safe? Isn’t it obvious all this stuff’s coming from Slytherin? The heir of Slytherin, the monster of Slytherin - why don’t they just chuck all the Slytherins out?’ he roared, to nods and scattered applause.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Percy Weasley was sitting in a chair behind Lee, but for once he didn’t seem keen to make his views heard. He was looking pale and stunned.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Percy’s in shock,’ George told Harry quietly. ‘That Ravenclaw girl -Penelope Clearwater - she’s a Prefect. I don’t think he thought the monster would dare attack a Prefect.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Harry was only half-listening. He didn’t seem to be able to get rid of the picture of Hermione, lying on the hospital bed as though carved out of stone. And if the culprit wasn’t caught soon, he was looking at a lifetime back with the Dursleys. Tom Riddle had turned Hagrid in because he was faced with the prospect of a Muggle orphanage if the school closed. Harry now knew exactly how he had felt.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’re we going to do?’ said Ron quietly in Harry’s ear. ‘D’you think they suspect Hagrid?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ve got to go and talk to him,’ said Harry, making up his mind. ‘I can’t believe it’s him this time, but if he set the monster loose last time he’ll know how to get inside the Chamber of Secrets, and that’s a start.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But McGonagall said we’ve got to stay in our tower unless we’re in class -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I think,’ said Harry, more quietly still, ‘it’s time to get my dad’s old Cloak out again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had inherited just one thing from his father: a long and silvery Invisibility Cloak. It was their only chance of sneaking out of the school to visit Hagrid without anyone knowing about it. They went to bed at the usual time, waited until Neville, Dean and Seamus had stopped discussing the Chamber of Secrets and finally fallen asleep, then got up, dressed again, and threw the Cloak over themselves.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The journey through the dark and deserted castle corridors wasn’t enjoyable. Harry, who had wandered the castle at night several times before, had never seen it so crowded after sunset. Teachers, Prefects and ghosts were marching the corridors in pairs, staring around for any unusual activity. Their Invisibility Cloak didn’t stop them making any noise, and there was a particularly tense moment when Ron stubbed his toe only yards from the spot where Snape was standing guard. Thankfully, Snape sneezed at almost exactly the moment Ron swore. It was with relief that they reached the oak front doors and eased them open.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was a clear, starry night. They hurried towards the lighted windows of Hagrid’s house, and pulled off the Cloak only when they were right outside his front door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Seconds after they had knocked, Hagrid flung it open. They found themselves face to face, with him aiming a crossbow at them, Fang the boarhound barking loudly behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ he said, lowering the weapon and staring at them. ‘What’re you two doin’ here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s that for?’ said Harry, pointing at the crossbow as they stepped inside.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Nothin’ … nothin’,’ Hagrid muttered. ‘I’ve bin expectin’ … doesn’ matter … Sit down … I’ll make tea …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He hardly seemed to know what he was doing. He nearly extinguished the fire, spilling water from the kettle on it, and then smashed the teapot with a nervous jerk of his massive hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you OK, Hagrid?’ said Harry. ‘Did you hear about Hermione?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I heard, all righ’,’ said Hagrid, a slight break in his voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He kept glancing nervously at the windows. He poured them both large mugs of boiling water (he had forgotten to add tea bags) and was just putting a slab of fruitcake on a plate, when there was a loud knock on the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid dropped the fruitcake. Harry and Ron exchanged panic-stricken looks, then threw the Invisibility Cloak back over themselves and retreated into a corner. Hagrid checked that they were hidden, seized his crossbow and flung open his door once more.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good evening, Hagrid.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was Dumbledore. He entered, looking deadly serious, and was followed by a second, very odd-looking man.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The stranger was a short, portly man with rumpled grey hair and an anxious expression. He was wearing a strange mixture of clothes: a pin-striped suit, a scarlet tie, a long black cloak and pointed purple boots. Under his arm he carried a lime-green bowler.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s Dad’s boss!’ Ron breathed. ‘Cornelius Fudge, the Minister of Magic!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry elbowed Ron hard to make him shut up.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid had gone pale and sweaty. He dropped into one of his chairs and looked from Dumbledore to Cornelius Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Bad business, Hagrid,’ said Fudge, in rather clipped tones. ‘Very bad business. Had to come. Four attacks on Muggle-borns. Things’ve gone far enough. Ministry’s got to act.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I never,’ said Hagrid, looking imploringly at Dumbledore, ‘you know I never, Professor Dumbledore, sir …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I want it understood, Cornelius, that Hagrid has my full confidence,’ said Dumbledore, frowning at Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Look, Albus,’ said Fudge, uncomfortably. ‘Hagrid’s record’s against him. Ministry’s got to do something - the school governors have been in touch.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yet again, Cornelius, I tell you that taking Hagrid away will not help in the slightest,’ said Dumbledore. His blue eyes were full of a fire Harry had never seen before.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Look at it from my point of view,’ said Fudge, fidgeting with his bowler. ‘I’m under a lot of pressure. Got to be seen to be doing something. If it turns out it wasn’t Hagrid, he’ll be back and no more said. But I’ve got to take him. Got to. Wouldn’t be doing my duty -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Take me?’ said Hagrid, who was trembling. ‘Take me where?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘For a short stretch only,’ said Fudge, not meeting Hagrid’s eyes. ‘Not a punishment, Hagrid, more a precaution. If someone else is caught, you’ll be let out with a full apology …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Not Azkaban?’ croaked Hagrid.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Before Fudge could answer, there was another loud rap on the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore answered it. It was Harry’s turn for an elbow in the ribs: he’d let out an audible gasp.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Lucius Malfoy strode into Hagrid’s hut, swathed in a long black travelling cloak, smiling a cold and satisfied smile. Fang started to growl.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Already here, Fudge,’ he said approvingly. ‘Good, good …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’re you doin’ here?’ said Hagrid furiously. ‘Get outta my house!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘My dear man, please believe me, I have no pleasure at all in being inside your - er - d’you call this a house?’ said Lucius Malfoy, sneering as he looked around the small cabin. ‘I simply called at the school and was told that the Headmaster was here.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And what exactly did you want with me, Lucius?’ said Dumbledore. He spoke politely, but the fire was still blazing in his blue eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Dreadful thing, Dumbledore,’ said Mr Malfoy lazily, taking out a long roll of parchment, ‘but the governors feel it’s time for you to step aside. This is an Order of Suspension - you’ll find all twelve signatures on it. I’m afraid we feel you’re losing your touch. How many attacks have there been now? Two more this afternoon, wasn’t it? At this rate, there’ll be no Muggle-borns left at Hogwarts, and we all know what an awful loss that would be to the school.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, now, see here, Lucius,’ said Fudge, looking alarmed, ‘Dumbledore suspended … no, no … last thing we want just now …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The appointment - or suspension - of the Headmaster is a matter for the governors, Fudge,’ said Mr Malfoy smoothly. ‘And as Dumbledore has failed to stop these attacks …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now look, Lucius, if Dumbledore can’t stop them -‘ said Fudge, whose upper lip was sweating now, ‘I mean to say, who can?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That remains to be seen,’ said Mr Malfoy, with a nasty smile. ‘But as all twelve of us have voted …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid leapt to his feet, his shaggy black head grazing the ceiling.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘An’ how many did yeh have ter threaten an’ blackmail before they agreed, Malfoy, eh?’ he roared.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Dear, dear, you know, that temper of yours will lead you into trouble one of these days, Hagrid,’ said Mr Malfoy. ‘I would advise you not to shout at the Azkaban guards like that. They won’t like it at all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeh can’ take Dumbledore!’ yelled Hagrid, making Fang the boarhound cower and whimper in his basket. ‘Take him away, an’ the Muggle-borns won’ stand a chance! There’ll be killin’s next!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Calm yourself, Hagrid,’ said Dumbledore sharply. He looked at Lucius Malfoy.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘If the governors want my removal, Lucius, I shall of course step aside.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But -‘ stuttered Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No!’ growled Hagrid.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore had not taken his bright blue eyes off Lucius Malfoy’s cold grey ones.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘However,’ said Dumbledore, speaking very slowly and clearly, so that none of them could miss a word, ‘you will find that I will only truly have left this school when none here are loyal to me. You will also find that help will always be given at Hogwarts to those who ask for it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: For a second, Harry was almost sure Dumbledore’s eyes flickered towards the corner where he and Ron stood hidden.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Admirable sentiments,’ said Malfoy, bowing. ‘We shall all miss your - er - highly individual way of running things, Albus, and only hope that your successor will manage to prevent any - ah - “killin’s”.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He strode to the cabin door, opened it and bowed Dumbledore out. Fudge, fiddling with his bowler, waited for Hagrid to go ahead of him, but Hagrid stood his ground, took a deep breath and said carefully, ‘If anyone wanted ter find out some stuff, all they’d have ter do would be ter follow the spiders. That’d lead ‘em right! That’s all I’m sayin’.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fudge stared at him in amazement.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘All right, I’m comin’,’ said Hagrid, pulling on his moleskin overcoat. But as he was about to follow Fudge through the door, he stopped again and said loudly, ‘An’ someone’ll need ter feed Fang while I’m away.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The door banged shut and Ron pulled the Invisibility Cloak off.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re in trouble now,’ he said hoarsely. ‘No Dumbledore. They might as well close the school tonight. There’ll be an attack a day with him gone.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fang started howling, scratching at the closed door.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Summer was creeping over the grounds around the castle; sky and lake alike turned periwinkle blue and flowers large as cabbages burst into bloom in the greenhouses. But with no Hagrid visible from the castle windows, striding the grounds with Fang at his heels, the scene didn’t look right to Harry; no better, in fact, than the inside of the castle, where things were so horribly wrong.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron had tried to visit Hermione, but visitors were now barred from the hospital wing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re taking no more chances,’ Madam Pomfrey told them severely through a crack in the hospital door. ‘No, I’m sorry, there’s every chance the attacker might come back to finish these people off …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: With Dumbledore gone, fear had spread as never before, so that the sun warming the castle walls outside seemed to stop at the mullioned windows. There was barely a face to be seen in the school that didn’t look worried and tense, and any laughter that rang through the corridors sounded shrill and unnatural and was quickly stifled.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry constantly repeated Dumbledore’s final words to himself. ‘I will only truly have left this school when none here are loyal to me … Help will always be given at Hogwarts to those who ask for it.’ But what good were these words? Who exactly were they supposed to ask for help, when everyone was just as confused and scared as they were?

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Hagrid’s hint about the spiders was far easier to understand - the trouble was, there didn’t seem to be a single spider left in the castle to follow. Harry looked everywhere he went, helped (rather reluctantly) by Ron. They were hampered, of course, by the fact that they weren’t allowed to wander off on their own, but had to move around the castle in a pack with the other Gryffindors. Most of their fellow students seemed glad that they were being shepherded from class to class by teachers, but Harry found it very irksome.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: One person, however, seemed to be thoroughly enjoying the atmosphere of terror and suspicion. Draco Malfoy was strutting around the school as though he had just been appointed Head Boy. Harry didn’t realise what he was so pleased about until the Potions lesson about a fortnight after Dumbledore and Hagrid had left, when, sitting right behind Malfoy, Harry overheard him gloating to Crabbe and Goyle.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I always thought Father might be the one who got rid of Dumbledore,’ he said, not troubling to keep his voice down. ‘I told you he thinks Dumbledore’s the worst Headmaster the school’s ever had. Maybe we’ll get a decent Headmaster now. Someone who won’t want the Chamber of Secrets closed. McGonagall won’t last long, she’s only filling in …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Snape swept past Harry, making no comment about Hermione’s empty seat and cauldron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir,’ said Malfoy loudly. ‘Sir, why don’t you apply for the Headmaster’s job?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, now, Malfoy,’ said Snape, though he couldn’t suppress a thin-lipped smile. ‘Professor Dumbledore has only been suspended by the governors. I dare say he’ll be back with us soon enough.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, right,’ said Malfoy, smirking. ‘I expect you’d have father’s vote, sir, if you wanted to apply for the job. I’ll tell father you’re the best teacher here, sir …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Snape smirked as he swept off around the dungeon, fortunately not spotting Seamus Finnigan, who was pretending to vomit into his cauldron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m quite surprised the Mudbloods haven’t all packed their bags by now,’ Malfoy went on. ‘bet you five Galleons the next one dies. Pity it wasn’t Granger …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The bell rang at that moment, which was lucky; at Malfoy’s last words, Ron had leapt off his stool, and in the scramble to collect bags and books, his attempts to reach Malfoy went unnoticed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Let me at him,’ Ron growled, as Harry and Dean hung onto his arms. ‘I don’t care, I don’t need my wand, I’m going to kill him with my bare hands -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hurry up, I’ve got to take you all to Herbology,’ barked Snape over the class’s heads, and off they went, crocodile fashion, with Harry, Ron and Dean bringing up the rear, Ron still trying to get loose. It was only safe to let go of him when Snape had seen them out of the castle, and they were making their way across the vegetable patch towards the greenhouses.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Herbology class was very subdued; there were now two missing from their number, Justin and Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Professor Sprout set them all to work pruning the Abyssinian Shrivelfigs. Harry went to tip an armful of withered stalks onto the compost heap and found himself face to face with Ernie Macmillan. Ernie took a deep breath and said, very formally, ‘I just want to say, Harry, that I’m sorry I ever suspected you. I know you’d never attack Hermione Granger, and I apologise for all the stuff I said. We’re all in the same boat now, and, well -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He held out a pudgy hand, and Harry shook it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ernie and his friend Hannah came to work at the same Shrivelfig as Harry and Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That Draco Malfoy character,’ said Ernie, breaking off dead twigs, ‘he seems very pleased about all this, doesn’t he? D’you know, I think he might be Slytherin’s heir.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s clever of you,’ said Ron, who didn’t seem to have forgiven Ernie as readily as Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Do you think it’s Malfoy, Harry?’ Ernie asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry, so firmly that Ernie and Hannah stared.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: A second later, Harry spotted something that made him hit Ron over the hand with his pruning shears.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ouch! What’re you -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry was pointing at the ground a few feet away. Several large spiders were scurrying across the earth.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yeah,’ said Ron, trying, and failing, to look pleased. ‘But we can’t follow them now …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ernie and Hannah were listening curiously.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry watched the spiders running away.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Looks like they’re heading for the Forbidden Forest …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And Ron looked even unhappier about that.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: At the end of the lesson Professor Sprout escorted the class to their Defence Against the Dark Arts lesson. Harry and Ron lagged behind the others so they could talk out of earshot.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ll have to use the Invisibility Cloak again,’ Harry told Ron. ‘We can take Fang with us. He’s used to going into the Forest with Hagrid, he might be some help.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Ron, who was twirling his wand nervously in his fingers. ‘Er - aren’t there - aren’t there supposed to be werewolves in the Forest?’ he added, as they took their usual places at the back of Lockhart’s classroom.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Preferring not to answer that question, Harry said, ‘There are good things in there, too. The centaurs are all right, and the unicorns.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron had never been into the Forbidden Forest before. Harry had entered it only once, and had hoped never to do so again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Lockhart bounded into the room and the class stared at him. Every other teacher in the place was looking grimmer than usual, but Lockhart appeared nothing short of buoyant.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Come now,’ he cried, beaming around him, ‘why all these long faces?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yes he would,’ said Ron, even more loudly than Dean.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I flatter myself I know a touch more about Hagrid’s arrest than you do, Mr Weasley,’ said Lockhart in a self-satisfied tone.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron started to say that he didn’t think so, somehow, but stopped in mid-sentence when Harry kicked him hard under the desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Lockhart’s disgusting cheeriness, his hints that he had always thought Hagrid was no good, his confidence that the whole business was now at an end, irritated Harry so much that he yearned to throw Gadding with Ghouls right in Lockhart’s stupid face. Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The Gryffindor common room was always very crowded these days, because from six o’clock onwards, the Gryffindors had nowhere else to go. They also had plenty to talk about, with the result that the common room often didn’t empty until past midnight.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry went to get the Invisibility Cloak out of his trunk right after dinner, and spent the evening sitting on it, waiting for the room to clear. Fred and George challenged Harry and Ron to a few games of Exploding Snap and Ginny sat watching them, very subdued in Hermione’s usual chair. Harry and Ron kept losing on purpose, trying to finish the games quickly, but even so, it was well past midnight when Fred, George and Ginny finally went to bed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron waited for the distant sounds of two dormitory doors closing before seizing the Cloak, throwing it over themselves, and climbing through the portrait hole.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: It was another difficult journey through the castle, dodging all the teachers. At last they reached the Entrance Hall, slid back the lock on the oak front doors, squeezed between them, trying to stop any creaking, and stepped out into the moonlit grounds.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Course,’ said Ron abruptly, as they strode across the black grass, ‘we might get to the Forest and find there’s nothing to follow. Those spiders might not’ve been going there at all. I know it looked like they were moving in that sort of general direction, but …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: His voice tailed away hopefully.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They reached Hagrid’s house, sad and sorry-looking with its blank windows. When Harry pushed the door open, Fang went mad with joy at the sight of them. Worried he might wake everyone at the castle with his deep, booming barks, they hastily fed him treacle fudge from a tin on the mantelpiece, which glued his teeth together.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry left the Invisibility Cloak on Hagrid’s table. There would be no need for it in the pitch-dark Forest.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘C’mon, Fang, we’re going for a walk,’ said Harry, patting his leg, and Fang bounded happily out of the house behind them, dashed to the edge of the Forest and lifted his leg against a large sycamore tree.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry took out his wand, murmured, ‘Lumos!’ and a tiny light appeared at the end of it, just enough to let them watch the path for signs of spiders.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good thinking,’ said Ron. ‘I’d light mine too, but you know - it’d probably blow up or something …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry tapped Ron on the shoulder, pointing at the grass. Two solitary spiders were hurrying away from the wandlight into the shade of the trees.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘OK,’ Ron sighed, as though resigned to the worst, ‘I’m ready. Let’s go.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: So, with Fang scampering around them, sniffing tree roots and leaves, they entered the Forest. By the glow of Harry’s wand, they followed the steady trickle of spiders moving along the path. They walked for about twenty minutes, not speaking, listening hard for noises other than breaking twigs and rustling leaves. Then, when the trees had become thicker than ever, so that the stars overhead were no longer visible, and Harry’s wand shone alone in the sea of dark, they saw their spider guides leaving the path.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry paused, trying to see where the spiders were going, but everything outside his little sphere of light was pitch black. He had never been this deep into the Forest before. He could vividly remember Hagrid advising him not to leave the Forest path last time he’d been in here. But Hagrid was miles away now, probably sitting in a cell in Azkaban, and he had also said to follow the spiders.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Something wet touched Harry’s hand and he jumped backwards, crushing Ron’s foot, but it was only Fang’s nose.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What d’you reckon?’ Harry said to Ron, whose eyes he could just make out, reflecting the light from his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ve come this far,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: So they followed the darting shadows of the spiders into the trees. They couldn’t move very quickly now; there were tree roots and stumps in their way, barely visible in the near blackness. Harry could feel Fang’s hot breath on his hand. More than once, they had to stop, so that Harry could crouch down and find the spiders in the wandlight.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They walked for what seemed like at least half an hour, their robes snagging on low-slung branches and brambles. After a while, they noticed that the ground seemed to be sloping downwards, though the trees were as thick as ever.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Then Fang suddenly let loose a great, echoing bark, making both Harry and Ron jump out of their skins.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘There’s something moving over there,’ Harry breathed. ‘Listen … Sounds like something big.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh no,’ said Ron. ‘Oh no, oh no, oh -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Shut up,’ said Harry frantically. ‘It’ll hear you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Hear me?’ said Ron in an unnaturally high voice. ‘It’s already heard Fang!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The darkness seemed to be pressing on their eyeballs as they stood, terrified, waiting. There was a strange rumbling noise and then silence.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What d’you think it’s doing?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Probably getting ready to pounce,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They waited, shivering, hardly daring to move.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘D’you think it’s gone?’ Harry whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Dunno -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Then, to their right, came a sudden blaze of light, so bright in the darkness that both of them flung up their hands to shield their eyes. Fang yelped and tried to run, but got lodged in a tangle of thorns and yelped even louder.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry!’ Ron shouted, his voice breaking with relief. ‘Harry, it’s our car!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry blundered after Ron towards the light, stumbling and tripping, and a moment later they had emerged into a clearing.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Weasley’s car was standing, empty, in the middle of a circle of thick trees under a roof of dense branches, its headlamps ablaze. As Ron walked, open-mouthed, towards it, it moved slowly towards him, exactly like a large, turquoise dog greeting its owner.

text_content: ‘It’s been here all the time!’ said Ron delightedly, walking around the car. ‘Look at it. The Forest’s turned it wild …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The wings of the car were scratched and smeared with mud. Apparently it had taken to trundling around the Forest on its own. Fang didn’t seem at all keen on it; he kept close to Harry, who could feel him quivering. His breathing slowing down again, Harry stuffed his wand back into his robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And we thought it was going to attack us!’ said Ron, leaning against the car and patting it. ‘I wondered where it had gone!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry squinted around on the floodlit ground for signs of more spiders, but they had all scuttled away from the glare of the headlights.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ve lost the trail,’ he said. ‘C’mon, let’s go and find them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron didn’t speak. He didn’t move. His eyes were fixed on a point some ten feet above the Forest floor, right behind Harry. His face was livid with terror.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t even have time to turn around. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Head hanging, Harry saw that what had hold of him was marching on six immensely long, hairy legs, the front two clutching him tightly below a pair of shining black pincers. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He never knew how long he was in the creature’s clutches; he only knew that the darkness suddenly lifted enough for him to see that the leaf-strewn ground was now swarming with spiders. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Spiders. Not tiny spiders like those surging over the leaves below. Spiders the size of carthorses, eight-eyed, eight-legged, black, hairy, gigantic. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry fell to the ground on all fours as the spider released him. Ron and Fang thudded down next to him. Fang wasn’t howling any more, but cowering silently on the spot. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry suddenly realised that the spider which had dropped him was saying something. It had been hard to tell, because he clicked his pincers with every word he spoke.

text_content: ‘What is it?’ he said, clicking his pincers rapidly.

text_content: ‘Men,’ clicked the spider who had caught Harry.

text_content: ‘Is it Hagrid?’ said Aragog, moving closer, his eight milky eyes wandering vaguely.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Strangers,’ clicked the spider who had brought Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Click, click, click went the pincers of the spiders all around the hollow.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Aragog paused.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry thought of getting to his feet, but decided against it; he didn’t think his legs would support him. So he spoke from the ground, as calmly as he could.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Aragog clicked his pincers furiously, and all around the hollow the sound was echoed by the crowd of spiders; it was like applause, except applause didn’t usually make Harry feel sick with fear.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But that was years ago,’ said Aragog fretfully. ‘Years and years ago. I remember it well. That’s why they made him leave the school. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And you … you didn’t come from the Chamber of Secrets?’ said Harry, who could feel cold sweat on his forehead.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I!’ said Aragog, clicking angrily. ‘I was not born in the castle. I come from a distant land. A traveller gave me to Hagrid when I was an egg. Hagrid was only a boy, but he cared for me, hidden in a cupboard in the castle, feeding me on scraps from the table. Hagrid is my good friend, and a good man. When I was discovered, and blamed for the death of a girl, he protected me. I have lived here in the Forest ever since, where Hagrid still visits me. He even found me a wife, Mosag, and you see how our family has grown, all through Hagrid’s goodness …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry summoned what remained of his courage.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So you never - never attacked anyone?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Never,’ croaked the old spider. ‘It would have been my instinct, but from respect of Hagrid, I never harmed a human. The body of the girl who was killed was discovered in a bathroom. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But then … Do you know what did kill that girl?’ said Harry. ‘Because whatever it is, it’s back and attacking people again -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: His words were drowned by a loud outbreak of clicking and the rustling of many long legs shifting angrily; large black shapes shifted all around him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The thing that lives in the castle,’ said Aragog, ‘is an ancient creature we spiders fear above all others. Well do I remember how I pleaded with Hagrid to let me go, when I sensed the beast moving about the school.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What is it?’ said Harry urgently.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: More loud clicking, more rustling; the spiders seemed to be closing in.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We do not speak of it!’ said Aragog fiercely. ‘We do not name it! I never even told Hagrid the name of that dread creature, though he asked me, many times.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t want to press the subject, not with the spiders pressing closer on all sides. Aragog seemed to be tired of talking. He was backing slowly into his domed web, but his fellow spiders continued to inch slowly towards Harry and Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ll just go, then,’ Harry called desperately to Aragog, hearing leaves rustling behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘But - but -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘My sons and daughters do not harm Hagrid, on my command. But I cannot deny them fresh meat, when it wanders so willingly into our midst. Goodbye, friend of Hagrid.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry spun around. Feet away, towering above him, was a solid wall of spiders, clicking, their many eyes gleaming in their ugly black heads …

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Even as he reached for his wand, Harry knew it was no good, there were too many of them, but as he tried to stand, ready to die fighting, a loud, long note sounded, and a blaze of light flamed through the hollow.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Weasley’s car was thundering down the slope, headlamps glaring, its horn screeching, knocking spiders aside; several were thrown onto their backs, their endless legs waving in the air. The car screeched to a halt in front of Harry and Ron and the doors flew open.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Get Fang!’ Harry yelled, diving into the front seat; Ron seized the boarhound round the middle and threw him, yelping, into the back of the car. The doors slammed shut. Ron didn’t touch the accelerator but the car didn’t need him; the engine roared and they were off, hitting more spiders. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry looked sideways at Ron. His mouth was still open in the silent scream, but his eyes weren’t popping any more.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you OK?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron stared straight ahead, unable to speak.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They smashed their way through the undergrowth, Fang howling loudly in the back seat, and Harry saw the wing mirror snap off as they squeezed past a large oak. After ten noisy, rocky minutes, the trees thinned, and Harry could again see patches of sky.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The car stopped so suddenly that they were nearly thrown into the windscreen. They had reached the edge of the Forest. Fang flung himself at the window in his anxiety to get out and when Harry opened the door, he shot off through the trees to Hagrid’s house, tail between his legs. Harry got out too, and after a minute or so, Ron seemed to regain the feeling in his limbs and followed, still stiff-necked and staring. Harry gave the car a grateful pat as it reversed back into the Forest and disappeared from view.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry went back into Hagrid’s cabin to get the Invisibility Cloak. Fang was trembling under a blanket in his basket. When Harry got outside again, he found Ron being violently sick in the pumpkin patch.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Follow the spiders,’ said Ron weakly, wiping his mouth on his sleeve. ‘I’ll never forgive Hagrid. We’re lucky to be alive.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I bet he thought Aragog wouldn’t hurt friends of his,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s exactly Hagrid’s problem!’ said Ron, thumping the wall of the cabin. ‘He always thinks monsters aren’t as bad as they’re made out, and look where it’s got him! A cell in Azkaban!’ He was shivering uncontrollably now. ‘What was the point of sending us in there? What have we found out, I’d like to know?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘That Hagrid never opened the Chamber of Secrets,’ said Harry, throwing the cloak over Ron and prodding him in the arm to make him walk. ‘He was innocent.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron gave a loud snort. Evidently, hatching Aragog out in a cupboard wasn’t his idea of being innocent.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: As the castle loomed nearer Harry twitched the Cloak to make sure their feet were hidden, then pushed the creaking front doors ajar. They walked carefully back across the Entrance Hall and up the marble staircase, holding their breath as they passed corridors where watchful sentries were walking. At last they reached the safety of the Gryffindor common room, where the fire had burned itself into glowing ash. They took off the Cloak and climbed the winding staircase to their dormitory.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron fell onto his bed without bothering to get undressed. Harry, however, didn’t feel very sleepy. He sat on the edge of his four-poster, thinking hard about everything Aragog had said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The creature that was lurking somewhere in the castle, he thought, sounded like a sort of monster Voldemort - even other monsters didn’t want to name it. But he and Ron were no closer to finding out what it was, or how it Petrified its victims. Even Hagrid had never known what was in the Chamber of Secrets.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry swung his legs up onto his bed and leaned back against his pillows, watching the moon glinting at him through the tower window.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He couldn’t see what else they could do. They had hit dead ends everywhere. Riddle had caught the wrong person, the heir of Slytherin had got off, and no one could tell whether it was the same person, or a different one, who had opened the Chamber this time. There was nobody else to ask. Harry lay down, still thinking about what Aragog said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He was becoming drowsy when what seemed like their very last hope occurred to him and he suddenly sat bolt upright.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron,’ he hissed through the dark. ‘Ron!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron woke with a yelp like Fang’s, stared wildly around and saw Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron - that girl who died. Aragog said she was found in a bathroom,’ said Harry, ignoring Neville’s snuffling snores from the corner. ‘What if she never left the bathroom? What if she’s still there?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Ron rubbed his eyes, frowning through the moonlight. And then he understood.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You don’t think - not Moaning Myrtle?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

text_content: ‘All those times we were in that bathroom, and she was just three toilets away,’ said Ron bitterly at breakfast next day, ‘and we could’ve asked her, and now …’

text_content: It had been hard enough trying to look for spiders. Escaping their teachers long enough to sneak into a girls’ bathroom, the girls’ bathroom, moreover, right next to the scene of the first attack, was going to be almost impossible.

text_content: ‘The whole point of keeping the school open at this time is for you to receive your education,’ she said sternly. ‘The exams will therefore take place as usual, and I trust you are all revising hard.’

text_content: ‘Professor Dumbledore’s instructions were to keep the school running as normally as possible,’ she said. ‘And that, I need hardly point out, means finding out how much you have learned this year.’

text_content: Harry looked down at the pair of white rabbits he was supposed to be turning into slippers. What had he learned so far this year? He couldn’t seem to think of anything that would be useful in an exam.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore crossed to one of the chairs by the fire.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Sit down, Harry,’ he said, and Harry sat, feeling unaccountably nervous.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘First of all, Harry, I want to thank you,’ said Dumbledore, eyes twinkling again. ‘You must have shown me real loyalty down in the Chamber. Nothing but that could have called Fawkes to you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He stroked the phoenix, which had fluttered down onto his knee. Harry grinned awkwardly as Dumbledore watched him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And so you met Tom Riddle,’ said Dumbledore thoughtfully. ‘I imagine he was most interested in you …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Suddenly, something that was nagging at Harry came tumbling out of his mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor Dumbledore … Riddle said I’m like him. Strange likenesses, he said …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Did he, now?’ said Dumbledore, looking thoughtfully under his thick silver eyebrows at Harry. ‘And what do you think, Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t think I’m like him!’ said Harry, more loudly than he’d intended. ‘I mean, I’m - I’m in Gryffindor, I’m …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But he fell silent, a lurking doubt resurfacing in his mind.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor,’ he started again after a moment, ‘the Sorting Hat told me I’d - I’d have done well in Slytherin. Everyone thought I was Slytherin’s heir for a while … because I can speak Parseltongue …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Voldemort put a bit of himself in me?’ Harry said, thunderstruck.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It certainly seems so.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So I should be in Slytherin,’ Harry said, looking desperately into Dumbledore’s face. ‘The Sorting Hat could see Slytherin’s power in me, and it -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Put you in Gryffindor,’ said Dumbledore calmly. ‘Listen to me, Harry. You happen to have many qualities Salazar Slytherin prized in his hand-picked students. You know why that was. Think.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It only put me in Gryffindor,’ said Harry in a defeated voice, ‘because I asked not to go in Slytherin …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Exactly,’ said Dumbledore, beaming once more. ‘Which makes you very different from Tom Riddle. book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore reached across to Professor McGonagall’s desk, picked up the blood-stained silver sword and handed it to Harry. Dully, Harry turned it over, the rubies blazing in the firelight. And then he saw the name engraved just below the hilt.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Godric Gryffindor.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Only a true Gryffindor could have pulled that out of the Hat, Harry,’ said Dumbledore simply.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What you need, Harry, is some food and sleep. I suggest you go down to the feast, while I write to Azkaban - we need our gamekeeper back. Dear me, we do seem to run through them, don’t we?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry got up and crossed to the door. He had just reached for the handle, however, when the door burst open so violently that it bounced back off the wall.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Good evening, Lucius,’ said Dumbledore pleasantly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Malfoy almost knocked Harry over as he swept into the room. Dobby went scurrying in after him, crouching at the hem of his cloak, a look of abject terror on his face.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So!’ said Lucius Malfoy, his cold eyes fixed on Dumbledore. ‘You’ve come back. The governors suspended you, but you still saw fit to return to Hogwarts.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, you see, Lucius,’ said Dumbledore, smiling serenely, ‘the other eleven governors contacted me today. It was something like being caught in a hailstorm of owls, to tell the truth. Several of them seemed to think that you had threatened to curse their families if they didn’t agree to suspend me in the first place.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Malfoy went even paler than usual, but his eyes were still slits of fury.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘So - have you stopped the attacks yet?’ he sneered. ‘Have you caught the culprit?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We have,’ said Dumbledore, with a smile.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Well?’ said Mr Malfoy sharply. ‘Who is it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘The same person as last time, Lucius,’ said Dumbledore. ‘But this time, Lord Voldemort was acting through somebody else. By means of this diary.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He held up the small black book with the large hole through the centre, watching Mr Malfoy closely. Harry, however, was watching Dobby.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The elf was doing something very odd. His great eyes fixed meaningfully on Harry, he kept pointing at the diary, then at Mr Malfoy, and then hitting himself hard on the head with his fist.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I see …’ said Mr Malfoy slowly to Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘A clever plan,’ said Dumbledore in a level voice, still staring Mr Malfoy straight in the eye. ‘Because if Harry here -‘ Mr Malfoy shot Harry a swift, sharp look, ‘and his friend Ron hadn’t discovered this book, why - Ginny Weasley might have taken all the blame. No one would ever have been able to prove she hadn’t acted of her own free will …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Malfoy said nothing. His face was suddenly mask-like.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘And imagine,’ Dumbledore went on, ‘what might have happened then … The Weasleys are one of our most prominent pure-blood families. Imagine the effect on Arthur Weasley and his Muggle Protection Act, if his own daughter was discovered attacking and killing Muggle-borns. Very fortunate the diary was discovered, and Riddle’s memories wiped from it. Who knows what the consequences might have been otherwise …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Mr Malfoy forced himself to speak.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Very fortunate,’ he said stiffly.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And still, behind his back, Dobby was pointing, first to the diary, then to Lucius Malfoy, then punching himself in the head.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And Harry suddenly understood. He nodded at Dobby, and Dobby backed into a corner, now twisting his ears in punishment.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t you want to know how Ginny got hold of that diary, Mr Malfoy?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Lucius Malfoy rounded on him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘How should I know how the stupid little girl got hold of it?’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Because you gave it to her,’ said Harry. ‘In Flourish and Blotts. You picked up her old Transfiguration book, and slipped the diary inside it, didn’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He saw Mr Malfoy’s white hands clench and unclench.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Prove it,’ he hissed.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, no one will be able to do that,’ said Dumbledore, smiling at Harry. ‘Not now Riddle has vanished from the book. On the other hand, I would advise you, Lucius, not to go giving out any more of Lord Voldemort’s old school things. If any more of them find their way into innocent hands, I think Arthur Weasley, for one, will make sure they are traced back to you …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Lucius Malfoy stood for a moment, and Harry distinctly saw his right hand twitch as though he was longing to reach for his wand. Instead, he turned to his house-elf.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re going, Dobby!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He wrenched open the door, and as the elf came hurrying up to him, he kicked him right through it. They could hear Dobby squealing with pain all the way along the corridor. Harry stood for a moment, thinking hard. Then it came to him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor Dumbledore,’ he said hurriedly, ‘can I give that diary back to Mr Malfoy, please?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He caught up with them at the top of the stairs.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Mr Malfoy,’ he gasped, skidding to a halt, ‘I’ve got something for you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And he forced the smelly sock into Lucius Malfoy’s hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What the -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ll meet the same sticky end as your parents one of these days, Harry Potter,’ he said softly. ‘They were meddlesome fools, too.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: He turned to go.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Master has given Dobby a sock,’ said the elf in wonderment. ‘Master gave it to Dobby.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s that?’ spat Mr Malfoy. ‘What did you say?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby has got a sock,’ said Dobby in disbelief. ‘Master threw it, and Dobby caught it, and Dobby - Dobby is free.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Lucius Malfoy stood frozen, staring at the elf. Then he lunged at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ve lost me my servant, boy!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: But Dobby shouted, ‘You shall not harm Harry Potter!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: There was a loud bang, and Mr Malfoy was thrown backwards. He crashed down the stairs, three at a time, landing in a crumpled heap on the landing below. He got up, his face livid, and pulled out his wand, but Dobby raised a long threatening finger.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘You shall go now,’ he said fiercely, pointing down at Mr Malfoy. ‘You shall not touch Harry Potter. You shall go now.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry Potter freed Dobby!’ said the elf shrilly, gazing up at Harry, moonlight from the nearest window reflected in his orb-like eyes. ‘Harry Potter set Dobby free!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Least I could do, Dobby,’ said Harry, grinning. ‘Just promise never to try and save my life again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The elf’s ugly brown face split suddenly into a wide, toothy smile.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve just got one question, Dobby,’ said Harry, as Dobby pulled on Harry’s sock with shaking hands. ‘You told me all this had nothing to do with He Who Must Not Be Named, remember? Well -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘It was a clue, sir,’ said Dobby, his eyes widening, as though this was obvious. ‘Dobby was giving you a clue. The Dark Lord, before he changed his name, could be freely named, you see?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Harry weakly. ‘Well, I’d better go. There’s a feast, and my friend Hermione should be awake by now …’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Dobby threw his arms around Harry’s middle and hugged him.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry Potter is greater by far than Dobby knew!’ he sobbed. ‘Farewell, Harry Potter!’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: And with a final loud crack, Dobby disappeared.

Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Harry had been to several Hogwarts feasts, but never one quite like this. Everybody was in their pyjamas, and the celebrations lasted all night. Harry didn’t know whether the best bit was Hermione running towards him, screaming, ‘You solved it! You solved it!’ or Justin hurrying over from the Hufflepuff table to wring his hand and apologise endlessly for suspecting him, or Hagrid turning up at half past three, cuffing Harry and Ron so hard on the shoulders that they were knocked into their plates of trifle, or his and Ron’s four hundred points securing Gryffindor the House Cup for the second year running, or Professor McGonagall standing up to tell them all that the exams had been cancelled as a school treat (‘Oh, no!’ said Hermione), or Dumbledore announcing that, unfortunately, Professor Lockhart would be unable to return next year, owing to the fact that he needed to go away and get his memory back. Quite a few of the teachers joined in the cheering that greeted this news.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Shame,’ said Ron, helping himself to a jam doughnut. ‘He was starting to grow on me.’

Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: The rest of the summer term passed in a haze of blazing sunshine. Hogwarts was back to normal, with only a few, small differences: Defence Against the Dark Arts classes were cancelled (‘but we’ve had plenty of practice at that anyway,’ Ron told a disgruntled Hermione) and Lucius Malfoy had been sacked as a school governor. Draco was no longer strutting around the school as though he owned the place. On the contrary, he looked resentful and sulky. On the other hand, Ginny Weasley was perfectly happy again.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Too soon, it was time for the journey home on the Hogwarts Express. Harry, Ron, Hermione, Fred, George and Ginny got a compartment to themselves. They made the most of the last few hours in which they were allowed to do magic before the holidays. They played Exploding Snap, set off the very last of Fred and George’s Filibuster Fireworks, and practised disarming each other by magic. Harry was getting very good at it.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: They were almost at King’s Cross when Harry remembered something.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Ginny - what did you see Percy doing, that he didn’t want you to tell anyone?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, that,’ said Ginny, giggling. ‘Well - Percy’s got a girlfriend.’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: Fred dropped a stack of books on George’s head.

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’

book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (UK)
