text_content: ‘Enough, enough!’ said Fudge, with a very supercilious look on his face. ‘I’m sorry to interrupt what I’m sure would have been a very well-rehearsed story -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore cleared his throat. The Wizengamot fell silent again.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We do, in fact, have a witness to the presence of Dementors in that alleyway,’ he said, ‘other than Dudley Dursley, I mean.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Fudge’s plump face seemed to slacken, as though somebody had let air out of it. He stared down at Dumbledore for a moment or two, then, with the appearance of a man pulling himself back together, said, ‘We haven’t got time to listen to more tarradiddles, I’m afraid, Dumbledore. I want this dealt with quickly -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I may be wrong,’ said Dumbledore pleasantly, ‘but I am sure that under the Wizengamot Charter of Rights, the accused has the right to present witnesses for his or her case? Isn’t that the policy of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement, Madam Bones?’ he continued, addressing the witch in the monocle.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘True,’ said Madam Bones. ‘Perfectly true.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, very well, very well,’ snapped Fudge. ‘Where is this person?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I brought her with me,’ said Dumbledore. ‘She’s just outside the door. Should I -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No - Weasley, you go,’ Fudge barked at Percy, who got up at once, ran down the stone steps from the judge’s balcony and hurried past Dumbledore and Harry without glancing at them.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A moment later, Percy returned, followed by Mrs Figg. She looked scared and more batty than ever. Harry wished she had thought to change out of her carpet slippers.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore stood up and gave Mrs Figg his chair, conjuring a second one for himself.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Full name?’ said Fudge loudly, when Mrs Figg had perched herself nervously on the very edge of her seat.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Arabella Doreen Figg,’ said Mrs Figg in her quavery voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And who exactly are you?’ said Fudge, in a bored and lofty voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m a resident of Little Whinging, close to where Harry Potter lives,’ said Mrs Figg.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We have no record of any witch or wizard living in Little Whinging, other than Harry Potter,’ said Madam Bones at once. ‘That situation has always been closely monitored, given … given past events.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m a Squib,’ said Mrs Figg. ‘So you wouldn’t have me registered, would you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘A Squib, eh?’ said Fudge, eyeing her suspiciously. ‘We’ll be checking that. You’ll leave details of your parentage with my assistant Weasley. Incidentally, can Squibs see Dementors?’ he added, looking left and right along the bench.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, we can!’ said Mrs Figg indignantly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Fudge looked back down at her, his eyebrows raised. ‘Very well,’ he said aloofly. ‘What is your story?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I had gone out to buy cat food from the corner shop at the end of Wisteria Walk, around about nine o’clock, on the evening of the second of August,’ gabbled Mrs Figg at once, as though she had learned what she was saying by heart, ‘when I heard a disturbance down the alleyway between Magnolia Crescent and Wisteria Walk. On approaching the mouth of the alleyway I saw Dementors running -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Running?’ said Madam Bones sharply. ‘Dementors don’t run, they glide.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s what I meant to say,’ said Mrs Figg quickly, patches of pink appearing in her withered cheeks. ‘Gliding along the alley towards what looked like two boys.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What did they look like?’ said Madam Bones, narrowing her eyes so that the edge of the monocle disappeared into her flesh.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, one was very large and the other one rather skinny -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No, no,’ said Madam Bones impatiently. ‘The Dementors … describe them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ said Mrs Figg, the pink flush creeping up her neck now. ‘They were big. Big and wearing cloaks.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry felt a horrible sinking in the pit of his stomach. Whatever Mrs Figg might say, it sounded to him as though the most she had ever seen was a picture of a Dementor, and a picture could never convey the truth of what these beings were like: the eerie way they moved, hovering inches over the ground; or the rotting smell of them; or that terrible rattling noise they made as they sucked on the surrounding air …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: In the second row, a dumpy wizard with a large black moustache leaned close to whisper in the ear of his neighbour, a frizzy-haired witch. She smirked and nodded.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Big and wearing cloaks,’ repeated Madam Bones coolly, while Fudge snorted derisively. ‘I see. Anything else?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Mrs Figg. ‘I felt them. Everything went cold, and this was a very warm summer’s night, mark you. And I felt … as though all happiness had gone from the world … and I remembered … dreadful things …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Her voice shook and died.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Madam Bones’s eyes widened slightly. Harry could see red marks under her eyebrow where the monocle had dug into it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What did the Dementors do?’ she asked, and Harry felt a rush of hope.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘They went for the boys,’ said Mrs Figg, her voice stronger and more confident now, the pink flush ebbing away from her face. ‘One of them had fallen. The other was backing away, trying to repel the Dementor. That was Harry. He tried twice and produced only silver vapour. On the third attempt, he produced a Patronus, which charged down the first Dementor and then, with his encouragement, chased the second one away from his cousin. And that … that is what happened,’ Mrs Figg finished, somewhat lamely.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Madam Bones looked down at Mrs Figg in silence. Fudge was not looking at her at all, but fidgeting with his papers. Finally, he raised his eyes and said, rather aggressively, ‘That’s what you saw, is it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That is what happened,’ Mrs Figg repeated.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Very well,’ said Fudge. ‘You may go.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Mrs Figg cast a frightened look from Fudge to Dumbledore, then got up and shuffled off towards the door. Harry heard it thud shut behind her.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Not a very convincing witness,’ said Fudge loftily.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I don’t know,’ said Madam Bones, in her booming voice. ‘She certainly described the effects of a Dementor attack very accurately. And I can’t imagine why she would say they were there if they weren’t.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But Dementors wandering into a Muggle suburb and just happening to come across a wizard?’ snorted Fudge. ‘The odds on that must be very, very long. Even Bagman wouldn’t have bet -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I don’t think any of us believe the Dementors were there by coincidence,’ said Dumbledore lightly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The witch sitting to the right of Fudge, with her face in shadow, moved slightly but everyone else was quite still and silent.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And what is that supposed to mean?’ Fudge asked icily.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It means that I think they were ordered there,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I think we might have a record of it if someone had ordered a pair of Dementors to go strolling through Little Whinging!’ barked Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Not if the Dementors are taking orders from someone other than the Ministry of Magic these days,’ said Dumbledore calmly. ‘I have already given you my views on this matter, Cornelius.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, you have,’ said Fudge forcefully, ‘and I have no reason to believe that your views are anything other than bilge, Dumbledore. The Dementors remain in place in Azkaban and are doing everything we ask them to.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Then,’ said Dumbledore, quietly but clearly, ‘we must ask ourselves why somebody within the Ministry ordered a pair of Dementors into that alleyway on the second of August.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: In the complete silence that greeted these words, the witch to the right of Fudge leaned forwards so that Harry saw her for the first time.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He thought she looked just like a large, pale toad. She was rather squat with a broad, flabby face, as little neck as Uncle Vernon and a very wide, slack mouth. Her eyes were large, round and slightly bulging. Even the little black velvet bow perched on top of her short curly hair put him in mind of a large fly she was about to catch on a long sticky tongue.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘The Chair recognises Dolores Jane Umbridge, Senior Undersecretary to the Minister,’ said Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The witch spoke in a fluttery, girlish, high-pitched voice that took Harry aback; he had been expecting a croak.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m sure I must have misunderstood you, Professor Dumbledore,’ she said, with a simper that left her big, round eyes as cold as ever. ‘So silly of me. But it sounded for a teensy moment as though you were suggesting that the Ministry of Magic had ordered an attack on this boy!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She gave a silvery laugh that made the hairs on the back of Harry’s neck stand up. A few other members of the Wizengamot laughed with her. It could not have been plainer that not one of them was really amused.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘If it is true that the Dementors are taking orders only from the Ministry of Magic, and it is also true that two Dementors attacked Harry and his cousin a week ago, then it follows logically that somebody at the Ministry might have ordered the attacks,’ said Dumbledore politely. ‘Of course, these particular Dementors may have been outside Ministry control -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘There are no Dementors outside Ministry control!’ snapped Fudge, who had turned brick red.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore inclined his head in a little bow.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Then undoubtedly the Ministry will be making a full inquiry into why two Dementors were so very far from Azkaban and why they attacked without authorisation.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It is not for you to decide what the Ministry of Magic does or does not do, Dumbledore!’ snapped Fudge, now a shade of magenta of which Uncle Vernon would have been proud.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course it isn’t,’ said Dumbledore mildly. ‘I was merely expressing my confidence that this matter will not go uninvestigated.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He glanced at Madam Bones, who readjusted her monocle and stared back at him, frowning slightly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I would remind everybody that the behaviour of these Dementors, if indeed they are not figments of this boy’s imagination, is not the subject of this hearing!’ said Fudge. ‘We are here to examine Harry Potter’s offences under the Decree for the Reasonable Restriction of Underage Sorcery!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course we are,’ said Dumbledore, ‘but the presence of Dementors in that alleyway is highly relevant. Clause Seven of the Decree states that magic may be used before Muggles in exceptional circumstances, and as those exceptional circumstances include situations which threaten the life of the wizard or witch him- or herself, or any witches, wizards or Muggles present at the time of the -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We are familiar with Clause Seven, thank you very much!’ snarled Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course you are,’ said Dumbledore courteously. ‘Then we are in agreement that Harry’s use of the Patronus Charm in these circumstances falls precisely into the category of exceptional circumstances the clause describes?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘If there were Dementors, which I doubt.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You have heard it from an eyewitness,’ Dumbledore interrupted. ‘If you still doubt her truthfulness, call her back, question her again. I am sure she would not object.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - that - not -‘ blustered Fudge, fiddling with the papers before him. ‘It’s - I want this over with today, Dumbledore!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But naturally, you would not care how many times you heard from a witness, if the alternative was a serious miscarriage of justice,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Serious miscarriage, my hat!’ said Fudge at the top of his voice. ‘Have you ever bothered to tot up the number of cock-and-bull stories this boy has come out with, Dumbledore, while trying to cover up his flagrant misuse of magic out of school? I suppose you’ve forgotten the Hover Charm he used three years ago -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That wasn’t me, it was a house-elf!’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘YOU SEE?’ roared Fudge, gesturing flamboyantly in Harry’s direction. ‘A house-elf! In a Muggle house! I ask you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘The house-elf in question is currently in the employ of Hogwarts School,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I can summon him here in an instant to give evidence if you wish.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - not - I haven’t got time to listen to house-elves! Anyway, that’s not the only - he blew up his aunt, for God’s sake!’ Fudge shouted, banging his fist on the judge’s bench and upsetting a bottle of ink.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And you very kindly did not press charges on that occasion, accepting, I presume, that even the best wizards cannot always control their emotions,’ said Dumbledore calmly, as Fudge attempted to scrub the ink off his notes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And I haven’t even started on what he gets up to at school.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But, as the Ministry has no authority to punish Hogwarts students for misdemeanours at school, Harry’s behaviour there is not relevant to this hearing,’ said Dumbledore, as politely as ever, but now with a suggestion of coolness behind his words.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oho!’ said Fudge. ‘Not our business what he does at school, eh? You think so?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘The Ministry does not have the power to expel Hogwarts students, Cornelius, as I reminded you on the night of the second of August,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Nor does it have the right to confiscate wands until charges have been successfully proven; again, as I reminded you on the night of the second of August. In your admirable haste to ensure that the law is upheld, you appear, inadvertently I am sure, to have overlooked a few laws yourself.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Laws can be changed,’ said Fudge savagely.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course they can,’ said Dumbledore, inclining his head. ‘And you certainly seem to be making many changes, Cornelius. Why, in the few short weeks since I was asked to leave the Wizengamot, it has already become the practice to hold a full criminal trial to deal with a simple matter of underage magic!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A few of the wizards above them shifted uncomfortably in their seats. Fudge turned a slightly deeper shade of puce. The toadlike witch on his right, however, merely gazed at Dumbledore, her face quite expressionless.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘As far as I am aware,’ Dumbledore continued, ‘there is no law yet in place that says this court’s job is to punish Harry for every bit of magic he has ever performed. He has been charged with a specific offence and he has presented his defence. All he and I can do now is to await your verdict.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore put his fingertips together again and said no more. Fudge glared at him, evidently incensed. Harry glanced sideways at Dumbledore, seeking reassurance; he was not at all sure that Dumbledore was right in telling the Wizengamot, in effect, that it was about time they made a decision. Again, however, Dumbledore seemed oblivious to Harry’s attempt to catch his eye. He continued to look up at the benches where the entire Wizengamot had fallen into urgent, whispered conversations.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked at his feet. His heart, which seemed to have swollen to an unnatural size, was thumping loudly under his ribs. He had expected the hearing to last longer than this. He was not at all sure that he had made a good impression. He had not really said very much. He ought to have explained more fully about the Dementors, about how he had fallen over, about how both he and Dudley had nearly been kissed …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Twice he looked up at Fudge and opened his mouth to speak, but his swollen heart was now constricting his air passages and both times he merely took a deep breath and looked back down at his shoes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Then the whispering stopped. Harry wanted to look up at the judges, but found that it was really much, much easier to keep examining his laces.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Those in favour of clearing the accused of all charges?’ said Madam Bones’s booming voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry’s head jerked upwards. There were hands in the air, many of them … more than half! Breathing very fast, he tried to count, but before he could finish, Madam Bones had said, ‘And those in favour of conviction?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Fudge raised his hand; so did half a dozen others, including the witch on his right and the heavily-moustached wizard and the frizzy-haired witch in the second row.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Fudge glanced around at them all, looking as though there was something large stuck in his throat, then lowered his own hand. He took two deep breaths and said, in a voice distorted by suppressed rage, ‘Very well, very well … cleared of all charges.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Excellent,’ said Dumbledore briskly, springing to his feet, pulling out his wand and causing the two chintz armchairs to vanish. ‘Well, I must be getting along. Good-day to you all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: And without looking once at Harry, he swept from the dungeon.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Dumbledore’s abrupt departure took Harry completely by surprise. He remained sitting where he was in the chained chair, struggling with his feelings of shock and relief. The Wizengamot were all getting to their feet, talking, gathering up their papers and packing them away. Harry stood up. Nobody seemed to be paying him the slightest bit of attention, except the toadlike witch on Fudge’s right, who was now gazing down at him instead of at Dumbledore. Ignoring her, he tried to catch Fudge’s eye, or Madam Bones’s, wanting to ask whether he was free to go, but Fudge seemed quite determined not to notice Harry, and Madam Bones was busy with her briefcase, so he took a few tentative steps towards the exit and, when nobody called him back, broke into a very fast walk.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: He took the last few steps at a run, wrenched open the door and almost collided with Mr Weasley, who was standing right outside, looking pale and apprehensive.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Dumbledore didn’t say -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Cleared,’ Harry said, pulling the door closed behind him, ‘of all charges!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Beaming, Mr Weasley seized Harry by the shoulders.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Harry, that’s wonderful! Well, of course, they couldn’t have found you guilty, not on the evidence, but even so, I can’t pretend I wasn’t -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: But Mr Weasley broke off, because the courtroom door had just opened again. The Wizengamot were filing out.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Merlin’s beard!’ exclaimed Mr Weasley wonderingly, pulling Harry aside to let them all pass. ‘You were tried by the full court?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘I think so,’ said Harry quietly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: One or two of the wizards nodded to Harry as they passed and a few, including Madam Bones, said, ‘Morning, Arthur,’ to Mr Weasley, but most averted their eyes. Cornelius Fudge and the toadlike witch were almost the last to leave the dungeon. Fudge acted as though Mr Weasley and Harry were part of the wall, but again, the witch looked almost appraisingly at Harry as she passed. Last of all to pass was Percy. Like Fudge, he completely ignored his father and Harry; he marched past clutching a large roll of parchment and a handful of spare quills, his back rigid and his nose in the air. The lines around Mr Weasley’s mouth tightened slightly, but other than this he gave no sign that he had seen his third son.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘I’m going to take you straight back so you can tell the others the good news,’ he said, beckoning Harry forwards as Percy’s heels disappeared up the steps to Level Nine. ‘I’ll drop you off on the way to that toilet in Bethnal Green. Come on …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘So, what will you have to do about the toilet?’ Harry asked, grinning. Everything suddenly seemed five times funnier than usual. It was starting to sink in: he was cleared, he was going back to Hogwarts.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Oh, it’s a simple enough anti-jinx,’ said Mr Weasley as they mounted the stairs, ‘but it’s not so much having to repair the damage, it’s more the attitude behind the vandalism, Harry. Muggle-baiting might strike some wizards as funny, but it’s an expression of something much deeper and nastier, and I for one -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Mr Weasley broke off in mid-sentence. They had just reached the ninth-level corridor and Cornelius Fudge was standing a few feet away from them, talking quietly to a tall man with sleek blond hair and a pointed, pale face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: The second man turned at the sound of their footsteps. He, too, broke off in mid-conversation, his cold grey eyes narrowed and fixed upon Harry’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Well, well, well … Patronus Potter,’ said Lucius Malfoy coolly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Harry felt winded, as though he had just walked into something solid. He had last seen those cold grey eyes through slits in a Death Eater’s hood, and last heard that man’s voice jeering in a dark graveyard while Lord Voldemort tortured him. Harry could not believe that Lucius Malfoy dared look him in the face; he could not believe that he was here, in the Ministry of Magic, or that Cornelius Fudge was talking to him, when Harry had told Fudge mere weeks ago that Malfoy was a Death Eater.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘The Minister was just telling me about your lucky escape, Potter,’ drawled Mr Malfoy. ‘Quite astonishing, the way you continue to wriggle out of very tight holes … snakelike, in fact.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Mr Weasley gripped Harry’s shoulder in warning.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Harry, ‘yeah, I’m good at escaping.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: Lucius Malfoy raised his eyes to Mr Weasley’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘And Arthur Weasley too! What are you doing here, Arthur?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘I work here,’ said Mr Weasley curtly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘Not here, surely?’ said Mr Malfoy, raising his eyebrows and glancing towards the door over Mr Weasley’s shoulder. ‘I thought you were up on the second floor … don’t you do something that involves sneaking Muggle artefacts home and bewitching them?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘No,’ Mr Weasley snapped, his fingers now biting into Harry’s shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Nine - The Woes of Mrs Weasley
text_content: ‘What are you doing here, anyway?’ Harry asked Lucius Malfoy.

text_content: ‘I know you’re not,’ said Harry and he grinned. But as Hermione and Ron dragged their trunks, Crookshanks and a caged Pigwidgeon off towards the engine end of the train, Harry felt an odd sense of loss. He had never travelled on the Hogwarts Express without Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on,’ Ginny told him, ‘if we get a move on we’ll be able to save them places.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Harry, picking up Hedwig’s cage in one hand and the handle of his trunk in the other. They struggled off down the corridor, peering through the glass-panelled doors into the compartments they passed, which were already full. Harry could not help noticing that a lot of people stared back at him with great interest and that several of them nudged their neighbours and pointed him out. After he had met this behaviour in five consecutive carriages he remembered that the Daily Prophet had been telling its readers all summer what a lying show-off he was. He wondered bleakly whether the people now staring and whispering believed the stories.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: In the very last carriage they met Neville Longbottom, Harry’s fellow fifth-year Gryffindor, his round face shining with the effort of pulling his trunk along and maintaining a one-handed grip on his struggling toad, Trevor.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hi, Harry,’ he panted. ‘Hi, Ginny … everywhere’s full … I can’t find a seat …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What are you talking about?’ said Ginny, who had squeezed past Neville to peer into the compartment behind him. ‘There’s room in this one, there’s only Loony Lovegood in here -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville mumbled something about not wanting to disturb anyone.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t be silly,’ said Ginny, laughing, ‘she’s all right.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She slid the door open and pulled her trunk inside. Harry and Neville followed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hi, Luna,’ said Ginny, ‘is it OK if we take these seats?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The girl beside the window looked up. She had straggly, waist-length, dirty blonde hair, very pale eyebrows and protuberant eyes that gave her a permanently surprised look. Harry knew at once why Neville had chosen to pass this compartment by. The girl gave off an aura of distinct dottiness. Perhaps it was the fact that she had stuck her wand behind her left ear for safekeeping, or that she had chosen to wear a necklace of Butterbeer corks, or that she was reading a magazine upside-down. Her eyes ranged over Neville and came to rest on Harry. She nodded.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Thanks,’ said Ginny, smiling at her.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry and Neville stowed the three trunks and Hedwig’s cage in the luggage rack and sat down. Luna watched them over her upside-down magazine, which was called The Quibbler. She did not seem to need to blink as much as normal humans. She stared and stared at Harry, who had taken the seat opposite her and now wished he hadn’t.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Had a good summer, Luna?’ Ginny asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Luna dreamily, without taking her eyes off Harry. ‘Yes, it was quite enjoyable, you know. You’re Harry Potter,’ she added.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I know I am,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville chuckled. Luna turned her pale eyes on him instead.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And I don’t know who you are.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m nobody,’ said Neville hurriedly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No you’re not,’ said Ginny sharply. ‘Neville Longbottom - Luna Lovegood. Luna’s in my year, but in Ravenclaw.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wit beyond measure is man’s greatest treasure,’ said Luna in a singsong voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She raised her upside-down magazine high enough to hide her face and fell silent. Harry and Neville looked at each other with their eyebrows raised. Ginny suppressed a giggle.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The train rattled onwards, speeding them out into open country. It was an odd, unsettled sort of day; one moment the carriage was full of sunlight and the next they were passing beneath ominously grey clouds.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Guess what I got for my birthday?’ said Neville.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Another Remembrall?’ said Harry, remembering the marble-like device Neville’s grandmother had sent him in an effort to improve his abysmal memory.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Neville. ‘I could do with one, though, I lost the old one ages ago … no, look at this …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He dug the hand that was not keeping a firm grip on Trevor into his schoolbag and after a little bit of rummaging pulled out what appeared to be a small grey cactus in a pot, except that it was covered with what looked like boils rather than spines.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Mimbulus mimbletonia,’ he said proudly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry stared at the thing. It was pulsating slightly, giving it the rather sinister look of some diseased internal organ.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s really, really rare,’ said Neville, beaming. ‘I don’t know if there’s one in the greenhouse at Hogwarts, even. I can’t wait to show it to Professor Sprout. My Great Uncle Algie got it for me in Assyria. I’m going to see if I can breed from it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry knew that Neville’s favourite subject was Herbology but for the life of him he could not see what he would want with this stunted little plant.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Does it - er - do anything?’ he asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Loads of stuff!’ said Neville proudly. ‘It’s got an amazing defensive mechanism. Here, hold Trevor for me …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He dumped the toad into Harry’s lap and took a quill from his schoolbag. Luna Lovegood’s popping eyes appeared over the top of her upside-down magazine again, to watch what Neville was doing. Neville held the Mimbulus mimbletonia up to his eyes, his tongue between his teeth, chose his spot, and gave the plant a sharp prod with the tip of his quill.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Liquid squirted from every boil on the plant; thick, stinking, dark green jets of it. They hit the ceiling, the windows, and spattered Luna Lovegood’s magazine; Ginny, who had flung her arms up in front of her face just in time, merely looked as though she was wearing a slimy green hat, but Harry, whose hands had been busy preventing Trevor’s escape, received a faceful. It smelled like rancid manure.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville, whose face and torso were also drenched, shook his head to get the worst out of his eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘S - sorry,’ he gasped. ‘I haven’t tried that before … didn’t realise it would be quite so … don’t worry, though, Stinksap’s not poisonous,’ he added nervously, as Harry spat a mouthful on to the floor.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: At that precise moment the door of their compartment slid open.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh … hello, Harry,’ said a nervous voice. ‘Um … bad time?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry wiped the lenses of his glasses with his Trevor-free hand. A very pretty girl with long, shiny black hair was standing in the doorway smiling at him: Cho Chang, the Seeker on the Ravenclaw Quidditch team.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh … hi,’ said Harry blankly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Um …’ said Cho. ‘Well … just thought I’d say hello … bye then.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Rather pink in the face, she closed the door and departed. Harry slumped back in his seat and groaned. He would have liked Cho to discover him sitting with a group of very cool people laughing their heads off at a joke he had just told; he would not have chosen to be sitting with Neville and Loony Lovegood, clutching a toad and dripping in Stinksap.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Never mind,’ said Ginny bracingly. ‘Look, we can easily get rid of all this.’ She pulled out her wand. ‘Scourgify!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Stinksap vanished.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Sorry,’ said Neville again, in a small voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Ron and Hermione did not turn up for nearly an hour, by which time the food trolley had already gone by. Harry, Ginny and Neville had finished their pumpkin pasties and were busy swapping Chocolate Frog Cards when the compartment door slid open and they walked in, accompanied by Crookshanks and a shrilly hooting Pigwidgeon in his cage.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m starving,’ said Ron, stowing Pigwidgeon next to Hedwig, grabbing a Chocolate Frog from Harry and throwing himself into the seat next to him. He ripped open the wrapper, bit off the Frog’s head and leaned back with his eyes closed as though he had had a very exhausting morning.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, there are two fifth-year prefects from each house,’ said Hermione, looking thoroughly disgruntled as she took her seat. ‘Boy and girl from each.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And guess who’s a Slytherin prefect?’ said Ron, still with his eyes closed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Malfoy,’ replied Harry at once, certain his worst fear would be confirmed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Course,’ said Ron bitterly, stuffing the rest of the Frog into his mouth and taking another.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And that complete cow Pansy Parkinson,’ said Hermione viciously. ‘How she got to be a prefect when she’s thicker than a concussed troll …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Who are Hufflepuff’s?’ Harry asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott,’ said Ron thickly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And Anthony Goldstein and Padma Patil for Ravenclaw,’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You went to the Yule Ball with Padma Patil,’ said a vague voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Everyone turned to look at Luna Lovegood, who was gazing unblinkingly at Ron over the top of The Quibbler. He swallowed his mouthful of Frog.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, I know I did,’ he said, looking mildly surprised.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘She didn’t enjoy it very much,’ Luna informed him. ‘She doesn’t think you treated her very well, because you wouldn’t dance with her. I don’t think I’d have minded,’ she added thoughtfully, ‘I don’t like dancing very much.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She retreated behind The Quibbler again. Ron stared at the cover with his mouth hanging open for a few seconds, then looked around at Ginny for some kind of explanation, but Ginny had stuffed her knuckles in her mouth to stop herself giggling. Ron shook his head, bemused, then checked his watch.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re supposed to patrol the corridors every so often,’ he told Harry and Neville, ‘and we can give out punishments if people are misbehaving. I can’t wait to get Crabbe and Goyle for something …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re not supposed to abuse your position, Ron!’ said Hermione sharply.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, right, because Malfoy won’t abuse it at all,’ said Ron sarcastically.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So you’re going to descend to his level?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No, I’m just going to make sure I get his mates before he gets mine.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘For heaven’s sake, Ron -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ll make Goyle do lines, it’ll kill him, he hates writing,’ said Ron happily. He lowered his voice to Goyle’s low grunt and, screwing up his face in a look of pained concentration, mimed writing in midair. ‘I … must … not … look … like … a … baboon’s … backside.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Everyone laughed, but nobody laughed harder than Luna Lovegood. She let out a scream of mirth that caused Hedwig to wake up and flap her wings indignantly and Crookshanks to leap up into the luggage rack, hissing. Luna laughed so hard her magazine slipped out of her grasp, slid down her legs and on to the floor.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That was funny!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Her prominent eyes swam with tears as she gasped for breath, staring at Ron. Utterly nonplussed, he looked around at the others, who were now laughing at the expression on Ron’s face and at the ludicrously prolonged laughter of Luna Lovegood, who was rocking backwards and forwards, clutching her sides.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you taking the mickey?’ said Ron, frowning at her.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Baboon’s … backside!’ she choked, holding her ribs.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Everyone else was watching Luna laughing, but Harry, glancing at the magazine on the floor, noticed something that made him dive for it. Upside-down it had been hard to tell what the picture on the front was, but Harry now realised it was a fairly bad cartoon of Cornelius Fudge; Harry only recognised him because of the lime-green bowler hat. One of Fudge’s hands was clenched around a bag of gold; the other hand was throttling a goblin. The cartoon was captioned: How Far Will Fudge Go to Gain Gringotts? Beneath this were listed the titles of other articles inside the magazine.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Corruption in the Quidditch League: How the Tornados are Taking Control Secrets of the Ancient Runes Revealed Sirius Black: Villain or Victim?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Can I have a look at this?’ Harry asked Luna eagerly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She nodded, still gazing at Ron, breathless with laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry opened the magazine and scanned the index. Until this moment he had completely forgotten the magazine Kingsley had handed Mr Weasley to give to Sirius, but it must have been this edition of The Quibbler.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He found the page, and turned excitedly to the article.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: This, too, was illustrated by a rather bad cartoon; in fact, Harry would not have known it was supposed to be Sirius if it hadn’t been captioned. Sirius was standing on a pile of human bones with his wand out. The headline on the article said:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: SIRIUS - BLACK AS HE’S PAINTED?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Notorious mass murderer or innocent singing sensation? Harry had to read this first sentence several times before he was convinced that he had not misunderstood it. Since when had Sirius been a singing sensation?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: For fourteen years Sirius Black has been believed guilty of the mass

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: murder of twelve innocent Muggles and one wizard. Black’s audacious

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: escape from Azkaban two years ago has led to the widest manhunt ever

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: conducted by the Ministry of Magic. None of us has ever questioned

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: that he deserves to be recaptured and handed back to the Dementors.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: BUT DOES HE? Startling new evidence has recently come to light that Sirius Black

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: may not have committed the crimes for which he was sent to Azkaban.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: In fact, says Doris Purkiss, of 18 Acanthia Way, Little Norton, Black

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: may not even have been present at the killings.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What people don’t realise is that Sirius Black is a false name,’ says

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Mrs Purkiss. ‘The man people believe to be Sirius Black is actually

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Stubby Boardman, lead singer of popular singing group The

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hobgoblins, who retired from public life after being struck on the ear

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: by a turnip at a concert in Little Norton Church Hall nearly fifteen

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: years ago. I recognised him the moment I saw his picture in the paper.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Now, Stubby couldn’t possibly have committed those crimes, because

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: on the day in question he happened to be enjoying a romantic candlelit

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: dinner with me. I have written to the Minister for Magic and am

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: expecting him to give Stubby, alias Sirius, a full pardon any day now.’ Harry finished reading and stared at the page in disbelief. Perhaps it was a joke, he thought, perhaps the magazine often printed spoof items. He flicked back a few pages and found the piece on Fudge.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Cornelius Fudge, the Minister for Magic, denied that he had any plans

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: to take over the running of the Wizarding Bank, Gringotts, when he

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: was elected Minister for Magic five years ago. Fudge has always

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: insisted that he wants nothing more than to ‘co-operate peacefully’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: with the guardians of our gold.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: BUT DOES HE? Sources close to the Minister have recently disclosed that Fudge’s

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: dearest ambition is to seize control of the goblin gold supplies and that

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: he will not hesitate to use force if need be.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It wouldn’t be the first time, either,’ said a Ministry insider.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Cornelius “Goblin-Crusher” Fudge, that’s what his friends call him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: If you could hear him when he thinks no one’s listening, oh, he’s

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: always talking about the goblins he’s had done in; he’s had them

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: drowned, he’s had them dropped off buildings, he’s had them poisoned,

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: he’s had them cooked in pies …’ Harry did not read any further. Fudge might have many faults but Harry found it extremely hard to imagine him ordering goblins to be cooked in pies. He flicked through the rest of the magazine. Pausing every few pages, he read: an accusation that the Tutshill Tornados were winning the Quidditch League by a combination of blackmail, illegal broom-tampering and torture; an interview with a wizard who claimed to have flown to the moon on a Cleansweep Six and brought back a bag of moon frogs to prove it; and an article on ancient runes which at least explained why Luna had been reading The Quibbler upside-down. According to the magazine, if you turned the runes on their heads they revealed a spell to make your enemy’s ears turn into kumquats. In fact, compared to the rest of the articles in The Quibbler, the suggestion that Sirius might really be the lead singer of The Hobgoblins was quite sensible.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Anything good in there?’ asked Ron as Harry closed the magazine.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course not,’ said Hermione scathingly, before Harry could answer. ‘The Quibbler‘s rubbish, everyone knows that.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Excuse me,’ said Luna; her voice had suddenly lost its dreamy quality. ‘My father’s the editor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - oh,’ said Hermione, looking embarrassed. ‘Well … it’s got some interesting … I mean, it’s quite …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ll have it back, thank you,’ said Luna coldly, and leaning forwards she snatched it out of Harry’s hands. Riffling through it to page fifty-seven, she turned it resolutely upside-down again and disappeared behind it, just as the compartment door opened for the third time.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked around; he had expected this, but that did not make the sight of Draco Malfoy smirking at him from between his cronies Crabbe and Goyle any more enjoyable.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ he said aggressively, before Malfoy could open his mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Manners, Potter, or I’ll have to give you a detention,’ drawled Malfoy, whose sleek blond hair and pointed chin were just like his father’s. ‘You see, I, unlike you, have been made a prefect, which means that I, unlike you, have the power to hand out punishments.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Harry, ‘but you, unlike me, are a git, so get out and leave us alone.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Ron, Hermione, Ginny and Neville laughed. Malfoy’s lip curled.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Tell me, how does it feel being second-best to Weasley, Potter?’ he asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Shut up, Malfoy,’ said Hermione sharply.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I seem to have touched a nerve,’ said Malfoy, smirking. ‘Well, just watch yourself, Potter, because I’ll be dogging your footsteps in case you step out of line.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get out!’ said Hermione, standing up.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Sniggering, Malfoy gave Harry a last malicious look and departed, with Crabbe and Goyle lumbering along in his wake. Hermione slammed the compartment door behind them and turned to look at Harry, who knew at once that she, like him, had registered what Malfoy had said and been just as unnerved by it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Chuck us another Frog,’ said Ron, who had clearly noticed nothing.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry could not talk freely in front of Neville and Luna. He exchanged another nervous look with Hermione, then stared out of the window.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He had thought Sirius coming with him to the station was a bit of a laugh, but suddenly it seemed reckless, if not downright dangerous … Hermione had been right … Sirius should not have come. What if Mr Malfoy had noticed the black dog and told Draco? What if he had deduced that the Weasleys, Lupin, Tonks and Moody knew where Sirius was hiding? Or had Malfoy’s use of the word ‘dogging’ been a coincidence?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The weather remained undecided as they travelled further and further north. Rain spattered the windows in a half-hearted way, then the sun put in a feeble appearance before clouds drifted over it once more. When darkness fell and lamps came on inside the carriages, Luna rolled up The Quibbler, put it carefully away in her bag and took to staring at everyone in the compartment instead.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry was sitting with his forehead pressed against the train window, trying to get a first distant glimpse of Hogwarts, but it was a moonless night and the rain-streaked window was grimy.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We’d better change,’ said Hermione at last. She and Ron pinned their prefect badges carefully to their chests. Harry saw Ron checking his reflection in the black window.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: At last, the train began to slow down and they heard the usual racket up and down it as everybody scrambled to get their luggage and pets assembled, ready to get off. As Ron and Hermione were supposed to supervise all this, they disappeared from the carriage again, leaving Harry and the others to look after Crookshanks and Pigwidgeon.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ll carry that owl, if you like,’ said Luna to Harry, reaching out for Pigwidgeon as Neville stowed Trevor carefully in an inside pocket.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh - er - thanks,’ said Harry, handing her the cage and hoisting Hedwig’s more securely into his arms.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They shuffled out of the compartment feeling the first sting of the night air on their faces as they joined the crowd in the corridor. Slowly, they moved towards the doors. Harry could smell the pine trees that lined the path down to the lake. He stepped down on to the platform and looked around, listening for the familiar call of ‘firs’-years over ‘ere … firs’-years …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But it did not come. Instead, a quite different voice, a brisk female one, was calling out, ‘First-years line up over here, please! All first-years to me!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A lantern came swinging towards Harry and by its light he saw the prominent chin and severe haircut of Professor Grubbly-Plank, the witch who had taken over Hagrid’s Care of Magical Creatures lessons for a while the previous year.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where’s Hagrid?’ he said out loud.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t know,’ said Ginny, ‘but we’d better get out of the way, we’re blocking the door.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yeah …’

If he had had to give them a name, he supposed he would have called them horses, though there was something reptilian about them, too. They were completely fleshless, their black coats clinging to their skeletons, of which every bone was visible. Their heads were dragonish, and their pupil-less eyes white and staring. Wings sprouted from each wither - vast, black leathery wings that looked as though they ought to belong to giant bats. Standing still and quiet in the gloom, the creatures looked eerie and sinister. Harry could not understand why the coaches were being pulled by these horrible horses when they were quite capable of moving along by themselves.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: Whatever his recent bitter feelings had been towards his Headmaster, Harry was somehow soothed to see Dumbledore standing before them all. Between the absence of Hagrid and the presence of those dragonish horses, he had felt that his return to Hogwarts, so long anticipated, was full of unexpected surprises, like jarring notes in a familiar song. But this, at least, was how it was supposed to be: their Headmaster rising to greet them all before the start-of-term feast.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: ‘To our newcomers,’ said Dumbledore in a ringing voice, his arms stretched wide and a beaming smile on his lips, ‘welcome! To our old hands - welcome back! There is a time for speech-making, but this is not it. Tuck in!’

text_content: There was an appreciative laugh and an outbreak of applause as Dumbledore sat down neatly and threw his long beard over his shoulder so as to keep it out of the way of his plate - for food had appeared out of nowhere, so that the five long tables were groaning under joints and pies and dishes of vegetables, bread and sauces and flagons of pumpkin juice.

text_content: ‘Excellent,’ said Ron, with a kind of groan of longing, and he seized the nearest plate of chops and began piling them on to his plate, watched wistfully by Nearly Headless Nick.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: ‘Well, now that we are all digesting another magnificent feast, I beg a few moments of your attention for the usual start-of-term notices,’ said Dumbledore. ‘First-years ought to know that the Forest in the grounds is out-of-bounds to students - and a few of our older students ought to know by now, too.’ (Harry, Ron and Hermione exchanged smirks.)

text_content: ‘Mr Filch, the caretaker, has asked me, for what he tells me is the four-hundred-and-sixty-second time, to remind you all that magic is not permitted in corridors between classes, nor are a number of other things, all of which can be checked on the extensive list now fastened to Mr Filch’s office door.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

Professor Sprout’s eyebrows had disappeared into her flyaway hair and Professor McGonagall’s mouth was as thin as Harry had ever seen it. No new teacher had ever interrupted Dumbledore before. Many of the students were smirking; this woman obviously did not know how things were done at Hogwarts.

text_content: ‘Well, it is lovely to be back at Hogwarts, I must say!’ She smiled, revealing very pointed teeth. ‘And to see such happy little faces looking up at me!’

text_content: Professor Umbridge cleared her throat again (‘hem, hem‘), but when she continued, some of the breathiness had vanished from her voice. She sounded much more businesslike and now her words had a dull learned-by-heart sound to them.

text_content: ‘The Ministry of Magic has always considered the education of young witches and wizards to be of vital importance. The rare gifts with which you were born may come to nothing if not nurtured and honed by careful instruction. The ancient skills unique to the wizarding community must be passed down the generations lest we lose them for ever. The treasure trove of magical knowledge amassed by our ancestors must be guarded, replenished and polished by those who have been called to the noble profession of teaching.’

chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: Professor Umbridge paused here and made a little bow to her fellow staff members, none of whom bowed back to her. Professor McGonagall’s dark eyebrows had contracted so that she looked positively hawklike, and Harry distinctly saw her exchange a significant glance with Professor Sprout as Umbridge gave another little ‘hem, hem’ and went on with her speech.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: ‘Every headmaster and headmistress of Hogwarts has brought something new to the weighty task of governing this historic school, and that is as it should be, for without progress there will be stagnation and decay. There again, progress for progress’s sake must be discouraged, for our tried and tested traditions often require no tinkering. A balance, then, between old and new, between permanence and change, between tradition and innovation …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: Harry found his attentiveness ebbing, as though his brain was slipping in and out of tune. The quiet that always filled the Hall when Dumbledore was speaking was breaking up as students put their heads together, whispering and giggling. Over on the Ravenclaw table Cho Chang was chatting animatedly with her friends. A few seats along from Cho, Luna Lovegood had got out The Quibbler again. Meanwhile, at the Hufflepuff table Ernie Macmillan was one of the few still staring at Professor Umbridge, but he was glassy-eyed and Harry was sure he was only pretending to listen in an attempt to live up to the new prefect’s badge gleaming on his chest.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: Professor Umbridge did not seem to notice the restlessness of her audience. Harry had the impression that a full-scale riot could have broken out under her nose and she would have ploughed on with her speech. The teachers, however, were still listening very attentively, and Hermione seemed to be drinking in every word Umbridge spoke, though, judging by her expression, they were not at all to her taste.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: ‘… because some changes will be for the better, while others will come, in the fullness of time, to be recognised as errors of judgement. Meanwhile, some old habits will be retained, and rightly so, whereas others, outmoded and outworn, must be abandoned. Let us move forward, then, into a new era of openness, effectiveness and accountability, intent on preserving what ought to be preserved, perfecting what needs to be perfected, and pruning wherever we find practices that ought to be prohibited.’

chapter: Chapter Eleven - The Sorting Hat’s New Song
text_content: She sat down. Dumbledore clapped. The staff followed his lead, though Harry noticed that several of them brought their hands together only once or twice before stopping. A few students joined in, but most had been taken unawares by the end of the speech, not having listened to more than a few words of it, and before they could start applauding properly, Dumbledore had stood up again.

text_content: ‘Thank you very much, Professor Umbridge, that was most illuminating,’ he said, bowing to her. ‘Now, as I was saying, Quidditch tryouts will be held …’

text_content: He had been stupid not to expect this, he thought angrily as he walked through the much emptier upstairs corridors.
