text_content: ‘No problem,’ he said. ‘He was the biggest, the ugliest an’ the laziest. Sittin’ there waitin’ ter be brought food by the others. Dead goats an’ such like. Name o’ Karkus. I’d put him at twenty-two, twenty-three feet an’ the weight o’ a couple o’ bull elephants. Skin like rhino hide an’ all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And you just walked up to him?’ said Hermione breathlessly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well … down ter him, where he was lyin’ in the valley. They was in this dip between four pretty high mountains, see, beside a mountain lake, an’ Karkus was lyin’ by the lake roarin’ at the others ter feed him an’ his wife. Olympe an’ I went down the mountainside -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But didn’t they try and kill you when they saw you?’ asked Ron incredulously.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It was def’nitely on some o’ their minds,’ said Hagrid, shrugging, ‘but we did what Dumbledore told us ter do, which was ter hold our gift up high an’ keep our eyes on the Gurg an’ ignore the others. So tha’s what we did. An’ the rest of ‘em went quiet an’ watched us pass an’ we got right up ter Karkus’s feet an’ we bowed an’ put our present down in front o’ him.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What do you give a giant?’ asked Ron eagerly. ‘Food?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Nah, he can get food all righ’ fer himself,’ said Hagrid. ‘We took him magic. Giants like magic, jus’ don’ like us usin’ it against ‘em. Anyway, that firs’ day we gave ‘im a branch o’ Gubraithian fire.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hermione said, ‘Wow!’ softly, but Harry and Ron both frowned in puzzlement.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘A branch of -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Everlasting fire,’ said Hermione irritably, ‘you ought to know that by now. Professor Flitwick’s mentioned it at least twice in class!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, anyway,’ said Hagrid quickly, intervening before Ron could answer back, ‘Dumbledore’d bewitched this branch to burn fer evermore, which isn’ somethin’ any wizard could do, an’ so I lies it down in the snow by Karkus’s feet and says, “A gift to the Gurg of the giants from Albus Dumbledore, who sends his respectful greetings.”’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And what did Karkus say?’ asked Harry eagerly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Nothin’,’ said Hagrid. ‘Didn’ speak English.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re kidding!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Didn’ matter,’ said Hagrid imperturbably, ‘Dumbledore had warned us tha’ migh’ happen. Karkus knew enough to yell fer a couple o’ giants who knew our lingo an’ they translated fer us.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And did he like the present?’ asked Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yeah, it went down a storm once they understood what it was,’ said Hagrid, turning his dragon steak over to press the cooler side to his swollen eye. ‘Very pleased. So then I said, “Albus Dumbledore asks the Gurg to speak with his messenger when he returns tomorrow with another gift.”’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Why couldn’t you speak to them that day?’ asked Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dumbledore wanted us ter take it very slow,’ said Hagrid. ‘Let ‘em see we kept our promises. We’ll come back tomorrow with another present, an’ then we do come back with another present - gives a good impression, see? An’ gives them time ter test out the firs’ present an’ find out it’s a good one, an’ get ‘em eager fer more. In any case, giants like Karkus - overload ‘em with information an’ they’ll kill yeh jus’ to simplify things. So we bowed outta the way an’ went off an’ found ourselves a nice little cave ter spend that night in an’ the followin’ mornin’ we went back an’ this time we found Karkus sittin’ up waitin’ fer us lookin’ all eager.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And you talked to him?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yeah. Firs’ we presented him with a nice battle helmet - goblin-made an’ indestructible, yeh know - an’ then we sat down an’ we talked.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What did he say?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Not much,’ said Hagrid. ‘Listened mostly. Bu’ there were good signs. He’d heard o’ Dumbledore, heard he’d argued against the killin’ o’ the last giants in Britain. Karkus seemed ter be quite int’rested in what Dumbledore had ter say. An’ a few o’ the others, ‘specially the ones who had some English, they gathered round an’ listened too. We were hopeful when we left that day. Promised ter come back next mornin’ with another present.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Bu’ that night it all wen’ wrong.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What d’you mean?’ said Ron quickly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, like I say, they’re not meant ter live together, giants,’ said Hagrid sadly. ‘Not in big groups like that. They can’ help themselves, they half kill each other every few weeks. The men fight each other an’ the women fight each other; the remnants of the old tribes fight each other, an’ that’s even without squabbles over food an’ the best fires an’ sleepin’ spots. Yeh’d think, seein’ as how their whole race is abou’ finished, they’d lay off each other, bu’ …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid sighed deeply.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That night a fight broke out, we saw it from the mouth of our cave, lookin’ down on the valley. Went on fer hours, yeh wouldn’ believe the noise. An’ when the sun came up the snow was scarlet an’ his head was lyin’ at the bottom o’ the lake.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Whose head?’ gasped Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Karkus’s,’ said Hagrid heavily. ‘There was a new Gurg, Golgomath.’ He sighed deeply. ‘Well, we hadn’ bargained on a new Gurg two days after we’d made friendly contact with the firs’ one, an’ we had a funny feelin’ Golgomath wouldn’ be so keen ter listen to us, bu’ we had ter try.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You went to speak to him?’ asked Ron incredulously. ‘After you’d watched him rip off another giant’s head?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Course we did,’ said Hagrid, ‘we hadn’ gone all that way ter give up after two days! We wen’ down with the next present we’d meant ter give ter Karkus.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I knew it was no go before I’d opened me mouth. He was sitting there wearin’ Karkus’s helmet, leerin’ at us as we got nearer. He’s massive, one o’ the biggest ones there. Black hair an’ matchin’ teeth an’ a necklace o’ bones. Human-lookin’ bones, some of ‘em. Well, I gave it a go - held out a great roll o’ dragon skin - an’ said, “A gift fer the Gurg of the giants -” Nex’ thing I knew, I was hangin’ upsidedown in the air by me feet, two of his mates had grabbed me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hermione clapped her hands to her mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How did you get out of that?’ asked Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wouldn’ta done if Olympe hadn’ bin there,’ said Hagrid. ‘She pulled out her wand an’ did some o’ the fastes’ spellwork I’ve ever seen. Ruddy marvellous. Hit the two holdin’ me right in the eyes with Conjunctivitus Curses an’ they dropped me straightaway - bu’ we were in trouble then, ‘cause we’d used magic against ‘em, an’ that’s what giants hate abou’ wizards. We had ter leg it an’ we knew there was no way we was going ter be able ter march inter the camp again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Blimey, Hagrid,’ said Ron quietly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So, how come it’s taken you so long to get home if you were only there for three days?’ asked Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We didn’ leave after three days!’ said Hagrid, looking outraged. ‘Dumbledore was relyin’ on us!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But you’ve just said there was no way you could go back!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Not by daylight we couldn’, no. We just had ter rethink a bit. Spent a couple o’ days lyin’ low up in the cave an’ watchin’. An’ wha’ we saw wasn’ good.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did he rip off more heads?’ asked Hermione, sounding squeamish.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Hagrid, ‘I wish he had.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What d’you mean?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I mean we soon found out he didn’ object ter all wizards - just us.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Death Eaters?’ said Harry quickly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yep,’ said Hagrid darkly. ‘Couple of ‘em were visitin’ him ev’ry day, bringin’ gifts ter the Gurg, an’ he wasn’ dangling them upsidedown.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How d’you know they were Death Eaters?’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Because I recognised one of ‘em,’ Hagrid growled. ‘Macnair, remember him? Bloke they sent ter kill Buckbeak? Maniac, he is. Likes killin’ as much as Golgomath; no wonder they were gettin’ on so well.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So Macnair’s persuaded the giants to join You-Know-Who?’ said Hermione desperately.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hold yer Hippogriffs, I haven’ finished me story yet!’ said Hagrid indignantly, who, considering he had not wanted to tell them anything in the first place, now seemed to be rather enjoying himself. ‘Me an’ Olympe talked it over an’ we agreed, jus’ ‘cause the Gurg looked like favourin’ You-Know-Who didn’ mean all of ‘em would. We had ter try an’ persuade some o’ the others, the ones who hadn’ wanted Golgomath as Gurg.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How could you tell which ones they were?’ asked Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, they were the ones bein’ beaten to a pulp, weren’ they?’ said Hagrid patiently. ‘The ones with any sense were keepin’ outta Golgomath’s way, hidin’ out in caves roun’ the gully jus’ like we were. So we decided we’d go pokin’ round the caves by night an’ see if we couldn’ persuade a few o’ them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You went poking around dark caves looking for giants?’ said Ron, with awed respect in his voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, it wasn’ the giants who worried us most,’ said Hagrid. ‘We were more concerned abou’ the Death Eaters. Dumbledore had told us before we wen’ not ter tangle with ‘em if we could avoid it, an’ the trouble was they knew we was around - ‘spect Golgomath told ‘em abou’ us. At night, when the giants were sleepin’ an’ we wanted ter be creepin’ inter the caves, Macnair an’ the other one were sneakin’ round the mountains lookin’ fer us. I was hard put to stop Olympe jumpin’ out at ‘em,’ said Hagrid, the corners of his mouth lifting his wild beard, ‘she was rarin’ ter attack ‘em … she’s somethin’ when she’s roused, Olympe … fiery, yeh know … ‘spect it’s the French in her …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid gazed misty-eyed into the fire. Harry allowed him thirty seconds of reminiscence before clearing his throat loudly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So, what happened? Did you ever get near any of the other giants?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What? Oh … oh, yeah, we did. Yeah, on the third night after Karkus was killed we crept outta the cave we’d bin hidin’ in an’ headed back down inter the gully, keepin’ our eyes skinned fer the Death Eaters. Got inside a few o’ the caves, no go - then, in abou’ the sixth one, we found three giants hidin’.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Cave must’ve been cramped,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wasn’ room ter swing a Kneazle,’ said Hagrid.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Didn’t they attack you when they saw you?’ asked Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Probably woulda done if they’d bin in any condition,’ said Hagrid, ‘but they was badly hurt, all three o’ them; Golgomath’s lot had beaten ‘em unconscious; they’d woken up an’ crawled inter the nearest shelter they could find. Anyway, one o’ them had a bit of English an’ ‘e translated fer the others, an’ what we had ter say didn’ seem ter go down too badly. So we kep’ goin’ back, visitin’ the wounded … I reckon we had abou’ six or seven o’ them convinced at one poin’.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Six or seven?’ said Ron eagerly. ‘Well that’s not bad - are they going to come over here and start fighting You-Know-Who with us?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But Hermione said, ‘What do you mean “at one point”, Hagrid?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid looked at her sadly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Golgomath’s lot raided the caves. The ones tha’ survived didn’ wan’ no more ter to do with us after that.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So … so there aren’t any giants coming?’ said Ron, looking disappointed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Nope,’ said Hagrid, heaving a deep sigh as he turned over his steak and applied the cooler side to his face, ‘but we did wha’ we meant ter do, we gave ‘em Dumbledore’s message an’ some o’ them heard it an’ I ‘spect some o’ them’ll remember it. Jus’ maybe, them that don’ want ter stay around Golgomath’ll move outta the mountains, an’ there’s gotta be a chance they’ll remember Dumbledore’s friendly to ‘em … could be they’ll come.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snow was filling up the window now. Harry became aware that the knees of his robes were soaked through: Fang was drooling with his head in Harry’s lap.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid?’ said Hermione quietly after a while.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Mmm?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you … was there any sign of … did you hear anything about your … your … mother while you were there?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid’s unobscured eye rested upon her and Hermione looked rather scared.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m sorry … I … forget it -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dead,’ Hagrid grunted. ‘Died years ago. They told me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh … I’m … I’m really sorry,’ said Hermione in a very small voice. Hagrid shrugged his massive shoulders.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No need,’ he said shortly. ‘Can’t remember her much. Wasn’ a great mother.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They were silent again. Hermione glanced nervously at Harry and Ron, plainly wanting them to speak.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But you still haven’t explained how you got in this state, Hagrid,’ Ron said, gesturing towards Hagrid’s bloodstained face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Or why you’re back so late,’ said Harry. ‘Sirius says Madame Maxime got back ages ago -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Who attacked you?’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I haven’ bin attacked!’ said Hagrid emphatically. ‘I -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But the rest of his words were drowned in a sudden outbreak of rapping on the door. Hermione gasped; her mug slipped through her fingers and smashed on the floor; Fang yelped. All four of them stared at the window beside the doorway. The shadow of somebody small and squat rippled across the thin curtain.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s her!’ Ron whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get under here!’ Harry said quickly; seizing the Invisibility Cloak, he whirled it over himself and Hermione while Ron tore around the table and dived under the Cloak as well. Huddled together, they backed away into a corner. Fang was barking madly at the door. Hagrid looked thoroughly confused.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid, hide our mugs!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid seized Harry and Ron’s mugs and shoved them under the cushion in Fang’s basket. Fang was now leaping up at the door; Hagrid pushed him out of the way with his foot and pulled it open.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Professor Umbridge was standing in the doorway wearing her green tweed cloak and a matching hat with earflaps. Lips pursed, she leaned back so as to see Hagrid’s face; she barely reached his navel.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ she said slowly and loudly, as though speaking to somebody deaf. ‘You’re Hagrid, are you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Without waiting for an answer she strolled into the room, her bulging eyes rolling in every direction.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get away,’ she snapped, waving her handbag at Fang, who had bounded up to her and was attempting to lick her face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Er - I don’ want ter be rude,’ said Hagrid, staring at her, ‘but who the ruddy hell are you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘My name is Dolores Umbridge.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Her eyes were sweeping the cabin. Twice they stared directly into the corner where Harry stood, sandwiched between Ron and Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dolores Umbridge?’ Hagrid said, sounding thoroughly confused. ‘I thought you were one o’ them Ministry - don’ you work with Fudge?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I was Senior Undersecretary to the Minister, yes,’ said Umbridge, now pacing around the cabin, taking in every tiny detail within, from the haversack against the wall to the abandoned travelling cloak. ‘I am now the Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Tha’s brave of yeh,’ said Hagrid, ‘there’s not many’d take tha’ job any more.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘- and Hogwarts High Inquisitor,’ said Umbridge, giving no sign that she had heard him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wha’s that?’ said Hagrid, frowning.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Precisely what I was going to ask,’ said Umbridge, pointing at the broken shards of china on the floor that had been Hermione’s mug.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ said Hagrid, with a most unhelpful glance towards the corner where Harry, Ron and Hermione stood hidden, ‘oh, tha’ was … was Fang. He broke a mug. So I had ter use this one instead.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid pointed to the mug from which he had been drinking, one hand still clamped over the dragon steak pressed to his eye. Umbridge stood facing him now, taking in every detail of his appearance instead of the cabin’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I heard voices,’ she said quietly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I was talkin’ ter Fang,’ said Hagrid stoutly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And was he talking back to you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well … in a manner o’ speakin’,’ said Hagrid, looking uncomfortable. ‘I sometimes say Fang’s near enough human -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘There are three sets of footprints in the snow leading from the castle doors to your cabin,’ said Umbridge sleekly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hermione gasped; Harry clapped a hand over her mouth. Luckily, Fang was sniffing loudly around the hem of Professor Umbridge’s robes and she did not appear to have heard.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I on’y jus’ got back,’ said Hagrid, waving an enormous hand at the haversack. ‘Maybe someone came ter call earlier an’ I missed ‘em.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘There are no footsteps leading away from your cabin door.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I … I don’ know why that’d be …’ said Hagrid, tugging nervously at his beard and again glancing towards the corner where Harry, Ron and Hermione stood, as though asking for help. ‘Erm …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Umbridge wheeled round and strode the length of the cabin, looking around carefully. She bent and peered under the bed. She opened Hagrid’s cupboards. She passed within two inches of where Harry, Ron and Hermione stood pressed against the wall; Harry actually pulled in his stomach as she walked by. After looking carefully inside the enormous cauldron Hagrid used for cooking, she wheeled round again and said, ‘What has happened to you? How did you sustain those injuries?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hagrid hastily removed the dragon steak from his face, which in Harry’s opinion was a mistake, because the black and purple bruising all around his eye was now clearly visible, not to mention the large amount of fresh and congealed blood on his face. ‘Oh, I … had a bit of an accident,’ he said lamely.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What sort of accident?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - I tripped.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You tripped,’ she repeated coolly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, tha’s right. Over … over a friend’s broomstick. I don’ fly, meself. Well, look at the size o’ me, I don’ reckon there’s a broomstick that’d hold me. Friend o’ mine breeds Abraxan horses, I dunno if you’ve ever seen ‘em, big beasts, winged, yeh know, I’ve had a bit of a ride on one o’ them an’ it was -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where have you been?’ asked Umbridge, cutting coolly through Hagrid’s babbling.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where’ve I -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Been, yes,’ she said. ‘Term started two months ago. Another teacher has had to cover your classes. None of your colleagues has been able to give me any information as to your whereabouts. You left no address. Where have you been?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was a pause in which Hagrid stared at her with his newly uncovered eye. Harry could almost hear his brain working furiously.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - I’ve been away for me health,’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘For your health,’ said Professor Umbridge. Her eyes travelled over Hagrid’s discoloured and swollen face; dragon blood dripped gently and silently on to his waistcoat. ‘I see.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Hagrid, ‘bit o’ - o’ fresh air, yeh know -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, as gamekeeper fresh air must be so difficult to come by,’ said Umbridge sweetly. The small patch of Hagrid’s face that was not black or purple, flushed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well - change o’ scene, yeh know -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Mountain scenery?’ said Umbridge swiftly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She knows, Harry thought desperately.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Mountains?’ Hagrid repeated, clearly thinking fast. ‘Nope, South o’ France fer me. Bit o’ sun an’ … an’ sea.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Really?’ said Umbridge. ‘You don’t have much of a tan.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah … well … sensitive skin,’ said Hagrid, attempting an ingratiating smile. Harry noticed that two of his teeth had been knocked out. Umbridge looked at him coldly; his smile faltered. Then she hoisted her handbag a little higher into the crook of her arm and said, ‘I shall, of course, be informing the Minister of your late return.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Righ’,’ said Hagrid, nodding.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You ought to know, too, that as High Inquisitor it is my unfortunate but necessary duty to inspect my fellow teachers. So I daresay we shall meet again soon enough.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She turned sharply and marched back to the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re inspectin’ us?’ Hagrid echoed blankly, looking after her.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yes,’ said Umbridge softly, looking back at him with her hand on the door handle. ‘The Ministry is determined to weed out unsatisfactory teachers, Hagrid. Goodnight.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She left, closing the door behind her with a snap. Harry made to pull off the Invisibility Cloak but Hermione seized his wrist.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Not yet,’ she breathed in his ear. ‘She might not be gone yet.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But as he stepped on to the landing he came to an abrupt halt, staring at the small window set into the double doors that marked the start of a corridor signposted SPELL DAMAGE. book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Blimey!’ said Ron, also staring at the man.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Well, hello there!’ he said. ‘I expect you’d like my autograph, would you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Hasn’t changed much, has he?’ Harry muttered to Ginny, who grinned.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Er - how are you, Professor?’ said Ron, sounding slightly guilty. book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘I’m very well indeed, thank you!’ said Lockhart exuberantly, pulling a rather battered peacock-feather quill from his pocket. ‘Now, how many autographs would you like? I can do joined-up writing now, you know!’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Er - we don’t want any at the moment, thanks,’ said Ron, raising his eyebrows at Harry, who asked, ‘Professor, should you be wandering around the corridors? Shouldn’t you be in a ward?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: The smile faded slowly from Lockhart’s face. For a few moments he gazed intently at Harry, then he said, ‘Haven’t we met?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Er … yeah, we have,’ said Harry. ‘You used to teach us at Hogwarts, remember?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Teach?’ repeated Lockhart, looking faintly unsettled. ‘Me? Did I?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: And then the smile reappeared upon his face so suddenly it was rather alarming.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Taught you everything you know, I expect, did I? Well, how about those autographs, then? Shall we say a round dozen, you can give them to all your little friends then and nobody will be left out!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But just then a head poked out of a door at the far end of the corridor and a voice called, ‘Gilderoy, you naughty boy, where have you wandered off to?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: A motherly-looking Healer wearing a tinsel wreath in her hair came bustling up the corridor, smiling warmly at Harry and the others.

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Oh, Gilderoy, you’ve got visitors! How lovely, and on Christmas Day, too! Do you know, he never gets visitors, poor lamb, and I can’t think why, he’s such a sweetie, aren’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘We’re doing autographs!’ Gilderoy told the Healer with another glittering smile. ‘They want loads of them, won’t take no for an answer! I just hope we’ve got enough photographs!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Listen to him,’ said the Healer, taking Lockhart’s arm and beaming fondly at him as though he were a precocious two-year-old. ‘He was rather well known a few years ago; we very much hope that this liking for giving autographs is a sign that his memory might be starting to come back. But,’ she lowered her voice to a whisper, ‘he’s a bit of a danger to himself, bless him … doesn’t know who he is, you see, wanders off and can’t remember how to get back … it is nice of you to have come to see him.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Er,’ said Ron, gesturing uselessly at the floor above, ‘actually, we were just - er -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But the Healer was smiling expectantly at them, and Ron’s feeble mutter of ‘going to have a cup of tea’ trailed away into nothingness. They looked at each other helplessly, then followed Lockhart and his Healer along the corridor.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Let’s not stay long,’ Ron said quietly.

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: The Healer pointed her wand at the door of the Janus Thickey Ward and muttered, ‘Alohomora.’ The door swung open and she led the way inside, keeping a firm grasp on Gilderoy’s arm until she had settled him into an armchair beside his bed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘This is our long-term residents’ ward,’ she informed Harry, Ron, Hermione and Ginny in a low voice. ‘For permanent spell damage, you know. Of course, with intensive remedial potions and charms and a bit of luck, we can produce some improvement. Gilderoy does seem to be getting back some sense of himself; and we’ve seen a real improvement in Mr Bode, he seems to be regaining the power of speech very well, though he isn’t speaking any language we recognise yet. Well, I must finish giving out the Christmas presents, I’ll leave you all to chat.’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Harry looked around. The ward bore unmistakeable signs of being a permanent home to its residents. book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘You can put them in envelopes,’ he said to Ginny, throwing the signed pictures into her lap one by one as he finished them. ‘I am not forgotten, you know, no, I still receive a very great deal of fan mail … Gladys Gudgeon writes weekly … I just wish I knew why …’ He paused, looking faintly puzzled, then beamed again and returned to his signing with renewed vigour. ‘I suspect it is simply my good looks …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: A sallow-skinned, mournful-looking wizard lay in the bed opposite staring at the ceiling; he was mumbling to himself and seemed quite unaware of anything around him. book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Here you are, Agnes,’ said the Healer brightly to the furry-faced woman, handing her a small pile of Christmas presents. ‘See, not forgotten, are you? And your son’s sent an owl to say he’s visiting tonight, so that’s nice, isn’t it?’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Agnes gave several loud barks.

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘And look, Broderick, you’ve been sent a pot plant and a lovely calendar with a different fancy Hippogriff for each month; they’ll brighten things up, won’t they?’ said the Healer, bustling along to the mumbling man, setting a rather ugly plant with long, swaying tentacles on the bedside cabinet and fixing the calendar to the wall with her wand. ‘And - oh, Mrs Longbottom, are you leaving already?’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Harry’s head spun round. chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: With a sudden rush of understanding, Harry realised who the people in the end beds must be. chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Neville jumped and cowered as though a bullet had narrowly missed him.

text_content: ‘Ah, yes,’ said his grandmother, peering at Harry and sticking out a shrivelled, clawlike hand for him to shake. ‘Yes, yes, I know who you are, of course. Neville speaks most highly of you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Er - thanks,’ said Harry, shaking hands. Neville did not look at him, but stared at his own feet, the colour deepening in his face all the while.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘And you two are clearly Weasleys,’ Mrs Longbottom continued, proffering her hand regally to Ron and Ginny in turn. ‘Yes, I know your parents - not well, of course - but fine people, fine people … and you must be Hermione Granger?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Hermione looked rather startled that Mrs Longbottom knew her name, but shook hands all the same.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Yes, Neville’s told me all about you. Helped him out of a few sticky spots, haven’t you? chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘What?’ said Ron, looking amazed. (Harry wanted to stamp on Ron’s foot, but that sort of thing is much harder to bring off unnoticed when you’re wearing jeans rather than robes.) ‘Is that your dad down the end, Neville?’

text_content: ‘What’s this?’ said Mrs Longbottom sharply. ‘Haven’t you told your friends about your parents, Neville?’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Neville took a deep breath, looked up at the ceiling and shook his head. Harry could not remember ever feeling sorrier for anyone, but he could not think of any way of helping Neville out of the situation.

text_content: ‘Well, it’s nothing to be ashamed of!’ said Mrs Longbottom angrily. ‘You should be proud, Neville, proud! They didn’t give their health and their sanity so their only son would be ashamed of them, you know!’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘I’m not ashamed,’ said Neville, very faintly, still looking anywhere but at Harry and the others. Ron was now standing on tiptoe to look over at the inhabitants of the two beds.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: ‘Well, you’ve got a funny way of showing it!’ said Mrs Longbottom. ‘My son and his wife,’ she said, turning haughtily to Harry, Ron, Hermione and Ginny, ‘were tortured into insanity by You-Know-Who’s followers.’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Hermione and Ginny both clapped their hands over their mouths. Ron stopped craning his neck to catch a glimpse of Neville’s parents and looked mortified.

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: Neville’s mother had come edging down the ward in her nightdress. chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Again?’ said Mrs Longbottom, sounding slightly weary. ‘Very well, Alice dear, very well - Neville, take it, whatever it is.’

chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But Neville had already stretched out his hand, into which his mother dropped an empty Drooble’s Best Blowing Gum wrapper.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Very nice, dear,’ said Neville’s grandmother in a falsely cheery voice, patting his mother on the shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But Neville said quietly, ‘Thanks, Mum.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: His mother tottered away, back up the ward, humming to herself. Neville looked around at the others, his expression defiant, as though daring them to laugh, but Harry did not think he’d ever found anything less funny in his life.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Well, we’d better get back,’ sighed Mrs Longbottom, drawing on long green gloves. ‘Very nice to have met you all. Neville, put that wrapper in the bin, she must have given you enough of them to paper your bedroom by now.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: But as they left, Harry was sure he saw Neville slip the sweet wrapper into his pocket.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: The door closed behind them.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘I never knew,’ said Hermione, who looked tearful.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Nor did I,’ said Ron rather hoarsely.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Nor me,’ whispered Ginny.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: They all looked at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Bellatrix Lestrange did that?’ whispered Hermione, horrified. ‘That woman Kreacher’s got a photo of in his den?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: There was a long silence, broken by Lockhart’s angry voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Three - Christmas on the Closed Ward
text_content: ‘Look, I didn’t learn joined-up writing for nothing, you know!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Kreacher, it transpired, had been lurking in the attic. Sirius said he had found him up there, covered in dust, no doubt looking for more relics of the Black family to hide in his cupboard. Though Sirius seemed satisfied with this story, it made Harry uneasy. Kreacher seemed to be in a better mood on his reappearance, his bitter muttering had subsided somewhat and he submitted to orders more docilely than usual, though once or twice Harry caught the house-elf staring at him avidly, but always looking quickly away whenever he saw that Harry had noticed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not mention his vague suspicions to Sirius, whose cheerfulness was evaporating fast now that Christmas was over. As the date of their departure back to Hogwarts drew nearer, he became more and more prone to what Mrs Weasley called ‘fits of the sullens’, in which he would become taciturn and grumpy, often withdrawing to Buckbeak’s room for hours at a time. His gloom seeped through the house, oozing under doorways like some noxious gas, so that all of them became infected by it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry didn’t want to leave Sirius again with only Kreacher for company; in fact, for the first time in his life, he was not looking forward to returning to Hogwarts. Going back to school would mean placing himself once again under the tyranny of Dolores Umbridge, who had no doubt managed to force through another dozen decrees in their absence; there was no Quidditch to look forward to now that he had been banned; there was every likelihood that their burden of homework would increase as the exams drew even nearer; and Dumbledore remained as remote as ever. In fact, if it hadn’t been for the DA, Harry thought he might have begged Sirius to let him leave Hogwarts and remain in Grimmauld Place.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Then, on the very last day of the holidays, something happened that made Harry positively dread his return to school.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, dear,’ said Mrs Weasley, poking her head into his and Ron’s bedroom, where the pair of them were playing wizard chess watched by Hermione, Ginny and Crookshanks, ‘could you come down to the kitchen? Professor Snape would like a word with you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not immediately register what she had said; one of his castles was engaged in a violent tussle with a pawn of Ron’s and he was egging it on enthusiastically.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Squash him - squash him, he’s only a pawn, you idiot. Sorry, Mrs Weasley, what did you say?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

Crookshanks, whom Hermione had been restraining with difficulty for the past quarter of an hour, leapt gleefully on to the board and set the pieces running for cover, squealing at the top of their voices.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Snape?’ said Harry blankly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: A minute or two later, he pushed open the kitchen door to find Sirius and Snape both seated at the long kitchen table, glaring in opposite directions. The silence between them was heavy with mutual dislike. A letter lay open on the table in front of Sirius.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: Snape looked around at him, his face framed between curtains of greasy black hair.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Sit down, Potter.’

text_content: ‘You know,’ said Sirius loudly, leaning back on his rear chair legs and speaking to the ceiling, ‘I think I’d prefer it if you didn’t give orders here, Snape. It’s my house, you see.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I was supposed to see you alone, Potter,’ said Snape, the familiar sneer curling his mouth, ‘but Black -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Why do I have to study Occlu— thing?’ he blurted out.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Why can’t Dumbledore teach Harry?’ asked Sirius aggressively. ‘Why you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

My office. If anybody asks, you are taking remedial Potions. Nobody who has seen you in my classes could deny you need them.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned to leave, his black travelling cloak billowing behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wait a moment,’ said Sirius, sitting up straighter in his chair.

text_content: Snape turned back to face them, sneering.

text_content: ‘I am in rather a hurry, Black. Unlike you, I do not have unlimited leisure time.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)

text_content: ‘How do that man and that room come to be inside your head, Potter?’ said Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It -‘ said Harry, looking everywhere but at Snape, ‘it was - just a dream I had.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘A dream?’ repeated Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was a pause during which Harry stared fixedly at a large dead frog suspended in a jar of purple liquid.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You do know why we are here, don’t you, Potter?’ said Snape, in a low, dangerous voice. ‘You do know why I am giving up my evenings to this tedious job?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Harry stiffly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Remind me why we are here, Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So I can learn Occlumency,’ said Harry, now glaring at a dead eel.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Correct, Potter. And dim though you may be -‘ Harry looked back at Snape, hating him ‘- I would have thought that after over two months of lessons you might have made some progress. How many other dreams about the Dark Lord have you had?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Just that one,’ lied Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Perhaps,’ said Snape, his dark, cold eyes narrowing slightly, ‘perhaps you actually enjoy having these visions and dreams, Potter. Maybe they make you feel special - important?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No, they don’t,’ said Harry, his jaw set and his fingers clenched tightly around the handle of his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That is just as well, Potter,’ said Snape coldly, ‘because you are neither special nor important, and it is not up to you to find out what the Dark Lord is saying to his Death Eaters.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No - that’s your job, isn’t it?’ Harry shot at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He had not meant to say it; it had burst out of him in temper. For a long moment they stared at each other, Harry convinced he had gone too far. But there was a curious, almost satisfied expression on Snape’s face when he answered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, Potter,’ he said, his eyes glinting. ‘That is my job. Now, if you are ready, we will start again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He raised his wand: ‘One - two - three - Legilimens!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A hundred Dementors were swooping towards Harry across the lake in the grounds … he screwed up his face in concentration … they were coming closer … he could see the dark holes beneath their hoods … yet he could also see Snape standing in front of him, his eyes fixed on Harry’s face, muttering under his breath … and somehow, Snape was growing clearer, and the Dementors were growing fainter …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry raised his own wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Protego!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape staggered - his wand flew upwards, away from Harry - and suddenly Harry’s mind was teeming with memories that were not his: a hook-nosed man was shouting at a cowering woman, while a small dark-haired boy cried in a corner … a greasy-haired teenager sat alone in a dark bedroom, pointing his wand at the ceiling, shooting down flies … a girl was laughing as a scrawny boy tried to mount a bucking broomstick -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘ENOUGH!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry felt as though he had been pushed hard in the chest; he staggered several steps backwards, hit some of the shelves covering Snape’s walls and heard something crack. Snape was shaking slightly, and was very white in the face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The back of Harry’s robes was damp. One of the jars behind him had broken when he fell against it; the pickled slimy thing within was swirling in its draining potion.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Reparo,’ hissed Snape, and the jar sealed itself at once. ‘Well, Potter … that was certainly an improvement …’ Panting slightly, Snape straightened the Pensieve in which he had again stored some of his thoughts before starting the lesson, almost as though he was checking they were still there. ‘I don’t remember telling you to use a Shield Charm … but there is no doubt that it was effective …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not speak; he felt that to say anything might be dangerous. He was sure he had just broken into Snape’s memories, that he had just seen scenes from Snape’s childhood. It was unnerving to think that the little boy who had been crying as he watched his parents shouting was actually standing in front of him with such loathing in his eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Let’s try again, shall we?’ said Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry felt a thrill of dread; he was about to pay for what had just happened, he was sure of it. They moved back into position with the desk between them, Harry feeling he was going to find it much harder to empty his mind this time.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘On the count of three, then,’ said Snape, raising his wand once more. ‘One - two -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not have time to gather himself together and attempt to clear his mind before Snape cried, ‘Legilimens!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He was hurtling along the corridor towards the Department of Mysteries, past the blank stone walls, past the torches - the plain black door was growing ever larger; he was moving so fast he was going to collide with it, he was feet from it and again he could see that chink of faint blue light -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The door had flown open! He was through it at last, inside a black-walled, black-floored circular room lit with blue-flamed candles, and there were more doors all around him - he needed to go on - but which door ought he to take -?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘POTTER!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry opened his eyes. He was flat on his back again with no memory of having got there; he was also panting as though he really had run the length of the Department of Mysteries corridor, really had sprinted through the black door and found the circular room.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Explain yourself!’ said Snape, who was standing over him, looking furious.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I … dunno what happened,’ said Harry truthfully, standing up. There was a lump on the back of his head from where he had hit the ground and he felt feverish. ‘I’ve never seen that before. I mean, I told you, I’ve dreamed about the door … but it’s never opened before …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You are not working hard enough!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: For some reason, Snape seemed even angrier than he had done two minutes before, when Harry had seen into his teacher’s memories.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You are lazy and sloppy, Potter, it is small wonder that the Dark Lord -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Can you tell me something, sir?’ said Harry, firing up again. ‘Why do you call Voldemort the Dark Lord? I’ve only ever heard Death Eaters call him that.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape opened his mouth in a snarl - and a woman screamed from somewhere outside the room.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape’s head jerked upwards; he was gazing at the ceiling.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What the -?’ he muttered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry could hear a muffled commotion coming from what he thought might be the Entrance Hall. Snape looked round at him, frowning.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you see anything unusual on your way down here, Potter?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry shook his head. Somewhere above them, the woman screamed again. Snape strode to his office door, his wand still held at the ready, and swept out of sight. Harry hesitated for a moment, then followed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The screams were indeed coming from the Entrance Hall; they grew louder as Harry ran towards the stone steps leading up from the dungeons. When he reached the top he found the Entrance Hall packed; students had come flooding out of the Great Hall, where dinner was still in progress, to see what was going on; others had crammed themselves on to the marble staircase. Harry pushed forwards through a knot of tall Slytherins and saw that the onlookers had formed a great ring, some of them looking shocked, others even frightened. Professor McGonagall was directly opposite Harry on the other side of the Hall; she looked as though what she was watching made her feel faintly sick.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Professor Trelawney was standing in the middle of the Entrance Hall with her wand in one hand and an empty sherry bottle in the other, looking utterly mad. Her hair was sticking up on end, her glasses were lopsided so that one eye was magnified more than the other; her innumerable shawls and scarves were trailing haphazardly from her shoulders, giving the impression that she was falling apart at the seams. Two large trunks lay on the floor beside her, one of them upside-down; it looked very much as though it had been thrown down the stairs after her. Professor Trelawney was staring, apparently terrified, at something Harry could not see but which seemed to be standing at the foot of the stairs.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No!’ she shrieked. ‘NO! This cannot be happening … it cannot … I refuse to accept it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You didn’t realise this was coming?’ said a high girlish voice, sounding callously amused, and Harry, moving slightly to his right, saw that Trelawney’s terrifying vision was nothing other than Professor Umbridge. ‘Incapable though you are of predicting even tomorrow’s weather, you must surely have realised that your pitiful performance during my inspections, and lack of any improvement, would make it inevitable that you would be sacked?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You c - can’t!’ howled Professor Trelawney, tears streaming down her face from behind her enormous lenses, ‘you c - can’t sack me! I’ve b - been here sixteen years! H - Hogwarts is m - my h - home!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It was your home,’ said Professor Umbridge, and Harry was revolted to see the enjoyment stretching her toadlike face as she watched Professor Trelawney sink, sobbing uncontrollably, on to one of her trunks, ‘until an hour ago, when the Minister for Magic countersigned your Order of Dismissal. Now kindly remove yourself from this Hall. You are embarrassing us.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But she stood and watched, with an expression of gloating enjoyment, as Professor Trelawney shuddered and moaned, rocking backwards and forwards on her trunk in paroxysms of grief. Harry heard a muffled sob to his left and looked around. Lavender and Parvati were both crying quietly, their arms round each other. Then he heard footsteps. Professor McGonagall had broken away from the spectators, marched straight up to Professor Trelawney and was patting her firmly on the back while withdrawing a large handkerchief from within her robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘There, there, Sybill … calm down … blow your nose on this … it’s not as bad as you think, now … you are not going to have to leave Hogwarts …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh really, Professor McGonagall?’ said Umbridge in a deadly voice, taking a few steps forward. ‘And your authority for that statement is … ?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That would be mine,’ said a deep voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The oaken front doors had swung open. Students beside them scuttled out of the way as Dumbledore appeared in the entrance. What he had been doing out in the grounds Harry could not imagine, but there was something impressive about the sight of him framed in the doorway against an oddly misty night. Leaving the doors wide open behind him he strode forwards through the circle of onlookers towards Professor Trelawney, tear-stained and trembling, on her trunk, Professor McGonagall alongside her.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yours, Professor Dumbledore?’ said Umbridge, with a singularly unpleasant little laugh. ‘I’m afraid you do not understand the position. I have here -‘ she pulled a parchment scroll from within her robes ‘- an Order of Dismissal signed by myself and the Minister for Magic. Under the terms of Educational Decree Number Twenty-three, the High Inquisitor of Hogwarts has the power to inspect, place upon probation and sack any teacher she - that is to say, I - feel is not performing to the standards required by the Ministry of Magic. I have decided that Professor Trelawney is not up to scratch. I have dismissed her.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: To Harry’s very great surprise, Dumbledore continued to smile. He looked down at Professor Trelawney, who was still sobbing and choking on her trunk, and said, ‘You are quite right, of course, Professor Umbridge. As High Inquisitor you have every right to dismiss my teachers. You do not, however, have the authority to send them away from the castle. I am afraid,’ he went on, with a courteous little bow, ‘that the power to do that still resides with the Headmaster, and it is my wish that Professor Trelawney continue to live at Hogwarts.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: At this, Professor Trelawney gave a wild little laugh in which a hiccough was barely hidden.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No - no, I’ll g - go, Dumbledore! I sh - shall - leave Hogwarts and s - seek my fortune elsewhere -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Dumbledore sharply. ‘It is my wish that you remain, Sybill.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned to Professor McGonagall.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Might I ask you to escort Sybill back upstairs, Professor McGonagall?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course,’ said McGonagall. ‘Up you get, Sybill …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Professor Sprout came hurrying forwards out of the crowd and grabbed Professor Trelawney’s other arm. Together, they guided her past Umbridge and up the marble stairs. Professor Flitwick went scurrying after them, his wand held out before him; he squeaked ‘Locomotor trunks!‘ and Professor Trelawney’s luggage rose into the air and proceeded up the staircase after her, Professor Flitwick bringing up the rear.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Professor Umbridge was standing stock-still, staring at Dumbledore, who continued to smile benignly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And what,’ she said, in a whisper that carried all around the Entrance Hall, ‘are you going to do with her once I appoint a new Divination teacher who needs her lodgings?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, that won’t be a problem,’ said Dumbledore pleasantly. ‘You see, I have already found us a new Divination teacher, and he will prefer lodgings on the ground floor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ve found -?’ said Umbridge shrilly. ‘You’ve found? Might I remind you, Dumbledore, that under Educational Decree Number Twenty-two -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘The Ministry has the right to appoint a suitable candidate if - and only if - the Headmaster is unable to find one,’ said Dumbledore. ‘And I am happy to say that on this occasion I have succeeded. May I introduce you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned to face the open front doors, through which night mist was now drifting. Harry heard hooves. There was a shocked murmur around the Hall and those nearest the doors hastily moved even further backwards, some of them tripping over in their haste to clear a path for the newcomer.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Through the mist came a face Harry had seen once before on a dark, dangerous night in the Forbidden Forest: white-blond hair and astonishingly blue eyes; the head and torso of a man joined to the palomino body of a horse.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘This is Firenze,’ said Dumbledore happily to a thunderstruck Umbridge. ‘I think you’ll find him suitable.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘I’ll bet you wish you hadn’t given up Divination now, don’t you, Hermione?’ asked Parvati, smirking.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: It was breakfast time, two days after the sacking of Professor Trelawney, and Parvati was curling her eyelashes around her wand and examining the effect in the back of her spoon. They were to have their first lesson with Firenze that morning.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Not really,’ said Hermione indifferently, who was reading the Daily Prophet. ‘I’ve never really liked horses.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: She turned a page of the newspaper and scanned its columns.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘He’s not a horse, he’s a centaur!’ said Lavender, sounding shocked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘A gorgeous centaur …‘ sighed Parvati.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Either way, he’s still got four legs,’ said Hermione coolly. ‘Anyway, I thought you two were all upset that Trelawney had gone?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘We are!’ Lavender assured her. ‘We went up to her office to see her; we took her some daffodils - not the honking ones that Sprout’s got, nice ones.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘How is she?’ asked Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Not very good, poor thing,’ said Lavender sympathetically. ‘She was crying and saying she’d rather leave the castle for ever than stay here where Umbridge is, and I don’t blame her, Umbridge was horrible to her, wasn’t she?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘I’ve got a feeling Umbridge has only just started being horrible,’ said Hermione darkly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Impossible,’ said Ron, who was tucking into a large plate of eggs and bacon. ‘She can’t get any worse than she’s been already.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘You mark my words, she’s going to want revenge on Dumbledore for appointing a new teacher without consulting her,’ said Hermione, closing the newspaper. ‘Especially another part-human. You saw the look on her face when she saw Firenze.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: After breakfast Hermione departed for her Arithmancy class as Harry and Ron followed Parvati and Lavender into the Entrance Hall, heading for Divination.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Aren’t we going up to North Tower?’ asked Ron, looking puzzled, as Parvati bypassed the marble staircase.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Parvati looked at him scornfully over her shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘How d’you expect Firenze to climb that ladder? We’re in classroom eleven now, it was on the noticeboard yesterday.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Classroom eleven was on the ground floor along the corridor leading off the Entrance Hall from the opposite side to the Great Hall. Harry knew it was one of those classrooms that were never used regularly, and therefore had the slightly neglected feeling of a cupboard or storeroom. When he entered it right behind Ron, and found himself in the middle of a forest clearing, he was therefore momentarily stunned.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘What the -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: The classroom floor had become springily mossy and trees were growing out of it; their leafy branches fanned across the ceiling and windows, so that the room was full of slanting shafts of soft, dappled, green light. The students who had already arrived were sitting on the earthy floor with their backs resting against tree trunks or boulders, arms wrapped around their knees or folded tightly across their chests, and all looking rather nervous. In the middle of the clearing, where there were no trees, stood Firenze.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Harry Potter,’ he said, holding out a hand when Harry entered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Er - hi,’ said Harry, shaking hands with the centaur, who surveyed him unblinkingly through those astonishingly blue eyes but did not smile. ‘Er - good to see you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘And you,’ said the centaur, inclining his white-blond head. ‘It was foretold that we would meet again.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Harry noticed there was the shadow of a hoof-shaped bruise on Firenze’s chest. As he turned to join the rest of the class on the ground, he saw they were all looking at him in awe, apparently deeply impressed that he was on speaking terms with Firenze, whom they seemed to find intimidating.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: When the door was closed and the last student had sat down on a tree stump beside the wastepaper basket, Firenze gestured around the room.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Professor Dumbledore has kindly arranged this classroom for us,’ said Firenze, when everyone had settled down, ‘in imitation of my natural habitat. I would have preferred to teach you in the Forbidden Forest, which was - until Monday - my home … but that is no longer possible.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Please - er - sir -‘ said Parvati breathlessly, raising her hand, ‘- why not? We’ve been in there with Hagrid, we’re not frightened!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘It is not a question of your bravery,’ said Firenze, ‘but of my position. I cannot return to the Forest. My herd has banished me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Herd?’ said Lavender in a confused voice, and Harry knew she was thinking of cows. ‘What - oh!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Comprehension dawned on her face. ‘There are more of you?’ she said, stunned.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Did Hagrid breed you, like the Thestrals?’ asked Dean eagerly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Firenze turned his head very slowly to face Dean, who seemed to realise at once that he had said something very offensive.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘I didn’t - I meant - sorry,’ he finished in a hushed voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Centaurs are not the servants or playthings of humans,’ said Firenze quietly. There was a pause, then Parvati raised her hand again.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Please, sir … why have the other centaurs banished you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Because I have agreed to work for Professor Dumbledore,’ said Firenze. ‘They see this as a betrayal of our kind.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Harry remembered how, nearly four years ago, the centaur Bane had shouted at Firenze for allowing Harry to ride to safety on his back; he had called him a ‘common mule’. He wondered whether it had been Bane who had kicked Firenze in the chest.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Let us begin,’ said Firenze. He swished his long palomino tail, raised his hand towards the leafy canopy overhead, then lowered it slowly, and as he did so, the light in the room dimmed, so that they now seemed to be sitting in a forest clearing by twilight, and stars appeared on the ceiling. There were oohs and gasps and Ron said audibly, ‘Blimey!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Lie back on the floor,’ said Firenze in his calm voice, ‘and observe the heavens. Here is written, for those who can see, the fortune of our races.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: Harry stretched out on his back and gazed upwards at the ceiling. A twinkling red star winked at him from overhead.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘I know that you have learned the names of the planets and their moons in Astronomy,’ said Firenze’s calm voice, ‘and that you have mapped the stars’ progress through the heavens. Centaurs have unravelled the mysteries of these movements over centuries. Our findings teach us that the future may be glimpsed in the sky above us -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Twenty-Seven - The Centaur and the Sneak
text_content: ‘Professor Trelawney did astrology with us!’ said Parvati excitedly, raising her hand in front of her so that it stuck up in the air as she lay on her back. ‘Mars causes accidents and burns and things like that, and when it makes an angle to Saturn, like now -‘ she drew a right-angle in the air above her ‘- that means people need to be extra careful when handling hot things -‘
