book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It was worth it, though,’ said Fred, who was taking orders from clamouring Gryffindors. ‘If you want to add your name to the waiting list, Hermione, it’s five Galleons for your Basic Blaze box and twenty for the Deflagration Deluxe …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Hermione returned to the table where Harry and Ron were sitting staring at their schoolbags as though hoping their homework would spring out and start doing itself.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, why don’t we have a night off?’ said Hermione brightly, as a silver-tailed Weasley rocket zoomed past the window. ‘After all, the Easter holidays start on Friday, we’ll have plenty of time then.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you feeling all right?’ Ron asked, staring at her in disbelief.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Now you mention it,’ said Hermione happily, ‘d’you know … I think I’m feeling a bit … rebellious.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry could still hear the distant bangs of escaped firecrackers when he and Ron went up to bed an hour later; and as he got undressed a sparkler floated past the tower, still resolutely spelling out the word ‘POO’.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He got into bed, yawning. With his glasses off, the occasional firework passing the window had become blurred, looking like sparkling clouds, beautiful and mysterious against the black sky. He turned on to his side, wondering how Umbridge was feeling about her first day in Dumbledore’s job, and how Fudge would react when he heard that the school had spent most of the day in a state of advanced disruption. Smiling to himself, Harry closed his eyes …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The whizzes and bangs of escaped fireworks in the grounds seemed to be growing more distant … or perhaps he was simply speeding away from them …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He had fallen right into the corridor leading to the Department of Mysteries. He was speeding towards the plain black door … let it open … let it open …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: It did. He was inside the circular room lined with doors … he crossed it, placed his hand on an identical door and it swung inwards …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Now he was in a long, rectangular room full of an odd mechanical clicking. There were dancing flecks of light on the walls but he did not pause to investigate … he had to go on …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was a door at the far end … it, too, opened at his touch …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: And now he was in a dimly lit room as high and wide as a church, full of nothing but rows and rows of towering shelves, each laden with small, dusty, spun-glass spheres … now Harry’s heart was beating fast with excitement … he knew where to go … he ran forwards, but his footsteps made no noise in the enormous, deserted room …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was something in this room he wanted very, very much …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Something he wanted … or somebody else wanted …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: His scar was hurting …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: BANG!

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry awoke instantly, confused and angry. The dark dormitory was full of the sound of laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Cool!’ said Seamus, who was silhouetted against the window. ‘I think one of those Catherine wheels hit a rocket and it’s like they mated, come and see!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry heard Ron and Dean scramble out of bed for a better look. He lay quite still and silent while the pain in his scar subsided and disappointment washed over him. He felt as though a wonderful treat had been snatched from him at the very last moment … he had got so close that time.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Glittering pink and silver winged piglets were now soaring past the windows of Gryffindor Tower. Harry lay and listened to the appreciative whoops of Gryffindors in the dormitories below them. His stomach gave a sickening jolt as he remembered that he had Occlumency the following evening.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry spent the whole of the next day dreading what Snape was going to say if he found out how much further into the Department of Mysteries Harry had penetrated during his last dream. With a surge of guilt he realised that he had not practised Occlumency once since their last lesson: there had been too much going on since Dumbledore had left; he was sure he would not have been able to empty his mind even if he had tried. He doubted, however, whether Snape would accept that excuse.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He attempted a little last-minute practice during classes that day, but it was no good. Hermione kept asking him what was wrong whenever he fell silent trying to rid himself of all thought and emotion and, after all, the best moment to empty his brain was not while teachers were firing revision questions at the class.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Resigned to the worst, he set off for Snape’s office after dinner. Halfway across the Entrance Hall, however, Cho came hurrying up to him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Over here,’ said Harry, glad of a reason to postpone his meeting with Snape, and beckoning her across to the corner of the Entrance Hall where the giant hour-glasses stood. Gryffindor’s was now almost empty. ‘Are you OK? Umbridge hasn’t been asking you about the DA, has she?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, no,’ said Cho hurriedly. ‘No, it was only … well, I just wanted to say … Harry, I never dreamed Marietta would tell …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, well,’ said Harry moodily. He did feel Cho might have chosen her friends a bit more carefully; it was small consolation that the last he had heard, Marietta was still up in the hospital wing and Madam Pomfrey had not been able to make the slightest improvement to her pimples.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘She’s a lovely person really,’ said Cho. ‘She just made a mistake -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked at her incredulously.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘A lovely person who made a mistake? She sold us all out, including you!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well … we all got away, didn’t we?’ said Cho pleadingly. ‘You know, her mum works for the Ministry, it’s really difficult for her -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron’s dad works for the Ministry too!’ Harry said furiously. ‘And in case you hadn’t noticed, he hasn’t got sneak written across his face -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That was a really horrible trick of Hermione Granger’s,’ said Cho fiercely. ‘She should have told us she’d jinxed that list -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I think it was a brilliant idea,’ said Harry coldly. Cho flushed and her eyes grew brighter.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yes, I forgot - of course, if it was darling Hermione‘s idea -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t start crying again,’ said Harry warningly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I wasn’t going to!’ she shouted.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah … well … good,’ he said. ‘I’ve got enough to cope with at the moment.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Go and cope with it then!’ Cho said furiously, turning on her heel and stalking off.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Fuming, Harry descended the stairs to Snape’s dungeon and, though he knew from experience how much easier it would be for Snape to penetrate his mind if he arrived angry and resentful, he succeeded in nothing but thinking of a few more things he should have said to Cho about Marietta before reaching the dungeon door.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re late, Potter,’ said Snape coldly, as Harry closed the door behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape was standing with his back to Harry, removing, as usual, certain of his thoughts and placing them carefully in Dumbledore’s Pensieve. He dropped the last silvery strand into the stone basin and turned to face Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ he said. ‘Have you been practising?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ Harry lied, looking carefully at one of the legs of Snape’s desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, we’ll soon find out, won’t we?’ said Snape smoothly. ‘Wand out, Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry moved into his usual position, facing Snape with the desk between them. His heart was pumping fast with anger at Cho and anxiety about how much Snape was about to extract from his mind.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘On the count of three then,’ said Snape lazily. ‘One - two -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape’s office door banged open and Draco Malfoy sped in.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor Snape, sir - oh - sorry -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Malfoy was looking at Snape and Harry in some surprise.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all right, Draco,’ said Snape, lowering his wand. ‘Potter is here for a little remedial Potions.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry had not seen Malfoy look so gleeful since Umbridge had turned up to inspect Hagrid.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I didn’t know,’ he said, leering at Harry, who knew his face was burning. He would have given a great deal to be able to shout the truth at Malfoy - or, even better, to hit him with a good curse.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, Draco, what is it?’ asked Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s Professor Umbridge, sir - she needs your help,’ said Malfoy.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘They’ve found Montague, sir, he’s turned up jammed inside a toilet on the fourth floor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How did he get in there?’ demanded Snape.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t know, sir, he’s a bit confused.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Very well, very well. Potter,’ said Snape, ‘we shall resume this lesson tomorrow evening.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned and swept from his office. Malfoy mouthed, ‘Remedial Potions?’ at Harry behind Snape’s back before following him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Seething, Harry replaced his wand inside his robes and made to leave the room. At least he had twenty-four more hours in which to practise; he knew he ought to feel grateful for the narrow escape, though it was hard that it came at the expense of Malfoy telling the whole school that he needed remedial Potions.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He was at the office door when he saw it: a patch of shivering light dancing on the doorframe. He stopped, and stood looking at it, reminded of something … then he remembered: it was a little like the lights he had seen in his dream last night, the lights in the second room he had walked through on his journey through the Department of Mysteries.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned around. The light was coming from the Pensieve sitting on Snape’s desk. The silver-white contents were ebbing and swirling within. Snape’s thoughts … things he did not want Harry to see if he broke through Snape’s defences accidentally …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry gazed at the Pensieve, curiosity welling inside him … what was it that Snape was so keen to hide from Harry?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The silvery lights shivered on the wall … Harry took two steps towards the desk, thinking hard. Could it possibly be information about the Department of Mysteries that Snape was determined to keep from him?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked over his shoulder, his heart now pumping harder and faster than ever. How long would it take Snape to release Montague from the toilet? Would he come straight back to his office afterwards, or accompany Montague to the hospital wing? Surely the latter … Montague was Captain of the Slytherin Quidditch team, Snape would want to make sure he was all right.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry walked the remaining few feet to the Pensieve and stood over it, gazing into its depths. He hesitated, listening, then pulled out his wand again. The office and the corridor beyond were completely silent. He gave the contents of the Pensieve a small prod with the end of his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The silvery stuff within began to swirl very fast. Harry leaned forwards over it and saw that it had become transparent. He was, once again, looking down into a room as though through a circular window in the ceiling … in fact, unless he was much mistaken, he was looking down into the Great Hall.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: His breath was actually fogging the surface of Snape’s thoughts … his brain seemed to be in limbo … it would be insane to do the thing he was so strongly tempted to do … he was trembling … Snape could be back at any moment … but Harry thought of Cho’s anger, of Malfoy’s jeering face, and a reckless daring seized him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He took a great gulp of breath, and plunged his face into the surface of Snape’s thoughts. At once, the floor of the office lurched, tipping Harry head-first into the Pensieve …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He was falling through cold blackness, spinning furiously as he went, and then -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He was standing in the middle of the Great Hall, but the four house tables were gone. Instead, there were more than a hundred smaller tables, all facing the same way, at each of which sat a student, head bent low, scribbling on a roll of parchment. The only sound was the scratching of quills and the occasional rustle as somebody adjusted their parchment. It was clearly exam time.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Sunshine was streaming through the high windows on to the bent heads, which shone chestnut and copper and gold in the bright light. Harry looked around carefully. Snape had to be here somewhere … this was his memory …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: And there he was, at a table right behind Harry. Harry stared. Snape-the-teenager had a stringy, pallid look about him, like a plant kept in the dark. His hair was lank and greasy and was flopping on to the table, his hooked nose barely half an inch from the surface of the parchment as he scribbled. Harry moved around behind Snape and read the heading of the examination paper: DEFENCE AGAINST THE DARK ARTS - ORDINARY WIZARDING LEVEL.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: So Snape had to be fifteen or sixteen, around Harry’s own age. His hand was flying across the parchment; he had written at least a foot more than his closest neighbours, and yet his writing was minuscule and cramped.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Five more minutes!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The voice made Harry jump. Turning, he saw the top of Professor Flitwick’s head moving between the desks a short distance away. Professor Flitwick was walking past a boy with untidy black hair … very untidy black hair …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry moved so quickly that, had he been solid, he would have knocked desks flying. Instead he seemed to slide, dreamlike, across two aisles and up a third. The back of the black-haired boy’s head drew nearer and … he was straightening up now, putting down his quill, pulling his roll of parchment towards him so as to reread what he had written …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry stopped in front of the desk and gazed down at his fifteen-year-old father.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Excitement exploded in the pit of his stomach: it was as though he was looking at himself but with deliberate mistakes. James’s eyes were hazel, his nose was slightly longer than Harry’s and there was no scar on his forehead, but they had the same thin face, same mouth, same eyebrows; James’s hair stuck up at the back exactly as Harry’s did, his hands could have been Harry’s and Harry could tell that, when James stood up, they would be within an inch of each other in height.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: James yawned hugely and rumpled up his hair, making it even messier than it had been. Then, with a glance towards Professor Flitwick, he turned in his seat and grinned at a boy sitting four seats behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: With another shock of excitement, Harry saw Sirius give James the thumbs-up. Sirius was lounging in his chair at his ease, tilting it back on two legs. He was very good-looking; his dark hair fell into his eyes with a sort of casual elegance neither James’s nor Harry’s could ever have achieved, and a girl sitting behind him was eyeing him hopefully, though he didn’t seem to have noticed. And two seats along from this girl - Harry’s stomach gave another pleasurable squirm - was Remus Lupin. He looked rather pale and peaky (was the full moon approaching?) and was absorbed in the exam: as he reread his answers, he scratched his chin with the end of his quill, frowning slightly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: So that meant Wormtail had to be around here somewhere, too … and sure enough, Harry spotted him within seconds: a small, mousy-haired boy with a pointed nose. Wormtail looked anxious; he was chewing his fingernails, staring down at his paper, scuffing the ground with his toes. Every now and then he glanced hopefully at his neighbour’s paper. Harry stared at Wormtail for a moment, then back at James, who was now doodling on a bit of scrap parchment. He had drawn a Snitch and was now tracing the letters ‘L.E.’. What did they stand for?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Quills down, please!’ squeaked Professor Flitwick. ‘That means you too, Stebbins! Please remain seated while I collect your parchment! Accio!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Over a hundred rolls of parchment zoomed into the air and into Professor Flitwick’s outstretched arms, knocking him backwards off his feet. Several people laughed. A couple of students at the front desks got up, took hold of Professor Flitwick beneath the elbows and lifted him back on to his feet.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Thank you … thank you,’ panted Professor Flitwick. ‘Very well, everybody, you’re free to go!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked down at his father, who had hastily crossed out the ‘L.E.’ he had been embellishing, jumped to his feet, stuffed his quill and the exam paper into his bag, which he slung over his back, and stood waiting for Sirius to join him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked around and glimpsed Snape a short way away, moving between the tables towards the doors to the Entrance Hall, still absorbed in his own exam paper. Round-shouldered yet angular, he walked in a twitchy manner that recalled a spider, and his oily hair was jumping about his face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A gang of chattering girls separated Snape from James, Sirius and Lupin, and by planting himself in their midst, Harry managed to keep Snape in sight while straining his ears to catch the voices of James and his friends.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you like question ten, Moony?’ asked Sirius as they emerged into the Entrance Hall.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Loved it,’ said Lupin briskly. ‘Give five signs that identify the werewolf. Excellent question.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘D’you think you managed to get all the signs?’ said James in tones of mock concern.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Think I did,’ said Lupin seriously, as they joined the crowd thronging around the front doors eager to get out into the sunlit grounds. ‘One: he’s sitting on my chair. Two: he’s wearing my clothes. Three: his name’s Remus Lupin.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Wormtail was the only one who didn’t laugh.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I got the snout shape, the pupils of the eyes and the tufted tail,’ he said anxiously, ‘but I couldn’t think what else -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How thick are you, Wormtail?’ said James impatiently. ‘You run round with a werewolf once a month -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Keep your voice down,’ implored Lupin.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry looked anxiously behind him again. Snape remained close by, still buried in his exam questions - but this was Snape’s memory and Harry was sure that if Snape chose to wander off in a different direction once outside in the grounds, he, Harry, would not be able to follow James any further. To his intense relief, however, when James and his three friends strode off down the lawn towards the lake, Snape followed, still poring over the exam paper and apparently with no fixed idea of where he was going. By keeping a little ahead of him, Harry managed to maintain a close watch on James and the others.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I thought that paper was a piece of cake,’ he heard Sirius say. ‘I’ll be surprised if I don’t get “Outstanding” on it at least.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Me too,’ said James. He put his hand in his pocket and took out a struggling Golden Snitch.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where’d you get that?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Nicked it,’ said James casually. He started playing with the Snitch, allowing it to fly as much as a foot away before seizing it again; his reflexes were excellent. Wormtail watched him in awe.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They stopped in the shade of the very same beech tree on the edge of the lake where Harry, Ron and Hermione had once spent a Sunday finishing their homework, and threw themselves down on the grass. Harry looked over his shoulder yet again and saw, to his delight, that Snape had settled himself on the grass in the dense shadow of a clump of bushes. He was as deeply immersed in the O.W.L. paper as ever, which left Harry free to sit down on the grass between the beech and the bushes and watch the foursome under the tree. The sunlight was dazzling on the smooth surface of the lake, on the bank of which the group of laughing girls who had just left the Great Hall were sitting, with their shoes and socks off, cooling their feet in the water.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Lupin had pulled out a book and was reading. Sirius stared around at the students milling over the grass, looking rather haughty and bored, but very handsomely so. James was still playing with the Snitch, letting it zoom further and further away, almost escaping but always grabbed at the last second. Wormtail was watching him with his mouth open. Every time James made a particularly difficult catch, Wormtail gasped and applauded. After five minutes of this, Harry wondered why James didn’t tell Wormtail to get a grip on himself, but James seemed to be enjoying the attention. Harry noticed that his father had a habit of rumpling up his hair as though to keep it from getting too tidy, and he also kept looking over at the girls by the water’s edge.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Put that away, will you,’ said Sirius finally, as James made a fine catch and Wormtail let out a cheer, ‘before Wormtail wets himself with excitement.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Wormtail turned slightly pink, but James grinned.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘If it bothers you,’ he said, stuffing the Snitch back in his pocket. Harry had the distinct impression that Sirius was the only one for whom James would have stopped showing off.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m bored,’ said Sirius. ‘Wish it was full moon.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You might,’ said Lupin darkly from behind his book. ‘We’ve still got Transfiguration, if you’re bored you could test me. Here …’ and he held out his book.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But Sirius snorted. ‘I don’t need to look at that rubbish, I know it all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘This’ll liven you up, Padfoot,’ said James quietly. ‘Look who it is …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Sirius’s head turned. He became very still, like a dog that has scented a rabbit.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Excellent,’ he said softly. ‘Snivellus.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry turned to see what Sirius was looking at.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape was on his feet again, and was stowing the O.W.L. paper in his bag. As he left the shadows of the bushes and set off across the grass, Sirius and James stood up.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Lupin and Wormtail remained sitting: Lupin was still staring down at his book, though his eyes were not moving and a faint frown line had appeared between his eyebrows; Wormtail was looking from Sirius and James to Snape with a look of avid anticipation on his face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘All right, Snivellus?’ said James loudly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape reacted so fast it was as though he had been expecting an attack: dropping his bag, he plunged his hand inside his robes and his wand was halfway into the air when James shouted, ‘Expelliarmus!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape’s wand flew twelve feet into the air and fell with a little thud in the grass behind him. Sirius let out a bark of laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Impedimenta!’ he said, pointing his wand at Snape, who was knocked off his feet halfway through a dive towards his own fallen wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Students all around had turned to watch. Some of them had got to their feet and were edging nearer. Some looked apprehensive, others entertained.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Snape lay panting on the ground. James and Sirius advanced on him, wands raised, James glancing over his shoulder at the girls at the water’s edge as he went. Wormtail was on his feet now, watching hungrily, edging around Lupin to get a clearer view.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘How’d the exam go, Snivelly?’ said James.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I was watching him, his nose was touching the parchment,’ said Sirius viciously. ‘There’ll be great grease marks all over it, they won’t be able to read a word.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Several people watching laughed; Snape was clearly unpopular. Wormtail sniggered shrilly. Snape was trying to get up, but the jinx was still operating on him; he was struggling, as though bound by invisible ropes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You - wait,’ he panted, staring up at James with an expression of purest loathing, ‘you - wait!’
