text_content: ‘He should be near here,’ whispered Harry, convinced that every step was going to bring the ragged form of Sirius into view on the darkened floor. ‘Anywhere here … really close …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Harry?’ said Hermione tentatively, but he did not want to respond. His mouth was very dry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Somewhere about … here …’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: They had reached the end of the row and emerged into more dim candlelight. There was nobody there. All was echoing, dusty silence.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘He might be …’ Harry whispered hoarsely, peering down the next alley. ‘Or maybe …’ He hurried to look down the one beyond that.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Harry?’ said Hermione again.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘What?’ he snarled.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘I … I don’t think Sirius is here.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: Nobody spoke. Harry did not want to look at any of them. He felt sick. He did not understand why Sirius was not here. He had to be here. This was where he, Harry, had seen him …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: He ran up the space at the end of the rows, staring down them. Empty aisle after empty aisle flickered past. He ran the other way, back past his staring companions. There was no sign of Sirius anywhere, nor any hint of a struggle.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Harry?’ Ron called.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘What?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: He did not want to hear what Ron had to say; did not want to hear Ron tell him he had been stupid or suggest that they ought to go back to Hogwarts, but the heat was rising in his face and he felt as though he would like to skulk down here in the darkness for a long while before facing the brightness of the Atrium above and the others’ accusing stares …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Have you seen this?’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘What?’ said Harry, but eagerly this time - it had to be a sign that Sirius had been there, a clue. He strode back to where they were all standing, a little way down row ninety-seven, but found nothing except Ron staring at one of the dusty glass spheres on the shelf.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘What?’ Harry repeated glumly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘It’s - it’s got your name on,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: Harry moved a little closer. Ron was pointing at one of the small glass spheres that glowed with a dull inner light, though it was very dusty and appeared not to have been touched for many years.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘My name?’ said Harry blankly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: He stepped forwards. Not as tall as Ron, he had to crane his neck to read the yellowish label affixed to the shelf right beneath the dusty glass ball. In spidery writing was written a date of some sixteen years previously, and below that:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: S.P.T. to A.P.W.B.D. Dark Lord and (?)Harry Potter

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: Harry stared at it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘What is it?’ Ron asked, sounding unnerved. ‘What’s your name doing down here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: He glanced along at the other labels on that stretch of shelf.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘I’m not here,’ he said, sounding perplexed. ‘None of the rest of us are here.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Harry, I don’t think you should touch it,’ said Hermione sharply, as he stretched out his hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Why not?’ he said. ‘It’s something to do with me, isn’t it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Don’t, Harry,’ said Neville suddenly. Harry looked at him. Neville’s round face was shining slightly with sweat. He looked as though he could not take much more suspense.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘It’s got my name on,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: And feeling slightly reckless, he closed his fingers around the dusty ball’s surface. He had expected it to feel cold, but it did not. On the contrary, it felt as though it had been lying in the sun for hours, as though the glow of light within was warming it. Expecting, even hoping, that something dramatic was going to happen, something exciting that might make their long and dangerous journey worthwhile after all, Harry lifted the glass ball down from its shelf and stared at it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: Nothing whatsoever happened. The others moved in closer around Harry, gazing at the orb as he brushed it free of the clogging dust.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: And then, from right behind them, a drawling voice spoke.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
chapter: Chapter Thirty-Four - The Department of Mysteries
text_content: ‘Very good, Potter. Now turn around, nice and slowly, and give that to me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Black shapes were emerging out of thin air all around them, blocking their way left and right; eyes glinted through slits in hoods, a dozen lit wand-tips were pointing directly at their hearts; Ginny gave a gasp of horror.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘To me, Potter,’ repeated the drawling voice of Lucius Malfoy as he held out his hand, palm up.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry’s insides plummeted sickeningly. They were trapped, and outnumbered two to one.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘To me,’ said Malfoy yet again.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where’s Sirius?’ Harry said.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Several of the Death Eaters laughed; a harsh female voice from the midst of the shadowy figures to Harry’s left said triumphantly, ‘The Dark Lord always knows!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Always,’ echoed Malfoy softly. ‘Now, give me the prophecy, Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I want to know where Sirius is!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I want to know where Sirius is!’ mimicked the woman to his left.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She and her fellow Death Eaters had closed in so that they were mere feet away from Harry and the others, the light from their wands dazzling Harry’s eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ve got him,’ said Harry, ignoring the rising panic in his chest, the dread he had been fighting since they had first entered the ninety-seventh row. ‘He’s here. I know he is.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘The little baby woke up fwightened and fort what it dweamed was twoo,’ said the woman in a horrible, mock baby voice. Harry felt Ron stir beside him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t do anything,’ Harry muttered. ‘Not yet -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The woman who had mimicked him let out a raucous scream of laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You hear him? You hear him? Giving instructions to the other children as though he thinks of fighting us!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, you don’t know Potter as I do, Bellatrix,’ said Malfoy softly. ‘He has a great weakness for heroics; the Dark Lord understands this about him. Now give me the prophecy, Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I know Sirius is here,’ said Harry, though panic was causing his chest to constrict and he felt as though he could not breathe properly. ‘I know you’ve got him!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: More of the Death Eaters laughed, though the woman laughed loudest of all.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s time you learned the difference between life and dreams, Potter,’ said Malfoy. ‘Now give me the prophecy, or we start using wands.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Go on, then,’ said Harry, raising his own wand to chest height. As he did so, the five wands of Ron, Hermione, Neville, Ginny and Luna rose on either side of him. The knot in Harry’s stomach tightened. If Sirius really was not here, he had led his friends to their deaths for no reason at all …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But the Death Eaters did not strike.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hand over the prophecy and no one need get hurt,’ said Malfoy coolly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: It was Harry’s turn to laugh.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, right!’ he said. ‘I give you this - prophecy, is it? And you’ll just let us skip off home, will you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The words were hardly out of his mouth when the female Death Eater shrieked: ‘Accio proph—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry was just ready for her: he shouted ‘Protego!’ before she had finished her spell, and though the glass sphere slipped to the tips of his fingers he managed to cling on to it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, he knows how to play, little bitty baby Potter,’ she said, her mad eyes staring through the slits in her hood. ‘Very well, then -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I TOLD YOU, NO!’ Lucius Malfoy roared at the woman. ‘If you smash it -!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry’s mind was racing. The Death Eaters wanted this dusty spun-glass sphere. He had no interest in it. He just wanted to get them all out of this alive, to make sure none of his friends paid a terrible price for his stupidity …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The woman stepped forward, away from her fellows, and pulled off her hood. Azkaban had hollowed Bellatrix Lestrange’s face, making it gaunt and skull-like, but it was alive with a feverish, fanatical glow.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You need more persuasion?’ she said, her chest rising and falling rapidly. ‘Very well - take the smallest one,’ she ordered the Death Eaters beside her. ‘Let him watch while we torture the little girl. I’ll do it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry felt the others close in around Ginny; he stepped sideways so that he was right in front of her, the prophecy held up to his chest.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ll have to smash this if you want to attack any of us,’ he told Bellatrix. ‘I don’t think your boss will be too pleased if you come back without it, will he?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: She did not move; she merely stared at him, the tip of her tongue moistening her thin mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So,’ said Harry, ‘what kind of prophecy are we talking about, anyway?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He could not think what to do but to keep talking. Neville’s arm was pressed against his, and he could feel him shaking; he could feel one of the others’ quickened breath on the back of his head. He was hoping they were all thinking hard about ways to get out of this, because his mind was blank.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What kind of prophecy?’ repeated Bellatrix, the grin fading from her face. ‘You jest, Harry Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Nope, not jesting,’ said Harry, his eyes flicking from Death Eater to Death Eater, looking for a weak link, a space through which they could escape. ‘How come Voldemort wants it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Several of the Death Eaters let out low hisses.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You dare speak his name?’ whispered Bellatrix.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Harry, maintaining his tight grip on the glass ball, expecting another attempt to bewitch it from him. ‘Yeah, I’ve got no problem with saying Vol—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Shut your mouth!’ Bellatrix shrieked. ‘You dare speak his name with your unworthy lips, you dare besmirch it with your halfblood’s tongue, you dare -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you know he’s a half-blood too?’ said Harry recklessly. Hermione gave a little moan in his ear. ‘Voldemort? Yeah, his mother was a witch but his dad was a Muggle - or has he been telling you lot he’s pure-blood?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUPEF—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘NO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A jet of red light had shot from the end of Bellatrix Lestrange’s wand, but Malfoy had deflected it; his spell caused hers to hit the shelf a foot to the left of Harry and several of the glass orbs there shattered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Two figures, pearly-white as ghosts, fluid as smoke, unfurled themselves from the fragments of broken glass upon the floor and each began to speak; their voices vied with each other, so that only fragments of what they were saying could be heard over Malfoy and Bellatrix’s shouts.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘… at the solstice will come a new …‘ said the figure of an old, bearded man.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘DO NOT ATTACK! WE NEED THE PROPHECY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘He dared - he dares -‘ shrieked Bellatrix incoherently, ‘he stands there - filthy half-blood -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘WAIT UNTIL WE’VE GOT THE PROPHECY!’ bawled Malfoy.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘… and none will come after …‘ said the figure of a young woman.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The two figures that had burst from the shattered spheres had melted into thin air. Nothing remained of them or their erstwhile homes but fragments of glass upon the floor. They had, however, given Harry an idea. The problem was going to be conveying it to the others.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You haven’t told me what’s so special about this prophecy I’m supposed to be handing over,’ he said, playing for time. He moved his foot slowly sideways, feeling around for someone else’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Do not play games with us, Potter,’ said Malfoy.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m not playing games,’ said Harry, half his mind on the conversation, half on his wandering foot. And then he found someone’s toes and pressed down upon them. A sharp intake of breath behind him told him they were Hermione’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ she whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dumbledore never told you the reason you bear that scar was hidden in the bowels of the Department of Mysteries?’ Malfoy sneered.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I - what?’ said Harry. And for a moment he quite forgot his plan. ‘What about my scar?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ whispered Hermione more urgently behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Can this be?’ said Malfoy, sounding maliciously delighted; some of the Death Eaters were laughing again, and under cover of their laughter, Harry hissed to Hermione, moving his lips as little as possible, ‘Smash shelves -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dumbledore never told you?’ Malfoy repeated. ‘Well, this explains why you didn’t come earlier, Potter, the Dark Lord wondered why -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘- when I say now -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘- you didn’t come running when he showed you the place where it was hidden in your dreams. He thought natural curiosity would make you want to hear the exact wording …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Did he?’ said Harry. Behind him he felt rather than heard Hermione passing his message to the others and he sought to keep talking, to distract the Death Eaters. ‘So he wanted me to come and get it, did he? Why?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Why?’ Malfoy sounded incredulously delighted. ‘Because the only people who are permitted to retrieve a prophecy from the Department of Mysteries, Potter, are those about whom it was made, as the Dark Lord discovered when he attempted to use others to steal it for him.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And why did he want to steal a prophecy about me?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘About both of you, Potter, about both of you … haven’t you ever wondered why the Dark Lord tried to kill you as a baby?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry stared into the slitted eye-holes through which Malfoy’s grey eyes were gleaming. Was this prophecy the reason Harry’s parents had died, the reason he carried his lightning-bolt scar? Was the answer to all of this clutched in his hand?

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Someone made a prophecy about Voldemort and me?’ he said quietly, gazing at Lucius Malfoy, his fingers tightening over the warm glass sphere in his hand. It was hardly larger than a Snitch and still gritty with dust. ‘And he’s made me come and get it for him? Why couldn’t he come and get it himself?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get it himself?’ shrieked Bellatrix, over a cackle of mad laughter. ‘The Dark Lord, walk into the Ministry of Magic, when they are so sweetly ignoring his return? The Dark Lord, reveal himself to the Aurors, when at the moment they are wasting their time on my dear cousin?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So, he’s got you doing his dirty work for him, has he?’ said Harry. ‘Like he tried to get Sturgis to steal it - and Bode?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Very good, Potter, very good …’ said Malfoy slowly. ‘But the Dark Lord knows you are not unintell—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘NOW!’ yelled Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Five different voices behind him bellowed, ‘REDUCTO!’ Five curses flew in five different directions and the shelves opposite them exploded as they hit; the towering structure swayed as a hundred glass spheres burst apart, pearly-white figures unfurled into the air and floated there, their voices echoing from who knew what long-dead past amid the torrent of crashing glass and splintered wood now raining down upon the floor -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘RUN!’ Harry yelled, as the shelves swayed precariously and more glass spheres began to fall from above. He seized a handful of Hermione’s robes and dragged her forwards, holding one arm over his head as chunks of shelf and shards of glass thundered down upon them. A Death Eater lunged forwards through the cloud of dust and Harry elbowed him hard in the masked face; they were all yelling, there were cries of pain, and thunderous crashes as the shelves collapsed upon themselves, weirdly echoing fragments of the Seers unleashed from their spheres -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry found the way ahead clear and saw Ron, Ginny and Luna sprint past him, their arms over their heads; something heavy struck him on the side of the face but he merely ducked his head and sprinted onwards; a hand caught him by the shoulder; he heard Hermione shout, ‘Stupefy!’ The hand released him at once -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They were at the end of row ninety-seven; Harry turned right and began to sprint in earnest; he could hear footsteps right behind him and Hermione’s voice urging Neville on; straight ahead, the door through which they had come was ajar; Harry could see the glittering light of the bell jar; he pelted through the doorway, the prophecy still clutched tight and safe in his hand, and waited for the others to hurtle over the threshold before slamming the door behind them -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Colloportus!’ gasped Hermione and the door sealed itself with an odd squelching noise.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Where - where are the others?’ gasped Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He had thought Ron, Luna and Ginny were ahead of them, that they would be waiting in this room, but there was nobody there.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘They must have gone the wrong way!’ whispered Hermione, terror in her face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Listen!’ whispered Neville.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Footsteps and shouts echoed from behind the door they had just sealed; Harry put his ear close to the door to listen and heard Lucius Malfoy roar, ‘Leave Nott, leave him, I say - his injuries will be nothing to the Dark Lord compared to losing that prophecy. Jugson, come back here, we need to organise! We’ll split into pairs and search, and don’t forget, be gentle with Potter until we’ve got the prophecy, you can kill the others if necessary - Bellatrix, Rodolphus, you take the left; Crabbe, Rabastan, go right - Jugson, Dolohov, the door straight ahead - Macnair and Avery, through here - Rookwood, over there - Mulciber, come with me!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘What do we do?’ Hermione asked Harry, trembling from head to foot.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, we don’t stand here waiting for them to find us, for a start,’ said Harry. ‘Let’s get away from this door.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They ran as quietly as they could, past the shimmering bell jar where the tiny egg was hatching and unhatching, towards the exit into the circular hallway at the far end of the room. They were almost there when Harry heard something large and heavy collide with the door Hermione had charmed shut.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Stand aside!’ said a rough voice. ‘Alohomora!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: As the door flew open, Harry, Hermione and Neville dived under desks. They could see the bottom of the two Death Eaters’ robes drawing nearer, their feet moving rapidly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘They might’ve run straight through to the hall,’ said the rough voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Check under the desks,’ said another.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry saw the knees of the Death Eaters bend; poking his wand out from under the desk, he shouted, ‘STUPEFY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A jet of red light hit the nearest Death Eater; he fell backwards into a grandfather clock and knocked it over; the second Death Eater, however, had leapt aside to avoid Harry’s spell and was pointing his own wand at Hermione, who was crawling out from under the desk to get a better aim.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Avada -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry launched himself across the floor and grabbed the Death Eater around the knees, causing him to topple and his aim to go awry. Neville overturned a desk in his anxiety to help; and pointing his wand wildly at the struggling pair, he cried:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘EXPELLIARMUS!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Both Harry’s and the Death Eater’s wands flew out of their hands and soared back towards the entrance to the Hall of Prophecy; both scrambled to their feet and charged after them, the Death Eater in front, Harry hot on his heels, and Neville bringing up the rear, plainly horrorstruck by what he had done.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get out of the way, Harry!’ yelled Neville, clearly determined to repair the damage.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry flung himself sideways as Neville took aim again and shouted:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUPEFY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The jet of red light flew right over the Death Eater’s shoulder and hit a glass-fronted cabinet on the wall full of variously shaped hour-glasses; the cabinet fell to the floor and burst apart, glass flying everywhere, sprang back up on to the wall, fully mended, then fell down again, and shattered -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Death Eater had snatched up his wand, which lay on the floor beside the glittering bell jar. Harry ducked down behind another desk as the man turned; his mask had slipped so that he couldn’t see. He ripped it off with his free hand and shouted: ‘STUP—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUPEFY!‘ screamed Hermione, who had just caught up with them. The jet of red light hit the Death Eater in the middle of his chest: he froze, his arm still raised, his wand fell to the floor with a clatter and he collapsed backwards towards the bell jar. Harry expected to hear a clunk, for the man to hit solid glass and slide off the jar on to the floor, but instead, his head sank through the surface of the bell jar as though it were nothing but a soap bubble and he came to rest, sprawled on his back on the table, with his head lying inside the jar full of glittering wind.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Accio wand!’ cried Hermione. Harry’s wand flew from a dark corner into her hand and she threw it to him.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Thanks,’ he said. ‘Right, let’s get out of -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Look out!’ said Neville, horrified. He was staring at the Death Eater’s head in the bell jar.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: All three of them raised their wands again, but none of them struck: they were all gazing, open-mouthed, appalled, at what was happening to the man’s head.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: It was shrinking very fast, growing balder and balder, the black hair and stubble retracting into his skull; his cheeks becoming smooth, his skull round and covered with a peachlike fuzz …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A baby’s head now sat grotesquely on top of the thick, muscled neck of the Death Eater as he struggled to get up again; but even as they watched, their mouths open, the head began to swell to its previous proportions again; thick black hair was sprouting from the pate and chin …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s Time,’ said Hermione in an awestruck voice. ‘Time …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Death Eater shook his ugly head again, trying to clear it, but before he could pull himself together it began to shrink back to babyhood once more …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was a shout from a room nearby, then a crash and a scream.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘RON?’ Harry yelled, turning quickly from the monstrous transformation taking place before them. ‘GINNY? LUNA?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry!’ Hermione screamed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Death Eater had pulled his head out of the bell jar. His appearance was utterly bizarre, his tiny baby’s head bawling loudly while his thick arms flailed dangerously in all directions, narrowly missing Harry, who had ducked. Harry raised his wand but to his amazement Hermione seized his arm.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You can’t hurt a baby!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was no time to argue the point; Harry could hear more footsteps growing louder from the Hall of Prophecy and knew, too late, that he ought not to have shouted and given away their position.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on!’ he said, and leaving the ugly baby-headed Death Eater staggering behind them they took off for the door that stood open at the other end of the room, leading back into the black hallway.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They had run halfway towards it when Harry saw through the open door two more Death Eaters running across the black room towards them; veering left, he burst instead into a small, dark, cluttered office and slammed the door behind them.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Collo—’ began Hermione, but before she could complete the spell the door had burst open and the two Death Eaters had come hurtling inside.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: With a cry of triumph, both yelled:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘IMPEDIMENTA!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry, Hermione and Neville were all knocked backwards off their feet; Neville was thrown over the desk and disappeared from view; Hermione smashed into a bookcase and was promptly deluged in a cascade of heavy books; the back of Harry’s head slammed into the stone wall behind him, tiny lights burst in front of his eyes and for a moment he was too dizzy and bewildered to react.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘WE’VE GOT HIM!’ yelled the Death Eater nearest Harry. ‘IN AN OFFICE OFF—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Silencio!’ cried Hermione and the man’s voice was extinguished. He continued to mouth through the hole in his mask, but no sound came out. He was thrust aside by his fellow Death Eater.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Petrificus Totalus!’ shouted Harry, as the second Death Eater raised his wand. His arms and legs snapped together and he fell forwards, face down on to the rug at Harry’s feet, stiff as a board and unable to move.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well done, Ha—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But the Death Eater Hermione had just struck dumb made a sudden slashing movement with his wand; a streak of what looked like purple flame passed right across Hermione’s chest. She gave a tiny ‘Oh!’ as though of surprise and crumpled on to the floor, where she lay motionless.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry fell to his knees beside her as Neville crawled rapidly towards her from under the desk, his wand held up in front of him. The Death Eater kicked out hard at Neville’s head as he emerged - his foot broke Neville’s wand in two and connected with his face. Neville gave a howl of pain and recoiled, clutching his mouth and nose. Harry twisted around, his own wand held high, and saw that the Death Eater had ripped off his mask and was pointing his wand directly at Harry, who recognised the long, pale, twisted face from the Daily Prophet: Antonin Dolohov, the wizard who had murdered the Prewetts.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Dolohov grinned. With his free hand, he pointed from the prophecy still clutched in Harry’s hand, to himself, then at Hermione. Though he could no longer speak, his meaning could not have been clearer. Give me the prophecy, or you get the same as her …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Like you won’t kill us all anyway, the moment I hand it over!’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A whine of panic inside his head was preventing him thinking properly: he had one hand on Hermione’s shoulder, which was still warm, yet did not dare look at her properly. Don’t let her be dead, don’t let her be dead, it’s my fault if she’s dead …

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Whaddever you do, Harry,’ said Neville fiercely from under the desk, lowering his hands to show a clearly broken nose and blood pouring down his mouth and chin, ‘don’d gib it to him!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Then there was a crash outside the door and Dolohov looked over his shoulder - the baby-headed Death Eater had appeared in the doorway, his head bawling, his great fists still flailing uncontrollably at everything around him. Harry seized his chance:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘PETRIFICUS TOTALUS!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The spell hit Dolohov before he could block it and he toppled forwards across his comrade, both of them rigid as boards and unable to move an inch.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione,’ Harry said at once, shaking her as the baby-headed Death Eater blundered out of sight again. ‘Hermione, wake up …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Whaddid he do to her?’ said Neville, crawling out from under the desk to kneel at her other side, blood streaming from his rapidly swelling nose.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I dunno …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville groped for Hermione’s wrist.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Dat’s a pulse, Harry, I’b sure id is.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Such a powerful wave of relief swept through Harry that for a moment he felt light-headed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘She’s alive?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, I dink so.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There was a pause in which Harry listened hard for the sound of more footsteps, but all he could hear were the whimpers and blunderings of the baby-headed Death Eater in the next room.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Neville, we’re not far from the exit,’ Harry whispered, ‘we’re right next to that circular room … if we can just get you across it and find the right door before any more Death Eaters come, I’ll bet you can get Hermione up the corridor and into the lift … then you could find someone … raise the alarm …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And whad are you going do do?’ said Neville, mopping his bleeding nose with his sleeve and frowning at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve got to find the others,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I’b going do find dem wid you,’ said Neville firmly.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘But Hermione -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ll dake her wid us,’ said Neville firmly. ‘I’ll carry her - you’re bedder at fighding dem dan I ab -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He stood up and seized one of Hermione’s arms, glaring at Harry, who hesitated, then grabbed the other and helped hoist Hermione’s limp form over Neville’s shoulders.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Wait,’ said Harry, snatching up Hermione’s wand from the floor and shoving it into Neville’s hand, ‘you’d better take this.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville kicked aside the broken fragments of his own wand as they walked slowly towards the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘My gran’s going do kill be,’ said Neville thickly, blood spattering from his nose as he spoke, ‘dat was by dad’s old wand.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry stuck his head out of the door and looked around cautiously. The baby-headed Death Eater was screaming and banging into things, toppling grandfather clocks and overturning desks, bawling and confused, while the glass-fronted cabinet that Harry now suspected had contained Time-Turners continued to fall, shatter and repair itself on the wall behind them.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s never going to notice us,’ he whispered. ‘C’mon … keep close behind me …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: They crept out of the office and back towards the door into the black hallway, which now seemed completely deserted. They walked a few steps forwards, Neville tottering slightly due to Hermione’s weight; the door of the Time Room swung shut behind them and the walls began to rotate once more. The recent blow on the back of Harry’s head seemed to have unsteadied him; he narrowed his eyes, swaying slightly, until the walls stopped moving again. With a sinking heart, Harry saw that Hermione’s fiery crosses had faded from the doors.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘So which way d’you reck—?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But before they could make a decision as to which way to try, a door to their right sprang open and three people fell out of it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron!’ croaked Harry, dashing towards them. ‘Ginny - are you all -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry,’ said Ron, giggling weakly, lurching forwards, seizing the front of Harry’s robes and gazing at him with unfocused eyes, ‘there you are … ha ha ha … you look funny, Harry … you’re all messed up …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Ron’s face was very white and something dark was trickling from the corner of his mouth. Next moment his knees had given way, but he still clutched the front of Harry’s robes, so that Harry was pulled into a kind of bow.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ginny?’ Harry said fearfully. ‘What happened?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But Ginny shook her head and slid down the wall into a sitting position, panting and holding her ankle.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I think her ankle’s broken, I heard something crack,’ whispered Luna, who was bending over her and who alone seemed to be unhurt. ‘Four of them chased us into a dark room full of planets; it was a very odd place, some of the time we were just floating in the dark -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, we saw Uranus up close!’ said Ron, still giggling feebly. ‘Get it, Harry? We saw Uranus - ha ha ha -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A bubble of blood grew at the corner of Ron’s mouth and burst.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘- anyway, one of them grabbed Ginny’s foot, I used the Reductor Curse and blew up Pluto in his face, but …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Luna gestured hopelessly at Ginny, who was breathing in a very shallow way, her eyes still closed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And what about Ron?’ said Harry fearfully, as Ron continued to giggle, still hanging off the front of Harry’s robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t know what they hit him with,’ said Luna sadly, ‘but he’s gone a bit funny, I could hardly get him along at all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry,’ said Ron, pulling Harry’s ear down to his mouth and still giggling weakly, ‘you know who this girl is, Harry? She’s Loony … Loony Lovegood … ha ha ha …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ve got to get out of here,’ said Harry firmly. ‘Luna, can you help Ginny?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Luna, sticking her wand behind her ear for safekeeping, then putting an arm around Ginny’s waist and pulling her up.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s only my ankle, I can do it myself!’ said Ginny impatiently, but next moment she had collapsed sideways and grabbed Luna for support. Harry pulled Ron’s arm over his shoulder just as, so many months ago, he had pulled Dudley’s. He looked around: they had a one in twelve chance of getting the exit right first time -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He heaved Ron towards a door; they were within a few feet of it when another door across the hall burst open and three Death Eaters sped in, led by Bellatrix Lestrange.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘There they are!’ she shrieked.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Stunning Spells shot across the room: Harry smashed his way through the door ahead, flung Ron unceremoniously from him and ducked back to help Neville in with Hermione: they were all over the threshold just in time to slam the door against Bellatrix.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Colloportus!’ shouted Harry, and he heard three bodies slam into the door on the other side.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It doesn’t matter!’ said a man’s voice. ‘There are other ways in - WE’VE GOT THEM, THEY’RE HERE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry spun round; they were back in the Brain Room and, sure enough, there were doors all around the walls. He could hear footsteps in the hall behind them as more Death Eaters came running to join the first.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Luna - Neville - help me!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The three of them tore around the room, sealing the doors as they went; Harry crashed into a table and rolled over the top of it in his haste to reach the next door:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Colloportus!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: There were footsteps running along behind the doors, every now and then another heavy body would launch itself against one, so it creaked and shuddered; Luna and Neville were bewitching the doors along the opposite wall - then, as Harry reached the very top of the room, he heard Luna cry:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Collo— aaaaaaaaargh …’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He turned in time to see her flying through the air; five Death Eaters were surging into the room through the door she had not reached in time; Luna hit a desk, slid over its surface and on to the floor on the other side where she lay sprawled, as still as Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Get Potter!’ shrieked Bellatrix, and she ran at him; he dodged her and sprinted back up the room; he was safe as long as they thought they might hit the prophecy -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Hey!’ said Ron, who had staggered to his feet and was now tottering drunkenly towards Harry, giggling. ‘Hey, Harry, there are brains in here, ha ha ha, isn’t that weird, Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron, get out of the way, get down -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But Ron had already pointed his wand at the tank.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Honest, Harry, they’re brains - look - Accio brain!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The scene seemed momentarily frozen. Harry, Ginny and Neville and each of the Death Eaters turned in spite of themselves to watch the top of the tank as a brain burst from the green liquid like a leaping fish: for a moment it seemed suspended in midair, then it soared towards Ron, spinning as it came, and what looked like ribbons of moving images flew from it, unravelling like rolls of film -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Ha ha ha, Harry, look at it -‘ said Ron, watching it disgorge its gaudy innards, ‘Harry, come and touch it; bet it’s weird -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘RON, NO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not know what would happen if Ron touched the tentacles of thought now flying behind the brain, but he was sure it would not be anything good. He darted forwards but Ron had already caught the brain in his outstretched hands.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The moment they made contact with his skin, the tentacles began wrapping themselves around Ron’s arms like ropes.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, look what’s happen— No - no - I don’t like it - no, stop - stop -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But the thin ribbons were spinning around Ron’s chest now; he tugged and tore at them as the brain was pulled tight against him like an octopus’s body.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Diffindo!’ yelled Harry, trying to sever the feelers wrapping themselves tightly around Ron before his eyes, but they would not break. Ron fell over, still thrashing against his bonds.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, it’ll suffocate him!’ screamed Ginny, immobilised by her broken ankle on the floor - then a jet of red light flew from one of the Death Eater’s wands and hit her squarely in the face. She keeled over sideways and lay there unconscious.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUBEFY!’ shouted Neville, wheeling around and waving Hermione’s wand at the oncoming Death Eaters, ‘STUBEFY, STUBEFY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: But nothing happened.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: One of the Death Eaters shot their own Stunning Spell at Neville; it missed him by inches. Harry and Neville were now the only two left fighting the five Death Eaters, two of whom sent off streams of silver light like arrows which missed but left craters in the wall behind them. Harry ran for it as Bellatrix Lestrange raced right at him: holding the prophecy high above his head, he sprinted back up the room; all he could think of doing was to draw the Death Eaters away from the others.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: It seemed to have worked; they streaked after him, knocking chairs and tables flying but not daring to bewitch him in case they hurt the prophecy, and he dashed through the only door still open, the one through which the Death Eaters themselves had come; inwardly praying that Neville would stay with Ron and find some way of releasing him. He ran a few feet into the new room and felt the floor vanish -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: He was falling down steep stone step after steep stone step, bouncing on every tier until at last, with a crash that knocked all the breath out of his body, he landed flat on his back in the sunken pit where the stone archway stood on its dais. The whole room was ringing with the Death Eaters’ laughter: he looked up and saw the five who had been in the Brain Room descending towards him, while as many more emerged through other doorways and began leaping from bench to bench towards him. Harry got to his feet though his legs were trembling so badly they barely supported him: the prophecy was still miraculously unbroken in his left hand, his wand clutched tightly in his right. He backed away, looking around, trying to keep all the Death Eaters within his sight. The back of his legs hit something solid: he had reached the dais where the archway stood. He climbed backwards on to it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Death Eaters all halted, gazing at him. Some were panting as hard as he was. One was bleeding badly; Dolohov, freed of the Body-Bind Curse, was leering, his wand pointing straight at Harry’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Potter, your race is run,’ drawled Lucius Malfoy, pulling off his mask, ‘now hand me the prophecy like a good boy.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Let - let the others go, and I’ll give it to you!’ said Harry desperately.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: A few of the Death Eaters laughed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘You are not in a position to bargain, Potter,’ said Lucius Malfoy, his pale face flushed with pleasure. ‘You see, there are ten of us and only one of you … or hasn’t Dumbledore ever taught you how to count?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s dot alone!’ shouted a voice from above them. ‘He’s still god be!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry’s heart sank: Neville was scrambling down the stone benches towards them, Hermione’s wand held fast in his trembling hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Neville - no - go back to Ron -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUBEFY!’ Neville shouted again, pointing his wand at each Death Eater in turn. ‘STUBEFY! STUBE—’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: One of the largest Death Eaters seized Neville from behind, pinioning his arms to his sides. He struggled and kicked; several of the Death Eaters laughed.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s Longbottom, isn’t it?’ sneered Lucius Malfoy. ‘Well, your grandmother is used to losing family members to our cause … your death will not come as a great shock.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Longbottom?’ repeated Bellatrix, and a truly evil smile lit her gaunt face. ‘Why, I have had the pleasure of meeting your parents, boy.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I DOE YOU HAB!’ roared Neville, and he fought so hard against his captor’s encircling grip that the Death Eater shouted, ‘Someone Stun him!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘No, no, no,’ said Bellatrix. She looked transported, alive with excitement as she glanced at Harry, then back at Neville. ‘No, let’s see how long Longbottom lasts before he cracks like his parents … unless Potter wants to give us the prophecy.’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘DON’D GIB ID DO DEM!’ roared Neville, who seemed beside himself, kicking and writhing as Bellatrix drew nearer to him and his captor, her wand raised. ‘DON’D GIB ID DO DEM, HARRY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Bellatrix raised her wand. ‘Crucio!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville screamed, his legs drawn up to his chest so that the Death Eater holding him was momentarily holding him off the ground. The Death Eater dropped him and he fell to the floor, twitching and screaming in agony.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘That was just a taster!’ said Bellatrix, raising her wand so that Neville’s screams stopped and he lay sobbing at her feet. She turned and gazed up at Harry. ‘Now, Potter, either give us the prophecy, or watch your little friend die the hard way!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Harry did not have to think; there was no choice. The prophecy was hot with the heat of his clutching hand as he held it out. Malfoy jumped forwards to take it.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Then, high above them, two more doors burst open and five more people sprinted into the room: Sirius, Lupin, Moody, Tonks and Kingsley.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Malfoy turned, and raised his wand, but Tonks had already sent a Stunning Spell right at him. Harry did not wait to see whether it had made contact, but dived off the dais out of the way. The Death Eaters were completely distracted by the appearance of the members of the Order, who were now raining spells down upon them as they jumped from step to step towards the sunken floor. Through the darting bodies, the flashes of light, Harry could see Neville crawling along. He dodged another jet of red light and flung himself flat on the ground to reach Neville.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you OK?’ he yelled, as another spell soared inches over their heads.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Neville, trying to pull himself up.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘And Ron?’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘I dink he’s all righd - he was still fighding de brain when I lefd -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The stone floor between them exploded as a spell hit it, leaving a crater right where Neville’s hand had been only seconds before; both scrambled away from the spot, then a thick arm came out of nowhere, seized Harry around the neck and pulled him upright, so that his toes were barely touching the floor.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘Give it to me,’ growled a voice in his ear, ‘give me the prophecy -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The man was pressing so tightly on Harry’s windpipe that he could not breathe. Through watering eyes he saw Sirius duelling with a Death Eater some ten feet away; Kingsley was fighting two at once; Tonks, still halfway up the tiered seats, was firing spells down at Bellatrix - nobody seemed to realise that Harry was dying. He turned his wand backwards towards the man’s side, but had no breath to utter an incantation, and the man’s free hand was groping towards the hand in which Harry was grasping the prophecy -

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘AARGH!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: Neville had come lunging out of nowhere; unable to articulate a spell, he had jabbed Hermione’s wand hard into the eyehole of the Death Eater’s mask. The man relinquished Harry at once with a howl of pain. Harry whirled around to face him and gasped:

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: ‘STUPEFY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
text_content: The Death Eater keeled over backwards and his mask slipped off: it was Macnair, Buckbeak’s would-be killer, one of his eyes now swollen and bloodshot.

book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (UK)
