text_content: Harry and Ron did not answer, but Harry knew that they were all thinking the same thing. There had been a horrible incident the day before, when Hannah Abbott had been taken out of Herbology to be told her mother had been found dead. They had not seen Hannah since.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: When they left the Gryffindor table five minutes later to head down to the Quidditch pitch, they passed Lavender Brown and Parvati Patil. Remembering what Hermione had said about the Patil twins’ parents wanting them to leave Hogwarts, Harry was unsurprised to see that the two best friends were whispering together, looking distressed. What did surprise him was that when Ron drew level with them, Parvati suddenly nudged Lavender, who looked round and gave Ron a wide smile. Ron blinked at her, then returned the smile uncertainly. His walk instantly became something more like a strut. Harry resisted the temptation to laugh, remembering that Ron had refrained from doing so after Malfoy had broken Harry’s nose; Hermione, however, looked cold and distant all the way down to the stadium through the cool, misty drizzle, and departed to find a place in the stands without wishing Ron good luck.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: As Harry had expected, the trials took most of the morning. Half of Gryffindor house seemed to have turned up, from first-years who were nervously clutching a selection of the dreadful old school brooms, to seventh-years who towered over the rest looking coolly intimidating. The latter included a large, wiry-haired boy Harry recognised immediately from the Hogwarts Express.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We met on the train, in old Sluggy’s compartment,’ he said confidently, stepping out of the crowd to shake Harry’s hand. ‘Cormac McLaggen, Keeper.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You didn’t try out last year, did you?’ asked Harry, taking note of the breadth of McLaggen and thinking that he would probably block all three goalhoops without even moving.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I was in the hospital wing when they held the trials,’ said McLaggen, with something of a swagger. ‘Ate a pound of Doxy eggs for a bet.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Harry. ‘Well … if you wait over there …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He pointed over to the edge of the pitch, close to where Hermione was sitting. He thought he saw a flicker of annoyance pass over McLaggen’s face and wondered whether McLaggen expected preferential treatment because they were both ‘old Sluggy’s’ favourites.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry decided to start with a basic test, asking all applicants for the team to divide into groups of ten and fly once around the pitch. This was a good decision: the first ten was made up of first-years and it could not have been plainer that they had hardly ever flown before. Only one boy managed to remain airborne for more than a few seconds, and he was so surprised he promptly crashed into one of the goalposts.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The second group comprised ten of the silliest girls Harry had ever encountered, who, when he blew his whistle, merely fell about giggling and clutching each other. Romilda Vane was amongst them. When he told them to leave the pitch they did so quite cheerfully and went to sit in the stands to heckle everyone else.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The third group had a pile-up halfway around the pitch. Most of the fourth group had come without broomsticks. The fifth group were Hufflepuffs.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘If there’s anyone else here who’s not from Gryffindor,’ roared Harry, who was starting to get seriously annoyed, ‘leave now, please!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was a pause, then a couple of little Ravenclaws went sprinting off the pitch, snorting with laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: After two hours, many complaints and several tantrums, one involving a crashed Comet Two Sixty and several broken teeth, Harry had found himself three Chasers: Katie Bell, returned to the team after an excellent trial, a new find called Demelza Robins, who was particularly good at dodging Bludgers, and Ginny Weasley, who had outflown all the competition and scored seventeen goals to boot. Pleased though he was with his choices, Harry had also shouted himself hoarse at the many complainers and was now enduring a similar battle with the rejected Beaters.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s my final decision and if you don’t get out of the way for the Keepers I’ll hex you,’ he bellowed.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Neither of his chosen Beaters had the old brilliance of Fred and George, but he was still reasonably pleased with them: Jimmy Peakes, a short but broad-chested third-year who had managed to raise a lump the size of an egg on the back of Harry’s head with a ferociously hit Bludger, and Ritchie Coote, who looked weedy but aimed well. They now joined the spectators in the stands to watch the selection of their last team member.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had deliberately left the trial of the Keepers until last, hoping for an emptier stadium and less pressure on all concerned. Unfortunately, however, all the rejected players and a number of people who had come down to watch after a lengthy breakfast had joined the crowd by now, so that it was larger than ever. As each Keeper flew up to the goalhoops, the crowd roared and jeered in equal measure. Harry glanced over at Ron, who had always had a problem with nerves; Harry had hoped that winning their final match last term might have cured it, but apparently not: Ron was a delicate shade of green.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: None of the first five applicants saved more than two goals apiece. To Harry’s great disappointment, Cormac McLaggen saved four penalties out of five. On the last one, however, he shot off in completely the wrong direction; the crowd laughed and booed and McLaggen returned to the ground grinding his teeth.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron looked ready to pass out as he mounted his Cleansweep Eleven.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good luck!’ cried a voice from the stands. Harry looked around, expecting to see Hermione, but it was Lavender Brown. He would have quite liked to have hidden his face in his hands, as she did a moment later, but thought that as the Captain he ought to show slightly more grit, and so turned to watch Ron do his trial.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Yet he need not have worried: Ron saved one, two, three, four, five penalties in a row. Delighted, and resisting joining in the cheers of the crowd with difficulty, Harry turned to McLaggen to tell him that, most unfortunately, Ron had beaten him, only to find McLaggen’s red face inches from his own. He stepped back hastily.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘His sister didn’t really try,’ said McLaggen menacingly. There was a vein pulsing in his temple like the one Harry had often admired in Uncle Vernon’s. ‘She gave him an easy save.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Rubbish,’ said Harry coldly. ‘That was the one he nearly missed.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: McLaggen took a step nearer Harry, who stood his ground this time.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Give me another go.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry. ‘You’ve had your go. You saved four. Ron saved five. Ron’s Keeper, he won it fair and square. Get out of my way.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He thought for a moment that McLaggen might punch him, but he contented himself with an ugly grimace and stormed away, growling what sounded like threats to thin air.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry turned round to find his new team beaming at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well done,’ he croaked. ‘You flew really well –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You did brilliantly, Ron!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: This time it really was Hermione running towards them from the stands; Harry saw Lavender walking off the pitch, arm in arm with Parvati, a rather grumpy expression on her face. Ron looked extremely pleased with himself and even taller than usual as he grinned around at the team and at Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: After fixing the time of their first full practice for the following Thursday, Harry, Ron and Hermione bade goodbye to the rest of the team and headed off towards Hagrid’s. A watery sun was trying to break through the clouds now and it had stopped drizzling at last. Harry felt extremely hungry; he hoped there would be something to eat at Hagrid’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I thought I was going to miss that fourth penalty,’ Ron was saying happily. ‘Tricky shot from Demelza, did you see, had a bit of spin on it –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, yes, you were magnificent,’ said Hermione, looking amused.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I was better than that McLaggen anyway,’ said Ron in a highly satisfied voice. ‘Did you see him lumbering off in the wrong direction on his fifth? Looked like he’d been Confunded …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: To Harry’s surprise, Hermione turned a very deep shade of pink at these words. Ron noticed nothing; he was too busy describing each of his other penalties in loving detail.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The great grey Hippogriff, Buckbeak, was tethered in front of Hagrid’s cabin. He clicked his razor-sharp beak at their approach and turned his huge head towards them.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh dear,’ said Hermione nervously. ‘He’s still a bit scary, isn’t he?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Come off it, you’ve ridden him, haven’t you?’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry stepped forwards and bowed low to the Hippogriff without breaking eye contact or blinking. After a few seconds, Buckbeak sank into a bow too.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘How are you?’ Harry asked him in a low voice, moving forwards to stroke the feathery head. ‘Missing him? But you’re OK here with Hagrid, aren’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oi!’ said a loud voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hagrid had come striding round the corner of his cabin wearing a large flowery apron and carrying a sack of potatoes. His enormous boarhound, Fang, was at his heels; Fang gave a booming bark and bounded forwards.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Git away from him! He’ll have yer fingers – oh. It’s yeh lot.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Fang was jumping up at Hermione and Ron, attempting to lick their ears. Hagrid stood and looked at them all for a split second, then turned and strode into his cabin, slamming the door behind him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh dear!’ said Hermione, looking stricken.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t worry about it,’ said Harry grimly. He walked over to the door and knocked loudly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid! Open up, we want to talk to you!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was no sound from within.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘If you don’t open the door, we’ll blast it open!’ Harry said, pulling out his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry!’ said Hermione, sounding shocked. ‘You can’t possibly –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, I can!’ said Harry. ‘Stand back –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But before he could say anything else, the door flew open again as Harry had known it would, and there stood Hagrid, glowering down at him and looking, despite the flowery pinny, positively alarming.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m a teacher!’ he roared at Harry. ‘A teacher, Potter! How dare yeh threaten ter break down my door!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m sorry, sir,’ said Harry, emphasising the last word as he stowed his wand inside his robes.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hagrid looked stunned.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Since when have yeh called me “sir”?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Since when have you called me “Potter”?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, very clever,’ growled Hagrid. ‘Very amusin’. That’s me outsmarted, innit? All righ’, come in then, yeh ungrateful little …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Mumbling darkly, he stood back to let them pass. Hermione scurried in after Harry, looking rather frightened.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well?’ said Hagrid grumpily, as Harry, Ron and Hermione sat down around his enormous wooden table, Fang laying his head immediately upon Harry’s knee and drooling all over his robes. ‘What’s this? Feelin’ sorry for me? Reckon I’m lonely or summat?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry at once. ‘We wanted to see you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ve missed you!’ said Hermione tremulously.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Missed me, have yeh?’ snorted Hagrid. ‘Yeah. Righ’.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He stomped around, brewing up tea in his enormous copper kettle, muttering all the while. Finally he slammed down three bucket-sized mugs of mahogany-brown tea in front of them and a plate of his rock cakes. Harry was hungry enough even for Hagrid’s cooking, and took one at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid,’ said Hermione timidly, when he joined them at the table and started peeling his potatoes with a brutality that suggested that each tuber had done him a great personal wrong, ‘we really wanted to carry on with Care of Magical Creatures, you know.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hagrid gave another great snort. Harry rather thought some bogies landed on the potatoes, and was inwardly thankful that they were not staying for dinner.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We did!’ said Hermione. ‘But none of us could fit it into our timetables!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah. Righ’,’ said Hagrid again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was a funny squelching sound and they all looked around: Hermione let out a tiny shriek and Ron leapt out of his seat and hurried around the table away from the large barrel standing in the corner that they had only just noticed. It was full of what looked like foot-long maggots; slimy, white and writhing.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What are they, Hagrid?’ asked Harry, trying to sound interested rather than revolted, but putting down his rock cake all the same.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Jus’ giant grubs,’ said Hagrid.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And they grow into …?’ said Ron, looking apprehensive.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘They won’ grow inter nuthin’,’ said Hagrid. ‘I got ’em ter feed ter Aragog.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And without warning, he burst into tears.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid!’ cried Hermione, leaping up, hurrying around the table the long way to avoid the barrel of maggots, and putting an arm around his shaking shoulders. ‘What is it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s … him …’ gulped Hagrid, his beetle-black eyes streaming as he mopped his face with his apron. ‘It’s … Aragog … I think he’s dyin’ … he got ill over the summer an’ he’s not gettin’ better … I don’ know what I’ll do if he … if he … we’ve bin tergether so long …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione patted Hagrid’s shoulder, looking at a complete loss for anything to say. Harry knew how she felt. He had known Hagrid to present a vicious baby dragon with a teddy bear, seen him croon over giant scorpions with suckers and stings, attempt to reason with his brutal giant of a half-brother, but this was perhaps the most incomprehensible of all his monster fancies: the gigantic talking spider, Aragog, that dwelled deep in the Forbidden Forest and which he and Ron had only narrowly escaped four years previously.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Is there – is there anything we can do?’ Hermione asked, ignoring Ron’s frantic grimaces and head-shakings.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’ think there is, Hermione,’ choked Hagrid, attempting to stem the flood of his tears. ‘See, the rest o’ the tribe … Aragog’s family … they’re gettin’ a bit funny now he’s ill … bit restive …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, I think we saw a bit of that side of them,’ said Ron in an undertone.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘… I don’ reckon it’d be safe fer anyone but me ter go near the colony at the mo’,’ Hagrid finished, blowing his nose hard on his apron and looking up. ‘But thanks fer offerin’, Hermione … it means a lot …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: After that the atmosphere lightened considerably, for although neither Harry nor Ron had shown any inclination to go and feed giant grubs to a murderous, gargantuan spider, Hagrid seemed to take it for granted that they would have liked to have done and became his usual self once more.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ar, I always knew yeh’d find it hard ter squeeze me inter yeh timetables,’ he said gruffly, pouring them more tea. ‘Even if yeh applied fer Time-Turners –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We couldn’t have done,’ said Hermione. ‘We smashed the entire stock of Ministry Time-Turners when we were there in the summer. It was in the Daily Prophet.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ar, well then,’ said Hagrid. ‘There’s no way yeh could’ve done it … I’m sorry I’ve bin – yeh know – I’ve jus’ bin worried abou’ Aragog … an’ I did wonder whether, if Professor Grubbly-Plank had bin teachin’ yeh –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: At which all three of them stated categorically and untruthfully that Professor Grubbly-Plank, who had substituted for Hagrid a few times, was a dreadful teacher, with the result that by the time Hagrid waved them off the premises at dusk, he looked quite cheerful.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m starving,’ said Harry, once the door had closed behind them and they were hurrying through the dark and deserted grounds; he had abandoned the rock cake after an ominous cracking noise from one of his back teeth. ‘And I’ve got that detention with Snape tonight, I haven’t got much time for dinner …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: As they came into the castle they spotted Cormac McLaggen entering the Great Hall. It took him two attempts to get through the doors; he ricocheted off the frame on the first attempt. Ron merely guffawed gloatingly and strode off into the Hall after him, but Harry caught Hermione’s arm and held her back.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ said Hermione defensively.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘If you ask me,’ said Harry quietly, ‘McLaggen looks like he was Confunded. And he was standing right in front of where you were sitting.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione blushed.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, all right then, I did it,’ she whispered. ‘But you should have heard the way he was talking about Ron and Ginny! Anyway, he’s got a nasty temper, you saw how he reacted when he didn’t get in – you wouldn’t have wanted someone like that on the team.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry. ‘No, I suppose that’s true. But wasn’t that dishonest, Hermione? I mean, you’re a prefect, aren’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, be quiet,’ she snapped, as he smirked.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What are you two doing?’ demanded Ron, reappearing in the doorway to the Great Hall and looking suspicious.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Nothing,’ said Harry and Hermione together, and they hurried after Ron. The smell of roast beef made Harry’s stomach ache with hunger, but they had barely taken three steps towards the Gryffindor table when Professor Slughorn appeared in front of them, blocking their path.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, Harry, just the man I was hoping to see!’ he boomed genially, twiddling the ends of his walrus moustache and puffing out his enormous belly. ‘I was hoping to catch you before dinner! What do you say to a spot of supper tonight in my rooms instead? We’re having a little party, just a few rising stars. I’ve got McLaggen coming, and Zabini, the charming Melinda Bobbin – I don’t know whether you know her? Her family owns a large chain of apothecaries – and, of course, I hope very much that Miss Granger will favour me by coming, too.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Slughorn made Hermione a little bow as he finished speaking. It was as though Ron was not present; Slughorn did not so much as look at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I can’t come, Professor,’ said Harry at once. ‘I’ve got a detention with Professor Snape.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh dear!’ said Slughorn, his face falling comically. ‘Dear, dear, I was counting on you, Harry! Well, now, I’ll just have to have a word with Severus and explain the situation, I’m sure I’ll be able to persuade him to postpone your detention. Yes, I’ll see you both later!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He bustled away out of the Hall.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s got no chance of persuading Snape,’ said Harry, the moment Slughorn was out of earshot. ‘This detention’s already been postponed once; Snape did it for Dumbledore, but he won’t do it for anyone else.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I wish you could come, I don’t want to go on my own!’ said Hermione anxiously; Harry knew that she was thinking about McLaggen.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I doubt you’ll be alone, Ginny’ll probably be invited,’ snapped Ron, who did not seem to have taken kindly to being ignored by Slughorn.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: After dinner they made their way back to Gryffindor Tower. The common room was very crowded, as most people had finished dinner by now, but they managed to find a free table and sat down; Ron, who had been in a bad mood ever since the encounter with Slughorn, folded his arms and frowned at the ceiling. Hermione reached out for a copy of the Evening Prophet, which somebody had left abandoned on a chair.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Anything new?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Not really …’ Hermione had opened the newspaper and was scanning the inside pages. ‘Oh, look, your dad’s in here, Ron – he’s all right!’ she added quickly, for Ron had looked round in alarm. ‘It just says he’s been to visit the Malfoys’ house. “This second search of the Death Eater’s residence does not seem to have yielded any results. Arthur Weasley of the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects said that his team had been acting upon a confidential tip-off.”’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, mine!’ said Harry. ‘I told him at King’s Cross about Malfoy and that thing he was trying to get Borgin to fix! Well, if it’s not at their house, he must have brought whatever it is to Hogwarts with him –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But how can he have done, Harry?’ said Hermione, putting down the newspaper with a surprised look. ‘We were all searched when we arrived, weren’t we?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Were you?’ said Harry, taken aback. ‘I wasn’t!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh no, of course you weren’t, I forgot you were late … well, Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the Entrance Hall. Any Dark object would have been found, I know for a fact Crabbe had a shrunken head confiscated. So you see, Malfoy can’t have brought in anything dangerous!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Momentarily stymied, Harry watched Ginny Weasley playing with Arnold the Pygmy Puff for a while before seeing a way around this objection.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Someone’s sent it to him by owl, then,’ he said. ‘His mother or someone.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘All the owls are being checked, too,’ said Hermione. ‘Filch told us so when he was jabbing those Secrecy Sensors everywhere he could reach.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Really stumped this time, Harry found nothing else to say. There did not seem to be any way Malfoy could have brought a dangerous or Dark object into the school. He looked hopefully at Ron, who was sitting with his arms folded, staring over at Lavender Brown.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Can you think of any way Malfoy –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, drop it, Harry,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Listen, it’s not my fault Slughorn invited Hermione and me to his stupid party, neither of us wanted to go, you know!’ said Harry, firing up.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, as I’m not invited to any parties,’ said Ron, getting to his feet again, ‘I think I’ll go to bed.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He stomped off towards the door to the boys’ dormitories, leaving Harry and Hermione staring after him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry?’ said the new Chaser, Demelza Robins, appearing suddenly at his shoulder. ‘I’ve got a message for you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘From Professor Slughorn?’ asked Harry, sitting up hopefully.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No … from Professor Snape,’ said Demelza. Harry’s heart sank. ‘He says you’re to come to his office at half past eight tonight to do your detention – er – no matter how many party invitations you’ve received. And he wanted you to know you’ll be sorting out rotten Flobberworms from good ones, to use in Potions, and – and he says there’s no need to bring protective gloves.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Right,’ said Harry grimly. ‘Thanks a lot, Demelza.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Where was Dumbledore, and what was he doing? Harry caught sight of the Headmaster only twice over the next few weeks. He rarely appeared at meals any more, and Harry was sure Hermione was right in thinking that he was leaving the school for days at a time. Had Dumbledore forgotten the lessons he was supposed to be giving Harry? Dumbledore had said that the lessons were leading to something to do with the prophecy; Harry had felt bolstered, comforted, and now he felt slightly abandoned.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Halfway through October came their first trip of the term to Hogsmeade. Harry had wondered whether these trips would still be allowed, given the increasingly tight security measures around the school, but was pleased to know that they were going ahead; it was always good to get out of the castle grounds for a few hours.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry woke early on the morning of the trip, which was proving stormy, and whiled away the time until breakfast by reading his copy of Advanced Potion-Making. He did not usually lie in bed reading his textbooks; that sort of behaviour, as Ron rightly said, was indecent in anybody except Hermione, who was simply weird that way. Harry felt, however, that the Half-Blood Prince’s copy of Advanced Potion-Making hardly qualified as a textbook. The more Harry pored over the book, the more he realised how much was in there, not only the handy hints and short cuts on potions that were earning him such a glowing reputation with Slughorn, but also the imaginative little jinxes and hexes scribbled in the margins which Harry was sure, judging by the crossings-out and revisions, that the Prince had invented himself.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had already attempted a few of the Prince’s self-invented spells. There had been a hex that caused toenails to grow alarmingly fast (he had tried this on Crabbe in the corridor, with very entertaining results); a jinx that glued the tongue to the roof of the mouth (which he had twice used, to general applause, on an unsuspecting Argus Filch); and, perhaps most useful of all, Muffliato, a spell that filled the ears of anyone nearby with an unidentifiable buzzing, so that lengthy conversations could be held in class without being overheard. The only person who did not find these charms amusing was Hermione, who maintained a rigidly disapproving expression throughout and refused to talk at all if Harry had used the Muffliato spell on anyone in the vicinity.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Sitting up in bed, Harry turned the book sideways so as to examine more closely the scribbled instructions for a spell that seemed to have caused the Prince some trouble. There were many crossings-out and alterations, but finally, crammed into a corner of the page, the scribble:

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Levicorpus (n-vbl)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: While the wind and sleet pounded relentlessly on the windows and Neville snored loudly, Harry stared at the letters in brackets. N-vbl … that had to mean non-verbal. Harry rather doubted he would be able to bring off this particular spell; he was still having difficulty with non-verbal spells, something Snape had been quick to comment on in every DADA class. On the other hand, the Prince had proved a much more effective teacher than Snape so far.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Pointing his wand at nothing in particular, he gave it an upward flick and said Levicorpus! inside his head.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Aaaaaaaargh!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was a flash of light and the room was full of voices: everyone had woken up as Ron had let out a yell. Harry sent Advanced Potion-Making flying in panic; Ron was dangling upside-down in midair as though an invisible hook had hoisted him up by the ankle.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sorry!’ yelled Harry, as Dean and Seamus roared with laughter and Neville picked himself up from the floor, having fallen out of bed. ‘Hang on – I’ll let you down –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He groped for the potion book and riffled through it in a panic, trying to find the right page; at last he located it and deciphered one cramped word underneath the spell: praying that this was the counter-jinx, Harry thought Liberacorpus! with all his might.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was another flash of light and Ron fell in a heap on to his mattress.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sorry,’ repeated Harry weakly, while Dean and Seamus continued to roar with laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Tomorrow,’ said Ron in a muffled voice, ‘I’d rather you set the alarm clock.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: By the time they had got dressed, padding themselves out with several of Mrs Weasley’s hand-knitted sweaters and carrying cloaks, scarves and gloves, Ron’s shock had subsided and he had decided that Harry’s new spell was highly amusing; so amusing, in fact, that he lost no time in regaling Hermione with the story as they sat down for breakfast.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘… and then there was another flash of light and I landed on the bed again!’ grinned Ron, helping himself to sausages.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione had not cracked a smile during this anecdote, and now turned an expression of wintry disapproval upon Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Was this spell, by any chance, another one from that potion book of yours?’ she asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry frowned at her.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Always jump to the worst conclusion, don’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Was it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well … yeah, it was, but so what?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So you just decided to try out an unknown, handwritten incantation and see what would happen?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Why does it matter if it’s handwritten?’ said Harry, preferring not to answer the rest of the question.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Because it’s probably not Ministry of Magic-approved,’ said Hermione. ‘And also,’ she added, as Harry and Ron rolled their eyes, ‘because I’m starting to think this Prince character was a bit dodgy.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Both Harry and Ron shouted her down at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It was a laugh!’ said Ron, up-ending a ketchup bottle over his sausages. ‘Just a laugh, Hermione, that’s all!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Dangling people upside-down by the ankle?’ said Hermione. ‘Who puts their time and energy into making up spells like that?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Fred and George,’ said Ron, shrugging, ‘it’s their kind of thing. And, er –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘My dad,’ said Harry. He had only just remembered.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ said Ron and Hermione together.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘My dad used this spell,’ said Harry. ‘I – Lupin told me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: This last part was not true; in fact, Harry had seen his father use the spell on Snape, but he had never told Ron and Hermione about that particular excursion into the Pensieve. Now, however, a wonderful possibility occurred to him. Could the Half-Blood Prince possibly be –?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Maybe your dad did use it, Harry,’ said Hermione, ‘but he’s not the only one. We’ve seen a whole bunch of people use it, in case you’ve forgotten. Dangling people in the air. Making them float along, asleep, helpless.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry stared at her. With a sinking feeling he, too, remembered the behaviour of the Death Eaters at the Quidditch World Cup. Ron came to his aid.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That was different,’ he said robustly. ‘They were abusing it. Harry and his dad were just having a laugh. You don’t like the Prince, Hermione,’ he added, pointing a sausage at her sternly, ‘because he’s better than you at Potions –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s got nothing to do with that!’ said Hermione, her cheeks reddening. ‘I just think it’s very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don’t even know what they’re for, and stop talking about “the Prince” as if it’s his title, I bet it’s just a stupid nickname and it doesn’t seem as though he was a very nice person to me!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t see where you get that from,’ said Harry heatedly, ‘if he’d been a budding Death Eater he wouldn’t have been boasting about being “Half-Blood”, would he?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Even as he said it, Harry remembered that his father had been pure-blood, but he pushed the thought out of his mind; he would worry about that later …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left,’ said Hermione stubbornly. ‘I expect most of them are half-bloods pretending to be pure. It’s only Muggle-borns they hate, they’d be quite happy to let you and Ron join up.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There is no way they’d let me be a Death Eater!’ said Ron indignantly, a bit of sausage flying off the fork he was now brandishing at Hermione and hitting Ernie Macmillan on the head. ‘My whole family are blood traitors! That’s as bad as Muggle-borns to Death Eaters!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And they’d love to have me,’ said Harry sarcastically. ‘We’d be best pals if they didn’t keep trying to do me in.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: This made Ron laugh; even Hermione gave a grudging smile, and a distraction arrived in the shape of Ginny.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hey, Harry, I’m supposed to give you this.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: It was a scroll of parchment with Harry’s name written upon it in familiar thin, slanting writing.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Thanks, Ginny … it’s Dumbledore’s next lesson!’ Harry told Ron and Hermione, pulling open the parchment and quickly reading its contents. ‘Monday evening!’ He felt suddenly light and happy. ‘Want to join us in Hogsmeade, Ginny?’ he asked.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m going with Dean – might see you there,’ she replied, waving at them as she left.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Filch was standing at the oak front doors as usual, checking off the names of people who had permission to go into Hogsmeade. The process took even longer than normal as Filch was triple-checking everybody with his Secrecy Sensor.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What does it matter if we’re smuggling Dark stuff OUT?’ demanded Ron, eyeing the long thin Secrecy Sensor with apprehension. ‘Surely you ought to be checking what we bring back IN?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: His cheek earned him a few extra jabs with the Sensor, and he was still wincing as they stepped out into the wind and sleet.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The walk into Hogsmeade was not enjoyable. Harry wrapped his scarf over his lower face; the exposed part soon felt both raw and numb. The road to the village was full of students bent double against the bitter wind. More than once Harry wondered whether they might not have had a better time in the warm common room, and when they finally reached Hogsmeade and saw that Zonko’s Joke Shop had been boarded up, Harry took it as confirmation that this trip was not destined to be fun. Ron pointed with a thickly gloved hand towards Honeydukes, which was mercifully open, and Harry and Hermione staggered in his wake into the crowded shop.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Thank God,’ shivered Ron as they were enveloped by warm, toffee-scented air. ‘Let’s stay here all afternoon.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, m’boy!’ said a booming voice from behind them.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, no,’ muttered Harry. The three of them turned to see Professor Slughorn, who was wearing an enormous furry hat and overcoat with matching fur collar, clutching a large bag of crystallised pineapple and occupying at least a quarter of the shop.

text_content: ‘Harry, that’s three of my little suppers you’ve missed now!’ said Slughorn, poking him genially in the chest. ‘It won’t do, m’boy, I’m determined to have you! Miss Granger loves them, don’t you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Hermione helplessly, ‘they’re really –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So why don’t you come along, Harry?’ demanded Slughorn.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I’ve had Quidditch practice, Professor,’ said Harry, who had indeed been scheduling practices every time Slughorn had sent him a little violet-ribbon-adorned invitation. This strategy meant that Ron was not left out and they usually had a laugh with Ginny imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, I certainly expect you to win your first match after all this hard work!’ said Slughorn. ‘But a little recreation never hurt anybody. Now, how about Monday night, you can’t possibly want to practise in this weather …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I can’t, Professor, I’ve got – er – an appointment with Professor Dumbledore that evening.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Unlucky again!’ cried Slughorn dramatically. ‘Ah, well … you can’t evade me for ever, Harry!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And with a regal wave, he waddled out of the shop, taking as little notice of Ron as though he had been a display of Cockroach Cluster.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I can’t believe you’ve wriggled out of another one,’ said Hermione, shaking her head. ‘They’re not that bad, you know … they’re even quite fun sometimes …’ But then she caught sight of Ron’s expression. ‘Oh, look – they’ve got Deluxe Sugar Quills – those would last hours!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Glad that Hermione had changed the subject, Harry showed much more interest in the new extra-large Sugar Quills than he would normally have done, but Ron continued to look moody and merely shrugged when Hermione asked him where he wanted to go next.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Let’s go to the Three Broomsticks,’ said Harry. ‘It’ll be warm.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: They bundled their scarves back over their faces and left the sweet shop. The bitter wind was like knives on their faces after the sugary warmth of Honeydukes. The street was not very busy; nobody was lingering to chat, just hurrying towards their destinations. The exceptions were two men a little ahead of them, standing just outside the Three Broomsticks. One was very tall and thin; squinting through his rain-washed glasses Harry recognised the barman who worked in the other Hogsmeade pub, the Hog’s Head. As Harry, Ron and Hermione drew closer, the barman drew his cloak more tightly around his neck and walked away, leaving the shorter man to fumble with something in his arms. They were barely feet from him when Harry realised who the man was.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Mundungus!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The squat, bandy-legged man with long straggly ginger hair jumped and dropped an ancient suitcase, which burst open, releasing what looked like the entire contents of a junk shop window.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, ’ello, ’Arry,’ said Mundungus Fletcher, with a most unconvincing stab at airiness. ‘Well, don’t let me keep ya.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And he began scrabbling on the ground to retrieve the contents of his suitcase with every appearance of a man eager to be gone.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you selling this stuff?’ asked Harry, watching Mundungus grabbing an assortment of grubby-looking objects from the ground.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, well, gotta scrape a living,’ said Mundungus. ‘Gimme that!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron had stooped down and picked up something silver.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hang on,’ Ron said slowly. ‘This looks familiar –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Thank you!’ said Mundungus, snatching the goblet out of Ron’s hand and stuffing it back into the case. ‘Well, I’ll see you all – OUCH!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had pinned Mundungus against the wall of the pub by the throat. Holding him fast with one hand, he pulled out his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry!’ squealed Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You took that from Sirius’s house,’ said Harry, who was almost nose-to-nose with Mundungus and was breathing in an unpleasant smell of old tobacco and spirits. ‘That had the Black family crest on it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I – no – what –?’ spluttered Mundungus, who was turning slowly purple.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What did you do, go back the night he died and strip the place?’ snarled Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I – no –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Give it to me!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, you mustn’t!’ shrieked Hermione, as Mundungus started to turn blue.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was a bang and Harry felt his hands fly off Mundungus’s throat. Gasping and spluttering, Mundungus seized his fallen case, then – CRACK – he Disapparated.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry swore at the top of his voice, spinning on the spot to see where Mundungus had gone.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘COME BACK, YOU THIEVING –!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There’s no point, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Tonks had appeared out of nowhere, her mousy hair wet with sleet.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Mundungus will probably be in London by now. There’s no point yelling.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s nicked Sirius’s stuff! Nicked it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, but still,’ said Tonks, who seemed perfectly untroubled by this piece of information, ‘you should get out of the cold.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She watched them through the door of the Three Broomsticks. The moment he was inside, Harry burst out, ‘He was nicking Sirius’s stuff!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I know, Harry, but please don’t shout, people are staring,’ whispered Hermione. ‘Go and sit down, I’ll get you a drink.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry was still fuming when Hermione returned to their table a few minutes later holding three bottles of Butterbeer.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Can’t the Order control Mundungus?’ Harry demanded of the other two in a furious whisper. ‘Can’t they at least stop him stealing everything that’s not fixed down when he’s at Headquarters?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Shh!’ said Hermione desperately, looking around to make sure nobody was listening; there were a couple of warlocks sitting close by who were staring at Harry with great interest, and Zabini was lolling against a pillar not far away. ‘Harry, I’d be annoyed too, I know it’s your things he’s stealing –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry gagged on his Butterbeer; he had momentarily forgotten that he owned number twelve, Grimmauld Place.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, it’s my stuff!’ he said. ‘No wonder he wasn’t pleased to see me! Well, I’m going to tell Dumbledore what’s going on, he’s the only one who scares Mundungus.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good idea,’ whispered Hermione, clearly pleased that Harry was calming down. ‘Ron, what are you staring at?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Nothing,’ said Ron, hastily looking away from the bar, but Harry knew he was trying to catch the eye of the curvy and attractive barmaid, Madam Rosmerta, for whom he had long nursed a soft spot.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I expect “nothing”’s in the back getting more Firewhisky,’ said Hermione waspishly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron ignored this jibe, sipping his drink in what he evidently considered to be a dignified silence. Harry was thinking about Sirius, and how he had hated those silver goblets anyway. Hermione drummed her fingers on the table, her eyes flickering between Ron and the bar.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The moment Harry drained the last drops in his bottle she said, ‘Shall we call it a day and go back to school, then?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The other two nodded; it had not been a fun trip and the weather was getting worse the longer they stayed. Once again they drew their cloaks tightly around them, rearranged their scarves, pulled on their gloves; then followed Katie Bell and a friend out of the pub and back up the High Street. Harry’s thoughts strayed to Ginny as they trudged up the road to Hogwarts through the frozen slush. They had not met up with her, undoubtedly, thought Harry, because she and Dean were cosily closeted in Madam Puddifoot’s teashop, that haunt of happy couples. Scowling, he bowed his head against the swirling sleet and trudged on.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: It was a little while before Harry became aware that the voices of Katie Bell and her friend, which were being carried back to him on the wind, had become shriller and louder. Harry squinted at their indistinct figures. The two girls were having an argument about something Katie was holding in her hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s nothing to do with you, Leanne!’ Harry heard Katie say.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: They rounded a corner in the lane, sleet coming thick and fast, blurring Harry’s glasses. Just as he raised a gloved hand to wipe them, Leanne made to grab hold of the package Katie was holding; Katie tugged it back and the package fell to the ground.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: At once, Katie rose into the air, not as Ron had done, suspended comically by the ankle, but gracefully, her arms outstretched, as though she were about to fly. Yet there was something wrong, something eerie … her hair was whipped around her by the fierce wind, but her eyes were closed and her face was quite empty of expression. Harry, Ron, Hermione and Leanne had all halted in their tracks, watching.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Then, six feet above the ground, Katie let out a terrible scream. Her eyes flew open but whatever she could see, or whatever she was feeling, was clearly causing her terrible anguish. She screamed and screamed; Leanne started to scream too, and seized Katie’s ankles, trying to tug her back to the ground. Harry, Ron and Hermione rushed forwards to help, but even as they grabbed Katie’s legs, she fell on top of them; Harry and Ron managed to catch her but she was writhing so much they could hardly hold her. Instead they lowered her to the ground where she thrashed and screamed, apparently unable to recognise any of them.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked around; the landscape seemed deserted.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Stay there!’ he shouted at the others over the howling wind. ‘I’m going for help!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He began to sprint towards the school; he had never seen anyone behave as Katie had just done and could not think what had caused it; he hurtled round a bend in the lane and collided with what seemed to be an enormous bear on its hind legs.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid!’ he panted, disentangling himself from the hedgerow into which he had fallen.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid, someone’s hurt back there, or cursed, or something –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Cursed? Who’s bin cursed – not Ron? Hermione?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, it’s not them, it’s Katie Bell – this way …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
