book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Get back!’ shouted Hagrid. ‘Lemme see her!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Something’s happened to her!’ sobbed Leanne. ‘I don’t know what –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hagrid stared at Katie for a second, then, without a word, bent down, scooped her into his arms and ran off towards the castle with her. Within seconds, Katie’s piercing screams had died away and the only sound was the roar of the wind.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione hurried over to Katie’s wailing friend and put an arm around her.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s Leanne, isn’t it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The girl nodded.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Did it just happen all of a sudden, or –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It was when that package tore,’ sobbed Leanne, pointing at the now sodden brown-paper package on the ground, which had split open to reveal a greenish glitter. Ron bent down, his hand outstretched, but Harry seized his arm and pulled him back.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t touch it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He crouched down. An ornate opal necklace was visible, poking out of the paper.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve seen that before,’ said Harry, staring at the thing. ‘It was on display in Borgin and Burkes ages ago. The label said it was cursed. Katie must have touched it.’ He looked up at Leanne, who had started to shake uncontrollably. ‘How did Katie get hold of this?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, that’s why we were arguing. She came back from the bathroom in the Three Broomsticks holding it, said it was a surprise for somebody at Hogwarts and she had to deliver it. She looked all funny when she said it … oh no, oh no, I bet she’d been Imperiused, and I didn’t realise!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Leanne shook with renewed sobs. Hermione patted her shoulder gently.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She didn’t say who’d given it to her, Leanne?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No … she wouldn’t tell me … and I said she was being stupid and not to take it up to school, but she just wouldn’t listen and … and then I tried to grab it from her … and – and –’ Leanne let out a wail of despair.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We’d better get up to school,’ said Hermione, her arm still around Leanne, ‘we’ll be able to find out how she is. Come on …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry hesitated for a moment, then pulled his scarf from around his face and, ignoring Ron’s gasp, carefully covered the necklace in it and picked it up.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We’ll need to show this to Madam Pomfrey,’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: As they followed Hermione and Leanne up the road, Harry was thinking furiously. They had just entered the grounds when he spoke, unable to keep his thoughts to himself any longer.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Malfoy knows about this necklace. It was in a case at Borgin and Burkes four years ago, I saw him having a good look at it while I was hiding from him and his dad. This is what he was buying that day when we followed him! He remembered it and he went back for it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I – I dunno, Harry,’ said Ron hesitantly. ‘Loads of people go to Borgin and Burkes … and didn’t that girl say Katie got it in the girls’ bathroom?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She said she came back from the bathroom with it, she didn’t necessarily get it in the bathroom itself –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘McGonagall!’ said Ron warningly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked up. Sure enough, Professor McGonagall was hurrying down the stone steps through swirling sleet to meet them.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hagrid says you four saw what happened to Katie Bell – upstairs to my office at once, please! What’s that you’re holding, Potter?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s the thing she touched,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good Lord,’ said Professor McGonagall, looking alarmed as she took the necklace from Harry. ‘No, no, Filch, they’re with me!’ she added hastily, as Filch came shuffling eagerly across the Entrance Hall holding his Secrecy Sensor aloft. ‘Take this necklace to Professor Snape at once, but be sure not to touch it, keep it wrapped in the scarf!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry and the others followed Professor McGonagall upstairs and into her office. The sleet-spattered windows were rattling in their frames and the room was chilly despite the fire crackling in the grate. Professor McGonagall closed the door and swept round her desk to face Harry, Ron, Hermione and the still-sobbing Leanne.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well?’ she said sharply. ‘What happened?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Haltingly, and with many pauses while she attempted to control her crying, Leanne told Professor McGonagall how Katie had gone to the bathroom in the Three Broomsticks and returned holding the unmarked package, how Katie had seemed a little odd and how they had argued about the advisability of agreeing to deliver unknown objects, the argument culminating in the tussle over the parcel, which tore open. At this point, Leanne was so overcome there was no getting another word out of her.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘All right,’ said Professor McGonagall, not unkindly, ‘go up to the hospital wing, please, Leanne, and get Madam Pomfrey to give you something for shock.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: When she had left the room, Professor McGonagall turned back to Harry, Ron and Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What happened when Katie touched the necklace?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She rose up in the air,’ said Harry, before either Ron or Hermione could speak. ‘And then began to scream, and collapsed. Professor, can I see Professor Dumbledore, please?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The Headmaster is away until Monday, Potter,’ said Professor McGonagall, looking surprised.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Away?’ Harry repeated angrily.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, Potter, away!’ said Professor McGonagall tartly. ‘But anything you have to say about this horrible business can be said to me, I’m sure!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: For a split second, Harry hesitated. Professor McGonagall did not invite confidences; Dumbledore, though in many ways more intimidating, still seemed less likely to scorn a theory, however wild. This was a life and death matter, though, and no moment to worry about being laughed at.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I think Draco Malfoy gave Katie that necklace, Professor.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: On one side of him, Ron rubbed his nose in apparent embarrassment; on the other, Hermione shuffled her feet as though quite keen to put a bit of distance between herself and Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That is a very serious accusation, Potter,’ said Professor McGonagall, after a shocked pause. ‘Do you have any proof?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry, ‘but …’ and he told her about following Malfoy to Borgin and Burkes and the conversation they had overheard between him and Borgin.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: When he had finished speaking, Professor McGonagall looked slightly confused.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Malfoy took something to Borgin and Burkes for repair?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, Professor, he just wanted Borgin to tell him how to mend something, he didn’t have it with him. But that’s not the point, the thing is that he bought something at the same time and I think it was that necklace –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You saw Malfoy leaving the shop with a similar package?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, Professor, he told Borgin to keep it in the shop for him –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But, Harry,’ Hermione interrupted, ‘Borgin asked him if he wanted to take it with him, and Malfoy said “no” –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Because he didn’t want to touch it, obviously!’ said Harry angrily.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What he actually said was, “How would I look carrying that down the street?”,’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, he would look a bit of a prat carrying a necklace,’ interjected Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, Ron,’ said Hermione despairingly, ‘it would be all wrapped up, so he wouldn’t have to touch it, and quite easy to hide inside a cloak, so nobody would see it! I think whatever he reserved at Borgin and Burkes was noisy or bulky; something he knew would draw attention to him if he carried it down the street – and in any case,’ she pressed on loudly, before Harry could interrupt, ‘I asked Borgin about the necklace, don’t you remember? When I went in to try and find out what Malfoy had asked him to keep, I saw it there. And Borgin just told me the price, he didn’t say it was already sold or anything –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, you were being really obvious, he realised what you were up to within about five seconds, of course he wasn’t going to tell you – anyway, Malfoy could’ve sent off for it since –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s enough!’ said Professor McGonagall, as Hermione opened her mouth to retort, looking furious. ‘Potter, I appreciate you telling me this, but we cannot point the finger of blame at Mr Malfoy purely because he visited the shop where this necklace might have been purchased. The same is probably true of hundreds of people –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– that’s what I said –’ muttered Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– and in any case, we have put stringent security measures in place this year, I do not believe that necklace can possibly have entered this school without our knowledge –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– but –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– and what is more,’ said Professor McGonagall, with an air of awful finality, ‘Mr Malfoy was not in Hogsmeade today.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry gaped at her, deflating.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘How do you know, Professor?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Because he was doing detention with me. He has now failed to complete his Transfiguration homework twice in a row. So, thank you for telling me your suspicions, Potter,’ she said as she marched past them, ‘but I need to go up to the hospital wing now to check on Katie Bell. Good day to you all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She held open her office door. They had no choice but to file past her without another word.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry was angry with the other two for siding with McGonagall; nevertheless, he felt compelled to join in once they started discussing what had happened.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So who do you reckon Katie was supposed to give the necklace to?’ asked Ron, as they climbed the stairs to the common room.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Goodness only knows,’ said Hermione. ‘But whoever it was has had a narrow escape. No one could have opened that package without touching the necklace.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It could’ve been meant for loads of people,’ said Harry. ‘Dumbledore – the Death Eaters would love to get rid of him, he must be one of their top targets. Or Slughorn – Dumbledore reckons Voldemort really wanted him and they can’t be pleased that he’s sided with Dumbledore. Or –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Or you,’ said Hermione, looking troubled.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Couldn’t have been,’ said Harry, ‘or Katie would’ve just turned round in the lane and given it to me, wouldn’t she? I was behind her all the way out of the Three Broomsticks. It would have made much more sense to deliver the parcel outside Hogwarts, what with Filch searching everyone who goes in and out. I wonder why Malfoy told her to take it into the castle?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, Malfoy wasn’t in Hogsmeade!’ said Hermione, actually stamping her foot in frustration.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He must have used an accomplice, then,’ said Harry. ‘Crabbe or Goyle – or, come to think of it, another Death Eater, he’ll have loads better cronies than Crabbe and Goyle now he’s joined up –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron and Hermione exchanged looks that plainly said ‘there’s no point arguing with him’.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Dilligrout,’ said Hermione firmly, as they reached the Fat Lady.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The portrait swung open to admit them to the common room. It was quite full and smelled of damp clothing; many people seemed to have returned from Hogsmeade early because of the bad weather. There was no buzz of fear or speculation, however: clearly, the news of Katie’s fate had not yet spread.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It wasn’t a very slick attack, really, when you stop and think about it,’ said Ron, casually turfing a first-year out of one of the good armchairs by the fire, so that he could sit down. ‘The curse didn’t even make it into the castle. Not what you’d call foolproof.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re right,’ said Hermione, prodding Ron out of the chair with her foot and offering it to the first-year again. ‘It wasn’t very well-thought-out at all.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But since when has Malfoy been one of the world’s great thinkers?’ asked Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Neither Ron nor Hermione answered him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Katie was removed to St Mungo’s Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries the following day, by which time the news that she had been cursed had spread all over the school, though the details were confused and nobody other than Harry, Ron, Hermione and Leanne seemed to know that Katie herself had not been the intended target.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, and Malfoy knows, of course,’ said Harry to Ron and Hermione, who continued their new policy of feigning deafness whenever Harry mentioned his Malfoy-is-a-Death-Eater theory.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had wondered whether Dumbledore would return from wherever he had been in time for Monday night’s lesson, but having had no word to the contrary, he presented himself outside Dumbledore’s office at eight o’clock, knocked, and was told to enter. There sat Dumbledore, looking unusually tired; his hand was as black and burned as ever, but he smiled when he gestured to Harry to sit down. The Pensieve was sitting on the desk again, casting silvery specks of light over the ceiling.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You have had a busy time while I have been away,’ Dumbledore said. ‘I believe you witnessed Katie’s accident.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, sir. How is she?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Still very unwell, although she was relatively lucky. She appears to have brushed the necklace with the smallest possible amount of skin: there was a tiny hole in her glove. Had she put it on, had she even held it in her ungloved hand, she would have died, perhaps instantly. Luckily Professor Snape was able to do enough to prevent a rapid spread of the curse –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Why him?’ asked Harry quickly. ‘Why not Madam Pomfrey?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Impertinent,’ said a soft voice from one of the portraits on the wall, and Phineas Nigellus Black, Sirius’s great-great-grandfather, raised his head from his arms where he had appeared to be sleeping. ‘I would not have permitted a student to question the way Hogwarts operated in my day.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, thank you, Phineas,’ said Dumbledore quellingly. ‘Professor Snape knows much more about the Dark Arts than Madam Pomfrey, Harry. Anyway, the St Mungo’s staff are sending me hourly reports and I am hopeful that Katie will make a full recovery in time.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Where were you this weekend, sir?’ Harry asked, disregarding a strong feeling that he might be pushing his luck, a feeling apparently shared by Phineas Nigellus, who hissed softly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I would rather not say just now,’ said Dumbledore. ‘However, I shall tell you in due course.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You will?’ said Harry, startled.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, I expect so,’ said Dumbledore, withdrawing a fresh bottle of silver memories from inside his robes and uncorking it with a prod of his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir,’ said Harry tentatively, ‘I met Mundungus in Hogsmeade.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ah, yes, I am already aware that Mundungus has been treating your inheritance with light-fingered contempt,’ said Dumbledore, frowning a little. ‘He has gone to ground since you accosted him outside the Three Broomsticks; I rather think he dreads facing me. However, rest assured that he will not be making away with any more of Sirius’s old possessions.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That mangy old half-blood has been stealing Black heirlooms?’ said Phineas Nigellus, incensed; and he stalked out of his frame, undoubtedly to visit his portrait in number twelve, Grimmauld Place.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor,’ said Harry, after a short pause, ‘did Professor McGonagall tell you what I told her after Katie got hurt? About Draco Malfoy?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She told me of your suspicions, yes,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And do you –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I shall take all appropriate measures to investigate anyone who might have had a hand in Katie’s accident,’ said Dumbledore. ‘But what concerns me now, Harry, is our lesson.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry felt slightly resentful at this: if their lessons were so very important, why had there been such a long gap between the first and second? However, he said no more about Draco Malfoy, but watched as Dumbledore poured the fresh memories into the Pensieve, and began swirling the stone basin once more between his long-fingered hands.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You will remember, I am sure, that we left the tale of Lord Voldemort’s beginnings at the point where the handsome Muggle, Tom Riddle, had abandoned his witch wife, Merope, and returned to his family home in Little Hangleton. Merope was left alone in London, expecting the baby who would one day become Lord Voldemort.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘How do you know she was in London, sir?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Because of the evidence of one Caractacus Burke,’ said Dumbledore, ‘who, by an odd coincidence, helped found the very shop whence came the necklace we have just been discussing.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He swilled the contents of the Pensieve as Harry had seen him swill them before, much as a gold prospector sifts for gold. Up out of the swirling, silvery mass rose a little old man, revolving slowly in the Pensieve, silver as a ghost but much more solid, with a thatch of hair that completely covered his eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, we acquired it in curious circumstances. It was brought in by a young witch just before Christmas, oh, many years ago now. She said she needed the gold badly, well, that much was obvious. Covered in rags and pretty far along … going to have a baby, see. She said the locket had been Slytherin’s. Well, we hear that sort of story all the time, “Oh, this was Merlin’s, this was, his favourite teapot,” but when I looked at it, it had his mark all right, and a few simple spells were enough to tell me the truth. Of course, that made it near enough priceless. She didn’t seem to have any idea how much it was worth. Happy to get ten Galleons for it. Best bargain we ever made!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore gave the Pensieve an extra-vigorous shake and Caractacus Burke descended back into the swirling mass of memory whence he had come.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He only gave her ten Galleons?’ said Harry indignantly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Caractacus Burke was not famed for his generosity,’ said Dumbledore. ‘So we know that, near the end of her pregnancy, Merope was alone in London and in desperate need of gold, desperate enough to sell her one and only valuable possession, the locket that was one of Marvolo’s treasured family heirlooms.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But she could do magic!’ said Harry impatiently. ‘She could have got food and everything for herself by magic, couldn’t she?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ah,’ said Dumbledore, ‘perhaps she could. But it is my belief – I am guessing again, but I am sure I am right – that when her husband abandoned her, Merope stopped using magic. I do not think that she wanted to be a witch any longer. Of course, it is also possible that her unrequited love and the attendant despair sapped her of her powers; that can happen. In any case, as you are about to see, Merope refused to raise her wand even to save her own life.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She wouldn’t even stay alive for her son?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore raised his eyebrows.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Could you possibly be feeling sorry for Lord Voldemort?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Harry quickly, ‘but she had a choice, didn’t she, not like my mother –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Your mother had a choice, too,’ said Dumbledore gently. ‘Yes, Merope Riddle chose death in spite of a son who needed her, but do not judge her too harshly, Harry. She was greatly weakened by long suffering and she never had your mother’s courage. And now, if you will stand …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Where are we going?’ Harry asked, as Dumbledore joined him at the front of the desk.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘This time,’ said Dumbledore, ‘we are going to enter my memory. I think you will find it both rich in detail and satisfyingly accurate. After you, Harry …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry bent over the Pensieve; his face broke the cool surface of the memory and then he was falling through darkness again … Seconds later his feet hit firm ground, he opened his eyes and found that he and Dumbledore were standing in a bustling, old-fashioned London street.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There I am,’ said Dumbledore brightly, pointing ahead of them to a tall figure crossing the road in front of a horse-drawn milk cart.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: This younger Albus Dumbledore’s long hair and beard were auburn. Having reached their side of the street, he strode off along the pavement, drawing many curious glances due to the flamboyantly cut suit of plum velvet that he was wearing.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Nice suit, sir,’ said Harry, before he could stop himself, but Dumbledore merely chuckled as they followed his younger self a short distance, finally passing through a set of iron gates into a bare courtyard that fronted a rather grim, square building surrounded by high railings. He mounted the few steps leading to the front door and knocked once. After a moment or two the door was opened by a scruffy girl wearing an apron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good afternoon. I have an appointment with a Mrs Cole, who, I believe, is the matron here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ said the bewildered-looking girl, taking in Dumbledore’s eccentric appearance. ‘Um … just a mo’ … MRS COLE!’ she bellowed over her shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry heard a distant voice shouting something in response. The girl turned back to Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Come in, she’s on ’er way.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore stepped into a hallway tiled in black and white; the whole place was shabby but spotlessly clean. Harry and the older Dumbledore followed. Before the front door had closed behind them, a skinny, harassed-looking woman came scurrying towards them. She had a sharp-featured face that appeared more anxious than unkind and she was talking over her shoulder to another aproned helper as she walked towards Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘… and take the iodine upstairs to Martha, Billy Stubbs has been picking his scabs and Eric Whalley’s oozing all over his sheets – chicken pox on top of everything else,’ she said to nobody in particular, and then her eyes fell upon Dumbledore and she stopped dead in her tracks, looking as astonished as if a giraffe had just crossed her threshold.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good afternoon,’ said Dumbledore, holding out his hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Mrs Cole simply gaped.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘My name is Albus Dumbledore. I sent you a letter requesting an appointment and you very kindly invited me here today.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Mrs Cole blinked. Apparently deciding that Dumbledore was not a hallucination, she said feebly, ‘Oh, yes. Well – well, then – you’d better come into my room. Yes.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She led Dumbledore into a small room that seemed part sitting room, part office. It was as shabby as the hallway and the furniture was old and mismatched. She invited Dumbledore to sit on a rickety chair and seated herself behind a cluttered desk, eyeing him nervously.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I am here, as I told you in my letter, to discuss Tom Riddle and arrangements for his future,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you family?’ asked Mrs Cole.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, I am a teacher,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I have come to offer Tom a place at my school.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What school’s this, then?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It is called Hogwarts,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And how come you’re interested in Tom?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We believe he has qualities we are looking for.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You mean he’s won a scholarship? How can he have done? He’s never been entered for one.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, his name has been down for our school since birth –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Who registered him? His parents?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was no doubt that Mrs Cole was an inconveniently sharp woman. Apparently Dumbledore thought so too, for Harry now saw him slip his wand out of the pocket of his velvet suit, at the same time picking up a piece of perfectly blank paper from Mrs Cole’s desktop.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Here,’ said Dumbledore, waving his wand once as he passed her the piece of paper, ‘I think this will make everything clear.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Mrs Cole’s eyes slid out of focus and back again as she gazed intently at the blank paper for a moment.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That seems perfectly in order,’ she said placidly, handing it back. Then her eyes fell upon a bottle of gin and two glasses that had certainly not been present a few seconds before.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Er – may I offer you a glass of gin?’ she said in an extra-refined voice.

text_content: ‘Nearly time,’ said Harry blithely.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The frosty grass crunched underfoot as they strode down to the stadium.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Pretty lucky the weather’s this good, eh?’ Harry asked Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Ron, who was pale and sick-looking.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ginny and Demelza were already wearing their Quidditch robes and waiting in the changing room.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Conditions look ideal,’ said Ginny, ignoring Ron. ‘And guess what? That Slytherin Chaser Vaisey – he took a Bludger in the head yesterday during their practice, and he’s too sore to play! And even better than that – Malfoy’s gone off sick too!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ said Harry, wheeling round to stare at her. ‘He’s ill? What’s wrong with him?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No idea, but it’s great for us,’ said Ginny brightly. ‘They’re playing Harper instead; he’s in my year and he’s an idiot.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry smiled vaguely back, but as he pulled on his scarlet robes his mind was far from Quidditch. Malfoy had once before claimed he could not play due to injury, but on that occasion he had made sure the whole match was rescheduled for a time that suited the Slytherins better. Why was he now happy to let a substitute go on? Was he really ill, or was he faking?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Fishy, isn’t it?’ he said in an undertone to Ron. ‘Malfoy not playing?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Lucky, I call it,’ said Ron, looking slightly more animated. ‘And Vaisey off too, he’s their best goal-scorer, I didn’t fancy – hey!’ he said suddenly, freezing halfway through pulling on his Keeper’s gloves and staring at Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I … you …’ Ron had dropped his voice; he looked both scared and excited. ‘My drink … my pumpkin juice … you didn’t …?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry raised his eyebrows, but said nothing except, ‘We’ll be starting in about five minutes, you’d better get your boots on.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: They walked out on to the pitch to tumultuous roars and boos. One end of the stadium was solid red and gold; the other, a sea of green and silver. Many Hufflepuffs and Ravenclaws had taken sides, too: amidst all the yelling and clapping Harry could distinctly hear the roar of Luna Lovegood’s famous lion-topped hat.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry stepped up to Madam Hooch, the referee, who was standing ready to release the balls from the crate.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Captains, shake hands,’ she said, and Harry had his hand crushed by the new Slytherin Captain, Urquhart. ‘Mount your brooms. On the whistle … three … two … one …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The whistle sounded, Harry and the others kicked off hard from the frozen ground, and they were away.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry soared around the perimeter of the grounds looking for the Snitch and keeping one eye on Harper, who was zigzagging far below him. Then a voice that was jarringly different from the usual commentator’s started up.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, there they go, and I think we’re all surprised to see the team that Potter’s put together this year. Many thought, given Ronald Weasley’s patchy performance as Keeper last year, that he might be off the team, but of course, a close personal friendship with the Captain does help …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: These words were greeted with jeers and applause from the Slytherin end of the pitch. Harry craned round on his broom to look towards the commentator’s podium. A tall, skinny blond boy with an upturned nose was standing there, talking into the magical megaphone that had once been Lee Jordan’s; Harry recognised Zacharias Smith, a Hufflepuff player whom he heartily disliked.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, and here comes Slytherin’s first attempt on goal, it’s Urquhart streaking down the pitch and –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry’s stomach turned over.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– Weasley saves it, well, he’s bound to get lucky sometimes, I suppose …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s right, Smith, he is,’ muttered Harry, grinning to himself, as he dived amongst the Chasers with his eyes searching all around for some hint of the elusive Snitch.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: With half an hour of the game gone, Gryffindor were leading sixty points to zero, Ron having made some truly spectacular saves, some by the very tips of his gloves, and Ginny having scored four of Gryffindor’s six goals. This effectively stopped Zacharias wondering loudly whether the two Weasleys were only there because Harry liked them, and he started on Peakes and Coote instead.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course, Coote isn’t really the usual build for a Beater,’ said Zacharias loftily, ‘they’ve generally got a bit more muscle –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hit a Bludger at him!’ Harry called to Coote as he zoomed past, but Coote, grinning broadly, chose to aim the next Bludger at Harper instead, who was just passing Harry in the opposite direction. Harry was pleased to hear the dull thunk that meant the Bludger had found its mark.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: It seemed as though Gryffindor could do no wrong. Again and again they scored, and again and again, at the other end of the pitch, Ron saved goals with apparent ease. He was actually smiling now, and when the crowd greeted a particularly good save with a rousing chorus of the old favourite Weasley is our King, he pretended to conduct them from on high.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Thinks he’s something special today, doesn’t he?’ said a snide voice, and Harry was nearly knocked off his broom as Harper collided with him hard and deliberately. ‘Your blood-traitor pal …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Madam Hooch’s back was turned, and though Gryffindors below shouted in anger, by the time she looked round Harper had already sped off. His shoulder aching, Harry raced after him, determined to ram him back …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And I think Harper of Slytherin’s seen the Snitch!’ said Zacharias Smith through his megaphone. ‘Yes, he’s certainly seen something Potter hasn’t!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Smith really was an idiot, thought Harry, hadn’t he noticed them collide? But next moment, his stomach seemed to drop out of the sky – Smith was right and Harry was wrong: Harper had not sped upwards at random; he had spotted what Harry had not: the Snitch was speeding along high above them, glinting brightly against the clear blue sky.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry accelerated; the wind was whistling in his ears so that it drowned all sound of Smith’s commentary or the crowd, but Harper was still ahead of him, and Gryffindor was only a hundred points up; if Harper got there first Gryffindor had lost … and now Harper was feet from it, his hand outstretched …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oi, Harper!’ yelled Harry in desperation. ‘How much did Malfoy pay you to come on instead of him?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He did not know what made him say it, but Harper did a double take; he fumbled the Snitch, let it slip through his fingers and shot right past it: Harry made a great swipe for the tiny, fluttering ball and caught it.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘YES!’ Harry yelled: wheeling round, he hurtled back towards the ground, the Snitch held high in his hand. As the crowd realised what had happened, a great shout went up that almost drowned the sound of the whistle that signalled the end of the game.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ginny, where’re you going?’ yelled Harry, who had found himself trapped in the midst of a mass midair hug with the rest of the team, but Ginny sped right on past them until, with an almighty crash, she collided with the commentator’s podium. As the crowd shrieked and laughed, the Gryffindor team landed beside the wreckage of wood under which Zacharias was feebly stirring; Harry heard Ginny saying blithely to an irate Professor McGonagall, ‘Forgot to brake, Professor, sorry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Laughing, Harry broke free of the rest of the team and hugged Ginny, but let go very quickly. Avoiding her gaze, he clapped a cheering Ron on the back instead as, all enmity forgotten, the Gryffindor team left the pitch arm in arm, punching the air and waving to their supporters.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The atmosphere in the changing room was jubilant.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Party up in the common room, Seamus said!’ yelled Dean exuberantly. ‘C’mon, Ginny, Demelza!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron and Harry were the last two in the changing room. They were just about to leave when Hermione entered. She was twisting her Gryffindor scarf in her hands and looked upset but determined.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I want a word with you, Harry.’ She took a deep breath. ‘You shouldn’t have done it. You heard Slughorn, it’s illegal.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What are you going to do, turn us in?’ demanded Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What are you two talking about?’ asked Harry, turning away to hang up his robes so that neither of them would see him grinning.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You know perfectly well what we’re talking about!’ said Hermione shrilly. ‘You spiked Ron’s juice with lucky potion at breakfast! Felix Felicis!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No I didn’t,’ said Harry, turning back to face them both.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes you did, Harry, and that’s why everything went right, there were Slytherin players missing and Ron saved everything!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I didn’t put it in!’ said Harry, now grinning broadly. He slipped his hand inside his jacket pocket and drew out the tiny bottle that Hermione had seen in his hand that morning. It was full of golden potion and the cork was still tightly sealed with wax. ‘I wanted Ron to think I’d done it, so I faked it when I knew you were looking.’ He looked at Ron. ‘You saved everything because you felt lucky. You did it all yourself.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He pocketed the potion again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There really wasn’t anything in my pumpkin juice?’ Ron said, astounded. ‘But the weather’s good … and Vaisey couldn’t play … I honestly haven’t been given lucky potion?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry shook his head. Ron gaped at him for a moment, then rounded on Hermione, imitating her voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You added Felix Felicis to Ron’s juice this morning, that’s why he saved everything! See! I can save goals without help, Hermione!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I never said you couldn’t – Ron, you thought you’d been given it, too!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But Ron had already strode past her out of the door with his broomstick over his shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Er,’ said Harry into the sudden silence; he had not expected his plan to backfire like this, ‘shall … shall we go up to the party, then?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You go!’ said Hermione, blinking back tears. ‘I’m sick of Ron at the moment, I don’t know what I’m supposed to have done …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And she stormed out of the changing room, too.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry walked slowly back up the grounds towards the castle through the crowd, many of whom shouted congratulations at him, but he felt a great sense of let-down; he had been sure that if Ron won the match, he and Hermione would be friends again immediately. He did not see how he could possibly explain to Hermione that what she had done to offend Ron was kiss Viktor Krum, not when the offence had occurred so long ago.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry could not see Hermione at the Gryffindor celebration party, which was in full swing when he arrived. Renewed cheers and clapping greeted his appearance and he was soon surrounded by a mob of people congratulating him. What with trying to shake off the Creevey brothers, who wanted a blow-by-blow match analysis, and the large group of girls that encircled him, laughing at his least amusing comments and batting their eyelids, it was some time before he could try and find Ron. At last, he extricated himself from Romilda Vane, who was hinting heavily that she would like to go to Slughorn’s Christmas party with him. As he was ducking towards the drinks table he walked straight into Ginny, Arnold the Pygmy Puff riding on her shoulder and Crookshanks mewing hopefully at her heels.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Looking for Ron?’ she asked, smirking. ‘He’s over there, the filthy hypocrite.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked into the corner she was indicating. There, in full view of the whole room, stood Ron wrapped so closely around Lavender Brown it was hard to tell whose hands were whose.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It looks like he’s eating her face, doesn’t it?’ said Ginny dispassionately. ‘But I suppose he’s got to refine his technique somehow. Good game, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She patted him on the arm; Harry felt a swooping sensation in his stomach, but then she walked off to help herself to more Butterbeer. Crookshanks trotted after her, his yellow eyes fixed upon Arnold.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry turned away from Ron, who did not look like surfacing soon, just in time to see the portrait hole closing. With a sinking feeling he thought he saw a mane of bushy brown hair whipping out of sight.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He darted forwards, sidestepped Romilda Vane again, and pushed open the portrait of the Fat Lady. The corridor outside seemed to be deserted.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hermione?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He found her in the first unlocked classroom he tried. She was sitting on the teacher’s desk, alone except for a small ring of twittering yellow birds circling her head, which she had clearly just conjured out of midair. Harry could not help admiring her spellwork at a time like this.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, hello, Harry,’ she said in a brittle voice. ‘I was just practising.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah … they’re – er – really good …’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He had no idea what to say to her. He was just wondering whether there was any chance that she had not noticed Ron, that she had merely left the room because the party was a little too rowdy, when she said, in an unnaturally high-pitched voice, ‘Ron seems to be enjoying the celebrations.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Er … does he?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t pretend you didn’t see him,’ said Hermione. ‘He wasn’t exactly hiding it, was –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The door behind them burst open. To Harry’s horror, Ron came in, laughing, pulling Lavender by the hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh,’ he said, drawing up short at the sight of Harry and Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oops!’ said Lavender, and she backed out of the room, giggling. The door swung shut behind her.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was a horrible swelling, billowing silence. Hermione was staring at Ron, who refused to look at her, but said with an odd mixture of bravado and awkwardness, ‘Hi, Harry! Wondered where you’d got to!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione slid off the desk. The little flock of golden birds continued to twitter in circles around her head so that she looked like a strange, feathery model of the solar system.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You shouldn’t leave Lavender waiting outside,’ she said quietly. ‘She’ll wonder where you’ve gone.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She walked very slowly and erectly towards the door. Harry glanced at Ron, who was looking relieved that nothing worse had happened.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oppugno!’ came a shriek from the doorway.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry spun round to see Hermione pointing her wand at Ron, her expression wild: the little flock of birds was speeding like a hail of fat golden bullets towards Ron, who yelped and covered his face with his hands, but the birds attacked, pecking and clawing at every bit of flesh they could reach.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Gerremoffme!’ he yelled, but with one last look of vindictive fury, Hermione wrenched open the door and disappeared through it. Harry thought he heard a sob before it slammed.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Snow was swirling against the icy windows once more; Christmas was approaching fast. Hagrid had already single-handedly delivered the usual twelve Christmas trees for the Great Hall; garlands of holly and tinsel had been twisted around the banisters of the stairs; everlasting candles glowed from inside the helmets of suits of armour and great bunches of mistletoe had been hung at intervals along the corridors. Large groups of girls tended to converge underneath the mistletoe bunches every time Harry went past, which caused blockages in the corridors; fortunately, however, Harry’s frequent night-time wanderings had given him an unusually good knowledge of the castle’s secret passageways, so that he was able, without too much difficulty, to navigate mistletoe-free routes between classes.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron, who might once have found the necessity of these detours a cause for jealousy rather than hilarity, simply roared with laughter about it all. Although Harry much preferred this new laughing, joking Ron to the moody, aggressive model he had been enduring for the last few weeks, the improved Ron came at a heavy price. Firstly, Harry had to put up with the frequent presence of Lavender Brown, who seemed to regard any moment that she was not kissing Ron as a moment wasted; and secondly, Harry found himself, once more, the best friend of two people who seemed unlikely ever to speak to each other again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Ron, whose hands and forearms still bore scratches and cuts from Hermione’s bird attack, was taking a defensive and resentful tone.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She can’t complain,’ he told Harry. ‘She snogged Krum. So she’s found out someone wants to snog me, too. Well, it’s a free country. I haven’t done anything wrong.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry did not answer, but pretended to be absorbed in the book they were supposed to have read before Charms the following morning (Quintessence: A Quest). Determined as he was to remain friends with both Ron and Hermione, he was spending a lot of time with his mouth shut tight.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I never promised Hermione anything,’ Ron mumbled. ‘I mean, all right, I was going to go to Slughorn’s Christmas party with her, but she never said … just as friends … I’m a free agent …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry turned a page of Quintessence, aware that Ron was watching him. Ron’s voice tailed away in mutters, barely audible over the loud crackling of the fire, though Harry thought he caught the words ‘Krum’ and ‘can’t complain’ again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione’s timetable was so full that Harry could only talk to her properly in the evenings, when Ron was in any case so tightly wrapped around Lavender that he did not notice what Harry was doing. Hermione refused to sit in the common room while Ron was there, so Harry generally joined her in the library, which meant that their conversations were held in whispers.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s at perfect liberty to kiss whomever he likes,’ said Hermione, while the librarian, Madam Pince, prowled the shelves behind them. ‘I really couldn’t care less.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She raised her quill and dotted an ‘i’ so ferociously that she punctured a hole in her parchment. Harry said nothing. He thought his voice might soon vanish from lack of use. He bent a little lower over Advanced Potion-Making and continued to make notes on Everlasting Elixirs, occasionally pausing to decipher the Prince’s useful additions to Libatius Borage’s text.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And incidentally,’ said Hermione, after a few moments, ‘you need to be careful.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘For the last time,’ said Harry, speaking in a slightly hoarse whisper after three-quarters of an hour of silence, ‘I am not giving back this book, I’ve learned more from the Half-Blood Prince than Snape or Slughorn have taught me in –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m not talking about your stupid so-called Prince,’ said Hermione, giving his book a nasty look as though it had been rude to her, ‘I’m talking about earlier. I went into the girls’ bathroom just before I came in here and there were about a dozen girls in there, including that Romilda Vane, trying to decide how to slip you a love potion. They’re all hoping they’re going to get you to take them to Slughorn’s party and they all seem to have bought Fred and George’s love potions, which I’m afraid to say probably work –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Why didn’t you confiscate them, then?’ demanded Harry. It seemed extraordinary that Hermione’s mania for upholding rules could have abandoned her at this crucial juncture.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘They didn’t have the potions with them in the bathroom,’ said Hermione scornfully. ‘They were just discussing tactics. As I doubt whether even the Half-Blood Prince,’ she gave the book another nasty look, ‘could dream up an antidote for a dozen different love potions at once, I’d just invite someone to go with you – that’ll stop all the others thinking they’ve still got a chance. It’s tomorrow night, they’re getting desperate.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There isn’t anyone I want to invite,’ mumbled Harry, who was still trying not to think about Ginny any more than he could help, despite the fact that she kept cropping up in his dreams in ways that made him devoutly thankful that Ron could not perform Legilimency.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, just be careful what you drink, because Romilda Vane looked like she meant business,’ said Hermione grimly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She hitched up the long roll of parchment on which she was writing her Arithmancy essay and continued to scratch away with her quill. Harry watched her with his mind a long way away.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Hang on a moment,’ he said slowly. ‘I thought Filch had banned anything bought at Weasleys’ Wizard Wheezes?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘And when has anyone ever paid attention to what Filch has banned?’ asked Hermione, still concentrating on her essay.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But I thought all the owls were being searched? So how come these girls are able to bring love potions into school?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Fred and George send them disguised as perfumes and cough potions,’ said Hermione. ‘It’s part of their Owl Order Service.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You know a lot about it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione gave him the kind of nasty look she had just given his copy of Advanced Potion-Making.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It was all on the back of the bottles they showed Ginny and me in the summer,’ she said coldly. ‘I don’t go around putting potions in people’s drinks … or pretending to, either, which is just as bad …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, well, never mind that,’ said Harry quickly. ‘The point is, Filch is being fooled, isn’t he? These girls are getting stuff into the school disguised as something else! So why couldn’t Malfoy have brought the necklace into the school –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, Harry … not that again …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on, why not?’ demanded Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Look,’ sighed Hermione, ‘Secrecy Sensors detect jinxes, curses and concealment charms, don’t they? They’re used to find Dark magic and Dark objects. They’d have picked up a powerful curse, like the one on that necklace, within seconds. But something that’s just been put in the wrong bottle wouldn’t register – and anyway, love potions aren’t Dark or dangerous –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Easy for you to say,’ muttered Harry, thinking of Romilda Vane.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘– so it would be down to Filch to realise it wasn’t a cough potion, and he’s not a very good wizard, I doubt he can tell one potion from –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hermione stopped dead; Harry had heard it too. Somebody had moved close behind them among the dark bookshelves. They waited and a moment later the vulture-like countenance of Madam Pince appeared round the corner, her sunken cheeks, her skin like parchment and her long hooked nose illuminated unflatteringly by the lamp she was carrying.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The library is now closed,’ she said. ‘Mind you return anything you have borrowed to the correct – what have you been doing to that book, you depraved boy?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It isn’t the library’s, it’s mine!’ said Harry hastily, snatching his copy of Advanced Potion-Making off the table as she lunged at it with a clawlike hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Despoiled!’ she hissed. ‘Desecrated! Befouled!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s just a book that’s been written in!’ said Harry, tugging it out of her grip.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She looked as though she might have a seizure; Hermione, who had hastily packed her things, grabbed Harry by the arm and frogmarched him away.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘She’ll ban you from the library if you’re not careful. Why did you have to bring that stupid book?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s not my fault she’s barking mad, Hermione. Or d’you think she overheard you being rude about Filch? I’ve always thought there might be something going on between them …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, ha, ha …’
