book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I rather think,’ said Dumbledore, putting his uninjured hand inside his robes and drawing out a short silver knife of the kind Harry used to chop potion ingredients, ‘that we are required to make payment to pass.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Payment?’ said Harry. ‘You’ve got to give the door something?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Blood, if I am not much mistaken.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Blood?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I said it was crude,’ said Dumbledore, who sounded disdainful, even disappointed, as though Voldemort had fallen short of the standards Dumbledore expected. ‘The idea, as I am sure you will have gathered, is that your enemy must weaken him or herself to enter. Once again, Lord Voldemort fails to grasp that there are much more terrible things than physical injury.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, but still, if you can avoid it …’ said Harry, who had experienced enough pain not to be keen for more.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sometimes, however, it is unavoidable,’ said Dumbledore, shaking back the sleeve of his robes and exposing the forearm of his injured hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor!’ protested Harry, hurrying forwards as Dumbledore raised his knife. ‘I’ll do it, I’m –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He did not know what he was going to say – younger, fitter? But Dumbledore merely smiled. There was a flash of silver, and a spurt of scarlet; the rock face was peppered with dark, glistening drops.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You are very kind, Harry,’ said Dumbledore, now passing the tip of his wand over the deep cut he had made in his own arm, so that it healed instantly, just as Snape had healed Malfoy’s wounds. ‘But your blood is worth more than mine. Ah, that seems to have done the trick, doesn’t it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The blazing silver outline of an arch had appeared in the wall once more, and this time it did not fade away: the blood-spattered rock within it simply vanished, leaving an opening into what seemed total darkness.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘After me, I think,’ said Dumbledore, and he walked through the archway with Harry on his heels, lighting his own wand hastily as he went.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: An eerie sight met their eyes: they were standing on the edge of a great black lake, so vast that Harry could not make out the distant banks, in a cavern so high that the ceiling, too, was out of sight. A misty greenish light shone far away in what looked like the middle of the lake; it was reflected in the completely still water below. The greenish glow and the light from the two wands were the only things that broke the otherwise velvety blackness, though their rays did not penetrate as far as Harry would have expected. The darkness was somehow denser than normal darkness.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Let us walk,’ said Dumbledore quietly. ‘Be very careful not to step into the water. Stay close to me.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He set off around the edge of the lake and Harry followed close behind him. Their footsteps made echoing, slapping sounds on the narrow rim of rock that surrounded the water. On and on they walked, but the view did not vary: on one side of them, the rough cavern wall; on the other, the boundless expanse of smooth, glassy blackness, in the very middle of which was that mysterious greenish glow. Harry found the place and the silence oppressive, unnerving.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor?’ he said finally. ‘Do you think the Horcrux is here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yes,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Yes, I’m sure it is. The question is, how do we get to it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We couldn’t … we couldn’t just try a Summoning Charm?’ Harry said, sure that it was a stupid suggestion, but much keener than he was prepared to admit on getting out of this place as soon as possible.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Certainly we could,’ said Dumbledore, stopping so suddenly that Harry almost walked into him. ‘Why don’t you do it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Me? Oh … OK …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had not expected this, but cleared his throat and said loudly, wand aloft, ‘Accio Horcrux!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: With a noise like an explosion, something very large and pale erupted out of the dark water some twenty feet away; before Harry could see what it was, it had vanished again with a crashing splash that made great, deep ripples on the mirrored surface. Harry leapt backwards in shock and hit the wall; his heart was still thundering as he turned to Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What was that?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Something, I think, that is ready to respond should we attempt to seize the Horcrux.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked back at the water. The surface of the lake was once more shining black glass: the ripples had vanished unnaturally fast; Harry’s heart, however, was still pounding.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Did you think that would happen, sir?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I thought something would happen if we made an obvious attempt to get our hands on the Horcrux. That was a very good idea, Harry; much the simplest way of finding out what we are facing.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But we don’t know what the thing was,’ said Harry, looking at the sinisterly smooth water.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What the things are, you mean,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I doubt very much that there is only one of them. Shall we walk on?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Do you think we’re going to have to go into the lake?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Into it? Only if we are very unfortunate.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You don’t think the Horcrux is at the bottom?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh no … I think the Horcrux is in the middle.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And Dumbledore pointed towards the misty green light in the centre of the lake.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So we’re going to have to cross the lake to get to it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, I think so.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry did not say anything. His thoughts were all of water-monsters, of giant serpents, of demons, kelpies and sprites …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Aha,’ said Dumbledore and he stopped again; this time, Harry really did walk into him; for a moment he toppled on the edge of the dark water and Dumbledore’s uninjured hand closed tightly around his upper arm, pulling him back. ‘So sorry, Harry, I should have given warning. Stand back against the wall, please; I think I have found the place.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry had no idea what Dumbledore meant; this patch of dark bank was exactly like every other bit as far as he could tell, but Dumbledore seemed to have detected something special about it. This time he was running his hand not over the rocky wall, but through the thin air, as though expecting to find and grip something invisible.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oho,’ said Dumbledore happily, seconds later. His hand had closed in midair upon something Harry could not see. Dumbledore moved closer to the water; Harry watched nervously as the tips of Dumbledore’s buckled shoes found the utmost edge of the rock rim. Keeping his hand clenched in midair, Dumbledore raised his wand with the other and tapped his fist with the point.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Immediately a thick coppery green chain appeared out of thin air, extending from the depths of the water into Dumbledore’s clenched hand. Dumbledore tapped the chain, which began to slide through his fist like a snake, coiling itself on the ground with a clinking sound that echoed noisily off the rocky walls, pulling something from the depths of the black water. Harry gasped as the ghostly prow of a tiny boat broke the surface, glowing as green as the chain, and floated, with barely a ripple, towards the place on the bank where Harry and Dumbledore stood.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘How did you know that was there?’ Harry asked in astonishment.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Magic always leaves traces,’ said Dumbledore, as the boat hit the bank with a gentle bump, ‘sometimes very distinctive traces. I taught Tom Riddle. I know his style.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Is … is this boat safe?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh yes, I think so. Voldemort needed to create a means to cross the lake without attracting the wrath of those creatures he had placed within it, in case he ever wanted to visit or remove his Horcrux.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So the things in the water won’t do anything to us if we cross in Voldemort’s boat?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I think we must resign ourselves to the fact that they will, at some point, realise we are not Lord Voldemort. Thus far, however, we have done well. They have allowed us to raise the boat.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But why have they let us?’ asked Harry, who could not shake off the vision of tentacles rising out of the dark water the moment they were out of sight of the bank.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Voldemort would have been reasonably confident that none but a very great wizard would have been able to find the boat,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I think he would have been prepared to risk what was, to his mind, the most unlikely possibility that somebody else would find it, knowing that he had set other obstacles ahead that only he would be able to penetrate. We shall see whether he is right.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked down into the boat. It really was very small.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It doesn’t look like it was built for two people. Will it hold both of us? Will we be too heavy together?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore chuckled.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Voldemort will not have cared about the weight, but about the amount of magical power that crossed his lake. I rather think an enchantment will have been placed upon this boat so that only one wizard at a time will be able to sail in it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But then –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I do not think you will count, Harry: you are under age and unqualified. Voldemort would never have expected a sixteen-year-old to reach this place: I think it unlikely that your powers will register compared to mine.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: These words did nothing to raise Harry’s morale; perhaps Dumbledore knew it, for he added, ‘Voldemort’s mistake, Harry, Voldemort’s mistake … age is foolish and forgetful when it underestimates youth … now, you first this time, and be careful not to touch the water.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore stood aside and Harry climbed carefully into the boat. Dumbledore stepped in, too, coiling the chain on to the floor. They were crammed in together; Harry could not comfortably sit, but crouched, his knees jutting over the edge of the boat, which began to move at once. There was no sound other than the silken rustle of the boat’s prow cleaving the water; it moved without their help, as though an invisible rope were pulling it onwards towards the light in the centre. Soon they could no longer see the walls of the cavern; they might have been at sea except that there were no waves.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry looked down and saw the reflected gold of his wand-light sparkling and glittering on the black water as they passed. The boat was carving deep ripples upon the glassy surface, grooves in the dark mirror …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And then Harry saw it, marble-white, floating inches below the surface.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor!’ he said, and his startled voice echoed loudly over the silent water.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I think I saw a hand in the water – a human hand!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, I am sure you did,’ said Dumbledore calmly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry stared down into the water, looking for the vanished hand, and a sick feeling rose in his throat.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘So that thing that jumped out of the water –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But Harry had his answer before Dumbledore could reply; the wand-light had slid over a fresh patch of water and showed him, this time, a dead man lying face up inches beneath the surface: his open eyes misted as though with cobwebs, his hair and his robes swirling around him like smoke.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There are bodies in here!’ said Harry, and his voice sounded much higher than usual and most unlike his own.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Dumbledore placidly, ‘but we do not need to worry about them at the moment.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘At the moment?’ Harry repeated, tearing his gaze from the water to look at Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Not while they are merely drifting peacefully below us,’ said Dumbledore. ‘There is nothing to be feared from a body, Harry, any more than there is anything to be feared from the darkness. Lord Voldemort, who of course secretly fears both, disagrees. But once again he reveals his own lack of wisdom. It is the unknown we fear when we look upon death and darkness, nothing more.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry said nothing; he did not want to argue, but he found the idea that there were bodies floating around them and beneath them horrible, and what was more, he did not believe that they were not dangerous.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But one of them jumped,’ he said, trying to make his voice as level and calm as Dumbledore’s. ‘When I tried to Summon the Horcrux, a body leapt out of the lake.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I am sure that once we take the Horcrux, we shall find them less peaceable. However, like many creatures that dwell in cold and darkness, they fear light and warmth, which we shall therefore call to our aid should the need arise. Fire, Harry,’ Dumbledore added with a smile, in response to Harry’s bewildered expression.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh … right …’ said Harry quickly. He turned his head to look at the greenish glow towards which the boat was still inexorably sailing. He could not pretend, now, that he was not scared. The great black lake, teeming with the dead … it seemed hours and hours ago that he had met Professor Trelawney, that he had given Ron and Hermione the Felix Felicis … he suddenly wished he had said a better goodbye to them … and he hadn’t seen Ginny at all …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Nearly there,’ said Dumbledore cheerfully.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Sure enough, the greenish light seemed to be growing larger at last, and within minutes, the boat had come to a halt, bumping gently into something that Harry could not see at first, but when he raised his illuminated wand he saw that they had reached a small island of smooth rock in the centre of the lake.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Careful not to touch the water,’ said Dumbledore again as Harry climbed out of the boat.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The island was no larger than Dumbledore’s office: an expanse of flat dark stone on which stood nothing but the source of that greenish light, which looked much brighter when viewed close to. Harry squinted at it; at first he thought it was a lamp of some kind, but then he saw that the light was coming from a stone basin rather like the Pensieve, which was set on top of a pedestal.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore approached the basin and Harry followed. Side by side they looked down into it. The basin was full of an emerald liquid emitting that phosphorescent glow.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What is it?’ asked Harry quietly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I am not sure,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Something more worrisome than blood and bodies, however.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore pushed back the sleeve of his robe over his blackened hand, and stretched out the tips of his burned fingers towards the surface of the potion.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir, no, don’t touch –!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I cannot touch,’ said Dumbledore, smiling faintly. ‘See? I cannot approach any nearer than this. You try.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Staring, Harry put his hand into the basin and attempted to touch the potion. He met an invisible barrier that prevented him coming within an inch of it. No matter how hard he pushed, his fingers encountered nothing but what seemed to be solid and inflexible air.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Out of the way, please, Harry,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He raised his wand and made complicated movements over the surface of the potion, murmuring soundlessly. Nothing happened, except perhaps that the potion glowed a little brighter. Harry remained silent while Dumbledore worked, but after a while Dumbledore withdrew his wand and Harry felt it was safe to talk again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You think the Horcrux is in there, sir?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yes.’ Dumbledore peered more closely into the basin. Harry saw his face reflected, upside-down, in the smooth surface of the green potion. ‘But how to reach it? This potion cannot be penetrated by hand, Vanished, parted, scooped up or siphoned away, nor can it be Transfigured, Charmed or otherwise made to change its nature.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Almost absent-mindedly, Dumbledore raised his wand again, twirled it once in midair and then caught the crystal goblet that he had conjured out of nowhere.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I can only conclude that this potion is supposed to be drunk.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What?’ said Harry. ‘No!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, I think so: only by drinking it can I empty the basin and see what lies in its depths.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But what if – what if it kills you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I doubt that it would work like that,’ said Dumbledore easily. ‘Lord Voldemort would not want to kill the person who reached this island.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry couldn’t believe it. Was this more of Dumbledore’s insane determination to see good in everyone?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir,’ said Harry, trying to keep his voice reasonable, ‘sir, this is Voldemort we’re –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m sorry, Harry; I should have said, he would not want immediately to kill the person who reached this island,’ Dumbledore corrected himself. ‘He would want to keep them alive long enough to find out how they managed to penetrate so far through his defences and, most importantly of all, why they were so intent upon emptying the basin. Do not forget that Lord Voldemort believes that he alone knows about his Horcruxes.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry made to speak again, but this time Dumbledore raised his hand for silence, frowning slightly at the emerald liquid, evidently thinking hard.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Undoubtedly,’ he said finally, ‘this potion must act in a way that will prevent me taking the Horcrux. It might paralyse me, cause me to forget what I am here for, create so much pain I am distracted, or render me incapable in some other way. This being the case, Harry, it will be your job to make sure I keep drinking, even if you have to tip the potion into my protesting mouth. You understand?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Their eyes met over the basin; each pale face lit with that strange, green light. Harry did not speak. Was this why he had been invited along – so that he could force-feed Dumbledore a potion that might cause him unendurable pain?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You remember,’ said Dumbledore, ‘the condition on which I brought you with me?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry hesitated, looking into the blue eyes that had turned green in the reflected light of the basin.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But what if –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You swore, did you not, to follow any command I gave you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, but –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I warned you, did I not, that there might be danger?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said Harry, ‘but –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, then,’ said Dumbledore, shaking back his sleeves once more and raising the empty goblet, ‘you have my orders.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Why can’t I drink the potion instead?’ asked Harry desperately.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Because I am much older, much cleverer, and much less valuable,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Once and for all, Harry, do I have your word that you will do all in your power to make me keep drinking?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Couldn’t –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Do I have it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Your word, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I – all right, but –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Before Harry could make any further protest, Dumbledore lowered the crystal goblet into the potion. For a split second Harry hoped that he would not be able to touch the potion with the goblet, but the crystal sank into the surface as nothing else had; when the glass was full to the brim, Dumbledore lifted it to his mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Your good health, Harry.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And he drained the goblet. Harry watched, terrified, his hands gripping the rim of the basin so hard that his fingertips were numb.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor?’ he said anxiously, as Dumbledore lowered the empty glass. ‘How do you feel?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore shook his head, his eyes closed. Harry wondered whether he was in pain. Dumbledore plunged the glass blindly back into the basin, refilled it, and drank once more.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: In silence, Dumbledore drank three gobletfuls of the potion. Then, halfway through the fourth goblet, he staggered and fell forwards against the basin. His eyes were still closed, his breathing heavy.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor Dumbledore?’ said Harry, his voice strained. ‘Can you hear me?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore did not answer. His face was twitching as though he were deeply asleep, but dreaming a horrible dream. His grip on the goblet was slackening; the potion was about to spill from it. Harry reached forwards and grasped the crystal cup, holding it steady.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Professor, can you hear me?’ he repeated loudly, his voice echoing around the cavern.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore panted and then spoke in a voice Harry did not recognise, for he had never heard Dumbledore frightened like this.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I don’t want … don’t make me …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry stared into the whitened face he knew so well, at the crooked nose and half-moon spectacles, and did not know what to do.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘… don’t like … want to stop …’ moaned Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You … you can’t stop, Professor,’ said Harry. ‘You’ve got to keep drinking, remember? You told me you had to keep drinking. Here …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Hating himself, repulsed by what he was doing, Harry forced the goblet back towards Dumbledore’s mouth and tipped it, so that Dumbledore drank the remainder of the potion inside.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No …’ he groaned, as Harry lowered the goblet back into the basin and refilled it for him. ‘I don’t want to … I don’t want to … let me go …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all right, Professor,’ said Harry, his hand shaking. ‘It’s all right, I’m here –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Make it stop, make it stop,’ moaned Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes … yes, this’ll make it stop,’ lied Harry. He tipped the contents of the goblet into Dumbledore’s open mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore screamed; the noise echoed all around the vast chamber, across the dead black water.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, no, no … no … I can’t … I can’t, don’t make me, I don’t want to …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all right, Professor, it’s all right!’ said Harry loudly, his hands shaking so badly he could hardly scoop up the sixth gobletful of potion; the basin was now half-empty. ‘Nothing’s happening to you, you’re safe, it isn’t real, I swear it isn’t real – take this, now, take this …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And obediently, Dumbledore drank, as though it was an antidote Harry offered him, but upon draining the goblet, he sank to his knees, shaking uncontrollably.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s all my fault, all my fault,’ he sobbed, ‘please make it stop, I know I did wrong, oh, please make it stop and I’ll never, never again …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘This will make it stop, Professor,’ Harry said, his voice cracking as he tipped the seventh glass of potion into Dumbledore’s mouth.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore began to cower as though invisible torturers surrounded him; his flailing hand almost knocked the refilled goblet from Harry’s trembling hands as he moaned, ‘Don’t hurt them, don’t hurt them, please, please, it’s my fault, hurt me instead …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Here, drink this, drink this, you’ll be all right,’ said Harry desperately, and once again Dumbledore obeyed him, opening his mouth even as he kept his eyes tight shut and shook from head to foot.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And now he fell forwards, screaming again, hammering his fists upon the ground, while Harry filled the ninth goblet.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Please, please, please, no … not that, not that, I’ll do anything …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Just drink, Professor, just drink …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore drank like a child dying of thirst, but when he had finished, he yelled again as though his insides were on fire.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No more, please, no more …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry scooped up a tenth gobletful of potion and felt the crystal scrape the bottom of the basin.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re nearly there, Professor, drink this, drink it …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He supported Dumbledore’s shoulders and again, Dumbledore drained the glass; Harry was on his feet once more, refilling the goblet as Dumbledore began to scream in more anguish than ever, ‘I want to die! I want to die! Make it stop, make it stop, I want to die!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Drink this, Professor, drink this …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore drank, and no sooner had he finished than he yelled, ‘KILL ME!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘This – this one will!’ gasped Harry. ‘Just drink this … it’ll be over … all over!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore gulped at the goblet, drained every last drop and then, with a great, rattling gasp, rolled over on to his face.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No!’ shouted Harry, who had stood to refill the goblet again; instead he dropped the cup into the basin, flung himself down beside Dumbledore and heaved him over on to his back; Dumbledore’s glasses were askew, his mouth agape, his eyes closed. ‘No,’ said Harry, shaking Dumbledore, ‘no, you’re not dead, you said it wasn’t poison, wake up, wake up – Rennervate!’ he cried, his wand pointing at Dumbledore’s chest; there was a flash of red light but nothing happened. ‘Rennervate – sir – please –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore’s eyelids flickered; Harry’s heart leapt.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir, are you –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Water,’ croaked Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Water,’ panted Harry, ‘– yes –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He leapt to his feet and seized the goblet he had dropped in the basin; he barely registered the golden locket lying curled beneath it.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Aguamenti!’ he shouted, jabbing the goblet with his wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The goblet filled with clear water; Harry dropped to his knees beside Dumbledore, raised his head and brought the glass to his lips – but it was empty. Dumbledore groaned and began to pant.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But I had some – wait – Aguamenti!’ said Harry again, pointing his wand at the goblet. Once more, for a second, clear water gleamed within it, but as he approached Dumbledore’s mouth, the water vanished again.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir, I’m trying, I’m trying!’ said Harry desperately, but he did not think that Dumbledore could hear him; he had rolled on to his side and was drawing great, rattling breaths that sounded agonising. ‘Aguamenti – Aguamenti – AGUAMENTI!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The goblet filled and emptied once more. And now Dumbledore’s breathing was fading. His brain whirling in panic, Harry knew, instinctively, the only way left to get water, because Voldemort had planned it so …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He flung himself over to the edge of the rock and plunged the goblet into the lake, bringing it up full to the brim of icy water that did not vanish.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir – here!’ Harry yelled, and lunging forwards he tipped the water clumsily over Dumbledore’s face.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: It was the best he could do, for the icy feeling on his arm not holding the cup was not the lingering chill of the water. A slimy white hand had gripped his wrist, and the creature to whom it belonged was pulling him, slowly, backwards across the rock. The surface of the lake was no longer mirror-smooth; it was churning, and everywhere Harry looked, white heads and hands were emerging from the dark water, men and women and children with sunken, sightless eyes were moving towards the rock: an army of the dead rising from the black water.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Petrificus Totalus!’ yelled Harry, struggling to cling on to the smooth, soaked surface of the island as he pointed his wand at the Inferius that had his arm: it released him, falling backwards into the water with a splash. He scrambled to his feet; but many more Inferi were already climbing on to the rock, their bony hands clawing at its slippery surface, their blank, frosted eyes upon him, trailing waterlogged rags, sunken faces leering.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Petrificus Totalus!’ Harry bellowed again, backing away as he swiped his wand through the air; six or seven of them crumpled, but more were coming towards him. ‘Impedimenta! Incarcerous!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: A few of them stumbled, one or two of them bound in ropes, but those climbing on to the rock behind them merely stepped over or on the fallen bodies. Still slashing at the air with his wand, Harry yelled, ‘Sectumsempra! SECTUMSEMPRA!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But though gashes appeared in their sodden rags and their icy skin, they had no blood to spill: they walked on, unfeeling, their shrunken hands outstretched towards him, and as he backed away still further he felt arms enclose him from behind, thin, fleshless arms cold as death, and his feet left the ground as they lifted him and began to carry him, slowly and surely, back to the water, and he knew there would be no release, that he would be drowned, and become one more dead guardian of a fragment of Voldemort’s shattered soul …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But then, through the darkness, fire erupted: crimson and gold, a ring of fire that surrounded the rock so that the Inferi holding Harry so tightly stumbled and faltered; they did not dare pass through the flames to get to the water. They dropped Harry; he hit the ground, slipped on the rock and fell, grazing his arms, but scrambled back up, raising his wand and staring around.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore was on his feet again, pale as any of the surrounding Inferi, but taller than any, too, the fire dancing in his eyes; his wand was raised like a torch and from its tip emanated the flames, like a vast lasso, encircling them all with warmth.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The Inferi bumped into each other, attempting, blindly, to escape the fire in which they were enclosed …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore scooped the locket from the bottom of the stone basin and stowed it inside his robes. Wordlessly, he gestured to Harry to come to his side. Distracted by the flames, the Inferi seemed unaware that their quarry was leaving as Dumbledore led Harry back to the boat, the ring of fire moving with them, around them, the bewildered Inferi accompanying them to the water’s edge, where they slipped gratefully back into their dark waters.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry, who was shaking all over, thought for a moment that Dumbledore might not be able to climb into the boat; he staggered a little as he attempted it; all his efforts seemed to be going into maintaining the ring of protective flame around them. Harry seized him and helped him back to his seat. Once they were both safely jammed inside again, the boat began to move back across the black water, away from the rock, still encircled by that ring of fire, and it seemed that the Inferi swarming below them did not dare resurface.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir,’ panted Harry, ‘sir, I forgot – about fire – they were coming at me and I panicked –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Quite understandable,’ murmured Dumbledore. Harry was alarmed to hear how faint his voice was.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: They reached the bank with a little bump and Harry leapt out, then turned quickly to help Dumbledore. The moment that Dumbledore reached the bank he let his wand hand fall; the ring of fire vanished, but the Inferi did not emerge again from the water. The little boat sank into the water once more; clanking and tinkling, its chain slithered back into the lake, too. Dumbledore gave a great sigh and leaned against the cavern wall.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I am weak …’ he said.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t worry, sir,’ said Harry at once, anxious about Dumbledore’s extreme pallor and his air of exhaustion. ‘Don’t worry, I’ll get us back … lean on me, sir …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And pulling Dumbledore’s uninjured arm around his shoulders, Harry guided his headmaster back around the lake, bearing most of his weight.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The protection was … after all … well designed,’ said Dumbledore faintly. ‘One alone could not have done it … you did well, very well, Harry …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Don’t talk now,’ said Harry, fearing how slurred Dumbledore’s voice had become, how much his feet dragged, ‘save your energy, sir … we’ll soon be out of here …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The archway will have sealed again … my knife …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There’s no need, I got cut on the rock,’ said Harry firmly, ‘just tell me where …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Here …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry wiped his grazed forearm upon the stone: having received its tribute of blood the archway reopened instantly. They crossed the outer cave and Harry helped Dumbledore back into the icy sea water that filled the crevice in the cliff.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s going to be all right, sir,’ Harry said over and over again, more worried by Dumbledore’s silence than he had been by his weakened voice. ‘We’re nearly there … I can Apparate us both back … don’t worry …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I am not worried, Harry,’ said Dumbledore, his voice a little stronger despite the freezing water. ‘I am with you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Once back under the starry sky, Harry heaved Dumbledore on to the top of the nearest boulder and then to his feet. Sodden and shivering, Dumbledore’s weight still upon him, Harry concentrated harder than he had ever done upon his destination: Hogsmeade. Closing his eyes, gripping Dumbledore’s arm as tightly as he could, he stepped forwards into that feeling of horrible compression.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He knew it had worked before he opened his eyes: the smell of salt, the sea breeze had gone. He and Dumbledore were shivering and dripping in the middle of the dark High Street in Hogsmeade. For one horrible moment Harry’s imagination showed him more Inferi creeping towards him around the sides of shops, but he blinked and saw that nothing was stirring; all was still, the darkness complete but for a few streetlamps and lit upper windows.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We did it, Professor!’ Harry whispered with difficulty; he suddenly realised that he had a searing stitch in his chest. ‘We did it! We got the Horcrux!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore staggered against him. For a moment, Harry thought that his inexpert Apparition had thrown Dumbledore off-balance; then he saw his face, paler and damper than ever in the distant light of a streetlamp.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir, are you all right?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve been better,’ said Dumbledore weakly, though the corners of his mouth twitched. ‘That potion … was no health drink …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And to Harry’s horror, Dumbledore sank on to the ground.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Sir – it’s OK, sir, you’re going to be all right, don’t worry –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He looked around desperately for help, but there was nobody to be seen and all he could think was that he must somehow get Dumbledore quickly to the hospital wing.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We need to get you up to the school, sir … Madam Pomfrey …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Dumbledore. ‘It is … Professor Snape whom I need … but I do not think … I can walk very far just yet …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Right – sir, listen – I’m going to knock on a door, find a place you can stay – then I can run and get Madam –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Severus,’ said Dumbledore clearly. ‘I need Severus …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘All right then, Snape – but I’m going to have to leave you for a moment so I can –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Before Harry could make a move, however, he heard running footsteps. His heart leapt: somebody had seen, somebody knew they needed help – and looking around he saw Madam Rosmerta scurrying down the dark street towards them on high-heeled, fluffy slippers, wearing a silk dressing-gown embroidered with dragons.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I saw you Apparate as I was pulling my bedroom curtains! Thank goodness, thank goodness, I couldn’t think what to – but what’s wrong with Albus?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: She came to a halt, panting, and stared down, wide-eyed, at Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s hurt,’ said Harry. ‘Madam Rosmerta, can he come into the Three Broomsticks while I go up to the school and get help for him?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You can’t go up there alone! Don’t you realise – haven’t you seen –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘If you help me support him,’ said Harry, not listening to her, ‘I think we can get him inside –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What has happened?’ asked Dumbledore. ‘Rosmerta, what’s wrong?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The – the Dark Mark, Albus.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And she pointed into the sky, in the direction of Hogwarts. Dread flooded Harry at the sound of the words … he turned and looked.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There it was, hanging in the sky above the school: the blazing green skull with a serpent tongue, the mark Death Eaters left behind whenever they had entered a building … wherever they had murdered …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘When did it appear?’ asked Dumbledore, and his hand clenched painfully upon Harry’s shoulder as he struggled to his feet.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Must have been minutes ago, it wasn’t there when I put the cat out, but when I got upstairs –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We need to return to the castle at once,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Rosmerta,’ and though he staggered a little, he seemed wholly in command of the situation, ‘we need transport – brooms –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve got a couple behind the bar,’ she said, looking very frightened. ‘Shall I run and fetch –?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, Harry can do it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry raised his wand at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Accio Rosmerta’s brooms.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: A second later they heard a loud bang as the front door of the pub burst open; two brooms had shot out into the street and were racing each other to Harry’s side, where they stopped dead, quivering slightly, at waist height.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Rosmerta, please send a message to the Ministry,’ said Dumbledore, as he mounted the broom nearest him. ‘It might be that nobody within Hogwarts has yet realised anything is wrong … Harry, put on your Invisibility Cloak.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry pulled his Cloak out of his pocket and threw it over himself before mounting his broom; Madam Rosmerta was already tottering back towards her pub as Harry and Dumbledore kicked off from the ground and rose up into the air. As they sped towards the castle, Harry glanced sideways at Dumbledore, ready to grab him should he fall, but the sight of the Dark Mark seemed to have acted upon Dumbledore like a stimulant: he was bent low over his broom, his eyes fixed upon the Mark, his long silver hair and beard flying behind him in the night air. And Harry, too, looked ahead at the skull, and fear swelled inside him like a venomous bubble, compressing his lungs, driving all other discomfort from his mind …

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: How long had they been away? Had Ron, Hermione and Ginny’s luck run out by now? Was it one of them who had caused the Mark to be set over the school, or was it Neville, or Luna, or some other member of the DA? And if it was … he was the one who had told them to patrol the corridors, he had asked them to leave the safety of their beds … would he be responsible, again, for the death of a friend?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: As they flew over the dark, twisting lane down which they had walked earlier, Harry heard, over the whistling of the night air in his ears, Dumbledore muttering in some strange language again. He thought he understood why as he felt his broom shudder for a moment when they flew over the boundary wall into the grounds: Dumbledore was undoing the enchantments he himself had set around the castle, so that they could enter at speed. The Dark Mark was glittering directly above the Astronomy Tower, the highest of the castle. Did that mean the death had occurred there?

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore had already crossed the crenellated ramparts and was dismounting; Harry landed next to him seconds later and looked around.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The ramparts were deserted. The door to the spiral staircase that led back into the castle was closed. There was no sign of a struggle, of a fight to the death, of a body.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘What does it mean?’ Harry asked Dumbledore, looking up at the green skull with its serpent’s tongue glinting evilly above them. ‘Is it the real Mark? Has someone definitely been – Professor?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: In the dim green glow from the Mark Harry saw Dumbledore clutching at his chest with his blackened hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Go and wake Severus,’ said Dumbledore faintly but clearly. ‘Tell him what has happened and bring him to me. Do nothing else, speak to nobody else and do not remove your Cloak. I shall wait here.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You swore to obey me, Harry – go!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry hurried over to the door leading to the spiral staircase, but his hand had only just closed upon the iron ring of the door when he heard running footsteps on the other side. He looked round at Dumbledore, who gestured to him to retreat. Harry backed away, drawing his wand as he did so.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The door burst open and somebody erupted through it and shouted: ‘Expelliarmus!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry’s body became instantly rigid and immobile, and he felt himself fall back against the Tower wall, propped like an unsteady statue, unable to move or speak. He could not understand how it had happened – Expelliarmus was not a Freezing Charm –

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Then, by the light of the Mark, he saw Dumbledore’s wand flying in an arc over the edge of the ramparts and understood … Dumbledore had wordlessly immobilised Harry, and the second he had taken to perform the spell had cost him the chance of defending himself.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Standing against the ramparts, very white in the face, Dumbledore still showed no sign of panic or distress. He merely looked across at his disarmer and said, ‘Good evening, Draco.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy stepped forwards, glancing around quickly to check that he and Dumbledore were alone. His eyes fell upon the second broom.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Who else is here?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘A question I might ask you. Or are you acting alone?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Harry saw Malfoy’s pale eyes shift back to Dumbledore in the greenish glare of the Mark.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ he said. ‘I’ve got back-up. There are Death Eaters here in your school tonight.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, well,’ said Dumbledore, as though Malfoy was showing him an ambitious homework project. ‘Very good indeed. You found a way to let them in, did you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Malfoy, who was panting. ‘Right under your nose and you never realised!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Ingenious,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Yet … forgive me … where are they now? You seem unsupported.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘They met some of your guard. They’re having a fight down below. They won’t be long … I came on ahead. I – I’ve got a job to do.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, then, you must get on and do it, my dear boy,’ said Dumbledore softly.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was silence. Harry stood imprisoned within his own invisible, paralysed body, staring at the two of them, his ears straining to hear sounds of the Death Eaters’ distant fight, and in front of him, Draco Malfoy did nothing but stare at Albus Dumbledore who, incredibly, smiled.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Draco, Draco, you are not a killer.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘How do you know?’ said Malfoy at once.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: He seemed to realise how childish the words had sounded; Harry saw him flush in the Mark’s greenish light.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You don’t know what I’m capable of,’ said Malfoy more forcefully, ‘you don’t know what I’ve done!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yes, I do,’ said Dumbledore mildly. ‘You almost killed Katie Bell and Ronald Weasley. You have been trying, with increasing desperation, to kill me all year. Forgive me, Draco, but they have been feeble attempts … so feeble, to be honest, that I wonder whether your heart has been really in it …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘It has been in it!’ said Malfoy vehemently. ‘I’ve been working on it all year, and tonight –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Somewhere in the depths of the castle below Harry heard a muffled yell. Malfoy stiffened and glanced over his shoulder.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Somebody is putting up a good fight,’ said Dumbledore conversationally. ‘But you were saying … yes, you have managed to introduce Death Eaters into my school which, I admit, I thought impossible … how did you do it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But Malfoy said nothing: he was still listening to whatever was happening below and seemed almost as paralysed as Harry was.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Perhaps you ought to get on with the job alone,’ suggested Dumbledore. ‘What if your back-up has been thwarted by my guard? As you have perhaps realised, there are members of the Order of the Phoenix here tonight, too. And after all, you don’t really need help … I have no wand at the moment … I cannot defend myself.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy merely stared at him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I see,’ said Dumbledore kindly, when Malfoy neither moved nor spoke. ‘You are afraid to act until they join you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m not afraid!’ snarled Malfoy, though he still made no move to hurt Dumbledore. ‘It’s you who should be scared!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But why? I don’t think you will kill me, Draco. Killing is not nearly as easy as the innocent believe … so tell me, while we wait for your friends … how did you smuggle them in here? It seems to have taken you a long time to work out how to do it.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy looked as though he was fighting down the urge to shout, or to vomit. He gulped and took several deep breaths, glaring at Dumbledore, his wand pointing directly at the latter’s heart. Then, as though he could not help himself, he said, ‘I had to mend that broken Vanishing Cabinet that no one’s used for years. The one Montague got lost in last year.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Aaaah.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore’s sigh was half a groan. He closed his eyes for a moment.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That was clever … there is a pair, I take it?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘The other’s in Borgin and Burkes,’ said Malfoy, ‘and they make a kind of passage between them. Montague told me that when he was stuck in the Hogwarts one, he was trapped in limbo but sometimes he could hear what was going on at school, and sometimes what was going on in the shop, as if the Cabinet was travelling between them, but he couldn’t make anyone hear him … in the end he managed to Apparate out, even though he’d never passed his test. He nearly died doing it. Everyone thought it was a really good story, but I was the only one who realised what it meant – even Borgin didn’t know – I was the one who realised there could be a way into Hogwarts through the Cabinets if I fixed the broken one.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Very good,’ murmured Dumbledore. ‘So the Death Eaters were able to pass from Borgin and Burkes into the school to help you … a clever plan, a very clever plan … and, as you say, right under my nose …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah,’ said Malfoy who, bizarrely, seemed to draw courage and comfort from Dumbledore’s praise. ‘Yeah, it was!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But there were times,’ Dumbledore went on, ‘weren’t there, when you were not sure you would succeed in mending the Cabinet? And you resorted to crude and badly judged measures such as sending me a cursed necklace that was bound to reach the wrong hands … poisoning mead there was only the slightest chance I might drink …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, well, you still didn’t realise who was behind that stuff, did you?’ sneered Malfoy, as Dumbledore slid a little down the ramparts, the strength in his legs apparently fading, and Harry struggled fruitlessly, mutely, against the enchantment binding him.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘As a matter of fact, I did,’ said Dumbledore. ‘I was sure it was you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Why didn’t you stop me, then?’ Malfoy demanded.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I tried, Draco. Professor Snape has been keeping watch over you on my orders –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He hasn’t been doing your orders, he promised my mother –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course that is what he would tell you, Draco, but –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s a double-agent, you stupid old man, he isn’t working for you, you just think he is!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘We must agree to differ on that, Draco. It so happens that I trust Professor Snape –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, you’re losing your grip, then!’ sneered Malfoy. ‘He’s been offering me plenty of help – wanting all the glory for himself – wanting a bit of the action – “What are you doing? Did you do the necklace, that was stupid, it could have blown everything –” But I haven’t told him what I’ve been doing in the Room of Requirement, he’s going to wake up tomorrow and it’ll all be over and he won’t be the Dark Lord’s favourite any more, he’ll be nothing compared to me, nothing!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Very gratifying,’ said Dumbledore mildly. ‘We all like appreciation for our own hard work, of course … but you must have had an accomplice, all the same … someone in Hogsmeade, someone who was able to slip Katie the – the – aaaah …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore closed his eyes again and nodded, as though he was about to fall asleep.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘… of course … Rosmerta. How long has she been under the Imperius Curse?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Got there at last, have you?’ Malfoy taunted.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: There was another yell from below, rather louder than the last. Malfoy looked nervously over his shoulder again, then back at Dumbledore, who went on, ‘So poor Rosmerta was forced to lurk in her own bathroom and pass that necklace to any Hogwarts student who entered the room unaccompanied? And the poisoned mead … well, naturally, Rosmerta was able to poison it for you before she sent the bottle to Slughorn, believing that it was to be my Christmas present … yes, very neat … very neat … poor Mr Filch would not, of course, think to check a bottle of Rosmerta’s … tell me, how have you been communicating with Rosmerta? I thought we had all methods of communication in and out of the school monitored.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Enchanted coins,’ said Malfoy, as though he was compelled to keep talking, though his wand hand was shaking badly. ‘I had one and she had the other and I could send her messages –’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Isn’t that the secret method of communication the group that called themselves Dumbledore’s Army used last year?’ asked Dumbledore. His voice was light and conversational, but Harry saw him slip an inch lower down the wall as he said it.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, I got the idea from them,’ said Malfoy, with a twisted smile. ‘I got the idea of poisoning the mead from the Mudblood Granger, as well, I heard her talking in the library about Filch not recognising potions …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Please do not use that offensive word in front of me,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy gave a harsh laugh.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘You care about me saying “Mudblood” when I’m about to kill you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy’s mouth contorted involuntarily, as though he had tasted something very bitter.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, about tonight,’ Dumbledore went on, ‘I am a little puzzled about how it happened … you knew that I had left the school? But of course,’ he answered his own question, ‘Rosmerta saw me leaving, she tipped you off using your ingenious coins, I’m sure …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘That’s right,’ said Malfoy. ‘But she said you were just going for a drink, you’d be back …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, they do that,’ said Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘There is little time, one way or another,’ said Dumbledore. ‘So let us discuss your options, Draco.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘My dear boy, let us have no more pretence about that. If you were going to kill me, you would have done it when you first Disarmed me, you would not have stopped for this pleasant chat about ways and means.’

text_content: ‘I haven’t got any options!’ said Malfoy, and he was suddenly as white as Dumbledore. ‘I’ve got to do it! He’ll kill me! He’ll kill my whole family!’

text_content: ‘I appreciate the difficulty of your position,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Why else do you think I have not confronted you before now? Because I knew that you would have been murdered if Lord Voldemort realised that I suspected you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy winced at the sound of the name.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘I did not dare speak to you of the mission with which I knew you had been entrusted, in case he used Legilimency against you,’ continued Dumbledore. ‘But now at last we can speak plainly to each other … no harm has been done, you have hurt nobody, though you are very lucky that your unintentional victims survived … I can help you, Draco.’

text_content: ‘No, you can’t,’ said Malfoy, his wand hand shaking very badly indeed. ‘Nobody can. He told me to do it or he’ll kill me. I’ve got no choice.’

text_content: ‘Come over to the right side, Draco, and we can hide you more completely than you can possibly imagine. book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy stared at Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But I got this far, didn’t I?’ he said slowly. ‘They thought I’d die in the attempt, but I’m here … and you’re in my power … I’m the one with the wand … you’re at my mercy …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, Draco,’ said Dumbledore quietly. ‘It is my mercy, and not yours, that matters now.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Malfoy did not speak. His mouth was open, his wand hand still trembling. Harry thought he saw it drop by a fraction –

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: A lumpy-looking man with an odd lopsided leer gave a wheezy giggle.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Dumbledore cornered!’ he said, and he turned to a stocky little woman who looked as though she could be his sister and who was grinning eagerly. ‘Dumbledore wandless, Dumbledore alone! Well done, Draco, well done!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Good evening, Amycus,’ said Dumbledore calmly, as though welcoming the man to a tea party. ‘And you’ve brought Alecto too … charming …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: The woman gave an angry little titter.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Think your little jokes’ll help you on your death bed, then?’ she jeered.

text_content: ‘Jokes? No, no, these are manners,’ replied Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Is that you, Fenrir?’ asked Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No, I cannot say that I am …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘But you know how much I like kids, Dumbledore.’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: And he raised a yellow fingernail and picked at his front teeth, leering at Dumbledore.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said the fourth Death Eater sharply. He had a heavy, brutal-looking face. ‘We’ve got orders. Draco’s got to do it. Now, Draco, and quickly.’

text_content: Malfoy was showing less resolution than ever. He looked terrified as he stared into Dumbledore’s face, which was even paler, and rather lower than usual, as he had slid so far down the rampart wall.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘He’s not long for this world anyway, if you ask me!’ said the lopsided man, to the accompaniment of his sister’s wheezing giggles. ‘Look at him – what’s happened to you, then, Dumby?’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, weaker resistance, slower reflexes, Amycus,’ said Dumbledore. ‘Old age, in short … one day, perhaps, it will happen to you … if you are lucky …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But at that moment, there were renewed sounds of scuffling from below and a voice shouted, ‘They’ve blocked the stairs – Reducto! REDUCTO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, Draco, quickly!’ said the brutal-faced man angrily.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: But Malfoy’s hand was shaking so badly that he could barely aim.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Severus …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Snape said nothing, but walked forwards and pushed Malfoy roughly out of the way. The three Death Eaters fell back without a word. Even the werewolf seemed cowed.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: Snape gazed for a moment at Dumbledore, and there was revulsion and hatred etched in the harsh lines of his face.

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Severus … please …’

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)

book: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (UK)
text_content: ‘Avada Kedavra!’
