text_content: ‘Obsession?’ said Hermione, in a low, fierce voice, when Harry was careless enough to use the word one evening, after Hermione had told him off for his lack of interest in locating more Horcruxes. ‘We’re not the ones with an obsession, Harry! We’re the ones trying to do what Dumbledore wanted us to do!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: But he was impervious to the veiled criticism. Dumbledore had left the sign of the Hallows for Hermione to decipher and he had also, Harry remained convinced of it, left the Resurrection Stone hidden in the golden Snitch. Neither can live while the other survives … master of death … why didn’t Ron and Hermione understand?

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘“The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death”,’ Harry quoted calmly.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I thought it was You-Know-Who we were supposed to be fighting?’ Hermione retorted, and Harry gave up on her.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Even the mystery of the silver doe, which the other two insisted on discussing, seemed less important to Harry now, a vaguely interesting sideshow. The only other thing that mattered to him was that his scar had begun to prickle again, although he did all he could to hide this fact from the other two. He sought solitude whenever it happened, but was disappointed by what he saw. The visions he and Voldemort were sharing had changed in quality; they had become blurred, shifting as though they were moving in and out of focus. Harry was just able to make out the indistinct features of an object that looked like a skull, and something like a mountain that was more shadow than substance. Used to images sharp as reality, Harry was disconcerted by the change. He was worried that the connection between himself and Voldemort had been damaged, a connection that he both feared and, whatever he had told Hermione, prized. Somehow Harry connected these unsatisfying, vague images with the destruction of his wand, as if it was the blackthorn wand’s fault that he could no longer see into Voldemort’s mind as well as before.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: As the weeks crept on, Harry could not help but notice, even through his new self-absorption, that Ron seemed to be taking charge. Perhaps because he was determined to make up for having walked out on them: perhaps because Harry’s descent into listlessness galvanised his dormant leadership qualities, Ron was the one now encouraging and exhorting the other two into action.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Three Horcruxes left,’ he kept saying. ‘We need a plan of action, come on! Where haven’t we looked? Let’s go through it again. The orphanage …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Diagon Alley, Hogwarts, the Riddle House, Borgin and Burkes, Albania, every place that they knew Tom Riddle had ever lived or worked, visited or murdered in, Ron and Hermione raked over them again, Harry joining in only to stop Hermione pestering him. He would have been happy to sit alone in silence, trying to read Voldemort’s thoughts, to find out more about the Elder Wand, but Ron insisted on journeying to ever more unlikely places simply, Harry was aware, to keep them moving.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You never know,’ was Ron’s constant refrain. ‘Upper Flagley is a wizarding village, he might’ve wanted to live there. Let’s go and have a poke around.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: These frequent forays into wizarding territory brought them within occasional sight of Snatchers.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Some of them are supposed to be as bad as Death Eaters,’ said Ron. ‘The lot that got me were a bit pathetic, but Bill reckons some of them are really dangerous. They said on Potterwatch -’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘On what?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Potterwatch, didn’t I tell you that’s what it was called? The programme I keep trying to get on the radio, the only one that tells the truth about what’s going on! Nearly all the programmes are following You-Know-Who’s line, all except Potterwatch. I really want you to hear it, but it’s tricky tuning in …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron spent evening after evening using his wand to beat out various rhythms on top of the wireless while the dials whirled. Occasionally they would catch snatches of advice on how to treat dragon pox, and once, a few bars of ‘A Cauldron Full of Hot, Strong Love’. While he tapped, Ron continued to try to hit on the correct password, muttering strings of random words under his breath.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘They’re normally something to do with the Order,’ he told them. ‘Bill had a real knack for guessing them. I’m bound to get one in the end …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: But not until March did luck favour Ron at last. Harry was sitting in the tent entrance, on guard duty, staring idly at a clump of grape hyacinths that had forced their way through the chilly ground, when Ron shouted excitedly from inside the tent.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ve got it, I’ve got it! Password was “Albus”! Get in here, Harry!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Roused for the first time in days from his contemplation of the Deathly Hallows, Harry hurried back inside the tent to find Ron and Hermione kneeling on the floor beside the little radio. Hermione, who had been polishing the sword of Gryffindor just for something to do, was sitting open-mouthed, staring at the tiny speaker, from which a most familiar voice was issuing.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘… apologise for our temporary absence from the airwaves, which was due to a number of house-calls in our area by those charming Death Eaters.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘But that’s Lee Jordan!’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I know!’ beamed Ron. ‘Cool, eh?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘… now found ourselves another secure location,’ Lee was saying, ‘and I’m pleased to tell you that two of our regular contributors have joined me here this evening. Evening, boys!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Hi.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Evening, River.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘“River”, that’s Lee,’ Ron explained. ‘They’ve all got code names, but you can usually tell -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Shh!’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘But before we hear from Royal and Romulus,’ Lee went on, ‘let’s take a moment to report those deaths that the Wizarding Wireless Network News and the Daily Prophet don’t think important enough to mention. It is with great regret that we inform our listeners of the murders of Ted Tonks and Dirk Cresswell.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry felt a sick swooping in his belly. He, Ron and Hermione gazed at one another in horror.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘A goblin by the name of Gornuk was also killed. It is believed that Muggle-born Dean Thomas and a second goblin, both believed to have been travelling with Tonks, Cresswell and Gornuk, may have escaped. If Dean is listening, or if anyone has any knowledge of his whereabouts, his parents and sisters are desperate for news.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Meanwhile, in Gaddley, a Muggle family of five has been found dead in their home. Muggle authorities are attributing the deaths to a gas leak, but members of the Order of the Phoenix inform me that it was the Killing Curse - more evidence, as if it were needed, of the fact that Muggle slaughter is becoming little more than a recreational sport under the new regime.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Finally, we regret to inform our listeners that the remains of Bathilda Bagshot have been discovered in Godric’s Hollow. The evidence is that she died several months ago. The Order of the Phoenix informs us that her body showed unmistakable signs of injuries inflicted by Dark Magic.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Listeners, I’d like to invite you now to join us in a minute’s silence in memory of Ted Tonks, Dirk Cresswell, Bathilda Bagshot, Gornuk and the unnamed, but no less regretted, Muggles murdered by the Death Eaters.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Silence fell, and Harry, Ron and Hermione did not speak. Half of Harry yearned to hear more, half of him was afraid of what might come next. It was the first time he had felt fully connected to the outside world for a long time.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Thank you,’ said Lee’s voice. ‘And now we turn to regular contributor, Royal, for an update on how the new wizarding order is affecting the Muggle world.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Thanks, River,’ said an unmistakable voice, deep, measured, reassuring.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Kingsley!’ burst out Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We know!’ said Hermione, hushing him.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Muggles remain ignorant of the source of their suffering as they continue to sustain heavy casualties,’ said Kingsley. ‘However, we continue to hear truly inspirational stories of wizards and witches risking their own safety to protect Muggle friends and neighbours, often without the Muggles’ knowledge. I’d like to appeal to all our listeners to emulate their example, perhaps by casting a protective charm over any Muggle dwellings in your street. Many lives could be saved if such simple measures are taken.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And what would you say, Royal, to those listeners who reply that in these dangerous times, it should be “wizards first”?’ asked Lee.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’d say that it’s one short step from “wizards first” to “purebloods first”, and then to “Death Eaters”,’ replied Kingsley. ‘We’re all human, aren’t we? Every human life is worth the same, and worth saving.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Excellently put, Royal, and you’ve got my vote for Minister for Magic if ever we get out of this mess,’ said Lee. ‘And now, over to Romulus for our popular feature: Pals of Potter.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Thanks, River,’ said another very familiar voice; Ron started to speak, but Hermione forestalled him in a whisper.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We know it’s Lupin!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Romulus, do you maintain, as you have every time you’ve appeared on our programme, that Harry Potter is still alive?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I do,’ said Lupin firmly. ‘There is no doubt at all in my mind that his death would be proclaimed as widely as possible by the Death Eaters if it had happened, because it would strike a deadly blow at the morale of those resisting the new regime. The “Boy Who Lived” remains a symbol of everything for which we are fighting: the triumph of good, the power of innocence, the need to keep resisting.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: A mixture of gratitude and shame welled up in Harry. Had Lupin forgiven him, then, for the terrible things he had said when they had last met?

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And what would you say to Harry if you knew he was listening, Romulus?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’d tell him we’re all with him in spirit,’ said Lupin, then hesitated slightly. ‘And I’d tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry looked at Hermione, whose eyes were full of tears.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Nearly always right,’ she repeated.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, didn’t I tell you?’ said Ron in surprise. ‘Bill told me Lupin’s living with Tonks again! And apparently she’s getting pretty big too.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘… and our usual update on those friends of Harry Potter’s who are suffering for their allegiance?’ Lee was saying.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, as regular listeners will know, several of the more outspoken supporters of Harry Potter have now been imprisoned, including Xenophilius Lovegood, erstwhile editor of The Quibbler -‘ said Lupin.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘At least he’s still alive!’ muttered Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We have also heard within the last few hours that Rubeus Hagrid -‘ all three of them gasped, and so nearly missed the rest of the sentence ‘- well-known gamekeeper at Hogwarts School, has narrowly escaped arrest within the grounds of Hogwarts, where he is rumoured to have hosted a “Support Harry Potter” party in his house. However, Hagrid was not taken into custody, and is, we believe, on the run.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I suppose it helps, when escaping from Death Eaters, if you’ve got a sixteen-foot-high half-brother?’ asked Lee.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘It would tend to give you an edge,’ agreed Lupin gravely. ‘May I just add that while we here at Potterwatch applaud Hagrid’s spirit, we would urge even the most devoted of Harry’s supporters against following Hagrid’s lead. “Support Harry Potter” parties are unwise in the present climate.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Indeed they are, Romulus,’ said Lee, ‘so we suggest that you continue to show your devotion to the man with the lightning scar by listening to Potterwatch! And now let’s move to news concerning the wizard who is proving just as elusive as Harry Potter. We like to refer to him as the Chief Death Eater, and here to give his views on some of the more insane rumours circulating about him, I’d like to introduce a new correspondent: Rodent.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘“Rodent”?’ said yet another familiar voice, and Harry, Ron and Hermione cried out together: ‘Fred!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘No - is it George?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s Fred, I think,’ said Ron, leaning in closer, as whichever twin it was said, ‘I’m not being “Rodent”, no way, I told you I wanted to be “Rapier”!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, all right then. “Rapier”, could you please give us your take on the various stories we’ve been hearing about the Chief Death Eater?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, River, I can,’ said Fred. ‘As our listeners will know, unless they’ve taken refuge at the bottom of a garden pond or somewhere similar, You-Know-Who’s strategy of remaining in the shadows is creating a nice little climate of panic. Mind you, if all the alleged sightings of him are genuine, we must have a good nineteen You-Know-Whos running around the place.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Which suits him, of course,’ said Kingsley. ‘The air of mystery is creating more terror than actually showing himself.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Agreed,’ said Fred. ‘So, people, let’s try and calm down a bit. Things are bad enough without inventing stuff as well. For instance, this new idea that You-Know-Who can kill with a single glance from his eyes. That’s a Basilisk, listeners. One simple test: check whether the thing that’s glaring at you has got legs. If it has, it’s safe to look into its eyes, although if it really is You-Know-Who, that’s still likely to be the last thing you ever do.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: For the first time in weeks and weeks, Harry was laughing: he could feel the weight of tension leaving him.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And the rumours that he keeps being sighted abroad?’ asked Lee.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, who wouldn’t want a nice little holiday after all the hard work he’s been putting in?’ asked Fred. ‘Point is, people, don’t get lulled into a false sense of security, thinking he’s out of the country. Maybe he is, maybe he isn’t, but the fact remains he can move faster than Severus Snape confronted with shampoo when he wants to, so don’t count on him being a long way away if you’re planning on taking any risks. I never thought I’d hear myself say it, but safety first!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Thank you very much for those wise words, Rapier,’ said Lee. ‘Listeners, that brings us to the end of another Potterwatch. We don’t know when it will be possible to broadcast again, but you can be sure we shall be back. Keep twiddling those dials: the next password will be “Mad-Eye”. Keep each other safe: keep faith. Goodnight.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The radio’s dial twirled and the lights behind the tuning panel went out. Harry, Ron and Hermione were still beaming. Hearing familiar, friendly voices was an extraordinary tonic; Harry had become so used to their isolation he had nearly forgotten that other people were resisting Voldemort. It was like waking from a long sleep.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Good, eh?’ said Ron happily.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Brilliant,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘It’s so brave of them,’ sighed Hermione admiringly. ‘If they were found …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, they keep on the move, don’t they?’ said Ron. ‘Like us.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘But did you hear what Fred said?’ asked Harry excitedly; now the broadcast was over, his thoughts turned again towards his all-consuming obsession. ‘He’s abroad! He’s still looking for the wand, I knew it!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Come on, Hermione, why are you so determined not to admit it? Vol—’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘HARRY, NO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘—demort’s after the Elder Wand!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘The name’s Taboo!’ Ron bellowed, leaping to his feet as a loud crack sounded outside the tent. ‘I told you, Harry, I told you, we can’t say it any more - we’ve got to put the protection back around us - quickly - it’s how they find -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: But Ron stopped talking, and Harry knew why. The Sneakoscope on the table had lit up and begun to spin; they could hear voices coming nearer and nearer: rough, excited voices. Ron pulled the Deluminator out of his pocket and clicked it: their lamps went out.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Come out of there with your hands up!’ came a rasping voice through the darkness. ‘We know you’re in there! You’ve got half a dozen wands pointing at you and we don’t care who we curse!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry looked round at the other two, now mere outlines in the darkness. He saw Hermione point her wand, not towards the outside, but into his face; there was a bang, a burst of white light, and he buckled in agony, unable to see. He could feel his face swelling rapidly under his hands, as heavy footfalls surrounded him.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Get up, vermin.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Unknown hands dragged Harry roughly off the ground. Before he could stop them, someone had rummaged through his pockets and removed the blackthorn wand. Harry clutched at his excruciatingly painful face, which felt unrecognisable beneath his fingers, tight, swollen and puffy as though he had suffered some violent allergic reaction. His eyes had been reduced to slits through which he could barely see; his glasses fell off as he was bundled out of the tent; all he could make out were the blurred shapes of four or five people wrestling Ron and Hermione outside too.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Get - off - her!’ Ron shouted. There was the unmistakable sound of knuckles hitting flesh: Ron grunted in pain and Hermione screamed, ‘No! Leave him alone, leave him alone!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Your boyfriend’s going to have worse than that done to him if he’s on my list,’ said the horribly familiar, rasping voice. ‘Delicious girl … what a treat … I do enjoy the softness of the skin …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry’s stomach turned over. He knew who this was: Fenrir Greyback, the werewolf who was permitted to wear Death Eater robes in return for his hired savagery.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Search the tent!’ said another voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry was thrown, face down, on to the ground. A thud told him that Ron had been cast down beside him. They could hear footsteps and crashes; the men were pushing over chairs inside the tent as they searched.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Now, let’s see who we’ve got,’ said Greyback’s gloating voice from overhead, and Harry was rolled over on to his back. A beam of wandlight fell into his face and Greyback laughed.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’ll be needing Butterbeer to wash this one down. What happened to you, ugly?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry did not answer immediately.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I said,’ repeated Greyback, and Harry received a blow to the diaphragm that made him double over in pain, ‘what happened to you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Stung,’ Harry muttered. ‘Been stung.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah, looks like it,’ said a second voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s your name?’ snarled Greyback.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dudley,’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And your first name?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I - Vernon. Vernon Dudley.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Check the list, Scabior,’ said Greyback, and Harry heard him move sideways to look down at Ron, instead. ‘And what about you, Ginger?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Stan Shunpike,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Like ‘ell you are,’ said the man called Scabior. ‘We know Stan Shunpike, ‘e’s put a bit of work our way.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: There was another thud.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’b Bardy,’ said Ron, and Harry could tell that his mouth was full of blood. ‘Bardy Weadley.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘A Weasley?’ rasped Greyback. ‘So you’re related to blood traitors even if you’re not a Mudblood. And lastly, your pretty little friend …’ The relish in his voice made Harry’s flesh crawl.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Easy, Greyback,’ said Scabior, over the jeering of the others.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, I’m not going to bite just yet. We’ll see if she’s a bit quicker at remembering her name than Barny. Who are you, girly?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Penelope Clearwater,’ said Hermione. She sounded terrified, but convincing.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What’s your Blood Status?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Half-blood,’ said Hermione.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Easy enough to check,’ said Scabior. ‘But the ‘ole lot of ‘em look like they could still be ‘Ogwarts age -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We’b lebt,’ said Ron.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Left, ‘ave you, Ginger?’ said Scabior. ‘And you decided to go camping? And you thought, just for a laugh, you’d use the Dark Lord’s name?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Nod a laugh,’ said Ron. ‘Aggiden.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Accident?’ There was more jeering laughter.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You know who used to like using the Dark Lord’s name, Weasley?’ growled Greyback. ‘The Order of the Phoenix. Mean anything to you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Doh.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Well, they don’t show the Dark Lord proper respect, so the name’s been Tabooed. A few Order members have been tracked that way. We’ll see. Bind them up with the other two prisoners!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Someone yanked Harry up by the hair, dragged him a short way, pushed him down into a sitting position, then started binding him back-to-back with other people. Harry was still half-blind, barely able to see anything through his puffed-up eyes. When at last the man tying them had walked away, Harry whispered to the other prisoners.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Anyone still got a wand?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Ron and Hermione from either side of him.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘This is all my fault. I said the name, I’m sorry -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: It was a new, but familiar, voice, and it came from directly behind Harry, from the person tied to Hermione’s left.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dean?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘It is you! If they find out who they’ve got -! They’re Snatchers, they’re only looking for truants to sell for gold -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Not a bad little haul for one night,’ Greyback was saying, as a pair of hobnailed boots marched close by Harry and they heard more crashes from inside the tent. ‘A Mudblood, a runaway goblin and three truants. You checked their names on the list yet, Scabior?’ he roared.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Yeah. There’s no Vernon Dudley on ‘ere, Greyback.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Interesting,’ said Greyback. ‘That’s interesting.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He crouched down beside Harry, who saw, through the infinitesimal gap left between his swollen eyelids, a face covered in matted, grey hair and whiskers, with pointed brown teeth and sores at the corners of his mouth. Greyback smelled as he had done at the top of the Tower where Dumbledore had died: of dirt, sweat and blood.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘So you aren’t wanted, then, Vernon? Or are you on that list under a different name? What house were you in at Hogwarts?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Slytherin,’ said Harry automatically.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)

She cut Hermione free from the other prisoners, then dragged her by the hair into the middle of the room while Greyback forced the rest of them to shuffle across to another door, into a dark passageway, his wand held out in front of him, projecting an invisible and irresistible force.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Reckon she’ll let me have a bit of the girl when she’s finished with her?’ Greyback crooned, as he forced them along the corridor. ‘I’d say I’ll get a bite or two, wouldn’t you, Ginger?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry could feel Ron shaking. They were forced down a steep flight of stairs, still tied back-to-back and in danger of slipping and breaking their necks at any moment. At the bottom was a heavy door. Greyback unlocked it with a tap of his wand, then forced them into a dank and musty room and left them in total darkness. The echoing bang of the slammed cellar door had not died away before there was a terrible, drawn-out scream from directly above them.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘HERMIONE!’ Ron bellowed, and he started to writhe and struggle against the ropes tying them together, so that Harry staggered. ‘HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Be quiet!’ Harry said. ‘Shut up, Ron, we need to work out a way -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘HERMIONE! HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We need a plan, stop yelling - we need to get these ropes off -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry?’ came a whisper through the darkness. ‘Ron? Is that you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron stopped shouting. There was a sound of movement close by them, then Harry saw a shadow moving closer.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry? Ron?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Luna?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes, it’s me! Oh, no, I didn’t want you to be caught!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Luna, can you help us get these ropes off?’ said Harry.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, yes, I expect so … there’s an old nail we use if we need to break anything … just a moment …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Hermione screamed again from overhead, and they could hear Bellatrix screaming too, but her words were inaudible, for Ron shouted again, ‘HERMIONE! HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Mr Ollivander?’ Harry could hear Luna saying. ‘Mr Ollivander, have you got the nail? If you just move over a little bit … I think it was beside the water jug …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: She was back within seconds.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You’ll need to stay still,’ she said.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry could feel her digging at the rope’s tough fibres to work the knots free. From upstairs they heard Bellatrix’s voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I’m going to ask you again! Where did you get this sword? Where?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We found it - we found it - PLEASE!’ Hermione screamed again; Ron struggled harder than ever and the rusty nail slipped on to Harry’s wrist.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron, please stay still!’ Luna whispered. ‘I can’t see what I’m doing -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘My pocket!’ said Ron. ‘In my pocket, there’s a Deluminator, and it’s full of light!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: A few seconds later, there was a click and the luminescent spheres the Deluminator had sucked from the lamps in the tent flew into the cellar: unable to rejoin their sources they simply hung there, like tiny suns, flooding the underground room with light. Harry saw Luna, all eyes in her white face, and the motionless figure of Ollivander the wandmaker, curled up on the floor in the corner. Craning round, he caught sight of their fellow prisoners: Dean and Griphook the goblin, who seemed barely conscious, kept standing by the ropes that bound him to the humans.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Oh, that’s much easier, thanks Ron,’ said Luna, and she began hacking at their bindings again. ‘Hello, Dean!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: From above came Bellatrix’s voice.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You are lying, filthy Mudblood, and I know it! You have been inside my vault at Gringotts! Tell the truth, tell the truth!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Another terrible scream -

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What else did you take? What else have you got? Tell me the truth or, I swear, I shall run you through with this knife!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘There!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry felt the ropes fall away and turned, rubbing his wrists, to see Ron running around the cellar, looking up at the low ceiling, searching for a trapdoor. Dean, his face bruised and bloody, said, ‘Thanks,’ to Luna and stood there, shivering, but Griphook sank on to the cellar floor looking groggy and disorientated, many welts across his swarthy face.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron was now trying to Disapparate without a wand.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘There’s no way out, Ron,’ said Luna, watching his fruitless efforts. ‘The cellar is completely escape-proof. I tried, at first. Mr Ollivander has been here for a long time, he’s tried everything.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Hermione was screaming again: the sound went through Harry like physical pain. Barely conscious of the fierce prickling of his scar, he, too, started to run around the cellar, feeling the walls for he hardly knew what, knowing in his heart that it was useless.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What else did you take, what else? ANSWER ME! CRUCIO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Hermione’s screams echoed off the walls upstairs, Ron was half sobbing as he pounded the walls with his fists, and Harry, in utter desperation, seized Hagrid’s pouch from around his neck and groped inside it: he pulled out Dumbledore’s Snitch and shook it, hoping for he did not know what - nothing happened; he waved the broken halves of the phoenix wand, but they were lifeless - the mirror fragment fell sparkling to the floor, and he saw a gleam of brightest blue -

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Dumbledore’s eye was gazing at him out of the mirror.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Help us!’ he yelled at it in mad desperation. ‘We’re in the cellar of Malfoy Manor, help us!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The eye blinked, and was gone.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry was not even sure that it had really been there. He tilted the shard of mirror this way and that, and saw nothing reflected there but the walls and ceiling of their prison, and upstairs Hermione was screaming worse than ever, and next to him, Ron was bellowing, ‘HERMIONE! HERMIONE!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘How did you get into my vault?’ they heard Bellatrix scream. ‘Did that dirty little goblin in the cellar help you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We only met him tonight!’ Hermione sobbed. ‘We’ve never been inside your vault … it isn’t the real sword! It’s a copy, just a copy!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘A copy?’ screeched Bellatrix. ‘Oh, a likely story!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘But we can find out easily!’ came Lucius’s voice. ‘Draco, fetch the goblin, he can tell us whether the sword is real or not!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry dashed across the cellar to where Griphook was huddled on the floor.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Griphook,’ he whispered into the goblin’s pointed ear, ‘you must tell them that sword’s a fake, they mustn’t know it’s the real one, Griphook, please -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He could hear someone scuttling down the cellar steps; next moment, Draco’s shaking voice spoke from behind the door.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Stand back. Line up against the back wall. Don’t try anything, or I’ll kill you!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: They did as they were bidden; as the lock turned Ron clicked the Deluminator and the lights whisked back into his pocket, restoring the cellar’s darkness. The door flew open; Malfoy marched inside, wand held out in front of him, pale and determined. He seized the little goblin by the arm and backed out again, dragging Griphook with him. The door slammed shut and at the same moment a loud crack echoed inside the cellar.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron clicked the Deluminator. Three balls of light flew back into the air from his pocket, revealing Dobby the house-elf, who had just Apparated into their midst.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘DOB—!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry hit Ron on the arm to stop him shouting, and Ron looked terrified at his mistake. Footsteps crossed the ceiling overhead: Draco marching Griphook to Bellatrix.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Dobby’s enormous, tennis-ball-shaped eyes were wide; he was trembling from his feet to the tips of his ears. He was back in the home of his old masters, and it was clear that he was petrified.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry Potter,’ he squeaked, in the tiniest quiver of a voice, ‘Dobby has come to rescue you.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘But how did you -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: An awful scream drowned Harry’s words: Hermione was being tortured again. He cut to the essentials.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You can Disapparate out of this cellar?’ he asked Dobby, who nodded, his ears flapping.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And you can take humans with you?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Dobby nodded again.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Right. Dobby, I want you to grab Luna, Dean and Mr Ollivander, and take them - take them to -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Bill and Fleur’s,’ said Ron. ‘Shell Cottage on the outskirts of Tinworth!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The elf nodded for a third time.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And then come back,’ said Harry. ‘Can you do that, Dobby?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Of course, Harry Potter,’ whispered the little elf. He hurried over to Mr Ollivander, who appeared to be barely conscious. He took one of the wandmaker’s hands in his own, then held out the other to Luna and Dean, neither of whom moved.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry, we want to help you!’ Luna whispered.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We can’t leave you here,’ said Dean.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Go, both of you! We’ll see you at Bill and Fleur’s.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: As Harry spoke, his scar burned worse than ever, and for a few seconds he looked down, not upon the wandmaker, but on another man who was just as old, just as thin, but laughing scornfully.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Kill me, then, Voldemort, I welcome death! But my death will not bring you what you seek … there is so much you do not understand …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He felt Voldemort’s fury, but as Hermione screamed again he shut it out, returning to the cellar and the horror of his own present.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Go!’ Harry beseeched Luna and Dean. ‘Go! We’ll follow, just go!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: They caught hold of the elf’s outstretched fingers. There was another loud crack, and Dobby, Luna, Dean and Ollivander vanished.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What was that?’ shouted Lucius Malfoy from over their heads. ‘Did you hear that? What was that noise in the cellar?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron stared at each other.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Draco - no, call Wormtail! Make him go and check!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Footsteps crossed the room overhead, then there was silence. Harry knew that the people in the drawing room were listening for more noises from the cellar.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘We’re going to have to try and tackle him,’ he whispered to Ron. They had no choice: the moment anyone entered the room and saw the absence of three prisoners, they were lost. ‘Leave the lights on,’ Harry added, and as they heard someone descending the steps outside the door, they backed against the wall on either side of it.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Stand back,’ came Wormtail’s voice. ‘Stand away from the door. I am coming in.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The door flew open. For a split second Wormtail gazed into the apparently empty cellar, ablaze with light from the three miniature suns floating in mid-air. Then Harry and Ron launched themselves upon him. Ron seized Wormtail’s wand arm and forced it upwards; Harry slapped a hand to his mouth, muffling his voice. Silently they struggled: Wormtail’s wand emitted sparks; his silver hand closed around Harry’s throat.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘What is it, Wormtail?’ called Lucius Malfoy from above.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Nothing!’ Ron called back, in a passable imitation of Wormtail’s wheezy voice. ‘All fine!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry could barely breathe.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You’re going to kill me?’ Harry choked, attempting to prise off the metal fingers. ‘After I saved your life? You owe me, Wormtail!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The silver fingers slackened. Harry had not expected it: he wrenched himself free, astonished, keeping his hand over Wormtail’s mouth. He saw the rat-like man’s small, watery eyes widen with fear and surprise: he seemed just as shocked as Harry at what his hand had done, at the tiny, merciful impulse it had betrayed, and he continued to struggle more powerfully, as though to undo that moment of weakness.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And we’ll have that,’ whispered Ron, tugging Wormtail’s wand from his other hand.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Wandless, helpless, Pettigrew’s pupils dilated in terror. His eyes had slid from Harry’s face to something else. His own silver fingers were moving inexorably towards his own throat.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘No -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Without pausing to think, Harry tried to drag back the hand, but there was no stopping it. The silver tool that Voldemort had given his most cowardly servant had turned upon its Disarmed and useless owner; Pettigrew was reaping his reward for his hesitation, his moment of pity; he was being strangled before their eyes.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘No!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron had released Wormtail too, and together he and Harry tried to pull the crushing metal fingers from around Wormtail’s throat, but it was no use. Pettigrew was turning blue.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Relashio!’ said Ron, pointing the wand at the silver hand, but nothing happened; Pettigrew dropped to his knees, and at the same moment, Hermione gave a dreadful scream from overhead. Wormtail’s eyes rolled upwards in his purple face, he gave a last twitch and was still.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry and Ron looked at each other, then, leaving Wormtail’s body on the floor behind them, ran up the stairs and back into the shadowy passageway leading to the drawing room. Cautiously they crept along it, until they reached the drawing-room door, which was ajar. Now they had a clear view of Bellatrix looking down at Griphook, who was holding Gryffindor’s sword in his long-fingered hands. Hermione was lying at Bellatrix’s feet. She was barely stirring.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Well?’ Bellatrix said to Griphook. ‘Is it the true sword?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry waited, holding his breath, fighting against the prickling of his scar.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘No,’ said Griphook. ‘It is a fake.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you sure?’ panted Bellatrix. ‘Quite sure?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Yes,’ said the goblin.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Relief broke across her face, all tension drained from it.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Good,’ she said, and with a casual flick of her wand she slashed another deep cut into the goblin’s face, and he dropped with a yell at her feet. She kicked him aside. ‘And now,’ she said, in a voice that burst with triumph, ‘we call the Dark Lord!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: And she pushed back her sleeve and touched her forefinger to the Dark Mark.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: At once, Harry’s scar felt as though it had split open again. His true surroundings vanished: he was Voldemort, and the skeletal wizard before him was laughing toothlessly at him; he was enraged at the summons he felt - he had warned them, he had told them to summon him for nothing less than Potter. If they were mistaken …

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Kill me, then!’ demanded the old man. ‘You will not win, you cannot win! That wand will never, ever be yours -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: And Voldemort’s fury broke: a burst of green light filled the prison room and the frail old body was lifted from its hard bed and then fell back, lifeless, and Voldemort returned to the window, his wrath barely controllable … they would suffer his retribution if they had no good reason for calling him back …

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘And I think,’ said Bellatrix’s voice, ‘we can dispose of the Mudblood. Greyback, take her if you want her.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘NOOOOOOOOOOOO!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron had burst into the drawing room; Bellatrix looked round, shocked; she turned her wand to face Ron instead -

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Expelliarmus!’ he roared, pointing Wormtail’s wand at Bellatrix, and hers flew into the air and was caught by Harry, who had sprinted after Ron. Lucius, Narcissa, Draco and Greyback wheeled about; Harry yelled, ‘Stupefy!’ and Lucius Malfoy collapsed on to the hearth. Jets of light flew from Draco’s, Narcissa’s and Greyback’s wands; Harry threw himself to the floor, rolling behind a sofa to avoid them.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘STOP OR SHE DIES!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Panting, Harry peered round the edge of the sofa. Bellatrix was supporting Hermione, who seemed to be unconscious, and was holding her short silver knife to Hermione’s throat.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Drop your wands,’ she whispered. ‘Drop them, or we’ll see exactly how filthy her blood is!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Ron stood rigid, clutching Wormtail’s wand. Harry straightened up, still holding Bellatrix’s.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘I said, drop them!’ she screeched, pressing the blade into Hermione’s throat: Harry saw beads of blood appear there.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘All right!’ he shouted, and he dropped Bellatrix’s wand on to the floor at his feet. Ron did the same with Wormtail’s. Both raised their hands to shoulder height.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Good!’ she leered. ‘Draco, pick them up! The Dark Lord is coming, Harry Potter! Your death approaches!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry knew it; his scar was bursting with the pain of it, and he could feel Voldemort flying through the sky from far away, over a dark and stormy sea, and soon he would be close enough to Apparate to them, and Harry could see no way out.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Now,’ said Bellatrix softly, as Draco hurried back with the wands, ‘Cissy, I think we ought to tie these little heroes up again, while Greyback takes care of Miss Mudblood. I am sure the Dark Lord will not begrudge you the girl, Greyback, after what you have done tonight.’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: At the last word there was a peculiar grinding noise from above. All of them looked upwards in time to see the crystal chandelier tremble; then, with a creak and an ominous jingling, it began to fall. Bellatrix was directly beneath it; dropping Hermione, she threw herself aside with a scream. The chandelier crashed to the floor in an explosion of crystal and chains, falling on top of Hermione and the goblin, who still clutched the sword of Gryffindor. Glittering shards of crystal flew in all directions: Draco doubled over, his hands covering his bloody face.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: As Ron ran to pull Hermione out of the wreckage, Harry took his chance; he leapt over an armchair and wrested the three wands from Draco’s grip, pointed all of them at Greyback and yelled: ‘Stupefy!’ The werewolf was lifted off his feet by the triple spell, flew up to the ceiling and then smashed to the ground.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: As Narcissa dragged Draco out of the way of further harm, Bellatrix sprang to her feet, her hair flying as she brandished the silver knife; but Narcissa had directed her wand at the doorway.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby!’ she screamed, and even Bellatrix froze. ‘You! You dropped the chandelier -?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The tiny elf trotted into the room, his shaking finger pointing at his old mistress.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You must not hurt Harry Potter,’ he squeaked.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Kill him, Cissy!’ shrieked Bellatrix, but there was another loud crack, and Narcissa’s wand, too, flew into the air and landed on the other side of the room.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘You dirty little monkey!’ bawled Bellatrix. ‘How dare you take a witch’s wand, how dare you defy your masters?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby has no master!’ squealed the elf. ‘Dobby is a free elf, and Dobby has come to save Harry Potter and his friends!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry’s scar was blinding him with pain. Dimly, he knew that they had moments, seconds before Voldemort was with them.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Ron, catch - and GO!’ he yelled, throwing one of the wands to him; then he bent down to tug Griphook out from under the chandelier. Hoisting the groaning goblin, who still clung to the sword, over one shoulder, Harry seized Dobby’s hand and he spun on the spot to Disapparate.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: As he turned into darkness, he caught one last view of the drawing room: of the pale, frozen figures of Narcissa and Draco, of the streak of red that was Ron’s hair, and a blur of flying silver, as Bellatrix’s knife flew across the room at the place where he was vanishing -

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Bill and Fleur’s … Shell Cottage …Bill and Fleur’s …

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He had disappeared into the unknown; all he could do was repeat the name of the destination and hope that it would suffice to take him there. The pain in his forehead pierced him and the weight of the goblin bore down upon him; he could feel the blade of Gryffindor’s sword bumping against his back; Dobby’s hand jerked in his; he wondered whether the elf was trying to take charge, to pull them in the right direction, and tried, by squeezing the fingers, to indicate that that was fine with him …

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: And then they hit solid earth and smelled salty air. Harry fell to his knees, relinquished Dobby’s hand and attempted to lower Griphook gently to the ground.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Are you all right?’ he said, as the goblin stirred, but Griphook merely whimpered.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: Harry squinted around through the darkness. There seemed to be a cottage a short way away under the wide, starry sky, and he thought he saw movement outside it.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby, is this Shell Cottage?’ he whispered, clutching the two wands he had brought from the Malfoys’, ready to fight if he needed to. ‘Have we come to the right place? Dobby?’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He looked around. The little elf stood feet from him.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘DOBBY!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The elf swayed slightly, stars reflected in his wide, shining eyes. Together, he and Harry looked down at the silver hilt of the knife protruding from the elf’s heaving chest.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby - no - HELP!’ Harry bellowed towards the cottage, towards the people moving there. ‘HELP!’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: He did not know or care whether they were wizards or Muggles, friends or foes; all he cared about was that a dark stain was spreading across Dobby’s front, and that he had stretched out his thin arms to Harry with a look of supplication. Harry caught him and laid him sideways on the cool grass.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Dobby, no, don’t die, don’t die -‘

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: The elf’s eyes found him, and his lips trembled with the effort to form words.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: ‘Harry … Potter …’

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
text_content: And then with a little shudder the elf became quite still, and his eyes were nothing more than great, glassy orbs sprinkled with light from the stars they could not see.

book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (UK)
